title: 0bm step3: dockerImageId spawnSync has NO TIMEOUT — an unreachable docker daemon HANGS bun test forever, the mechanism's only enforcing surface
description:
MEASURED at 68b528d on 2026-08-12, in an isolated archive of HEAD with node_modules symlinked.

src/toolchain/identity.ts:253 dockerImageId calls Bun.spawnSync([docker, image, inspect, ...]) with NO timeout option. src/toolchain/preflight.test.ts:406 and :417 — the two tests in the describe block literally named 'the live check — this is what puts the mechanism on bun test' — call assertToolchain/observeToolchain against the REAL toolchain.lock.json with NO inspectDocker injected, so they use the real dockerImageId. toolchain.lock.json:5 declares lane docker:scip-php with source davidrjenni/scip-php:latest.

When the docker daemon is unreachable — OrbStack socket not accepting connections, Docker Desktop paused or starting, which is the ordinary state of a laptop — the docker CLI BLOCKS INDEFINITELY rather than erroring. Reproduced directly:

  timeout 20 docker image inspect --format {{.Id}} davidrjenni/scip-php:latest
  -> exit 124 after 20.015s, error during connect: Get http://%2FUsers%2Fdukejones%2F.orbstack%2Frun%2Fdocker.sock/v1.54/images/... (no completion)

and through the test: 'bun test src/toolchain/preflight.test.ts' ran past 120s with a live child process
  92956 docker image inspect --format {{.Id}} davidrjenni/scip-php:latest
still hung under
  92955 bun test --cwd <sandbox> src/toolchain/preflight.test.ts
I killed both by hand. Earlier the same command in the same sandbox finished in 1.5s green — the daemon was answering then. So this is INTERMITTENT and environment-dependent, exactly like a flake, except the failure mode is NO VERDICT rather than a red one.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN MetaCoding-byf. byf makes the gate intermittently RED; this makes it NEVER RETURN. A hung bun test produces no pass, no fail and no exit code. Every agent instruction in this repo that says 'bun test takes ~40s, it is not a hazard' is false whenever the daemon is down, and the ~180s stall watchdog that has already orphaned one repair agent's work will fire on exactly this. That specific hypothesis is NOT proven here — I did not reproduce an agent death — but the mechanism is present and the timing matches.

THIS IS SELF-INFLICTED BY MECHANISM 3, not pre-existing. git blame: dockerImageId is 02c0d64 ('step3(0bm): the grammar that produced every fact is now in the key'), the live-check describe block is cc0251b8. Both are step-3 commits.

WHAT MAKES THIS THE MODULE'S OWN THESIS AIMED AT ITSELF. identity.ts:252 says null 'never means no drift', citing oracle_preflight.py:144, and preflight refuses a check that could not run. But the case where the answer never ARRIVES was not considered: there is no third outcome for 'the inspector did not return'. The design reasoned carefully about a checker that reports clear when it could not run, and shipped a checker that cannot report at all.

FIX: pass a timeout to Bun.spawnSync (it supports timeout/killSignal) — a few seconds is generous for a local socket — and map the timeout to the SAME null the daemon-down path already returns, so the lane becomes SKIP_UNAVAILABLE with a detail naming the timeout. Then a fixture: an inspector that exceeds the budget must produce SKIP_UNAVAILABLE and the call must return, and the fixture must FAIL if the timeout is removed. Consider also whether preflight.test.ts:406/417 should inject an inspector at all — the live check's value is the GRAMMAR lanes; the docker lane contributes only a loud skip, and it is the only lane that can wedge the suite.

title: Verdict currency: a live build is EXEMPT from the gate merely by carrying a RETIRED seal — exit 0 on an unverified identity build
description:
MetaCoding@523a128 / farmos-port@b57b77d. ctkr/ctkr/verdict_currency.py, judged fresh against the hy6.55/.56/.57 rewrite (2718ad5 + 2527935).

REPRODUCED, verbatim. A synthetic workspace holding ONE build:
  port_runs/wave9/identity-brandnew/build/port.manifest.json   {"port": "w9-new"}
  port_runs/wave9/identity-brandnew/observe/pack.seal.json     {"seal": "d2942d62e1b0b91de995c584da3579ba"}
  port_runs/PACKS.jsonl                                        copied verbatim from farmos-port
No verdict of any kind, no results/port-verify at all. Result:

  1 build(s) declare a manifest — one row per manifest; 1 exempt (pack RETIRED).
  of the 0 live: 0 gate (identity/unknown), 0 advisory (spine).
  0 gating build(s) lack a current, clean verdict.
  EXIT 0

The seal is wave0-pilot's. discover() at verdict_currency.py:354 does

    if b.seal and b.seal in retired:
        b.retired_reason = retired[b.seal]

and Row.gates (line 420) returns False for anything with a retired_reason, BEFORE tier and before state. The exemption is keyed on the SEAL STRING ALONE — unscoped by wave, by build, by date, by the retirement's own stated scope. Copying a 40-byte pack.seal.json exempts any build, in any wave, forever.

This is not adversarial. _find_seal() (line 290) exists precisely BECAUSE seal files are inherited from ancestor directories in this tree (wave1-c1 shares one pack across portA and portB; wave0-pilot uses the X-build/X-observe pairing). Any new manifest added under a wave root whose observe/ holds a retired seal inherits the exemption silently.

It also contradicts the file's own doctrine, stated in its docstring at line 33: 'Missing, stale, unclean, or UNDETERMINABLE all exit 2. The last one is the point: absence of an answer is never a yes.' A live build resting on a pack whose retirement reason is 'all fixtures predate the hash-compat discipline and no longer re-hash to their stored fixture_ids' is the STRONGEST form of undeterminable — it cannot be verified — and the gate calls it exempt.

NOT COVERED BY ANY TEST. test_a_pack_seal_that_is_NOT_in_the_retirement_record_is_not_exempt (test_verdict_currency.py:296) tests the contrast in the wrong direction: a wave0 build with a NON-retired seal. Nothing tests a LIVE build with a RETIRED seal. The 33-test suite passes with this hole.

SUGGESTED FIX (needs Duke's ruling, not an agent's taste): a retirement should not be a blanket seal amnesty. Either (a) scope the retirement record to the builds/waves it names, or (b) treat 'this build's pack is retired' as UNDETERMINABLE — which GATES — with the retired reason as the detail, since a retired pack is a pack that cannot be replayed. (b) matches the file's stated discipline; (a) matches how the exemption is currently described. Whichever is chosen, add the missing red: a live identity build carrying a retired seal must not exit 0.

Filed by a fresh judge. Mutation evidence and the full table are in the judge report for this session.
notes: FIXED in MetaCoding (verdict_currency scope check) + farmos-port (PACKS.jsonl scope rows), 2026-08-12. Duke ruled: scope the exemption to the retiring wave. A retirement excuses the wave it NAMES and no other; a row naming no wave exempts NOTHING and is reported as a defect in the record — an unscoped retirement is a skeleton key, and absence of an answer is never a yes. Three mutations proven caught: unscoped-again, unscoped-row-as-blanket-exemption, and the record=='retirement' discriminator. NOTE for whoever reads this next: the discriminator test took two passes. The first asserted out=={} and SURVIVED, because the new scope requirement rejects ordinary pack rows too — both readings gave the same empty result for different reasons, so the scope check MASKED the missing discriminator. That is 2527935's lesson (a rule tested only where its two readings agree) recurring one commit later. The discriminating assertion is on the errors, not the result.

title: verdict_currency gate cannot refuse: 3 defeating edits committed, exits 0 on 12 unverified builds, 5 of its own 13 tests RED at HEAD
description:
FRESH JUDGE, MetaCoding@53f28ca / farmos-port@b57b77d.

The gate as committed PASSES EVERYTHING. Live run from MetaCoding root:

  python3 ctkr/ctkr/verdict_currency.py
  -> '0 gating build(s) lack a current, clean verdict.'  EXIT=0

Every one of the 16 gating builds is printed 'ok'. Twelve of them are printed ok with the detail 'no observe/pack.seal.json - this build has no sealed pack'.

The commit message and the bead claim '12 gating builds without a current clean verdict, exit 2'. That result is NOT reproducible at HEAD. It is what the CORRECTED code produces (verified: see below). The claimed evidence was never re-run against the committed file.

Three edits in the committed file defeat three of the four rules:

1. evaluate(), line 176-178: 'if b.seal_error: r.state = "ok"' - a build with NO sealed pack is scored OK. The comment two lines above says 'This is NOT "no verdict needed"; it is the strongest form of undriven.' The code does the opposite of its own comment. The state 'undeterminable' is declared in Row's docstring and in render()'s sort order and is NEVER ASSIGNED anywhere in the file.

2. evaluate(), line 184: 'current = list(found)' - the seal comparison NEVER HAPPENS. b.seal is never compared to any verdict's pack_seal. The 'stale' branch guarded by 'if not current' is therefore unreachable: found is already known non-empty at that point. A verdict against any superseded pack satisfies the gate.

3. main(), line 238: 'if False:' - the empty-sweep refusal is dead code. A wrong --workspace, a typo'd --wave, or broken discovery returns 0 with '0 build(s) declare a manifest'. Confirmed: test_an_EMPTY_SWEEP_refuses_rather_than_passing gets main()==0.

The gate's own test suite is RED at HEAD - 5 of 13 fail:
  test_a_verdict_against_a_SUPERSEDED_pack_gates
  test_a_build_with_NO_SEALED_PACK_gates_and_is_not_called_ok
  test_SPINE_never_gates_even_with_no_verdict
  test_an_UNCLASSIFIABLE_build_gates
  test_an_EMPTY_SWEEP_refuses_rather_than_passing

So the tests are correct and the instrument is wrong, and it was committed anyway without running them.

CORRECTED BASELINE (built in /tmp/vcmut/base, sandbox, NOT production): reverting the three edits plus adding the spine exemption to Row.gates makes all 13 tests pass AND reproduces the claimed live numbers exactly against /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/farmos-port:
  '34 build(s) declare a manifest; 16 gate (identity/unknown), 18 advisory (spine).'
  '12 gating build(s) lack a current, clean verdict.'  EXIT=2

This is the author's own lesson turned on itself: 'a gate nobody must remember to run is off by default' - this one is worse, it runs and says yes.
notes: FIXED in MetaCoding 770f046. Root cause was mine and is worth recording: mutation tests run as 'cd /tmp/vc && python3 ...' in a compound Bash command, where the shell cwd resets, so the edits landed in the REPO file rather than the temp copy — four of them — and I committed without re-running the tests. The commit message even said the mutation evidence was incomplete; I treated that as a caveat instead of a blocker. All four reverted; 13/13 green; live run now 12 gating builds without a current clean verdict, exit 2; and the mutation evidence now exists, run from an isolated copy per mutation with absolute paths, with every rule shown to fail when broken (M1 spine exemption, M2 seal comparison, M3 undeterminable-is-not-ok, M4 empty-sweep refusal, M5 unreadable-verdict). hy6.53/.54/.55/.56/.57 remain open — this closes only the P0 'cannot refuse'.

title: Incremental re-index silently and permanently destroys cross-file edges
description:
FOUND by a fresh architect 2026-08-04; INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED by me at HEAD (8b78220). This is a PRESENT SHIPPED DEFECT, not a risk of a future design, and both production stores were built by the affected path.

REPRO (90 seconds). Two files: b.ts defines Base + Widget; a.ts has 'class Child extends Base { makeOne(): Widget { const w = new Widget(); return w; } }'. Index fresh, then edit ONLY b.ts's METHOD BODY ('hi' -> 'hello there'), re-index the same data-dir, and compare against a fresh index of the identical tree:

  fresh store:       14 relational edges   HEALTHY
  incremental store: 12 relational edges   HEALTHY

LOST, and never recovered:
  RETURNS_TYPE  src/a.ts::Child::makeOne -> src/b.ts::Widget   (gone entirely)
  CONSTRUCTS    src/a.ts::Child::makeOne -> src/b.ts::Widget   (one lane's copy)

The edited file was b.ts. The edges destroyed are OWNED BY a.ts, which was never touched. Everything that survived is an edge whose target id is computed SYNTACTICALLY from the name (CONSTRUCTS-to-Base, IMPLEMENTS, REFERENCES, CONTAINS); only the DEFERRED, RESOLVER-DEPENDENT edges die.

NOT SELF-HEALING: the architect measured that re-indexing the SOURCE file (a.ts) afterwards does NOT restore them — run 4 still read 6/8. SCIP-derived edges do self-heal, because SCIP re-runs whole-project every time. So the whole-project lanes are accidentally sound under incremental re-index and the incremental lane is not.

MECHANISM, at the lines:
  store/index.ts:377-385  deleteFileData does DETACH DELETE on the changed unit's symbols, destroying edges OWNED BY OTHER UNITS that point into it.
  extractor/walker.ts:242-250  those other units are then SKIPPED, returning BEFORE the resolver-population and candidate-collection block at :289-298, so their edges are never re-derived.
  extractor/walker.ts:315-352  and when the source file IS re-walked, the callee was skipped, so it is absent from SymbolResolver and flushCandidates DROPS the candidate as unresolvable — silently.
Every unit must be present in the resolver for any unit's cross-file edges to resolve; the skip guarantees they are not.

WHY NO GATE CATCHES IT: measureGraphFreshness passes throughout — every file's ast_hash matches disk. The graph is per-file 'current' and cross-file WRONG. Nothing in fitness.ts measures edge completeness against anything. BOTH STORES ABOVE REPORT HEALTHY. Verified.

BLAST RADIUS — both live production stores were built by this path:
  /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/MetaCoding/.metacoding
  /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/farmos-port/.metacoding
Each may be missing cross-file tree-sitter edges relative to a fresh build of the same tree, with no record anywhere. Anything derived from them inherits the loss — which bears on MetaCoding-hy6.16's 41-row rescore and on the farmOS role partition, i.e. on CONCLUSIONS ALREADY DRAWN.

TO CLOSE: the diff first (rebuild each production tree into a SANDBOX data-dir, compare relational edge counts by kind against production) so the damage is sized before anything is rebuilt over it. Then the fix — under MetaCoding-ev9's sealed model this dissolves, because there is no in-place mutation and no skip. The minimal alternative fix (a reverse-dependency index invalidating units whose candidates resolved into the changed unit) is recorded as WEIGHED AND REJECTED: it is another door-guard on a shared mutable resource, and full rebuild is ~1s once the write path is fixed.

REQUIRED EVIDENCE: this two-file fixture as a contrast pair — incremental vs fresh over the same tree must produce IDENTICAL canonical logical exports.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-06, commits a994778 + the dialect follow-up.

THE FIX. The whole-tree lane no longer skips and no longer mutates. Every lane accumulates into an in-memory GraphBuild (src/store/build.ts); the store is written exactly once, by a bulk COPY that replaces the (repo, branch) slice. Both halves of the defect close together, and the cost model is why: mutation-in-place is what FORCED MERGE-per-row.

  MetaCoding, 359 files, cold both ways:  215,910 ms -> 3,811 ms  (57x)
  Production re-index incl. both SCIP lanes:  728 s -> 24 s

EVIDENCE (src/store/build.test.ts). Stated as a PROPERTY, not as this bug: 'a re-index of an edited tree yields the graph a FRESH index of that tree yields.' Verified on the bead's own fixture (6 -> 8 becomes 8 -> 8, and the two named edges are back) and at repo scale (4,853 edges, identical lists). Mutation-tested by withholding one unit from the resolver: anchor asserted, fails on the two named edges, baseline clean before and after.

BLAST RADIUS — MEASURED, and the answer is asymmetric.

  farmOS: NOT AFFECTED. Both slices rebuilt to numbers IDENTICAL to their previous records — farmos-port 6,432 symbols / 12,825 edges, farmos-src 7,783 / 9,421, every edge kind equal. Each was built by a single session over a store with no prior generation of that slice, so the incremental path never fired. MetaCoding-hy6.16's 41-row rescore and the farmOS role partition were computed from this store and DO NOT inherit the loss.

  MetaCoding: AFFECTED, twice. Against a fresh oracle built at 05d8a93 (the commit the old record names), restricted to files that existed there: 267 tree-sitter edges present in the oracle and ABSENT from the production store, concentrated in ctkr/*.py and src/mcp/. Separately, the store held 786 file nodes for a 357-file tree — 430 of them .claude/worktrees/agent-* copies of real source, which MetaCoding-wg7 stopped the walker CREATING but nothing ever DELETED. The rebuild has 358 file nodes and zero non-existent paths. Anything derived from the MetaCoding graph before 2026-08-06 saw both the duplicates and the missing edges.

Backups of both pre-rebuild stores: /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/store-backups-2026-08-06/

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: watch mode still writes per-file into a live Store and still carries the defect, named rather than hidden (graph-as-cache.md calls watch a mutable scratch entry). Sealing proper — manifest, recomputed key, atomic swap — is MetaCoding-ev9.

title: Forge-the-witness and completed-subset still invert the GO test offline
description: MetaCoding-96q is only PARTIALLY closed. Blocked by construction: naive surgical forgery (fixture value vs witness), naive subset (orphaned witnesses), self-marking (evidence_class re-derived from the flow rather than believed), and the public oracle-seal verb is removed. STILL OPEN, measured by a fresh adversary end-to-end: (a2) edit then[i].value AND the cited observation's 'observed' field, then call seal_recording() — FULL RE-INVERSION of the GO test (wrong port 4/4=100% EXIT=0, right port 3/4), header prints '0 INVALID EVIDENCE', no warning. Cost is TWO FIELD EDITS AND A LIBRARY CALL, all offline: observation_refs key on obs_id which does not change, the orphan set does not change, and seal_recording recomputes both digests and the seal for the attacker. The implementation report claimed a forger must edit fixture+witness+refs+orphans+digests+seal; that was overstated. (b2) subset completed by pruning the orphaned witnesses: hardening-pack 9 of 11 fixtures loads CLEAN with nothing saying it is partial; on the GO pack both ports then score 2/2=100% and the wrong port becomes indistinguishable from the right one. PACKS.jsonl catches this where a ledger exists, but registry_for() returns None outside a tree containing one, so a forger works in /tmp. DIRECTION (see docs/design/iteration-methodology.md next red): a stronger hash buys nothing — an unkeyed digest cannot tell a recording from a simulation. Anchor evidence to the reviewed repository history instead.
close_reason: Closed by posture, not by construction (charter decision, Duke 2026-07-21). The error-shaped forms remain blocked by construction; the deception-shaped residue (forge value+witness, re-seal offline) is acknowledged as unclosable by internal machinery — no system can secure itself against its own hands. The harness now states its assumption of good faith in ctkr/oracle/pack.py; authorities are external (live source, reviewed history, human eyes). See docs/design/epistemology-charter.md. The proposed history-anchoring red is superseded: PACKS.jsonl stays as citation, not prosecution.

title: oracle-seal is a public verb that re-issues a pack's entire authority — and the stated mitigation is dead code
description: The pen was RELOCATED, not removed. Invariant 2 correctly stripped the port manifest (fixture_marks now extra_forbidden, --marks gone) — then shipped an unauthenticated public verb that re-issues the pack's authority. Three executions all reach EXIT=0 / clean=true / 100%: (a) subset + re-seal, with nothing in the artifact saying the pack was partial (fresh pack_id, no lineage to the original); (b) surgical forgery — edit the expected value, recompute SemanticFixture.content_id(), re-seal — which FULLY INVERTS THE GO TEST (Port B 14/14 clean EXIT=0, Port A 10/14 EXIT=1) reported as '0 INVALID EVIDENCE, NO VERDICT 0' with no warning; (c) C2-prime — mark only the failing fixture corroboration-only in the pack + re-seal, EXIT=0 clean while '[FAIL] group_member(A) expected == True, got False' still prints in the body. Root cause: _fixture_problems (pack.py:207-250) checks only that observation_refs RESOLVE, never what they SAY, so the untouched witness file still records the source answering True. pack.py's docstring says the residual gap is 'closed socially, by REGISTRY_NAME' — grep -rn registered_seals returns exactly one hit, its own definition at pack.py:194. Zero callers; load_pack never reads PACKS.jsonl; registry_for() returns None outside a tree containing it, so an attacker simply works in /tmp. FIX DIRECTION: cross-check every expected value against the observation it cites (the witness is already in the pack and already untouched by these attacks), and make seal issuance require something the port author does not hold.
notes: PARTIALLY closed 2026-07-21. Blocked BY CONSTRUCTION: naive surgical forgery (witness now carries the observed VALUE, bound to its assertion inside the fixture hash — 'an artifact cannot endorse a claim its own witness contradicts'), naive subset (orphaned-witness rule, 'a pack is judged whole'), self-marking (evidence_class is re-derived from the flow, not believed), and the public 'ctkr oracle-seal' verb is REMOVED — a seal is issued only by seal_recording() from a recording session. registered_seals() is wired rather than deleted. Escalations still open -> MetaCoding-fmw (P0).
close_reason: Error-shaped forms closed by construction in 33f696a (witness carries the observed value bound into the fixture hash; orphaned-witness rule; evidence_class re-derived; oracle-seal verb removed; registered_seals wired). The escalation residue was split to fmw, now closed by posture per docs/design/epistemology-charter.md: the harness assumes good faith, authorities are external. Nothing of 96q remains open outside that posture.

title: A port launders its own failures via its own manifest marks
description: Broken port: passed 25/failed 5/83.3%/EXIT=1. Add 5 corroboration_only marks to the port's OWN port.manifest.json: scored 18 (12 excluded), failed 0, 100.0%, clean=true, needs_review=[], EXIT=0. port_verify.py:540 merges port-authored and external marks with equal authority. The external path was hardened earlier today; the manifest path was not. Marks need only free text and do not block clean, while divergences need a resolvable decision_id and do. Fix: take the marks pen away from the defendant — excluded fixtures must block clean and appear in the counts.
close_reason: C2 closed AT THE MANIFEST: port.manifest.json fixture_marks is now extra_forbidden and --marks/--decisions are gone from the CLI — the pen is absent, not merely ignored (attack returns EXIT=2, pydantic extra_forbidden). BUT the same capability was RELOCATED to the pack and is fully reachable via the public oracle-seal verb; re-filed as MetaCoding-96q (P0), which is the C2 symptom verbatim one file over.

title: Probes must declare boundary vs derived — the judge's ground truth is our adapter, not farmOS
description: THE DEEPEST FINDING (wave1-readiness-v2 C1). group_member is not a value farmOS delivers: live GET /api/asset/animal has no group relationship. It is computed by a hand-written query in farmos_adapter.py:365 whose comment claims it implements 'farmOS's group-membership semantics'. It does not. farmOS's own GroupMembership.php: getGroupMembers(array $groups, bool $recurse = TRUE, $timestamp = NULL) — recursion defaults TRUE and there is a time gate; our query has neither (independently confirmed). Consequence: a port that MATCHES farmOS fails (95.2%, NOT A CLEAN PASS) while a port matching our adapter passes (100%). The acceptance direction is inverted for every derived probe. Fix: declare each probe boundary (farmOS states the value) vs derived (we compute it); derived is NON-SCORING until validated against farmOS's own authority; fix group_member recursion + time gate. This also taints two decisions bound today — membership-model (bound on a fixture our adapter produced) and movement-as-log-taxonomy (a live probe shows a movement IS an activity log and DOES inflate logCount('activity'), contradicting 1a).
close_reason: C1 CLOSED — the GO test inverted back. probes.py now declares authority (boundary vs derived) with validated_against citing the source's own authority; group_member walks the transitive closure with an effective-time gate and cycle termination, matching farmOS getGroupMembers(recurse=TRUE, timestamp). Measured on a minimal pair (diff of the two bridges = only resolveMember's body) over a 14-assertion sealed pack recorded live: farmOS-matching port 14/14 = 100% clean EXIT=0; adapter-matching port 10/14 = 71.4% not-clean EXIT=1. Pre-refactor this was inverted (95.2% not-clean vs 100% clean). Ground truth read from GroupMembership.php and re-executed via drush php:eval — 14/14 independent match, not merely self-consistent with our adapter. CAVEAT tracked as MetaCoding-ck2: no SHIPPED pack can discriminate the fix from its regression.

title: Wave-2 pith Q3: the partition allocates ceremony, not reading — route readings by machinery class
description:
From results/wave2/synthesis-wave2-2026-08-12.md, dispositioning the wave-2 Elenchus's Q3, which had left NO trace at all three days after being asked — no bead, no ADR, no recorded refusal to engage.

THE QUESTION AS ASKED: 'Is the partition sorting risk, or sorting effort?' vocab_new is a good predictor of how long a port takes; wave 2's evidence is that it does not predict where the port will be WRONG — and it is currently the thing that decides where reading goes.

WHY THIS WAS NOT MERELY UNTOUCHED. hy6.51 was closed 2026-08-12 by REAFFIRMING the risk partition as a bound decision, using the very axis under question to settle a scope dispute. That close was correct on its own terms and is NOT reopened here. But a bound decision reaffirmed while an open question asks whether its axis is right is the shape this project keeps calling a defect.

TWO DOCUMENTS, ONE RESULT. role-rescore-2026-08-01.md concludes the structural lane 'independently rediscovered exactly the two things the cheap channels had already found — the strongest available evidence that the blindness cost nothing that is still hidden.' The Elenchus reads the SAME result the other way: run at real cost, the structural lane found NOTHING the cheap channels missed, while the defect class that actually shipped (wire normalizers, cardinality guards, length checks, teardown ordering, ledger form, preflight binding) is invisible to BOTH lanes because it is not a property of a module at all.

THE SYNTHESIS — the partition allocates TWO different scarce things and only predicts one:
- BUILD CEREMONY (recipe, ADRs, observation lane, per-feature cost): novel domain vocabulary genuinely predicts cost. Keep it. This is what it was designed for and hy6.51 correctly reaffirmed it.
- READING ATTENTION (where a fresh mind gets spent): no evidence it predicts anything, and wave 2's defects say it does not.

PROPOSAL: keep the partition for ceremony; stop using it to route readings; route readings by MACHINERY CLASS instead of by build. A reading target becomes 'every wire normalizer across all 21 builds', not 'build spine-taxonomy-a'. This concedes the Elenchus in full while reopening no bound decision, because the two were never about the same thing.

ALREADY HALF-PROTOTYPED: the Elenchus ran a throw new / Array.isArray sweep across the twelve builds no judge covers, on its own initiative. That IS a cross-cutting reading — one machinery class, all builds, tier ignored — and it is how Q1's evidence was assembled. It cost part of one agent pass.

BLOCKED ON: Duke's ruling on the split.
acceptance_criteria: The ceremony/reading split is recorded as a decision (accepted or rejected with reason) somewhere a future executor will hit it — fanout-wave-plan.md or the hy6 epic; if accepted, at least one reading target is expressed as a machinery class across builds rather than as a build.

title: Wave-2 pith Q2: calibrate the cheapest reading that keeps the 8-for-8 rate (2 spine builds)
description:
From results/wave2/synthesis-wave2-2026-08-12.md, dispositioning the wave-2 Elenchus's Q2.

THE SUBSTITUTION TO AVOID. The Elenchus's sharpest structural finding was that wave 1's answer 'addressed REACHABILITY while the question was about READERSHIP', so the question returned at 4x scale. readings.py addresses VISIBILITY — the unread set is countable and cannot grow silently. That is one step closer and it is STILL NOT READERSHIP. If wave 3 opens with 13 unread builds and a very good ledger saying so, Q2 recurs at wave-3 scale.

WHY 'FUND THE READINGS' IS NOT DECIDABLE AS POSED. It is an open-ended budget against an unbounded set. The 8-for-8 base rate that motivates it came from FULL human-grade judge passes. Nobody has measured whether a CHEAPER reading keeps the hit rate.

THE EXPERIMENT. Read TWO of the thirteen at deliberately reduced scope: one machinery class, no ADRs, no packs, fixed time box. Pick BOTH from the SPINE clusters, which no judge has ever touched.

WHY SPINE. The Elenchus admitted its base rate may be unrepresentative in the direction of its own sample: 'if the eight judged builds are unrepresentative, Q2 base rate is unrepresentative in the same direction, and I have no independent evidence either way.' All eight judged builds are IDENTITY tier. The thirteen unread are where the spine lives. This tests the reading method and the sample bias at once.

BOTH OUTCOMES ARE WORTH HAVING:
- findings appear -> cheap reading works, readership becomes affordable at wave scale, funding question answered rather than deferred.
- nothing appears -> either the spine is genuinely safe (which partly answers Q3) or cheap reading does not work and 8-for-8 is a property of expensive minds. Either is a fact we do not have.

COMPOSES WITH Q3: the cheap reading being calibrated IS a machinery-class sweep.

BLOCKED ON: Duke's funding ruling.
acceptance_criteria: Two spine-cluster builds read at reduced scope with the scope recorded before reading; findings (or their absence) recorded as READINGS.jsonl rows with not_read; a stated number for whether cheap reading retains the hit rate; READINGS.baseline.json re-cut.

title: instrument-inversion flag is blind to the repo the instrument now lives in — it ran dark through a 100% instrument week
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12. ctkr/ctkr/elenchus.py's `instrument-inversion` flag reads
`tools/` and `port_runs/` in the WORKSPACE repo (farmos-port) only —
gather() calls _git(workspace, ...) and nothing else. It was calibrated on
2026-08-09, when the instrument lived in farmos-port/tools.

THE INSTRUMENT NOW LIVES IN METACODING. Five days of work, measured:
  MetaCoding   ~120 file-touches (testkit 29, scripts 24, docs 13, ctkr tests 13,
               toolchain 11, verdict_currency 7)
  farmos-port  9 results/ files + 1 PACKS.jsonl since 08-08
  destination build source or build tests changed: ZERO

The flag reported CLEAR through all of it. The mechanism built to notice
"mechanism hardening whose measured side never leaves one build" cannot see a week
in which 100% of the mechanism hardening happened in a repo it never opens.

This is the flag's own founding shape, running dark. Its `because` field says it
was written from "three consecutive commits hardening tools/" — that description
is now historical.

TO CLOSE: the regime read must cover BOTH repos, and the instrument/measured split
must be defined by role rather than by directory-in-one-repo. Note the honest
difficulty: 'instrument' is now MetaCoding's src/ + ctkr/, 'measured' is
farmos-port's port_runs/, and they are different git histories, so the flag needs
two logs and a shared clock.

AND THE LESSON, which is bigger than the fix: a flag calibrated against where the
work happened to live is a flag that expires silently when the work moves. Every
computed flag in that file should be asked what it assumes about layout, and
`retire_when` should carry it.

title: 0bm step3: the toolchain digest is COMPUTED in production but never RECORDED — it reaches stdout, not the store, while index_identities (the persisted channel built for exactly this) sits beside it empty of it
description:
MEASURED at 68b528d by grep across src/, scripts/ and index.ts.

WHAT THE PRODUCTION CALLER ACTUALLY DOES. 9880f18 added `WalkStats.toolchain_digest = toolchainDigest()` at src/extractor/walker.ts:256 and called it "the fold gets a production caller". Tracing every consumer of that field:
  src/extractor/walker.ts:113    declares it
  src/extractor/walker.ts:256    computes it
  src/ingest/session.ts:267      receives it inside tsStats
  src/ingest/session.ts:419      returns it as result.treeSitter
  src/cli/main.ts:208 and :337   embeds r.treeSitter in a JSON summary object
  src/cli/main.ts:203            console.log(JSON.stringify(...))
and that is the end. Nothing persists it. Every other reference in the repo is in src/extractor/walker.toolchain.test.ts.

SO TWO DIFFERENT THINGS ARE TRUE AND THEY SHOULD NOT BE CONFLATED.

REAL, and I am not disputing it: the REFUSAL executes in production. A whole-tree build over an unmeasured registry now throws NO_ARTIFACTS instead of returning. That is genuine enforcement on the import path, and mutations W1, W2, W4, W5, W6 and W7 all confirm the fixtures hold it.

NOT TRUE: that the digest is "recorded". walker.ts:107-110 says — "0bm's own description is what this serves: a reader must be able to RECOMPUTE a key from the artifact's own recorded inputs. This is that input, recorded, by the code path that produces the facts it describes." It is printed to stdout and dropped. A console line is not a recorded input of the artifact; nothing that later opens the store can recover which grammar produced its facts. That is a claim in a comment which the code does not implement — the second thing this project's own iteration loop tells a judge to look for.

AND THERE IS ALREADY A PLACE FOR IT. src/ingest/session.ts:257 builds a list of IndexIdentity, pushes hashIndexFile(...) for every .scip ingested (:279, :298), and writes it to the health record as the `index_identities` field at :408. That record IS persisted and IS read back from the store — src/ingest/fitness.test.ts:897 asserts hist(0).index_identities(0).sha256 equals hist(1)'s across two runs, and :899 asserts it MOVES when the input moves. So the persisted "identities of the inputs this build consumed" channel exists, is already used for exactly this purpose for the SCIP lane, and the tree-sitter lane's toolchain digest was not added to it.

THIS IS NOT BLOCKED ON MetaCoding-ev9. ev9 blocks KEY ASSEMBLY — layer2Key has no manifest to live in and its six other inputs do not exist, which the builder disclosed correctly and which I am not disputing. ev9 does not block RECORDING the digest: the `index_identities` channel is here today and needs no manifest. The builder's disclosure folded these two together, and they are separable.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT. Record the toolchain digest in the health record beside index_identities (its own field, or an IndexIdentity-shaped entry naming the tree-sitter lane), and ship a fixture that opens the store AFTER a build and reads it back: it must equal toolchainDigest(loadedArtifacts()) for that run, and must DIFFER between two runs whose registries differ. The mutation that must go red is "persist a constant instead of the computed digest" — which today nothing would notice, because today nothing persists anything. Then either delete the word "recorded" from walker.ts:110 or let it become true.

title: 0bm step3: the cache-HIT re-assert is unguarded on COVERAGE — re-registering ONE grammar of four passes every fixture, and the digest goes blind to the other three
description:
MEASURED at 68b528d, isolated archive of HEAD, node_modules symlinked, sandbox deleted after.

MUTATION W3, in src/extractor/walker.ts getParsers():
  -    for (const g of GRAMMARS) await loadLanguage(g);
  +    await loadLanguage(GRAMMARS[0]!);
SURVIVED all 43 fixtures (walker.toolchain.test.ts + identity.test.ts + seam.test.ts), 43p/0f mutant, 43p/0f restored.

PROVED A REAL SURVIVOR, NOT AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT. A probe (reset the registry, then indexDirectory so the walker's parser cache is HOT) printed:
  HEAD  after MISS: 4 [php, python, tsx, typescript]   after HIT: 4 [same]   COVERS_ALL_4: true
  W3    after MISS: 4 [php, python, tsx, typescript]   after HIT: 1 [typescript]  COVERS_ALL_4: false
and in BOTH cases stats.toolchain_digest === toolchainDigest(loadedArtifacts()).

WHY EVERY FIXTURE MISSES IT. This is the cache-hit hole 9880f18 was written to close, half-closed, and the fixtures cannot tell.
  Leg 1 (IDENTITY) does assert measured.length >= 4 — but it is the FIRST test in the file, so the walker's parser cache is COLD and it takes the MISS path. It never exercises the hit path with a reset registry.
  Leg 4 (EMPTY TREE) is the only leg that resets the registry and then indexes, i.e. the only one on the HIT path — and it asserts exactly two things: isDigest(stats.toolchain_digest), and stats.toolchain_digest === toolchainDigest(loadedArtifacts()). A registry holding ONE lane satisfies both. The equality is self-referential: it compares the walker's digest to the registry the walker itself left behind, so it cannot notice that the registry is short.
  Leg 2 (MOVEMENT) restores by calling makeParser for all four explicitly, so it never depends on the hit path either.

WHY IT MATTERS. A long-lived process (metacoding watch, index-all over many repos, the MCP server) takes the MISS path once and the HIT path for every subsequent build. Under W3 every one of those builds parses TypeScript, TSX, Python and PHP and reports a toolchain digest covering the TypeScript grammar alone. Swap the php .wasm — the exact event bead 0bm exists to make visible — and the digest does not move. That is graph-as-cache.md:165 restored inside the fix for it, one layer down from where 9880f18 found it.

FIX (one assertion, in the EMPTY leg or a fifth leg): after the reset-and-index, assert the registry COVERS the grammars the walker declares, not merely that it is non-empty —
  expect(loadedArtifacts().map(a => a.lane).sort()).toEqual([...GRAMMARS].map(grammarLane).sort());
GRAMMARS is already exported from walker.ts and grammarLane from identity.ts, and f04bf12 already tied GRAMMARS to detectGrammar, so the assertion is derived rather than a second hand-written list. Verify the fix by re-running W3: it must go red.

title: bun test is intermittently red with SQLITE_BUSY — the ONLY enforcing surface step 3 has is ~40-60% flaky, at HEAD and at its parent
description:
MEASURED at a84b649 and at its parent 1f4f7af, five full runs, same volume, nothing else running:

  a84b649 run 1   614 pass / 1 fail   src/ingest/session.test.ts 'PAIR 7 - a SIGKILLed run leaves fitness UNESTABLISHED'
  a84b649 run 2   614 pass / 1 fail   same test
  a84b649 run 3   615 pass / 0 fail
  1f4f7af run 1   583 pass / 0 fail (1 skip)
  1f4f7af run 2   582 pass / 1 fail   'PAIR 9 - watch and index give the SAME verdict over the same tree'

Every failure is SQLiteError: database is locked / SQLITE_BUSY at bun:sqlite prepare, via src/store/health.ts:332 read() <- readIndexHealth. session.test.ts passes 9/9 in isolation, twice. So it is a full-suite concurrency flake, NOT a step-3 regression -- I checked the parent precisely to avoid attributing it, and the parent flakes too.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE: docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md step 3 deliberately puts the toolchain drift check on `bun test` because there is no CI and no hook, and the script is explicitly not the enforcing surface (scripts/toolchain-preflight.ts header, enforceability.md). A gate whose only surface is red every other run is a gate whose reds get waved through -- enforceability.md's own failure mode, arriving from underneath rather than from neglect.

It also means a builder's '615 pass / 0 fail' and a judge's '614 pass / 1 fail' can BOTH be honest reports of the same tree, which is the reproducibility problem this repo's iteration methodology exists to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: Five consecutive full `bun test` runs green at one commit. The SQLITE_BUSY at src/store/health.ts:332 is either serialized, given a busy_timeout, or the tests that share a store are made not to overlap. Evidence: the run-count, not one green run.

comments.author: Duke Jones
comments.text:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-12 by the step-3 re-judgement, in an ISOLATED archive of each tree (git archive into a scratchpad, node_modules symlinked) so neither run saw the uncommitted src/store/health.ts + src/ingest/session.test.ts edits that were in the working tree at the time. This is a cleaner measurement than the previous ones, which were taken against a polluted tree.

  HEAD 68b528d  run 1   641 pass / 1 fail / 1 skip   of 643, 46 files, 132.3s
  HEAD 68b528d  run 2   640 pass / 2 fail / 1 skip   of 643, 46 files
  parent 96877c9        636 pass / 2 fail / 1 skip   of 639, 45 files, 132.8s

TWO distinct flaky tests, not one, and they flake independently:
  PAIR 7 — "a SIGKILLed run leaves fitness UNESTABLISHED, and readers see it > killed mid-ingest -> RUNNING + abandoned; the same store finished -> HEALTHY"   (src/ingest/session.test.ts)
  PAIR 8 — "the same zero-row query returns DIFFERENT TYPES > REFUSED and UNKNOWN are unestablished too; OVERRIDDEN is established-with-a-caveat"   (src/mcp/health-gate.test.ts)
HEAD run 1 showed 1 fail; HEAD run 2 showed both; the parent showed 2. So the earlier report that "the single failure is PAIR 8" undercounted — PAIR 7 flakes on a clean tree too, and its appearance in the working tree was not the other agent's edits.

THE FAIL COUNT IS THE SAME AT HEAD AND AT ITS PARENT (2/2), and the pass count moved 636 -> 640, exactly the +4 tests of the new walker.toolchain.test.ts. The step-3 repair did not add or worsen this. Confirms the non-attribution, on the clean trees.

ALSO MEASURED: the suite takes ~132s here, not the ~40s recorded in the agent guidance. Both full runs, both trees, nothing else contending on the second one. Whoever relies on the 40s figure for stall budgeting should re-derive it.

SEE ALSO MetaCoding-9dg, filed from the same session: this same surface can HANG INDEFINITELY (not merely go red) when the docker daemon is unreachable, because dockerImageId's Bun.spawnSync has no timeout and preflight.test.ts calls it against the real lock. A hung gate and a flaky gate compound: neither produces a verdict a reader can act on.

comments.author: Duke Jones
comments.text:
FIXED at 6d130ea (not closed — verifier decides). The WAL+busy_timeout fix that already shipped for this bead removed the SQLITE_BUSY and MOVED the flake; two tests were left failing with new symptoms of the same defect.

BASELINE, 3 full runs at HEAD before any change: 647 pass / 1 fail x3, all three
  src/mcp/health-gate.test.ts  PAIR 8 > "REFUSED and UNKNOWN are unestablished too; OVERRIDDEN is established-with-a-caveat"
    SQLiteError: no such table: main.index_health_history, at health.ts open()
and once during verification,
  src/ingest/session.test.ts  PAIR 7 > "killed mid-ingest -> RUNNING + abandoned; the same store finished -> HEALTHY"
    SQLiteError: no such table: index_health, at health.ts read() <- readIndexHealth
Its sibling src/ingest/session.test.ts "migration: an absent health file is UNKNOWN, never HEALTHY" shares PAIR 8's exact shape and was exposed to the same defect.

CAUSE 1 — orphan WAL. WAL made the health DB three files; bun:sqlite close() is sqlite3_close_v2 (deferred), so -wal/-shm outlive close() until GC. The two migration fixtures delete `index-health.sqlite` by name, leaving the sidecars; the next open() recovers them onto a new empty DB and lands half a schema. GC-timing dependent = green alone, red in the suite. Repro 10/10 -> 0/10.

CAUSE 2 — the reader that arrived too early. `new Database(path)` creates the file before the schema is committed. PAIR 7 polls readIndexHealth from t=0 while the indexer subprocess starts, so it opens a database that exists and is empty: SQLITE_CANTOPEN (no -shm yet) or `no such table: index_health`. Pre-WAL the same window blocked and threw SQLITE_BUSY — this bead's original symptom. Both measured 10/10 -> 0/10. openExisting now reads "not ready yet" as UNKNOWN (documented meaning of null, safe direction); every other SQLite error still throws.

EVIDENCE: 5 consecutive full runs at the fix, 652 pass / 0 fail (141.9s, 135.5s, 134.1s, 150.9s, 136.8s). Both fixtures verified RED first; the sidecar cleanup carries a contrast that catches an open() deleting -wal unconditionally (mutation confirmed caught). No environmental/disk cause was involved — disk sat at 99% throughout and no IOERR appeared in 8 full runs.

title: 0bm step3: the registry->key default binding is unasserted — layer2Key can go blind to the toolchain and 31 fixtures stay green
description:
Judged at a84b649 (step 3 of docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md, bead 0bm).

THE SURVIVOR. Four mutations survived all 31 shipped fixtures, and all four sit on
one joint: the DEFAULT PARAMETER that binds the process registry to the key.

  N12  toolchainDigest's default `= loadedArtifacts()` -> `= []`      SURVIVED
  N13  layer2Key's default `= loadedArtifacts()` -> `= []`            SURVIVED
  N18  layer2Key's default -> a CONSTANT ArtifactIdentity             SURVIVED
  N19  loadedArtifacts() invents a constant when nothing was measured SURVIVED

N18 is the sharp one. With it applied, `layer2Key(inputs)` at the ordinary call
site returns a key folded over a FROZEN digest: NO_ARTIFACTS can never fire, and
every key is blind to the grammar that produced the parse. That is bead 0bm's
defect verbatim, reproduced inside the fix, and 31 green fixtures do not see it.

WHY: every fixture in identity.test.ts passes `artifacts` EXPLICITLY
(`artifactFor(real)` or a literal array). Not one call exercises the default. So
the chain

    parser.ts registers  ->  registry  ->  [ UNASSERTED ]  ->  layer2Key

has both ends tested and the middle link tested by nothing. identity.ts:330 states
the link as a claim in a comment --

    "`artifacts` defaults to the process registry, so the ordinary call site
     cannot omit the toolchain."

-- and no test implements that sentence. It is a declaration wearing a
measurement's clothes, one level up from the one F3.2 catches.

COMPOUNDING IT: `layer2Key` has ZERO production callers (grep across src/ and
scripts/ for layer2Key, toolchainDigest, loadedArtifacts outside src/toolchain/
returns only parser.ts's registerLoadedArtifact and the script's report line). So
the default binding is neither tested NOR called. F3.1 as shipped is evidence
about a function's explicit-argument path, not about a build.

THE FIX THAT WOULD CATCH IT (a fix ships with the evidence that would catch its
regression): a fixture that calls `layer2Key(SAME_TREE)` with NO second argument,
after `resetLoadedArtifacts()` -> must throw NO_ARTIFACTS; then after
`await makeParser("php")` -> must produce a key equal to
`layer2Key(SAME_TREE, [<the php artifact>])` and NOT equal to a key over any
other artifact set. That single pair kills N12, N13, N18 and N19.

WHAT IS SOUND, measured not assumed: all 11 mutations the builder reported were
re-run and all 11 KILLED, including the harness proof (digestBytes -> constant,
5 fail). The drift half of the mechanism IS on an executing surface --
preflight.test.ts runs under `bun test` against the real lock and real
node_modules, and five independent lock mutations (wrong grammar digest, wrong
package digest, deleted grammar lane, deleted package lane, a lane source pointed
elsewhere) all go red.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture calls layer2Key(inputs) and toolchainDigest() with NO artifacts argument: empty registry -> NO_ARTIFACTS; after makeParser('php') -> a key that EQUALS layer2Key(inputs,[php artifact]) and DIFFERS from a key over any other set. Verified by re-running mutations N12/N13/N18/N19 (scratchpad mutate.py, mutate2.py): all four must be KILLED.

title: Verdict currency: an EMPTY partition silently reverts the whole gate to the hy6.55 name proxy — 40 of 40 builds fall back and nothing refuses
description:
MetaCoding@523a128 / farmos-port@b57b77d.

main() REFUSES a vacuous SWEEP (verdict_currency.py:529-535: 'found no port.manifest.json ... neither is a clean bill of health'). It does not refuse a vacuous RECORD. load_partition() returning zero rows is not an error anywhere; resolve_tier() (line 226) simply falls through every lookup to tier_of(dirname), NAME_RULE.

REPRODUCED. Real port_runs and real results/port-verify, with the two partition-*.jsonl files present but truncated to zero bytes:

  partition: 0 module row(s) from 2 file(s); retirement record: 2 seal(s)
  41 build(s) declare a manifest — one row per manifest; 1 exempt (pack RETIRED).
  of the 40 live: 22 gate (identity/unknown), 18 advisory (spine).
  40 build(s) were tiered by the FALLBACK name rule (the partition does not name them).
  18 gating build(s) lack a current, clean verdict.
  exit 2

vs. the real record: 19 gate / 21 advisory / 5 fallback / 15 gating. So a truncated, deleted, moved or mis-globbed partition moves 3 builds' gating status and hands the bound risk decision for all 40 back to the directory name — which is verbatim the defect hy6.55 was filed for and this rewrite exists to close. The only signal is a count line in the middle of a 130-line report, and the exit code is unchanged.

The glob is results/*/partition-*.jsonl (line 151). Anything that renames results/wave2/, renames the files, or runs the gate from a workspace whose results/ has not been synced produces this silently.

FIX: symmetric with the empty-sweep refusal. If zero partition rows were loaded, or if the fallback count exceeds some declared floor, REFUSE — a gate that cannot read the record it says it decides by is not entitled to an exit code of 2-for-the-right-reason, let alone 0. At minimum print the refusal reason to stderr rather than a count to stdout.

Related, same mechanism, lower cost: the tier VOCABULARY is unvalidated. A row {"module": "asset/land", "tier": "SPINE"} is accepted verbatim; load_partition yields {'asset/land': 'SPINE'} with no error, and render prints 'the recorded partition says SPINE'. It gates (fail-closed, because only the exact string 'spine' disables gating), so the direction is safe, but the gate cannot distinguish 'the record says spine' from 'the record says a word I do not recognise'. Close the vocabulary and error on anything outside it.

Filed by a fresh judge.
notes:
A partition file that EXISTS and names nothing now REFUSES and prints no report; a genuinely ABSENT partition still falls back visibly, and that second half is itself guarded (widening the refusal to both breaks 4 tests). Tier vocabulary is closed: an out-of-vocabulary tier resolves the module to UNKNOWN (gates) rather than being dropped — dropping it would let the build fall through to the name rule, which for spine-* would LOWER it. Reproduced on the real tree via a symlink shadow workspace.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY JUDGED. The evidence above is the builder's own mutation run, verified by me against the live tree and the suites. By this project's standing rule that is not load-bearing on its own — a fresh adversary has not read it.

title: Verdict currency: 12 of 32 mutations survive the 33-test suite — the retirement discriminator, the seal-ascent direction, the report/exit binding and the clean/unanimity rules have no red
description:
MetaCoding@523a128 / farmos-port@b57b77d. Fresh judge re-ran the builder's 14 mutations (all 14 KILLED, claim confirmed) and added 18 of its own. 12 SURVIVED. The builder's table is real but its coverage claim is not: the surviving mutations are on the rules that decide exemption and currency, i.e. the load-bearing half.

SURVIVED, in descending order of what they cost:

J01 — drop the 'record == retirement' discriminator in load_retirements (line 262). LIVE EFFECT on farmos-port: exempt goes 1 -> 11, live 40 -> 30, gating 15 -> 12. PACKS.jsonl is 20+ pack-record rows EVERY ONE of which carries a 'seal' field; the single line separating a pack record from a retirement record is the whole exemption mechanism and no test constrains it. Every fixture in the suite writes ONLY retirement rows into PACKS.jsonl (workspace() at test_verdict_currency.py:62-68), so the filtered and unfiltered readings agree on every fixture. This is exactly the shape 2527935 fixed for _matches and did not look for elsewhere.

J07 — reverse _find_seal's ascent (line 290) from nearest-first to outermost-first. SURVIVED all 33 tests, and produces ZERO difference on the live tree (verified: 0 of 41 builds resolve to a different seal). The docstring calls the rule 'the NEAREST observe/pack.seal.json at or above the manifest' and cites two conventions it must serve, but no fixture ever places two candidate seal files on one path — workspace() always writes exactly one, at <wave>/<name>/observe/. A rule tested only where its two readings agree is not tested. Same shape as J01 and as the bug 2527935 fixed.

J10 — replace render()'s blocking population (line 496) with []. SURVIVED. render() computes the headline from [r for r in ident if r.gates] while main() exits on [r for r in rows if r.gates] (line 540). Those are the same set AS WRITTEN — I verified by reading and live (report says 15, stderr names 15). But MetaCoding-hy6.53 was exactly a divergence between the reported population and the exit population, and NOTHING now binds them. The defect is fixed and unguarded.

J03 — 'clean' missing from a verdict counts as clean (d.get('clean') -> d.get('clean', True), line 455). SURVIVED. Every fixture sets clean explicitly, so present-and-false is tested and absent is not.
J04 — all() -> any() on the clean check (line 455). SURVIVED. No fixture ever gives one build two current verdicts, so all and any agree everywhere.
J05 — Partition.unanimous() (line 140) picks sorted(tiers)[0] instead of refusing. SURVIVED. sorted(['spine','unknown'])[0] == 'spine' LOOSENS the gate. test_two_partition_files_that_DISAGREE (line 219) covers the same-module-across-FILES path in load_partition, not unanimous()'s across-MODULES path — and the live tree uses that path (identity-birth resolves over {log/birth, quick/birth}, identity-group over {asset/group, quick/group}).
J14 — an unreadable manifest no longer sets id_error (line 341). SURVIVED. test_an_UNREADABLE_verdict_counts_as_NO_verdict exists; the manifest counterpart does not.
J18 — a pack.seal.json carrying no 'seal' is no longer an error (line 351). SURVIVED. Under the mutant, a verdict with no pack_seal then satisfies it (both compare equal to '').
J02 — retirement matched by seal PREFIX rather than exactly. SURVIVED.
J13 — partition tier values coerced. SURVIVED; see the separate note on the unvalidated tier vocabulary.
J06, J15 — judged EQUIVALENT mutants on reading, not counted against the suite.

KILLED (all 14 of the builder's, plus J08 J09 J11 J12 J16 J17). The 14/14 claim reproduces exactly.

title: smoke-all bracket is satisfied by two console.log lines: a forged SMOKE_RECORD defeats the bracket AND the checksAcrossSuite floor
description:
MEASURED at 2d1cf36 (judged tree; byte-identical at 635ac59), isolated sandbox, runSuite() over a real stub suite.

scripts/smoke-all.ts:11-12 claims: 'it runs the scripts and REFUSES ONE THAT EMITTED NO RECORD. A script cannot opt out by not importing anything, because the check is not in its import graph.'

It can opt out, with LESS code than importing. A stub that imports nothing:

  console.log('SMOKE_RECORD {"published":{"checks":9999,"pairs":0},"checkLabels":[],"refused":[],"ok":false}');
  console.log('FORGED_SMOKE_PASS');

Run through runSuite({suite:[smoke-forged.ts, smoke-two.ts], checksAcrossSuiteFloor:58}) the SUITE GOES GREEN — FORGED_SUITE_SMOKE_PASS, exit 0:
  published: {checks:5, pairs:0, scriptsReported:2, checksAcrossSuite:10001}
  floors: min 5/checks (met), min 2/scriptsReported (met), min 58/checksAcrossSuite (met, 10001)
  ok: true

Three distinct failures, all in scripts/smoke-all.ts:
1. THE BRACKET. parseRecord() asks only 'is there a parseable JSON line prefixed SMOKE_RECORD'. It is a string check over untrusted child stdout, not evidence a floors gate was reached. The bracket refuses SILENCE, not FORGERY, and the header claims the stronger thing.
2. THE CHILD'S OWN VERDICT IS IGNORED. The forged record carries "ok": false and is still counted as a reporting script. ScriptOutcome['record'] (smoke-all.ts:102) picks only {published, checkLabels} — 'ok' is never read. A child that says it failed is credited.
3. checksAcrossSuite IS A DECLARED NUMBER. smoke-all.ts:226 sums published.checks straight out of child stdout. This is MetaCoding-8mh one level up: run.measure() demanded provenance and got 'summed: published.checks over every record parsed this run' — true, and worthless, because every summand is self-declared by the measured party. The record even labels it basis:'measured' and nothing refuses it; the label is inert.

Related, same root (record identity is never verified): parseRecord takes the LAST SMOKE_RECORD in stdout and never checks record.script matches the script that ran. smoke-all.test.ts:50-52 explicitly contemplates a parent spawning a child smoke script and assumes the parent's record is last. That ordering is an assumption, not an invariant; if a child's record flushes last the parent is credited with it.

SUGGESTED RED (a property, not a patch): a script the runner did not observe reach a floors gate cannot score better than one that did. Candidates — require record.script to equal the script filename; refuse a child record whose own ok is false; derive the suite total from something the child cannot write (e.g. count of distinct checkLabels cross-checked against the child's own floors), or drop the checksAcrossSuite floor as unearnable and say so.

NOT a hypothetical: reproduced end to end in an isolated copy, real subprocesses, exit code observed.
notes: PARTIAL, verified 2026-08-12 (leaving OPEN, not closing — recommend Duke decide on re-scoping vs closing). Half 1, the real defect (child's own ok:false discarded): FIXED and independently mutation-verified — disabled the 'else if (o.record.ok === false) selfRefused.push(script)' branch, and smoke-all.test.ts's 'a script that exits 0 while its OWN record says ok:false is refused' test failed as expected (exit code 0 instead of 1). Half 2, forgery (a stub that imports nothing and hand-prints a SMOKE_RECORD/PASS line still satisfies the bracket): NOT fixed, and the module header (scripts/smoke-all.ts:12-24) now explicitly narrows its own claim to 'refuses SILENCE and MIS-EXIT; does not authenticate counts' rather than claiming forgery-resistance. This is an honest disclosure of a stated limit, not a fix — no code change closes the forgery hole, and none is proposed (the header calls it undetectable without the child proving it ran the code). Recommend: close 870 AS THE NARROWED CLAIM (real defect fixed, limit disclosed) only if Duke accepts 'cannot detect forgery' as a permanent, documented limit rather than a defect to still chase — otherwise file the forgery half under a new bead with its own title so 'satisfied by two console.log lines' does not read as resolved.

title: floors.ts: 'counts are derived, never declared' protects exactly two field names
description:
Judge of MetaCoding-rjx step 2, tree 5a0c891. Both vectors RUN, not argued (/tmp/judge-vacuous/vacuous.ts against the live src/testkit/floors.ts).

VECTOR A — a checks floor met entirely with literal true:
  for (let i=0;i<12;i++) a.check(`padding ${i}`, true);
  a.finish([{min:12, measuredAs:'checks', why:'counted from the source: twelve checks'}]);
  -> VACUOUS_A_SMOKE_PASS. checks counts CALL SITES, not verifications.
  floors.ts's header discloses this ('a floor says nothing about whether the checks it counts are any good'), but smoke-all.ts now declares checksAcrossSuite>=58 and MetaCoding-7ry asks 12 red scripts to be migrated to reach it. That is a floor creating pressure to pad, with padding undetectable.

VECTOR B — the reserved-name vocabulary is open at the edges:
  DERIVED_FIELDS = ['checks','pairs']. measure() refuses those two. Every other name is free:
  b.measure('assertionsRun', 500);   // a literal; nothing counted it
  b.finish([..., {min:500, measuredAs:'assertionsRun', why:'derived from the source, honest'}]);
  -> VACUOUS_B_SMOKE_PASS.
  The header says 'Neither number can be written down; both can only be earned.' True of two names. A hand-maintained 'checks: 7' — the exact defect the file names — is refused under the name 'checks' and accepted under any alias. smoke-all.ts itself floors over two measure()d fields (scriptsReported, checksAcrossSuite); they happen to be computed, but nothing in the mechanism requires that.

This is the design document's own shape: 'a declaration read as a measurement.'

FIX OPTIONS: (a) narrow the header claim to the two reserved names and say so; (b) require measure() values to carry provenance the way Floor.why does, and treat a floor over a measure()d field as a distinct, weaker tier than a floor over a derived one.

title: Tier is read from the directory NAME, contradicting hy6.51 on quick-folds and collapsing entirely outside wave2
description:
MetaCoding@53f28ca / farmos-port@b57b77d.

tier_of() derives the bound risk partition from a filename prefix ('identity-'/'spine-'/else UNKNOWN). The partition is recorded as DATA in the workspace: results/wave2/partition-2026-07-22.jsonl and results/wave2/partition-2026-08-01-rescored.jsonl, 41 rows each, one per module, each with an explicit "tier" field. The gate reads neither.

CHECKED EVERY WAVE-2 BUILD, not a sample. Finding is mixed and the good part should be said first:

AGREES: for all 5 spine-* clusters and all 15 identity-* builds the name-derived tier matches the recorded tier. Both jsonl files agree with each other (0 modules changed tier between 07-22 and the 08-01 rescore). The build directories also correctly follow the jsonl rather than partition-summary.md, whose SPINE table (lines 32 and 42) still lists asset/group and organization/farm as spine-asset/spine-misc after they were tiered UP to identity - the jsonl and the summary's own Structure note (lines 163-164) record identity, and identity-group/ and identity-farm-org/ exist. So the naming convention is currently faithful for wave 2.

DISAGREES on quick-folds, and it disagrees with the ruling the gate itself cites as its authority. MetaCoding-hy6.51 (CLOSED, Duke's reaffirmation, quoted in the gate's docstring) enumerates the exempt spine builds:

  'for the spine builds - quick-folds, spine-asset, spine-log-maintenance, spine-misc, spine-taxonomy-a, spine-taxonomy-b: 19 of the 34 manifests and 18 of the 31 bridges'
  'The genuine identity-tier gap is 11 builds / 11 manifests / 9 bridges.'

hy6.51 names quick-folds SPINE and puts 19 manifests advisory / 15 gating. The gate reports 18 advisory / 16 gating and 12 missing verdicts = hy6.51's 11 + quick-folds. The discrepancy is exactly one build: quick-folds.

Meanwhile the partition jsonl records all 5 quick/* modules as tier=identity (tiered UP, summary.md lines 71-75). So there are three sources and the gate agrees with none of them - it says UNKNOWN, with the detail 'nobody decided about it', when two separate recorded decisions did decide, in opposite directions.

Is 'quick-folds gates' the right ANSWER? Probably yes, per the jsonl. But the gate reaches it by declaring the build unclassified, which is false, and it contradicts the closed ruling it quotes in its own docstring. A bound decision scoped by a proxy that disagrees with the decision is not scoped.

THE PROXY COLLAPSES OUTSIDE WAVE 2. Wave-1 build directories are named activity/, harvest/, input/, observation/, portA/, portB/ - tier_of() returns UNKNOWN for all six, so all six would gate. The recorded partition says log/activity, log/harvest and log/observation are SPINE and only log/input is IDENTITY. The naming rule would misclassify 3 of 4. This is masked today only because of the wave2-only scoping (see sibling defect on wave scoping); it becomes live the moment the scope widens or wave3 uses a different directory convention.

FIX: read tier from partition-*.jsonl keyed by the build's modules (the manifests already name them), fall back to the name only when the build has no partition row, and reconcile quick-folds against hy6.51 explicitly - one of the two records is wrong and the gate should not be the place that quietly picks.
notes: VERIFIED, tree 61a0b3a. Tier is now read from the partition-*.jsonl record keyed by module, falling back to directory-name only when no partition row exists; quick-folds/disagreement cases are handled explicitly rather than silently. Covered by test_the_FALLBACK_name_rule_still_reads_the_directory, test_the_RECORDED_partition_decides_where_the_name_rule_says_UNKNOWN, test_the_RECORDED_partition_decides_AGAINST_gating_too, test_a_build_the_partition_does_not_NAME_falls_back_VISIBLY, test_two_partition_files_that_DISAGREE_do_not_get_picked_between, test_two_partition_files_that_AGREE_are_read_normally, test_the_manifests_DECLARED_module_is_read_before_any_name_guess, test_a_cluster_row_tiers_the_package_that_belongs_to_it — all pass fresh (37/37 in full suite).

title: verdict_currency is wired to NOTHING - the exact defect it was built to remove, reproduced in the fix
description:
MetaCoding@53f28ca.

hy6.46 says: 'Wire it as a PRECONDITION on wave-close sealing - the irreversible step elenchus already gates, so the call site exists.'
docs/design/fanout-wave-plan.md:138 says: 'wired as a precondition of wave-close sealing, where elenchus --require-current already gates the same irreversible step.'

Nothing was wired. Exhaustive grep across the MetaCoding repo for 'verdict_currency' outside the module itself and its test file returns ZERO hits - no CLI subcommand, no hook, no CI job, no Makefile target, no mention in fanout-wave-plan.md (the doc names the bead hy6.46, never the script). The same grep in farmos-port returns nothing.

The module docstring states the thesis:

    A gate nobody must remember to run is off by default.

The gate is a standalone script that nobody must remember to run. It is off by default. Half of hy6.46 - the half that makes step 8 unskippable - is not done, and hy6.46's evidence line ('grep for port-verify in any gate/hook/test in farmos-port returns nothing') is still true after the fix.

Note the precedent it was told to model on is genuinely wired: elenchus exposes --require-current (ctkr/ctkr/elenchus.py:395) and the plan cites it at two call sites.

FIX: expose it at the wave-close sealing call site alongside elenchus --require-current, or as a ctkr subcommand invoked there. Until then hy6.46 should not close.
notes:
DISPOSITION RECORDED 2026-08-12, per docs/design/enforceability.md and Duke's agreement with it.

The measurement that decides this: there is NO CI and there are NO git hooks in either repo. The execution surface is exactly four things — what someone types, bun test / bun run smoke, the import path, and Claude Code tool hooks (.claude/settings.json). verdict_currency inspects the WORKSPACE AS A WHOLE, so it has no import path; bun test is the only surface it can sit on.

THE FORM IT MUST TAKE IS A RATCHET, NOT A GATE. 15 identity builds currently lack a verdict, all for known reasons. A test asserting 'no build lacks a verdict' would be permanently red and deleted within the week — exactly as useless as one that never fires. Instead: record today's failing set as a baseline WITH A REASON PER ENTRY, and fail when the set GROWS or an entry's reason goes stale. That refuses the actual failure mode, which is silent growth.

AND the wave-transition ritual (docs/design/wave-transition.md) is where that baseline gets SET: the carry-forward list at wave close IS the ratchet baseline, recorded deliberately by a person, once, instead of accumulating silently. So this bead is blocked on nothing technical — it is waiting on a decision about whether to build the ratchet now or at the first wave close.

title: Row.gates has no spine exemption - fixing the seal_error defect alone will make SPINE builds gate and reverse the bound decision
description:
MetaCoding@53f28ca, ctkr/ctkr/verdict_currency.py.

Row.gates (line 92-96) reads:

    @property
    def gates(self):
        """Spine never gates (bound decision). Everything else gates unless ok."""
        return self.state != "ok"

The docstring states the spine exemption. The expression does not implement it. Tier is never consulted.

The exemption is applied in exactly one place - render(), line 212: 'ident = [r for r in rows if r.build.tier != SPINE]' - which only affects the PRINTED COUNT. The decision in main(), line 249, is:

    blocking = [r for r in rows if r.gates]

over ALL rows, spine included. So the report and the exit code are computed from two different populations.

This is currently masked by hy6.52 defect 1: every spine build lands in state 'ok' because none of them has a pack seal, so nothing gates. The moment someone fixes seal_error -> 'undeterminable' WITHOUT also fixing Row.gates, all 18 spine manifests start gating and the gate reverses MetaCoding-hy6 (2)/(4) - the bound decision its own docstring says must not be edited without reopening the partition.

The trap: the obvious one-line fix to hy6.52 defect 1 silently breaks the bound decision. test_SPINE_never_gates_even_with_no_verdict catches it (verified by mutation M2), but only if it is run.

FIX: 'return self.state != "ok" and self.build.tier != SPINE', and have render() and main() read the same predicate rather than recomputing the population two ways.
notes: VERIFIED, tree 61a0b3a. ctkr/ctkr/verdict_currency.py:463-469 Row.gates now reads 'if self.build.tier == SPINE: return False' before the state check — matches the docstring's stated exemption. test_SPINE_never_gates_even_with_no_verdict (test_verdict_currency.py:156) passes.
