title: discriminate(): integer-like tags silently REORDER — the documented sequential order is false
description:
src/testkit/discriminate.ts:104-110 documents: 'Cases run SEQUENTIALLY in declaration order, never concurrently, so a case may depend on state a previous case established (see seam.test.ts, where class 6 is the same call once the slice reads HEALTHY).'

That is FALSE for any tag that is an integer-like string. The closed vocabulary is Object.keys(spec.cases) (discriminate.ts:138), and JS object key order puts array-index-like keys FIRST, in ascending numeric order, regardless of literal order.

MEASURED (fresh adversary, 2026-08-12, tree 751e7442):
  cases: { "2": .., "10": .., "1": .. }  ->  ran 1, 2, 10.  ok = true, silently.

Order is LOAD-BEARING and this was measured too: mutating discriminate.ts to iterate [...declared].reverse() KILLS seam.test.ts's F1.3 (32 pass / 1 fail), because class 6 depends on the runIndexSession class 5 performed. So a pair that reorders is a pair that silently ran a different experiment, and nothing reports it.

WHY THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the design document's named next target for discriminate() (docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md:96) is scripts/smoke-incremental.ts's FIVE PASSES — 'each pass declares its tags'. Numeric pass tags are the obvious naming and they are exactly the ones that reorder.

FIX (one of):
  a) refuse an integer-like tag (/^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/) as a declared tag, same shape as RESERVED_TAG_DECLARED; or
  b) take cases as an ordered array of {tag, input} / a Map, so declaration order is not the object's to decide.
A fixture is required either way: a pair whose numeric tags would reorder must FAIL (or run in literal order), and the contrast with non-numeric tags must PASS.
acceptance_criteria: A pair declared with integer-like tags either refuses by name or runs in literal declaration order, with a discriminating fixture and its passing contrast. Re-running the reverse-order mutation on discriminate.ts still kills seam.test.ts F1.3.
notes: VERIFIED BY FRESH MUTATION, tree 61a0b3a. Integer-like tags now refused via INDEX_LIKE_TAG (regex /^[+-]?\d+$/ over declared tags in observeDiscrimination). Independently re-mutated: disabled the INDEX_LIKE.test(tag) branch — discriminate.test.ts test 'a lone integer-like tag among named ones is still refused' failed as expected (r.ok was true instead of false). Tree restored, diff-verified clean. Regression tests around discriminate.test.ts:319-360.

title: bun run smoke is RED at smoke-extractor.ts — baseline, predates MetaCoding-9nu
description:
`bun run smoke` fails at the THIRD script, scripts/smoke-extractor.ts:27: it calls indexDirectory(store, dir) with no opts, and src/extractor/walker.ts:131 reads opts.branch -> TypeError: undefined is not an object.

Measured on a CLEAN tree at 3c19efb, BEFORE any 9nu work, and again after: byte-identical failure. Only two smoke scripts (smoke-ladybug, smoke-store) run at all; the remaining 19 are never reached, so `bun run smoke` currently reports nothing about them either way.

Almost certainly the ingest-seam/ticket work (MetaCoding-9ed): indexDirectory now requires an IngestTicket in opts and this smoke script was never updated. It is also mechanism-4 shaped — a suite that stops at script 3 of 22 and a suite that runs all 22 are distinguishable only by reading stderr.
notes:
PARTIALLY FIXED 2026-08-12 (MetaCoding ef99adf). Be precise about what changed, because this bead has been cited as 'known baseline red' in three commit messages and two judge reports.

THE CRASH IS FIXED AND VERIFIED. smoke-extractor.ts called indexDirectory(store, 'src') with two arguments to a function that grew a required third at 037926f, when hy6.9ed turned the ingest seam into a capability and the walker started demanding a ticket. It died on opts.branch of undefined. Now mints a ticket via issueIngestTicket and passes opts. Also made its paths absolute (import.meta.dir) — they were relative, so it worked from the repo root and died with ENOENT anywhere else, including from a mutation sandbox, which is exactly where an instrument gets run when someone is checking whether it can fail. Verified: EXTRACTOR_SMOKE_PASS standalone, twice, indexing 116 files / 3048 symbols / 5344 edges / 62533 tokens in ~88s.

CONSEQUENCE NOBODY HAD MEASURED: bun run smoke fails FAST, so while this script was broken ONLY 2 OF 22 SCRIPTS EVER RAN. Every 'smoke is red at baseline' note this week was describing a suite that was 91% not executing.

WHAT IS STILL RED, and why this stays open:
1. smoke-extractor emits NO SMOKE_RECORD — it is one of the 12 scripts not yet migrated onto floors.ts (MetaCoding-7ry). The suite bracket correctly refuses a script that exits 0 having said nothing, so the suite still exits 1 even when this script passes. That half belongs to 7ry.
2. UNDER CONCURRENT LOAD it fails with SQLITE_IOERR_VNODE. Reproduced: passes standalone, failed inside the suite while four agents and a workflow were running. The disk has been at 99-100% (460 GiB volume, 2-5 GiB free) for this whole session. This is environmental, not a defect in the script — but it means the smoke suite is not reliably runnable while agents are working, which is worth knowing before anyone treats a red suite as a code signal. It is also the leading remaining candidate for this session's unexplained agent stalls, since a full disk presents as an unrelated error in whatever ran next.

title: Step 8's completion condition contradicts the hy6 epic's own risk partition — SPINE builds were exempted from per-feature ceremony by decision
description:
Step 8 states a universal completion condition: 'A build with a bridge and no recorded verdict is not done.' The recipe it sits in is headed 'The per-feature production recipe (what each wave runs)' — no scope qualifier anywhere in docs/design/fanout-wave-plan.md, which never uses the words spine or identity.

The hy6 epic description says the opposite, as a recorded decision:

  (2) SPINE: bulk port, one-mind-per-cluster builders on kernel v1.3,
      NO PER-FEATURE CEREMONY — build + existing regression + smoke.
  (3) IDENTITY: the full recipe.
  (4) READINGS TRAIL ASYNC — packs recorded behind the builds, defects filed,
      NOTHING BLOCKS ON THEM.

So for the spine builds — quick-folds, spine-asset, spine-log-maintenance, spine-misc, spine-taxonomy-a, spine-taxonomy-b: 19 of the 34 manifests and 18 of the 31 bridges — the absence of a per-feature verdict is the plan working as recorded, not a defect. Step 8 as written silently reverses (2) and (4) for the majority of the bridge surface, and the commit message presents that reversal as a discovery.

The genuine identity-tier gap is 11 builds / 11 manifests / 9 bridges. That is still serious and is the number the step should be defending.

RESOLVE, do not paper over: either scope step 8 to identity-tier builds and say so in the step, or reopen the risk partition explicitly and record the reversal with its reason — but the recipe and the epic must not disagree about what 'done' means. Two competent executors reading these two documents today reach opposite verdicts on spine-asset.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-12, after reading the record myself: MY OWN CLOSING NOTE WAS WRONG
ABOUT quick-folds, and it was wrong by the same proxy this whole thread is about.

The note (inherited from the step-8 judge's report) listed "quick-folds" among "the
spine builds". It is not spine. Both partition files record all five quick/* modules
as tier=identity, and the evidence field says exactly why:

  "composite multi-entity fold (QuickForm creates asset+log+relations); vocab 0 but
   structure lane UNAVAILABLE (u00) — tiered UP per cost-asymmetry"

So it is the case the partition thought hardest about: vocab_new=0, which the naive
rule ("no new vocabulary/roles = SPINE") would sort to spine — and it was tiered UP
deliberately, because a composite multi-entity fold IS the "folds" half of the
IDENTITY definition, because role_classes_new=1 for quick/birth, quick/group and
quick/movement, and because the structure lane was blind (u00) so the cheap error was
to over-check rather than under-check.

WHY THE MISTAKE HAPPENED: the judge grouped builds by "not named identity-*", which
is the directory-name proxy — the very thing hy6.55 was filed about — and I closed
this bead quoting that list without checking it against the jsonl. A bound decision
was being cited from prose that had silently re-derived it from a filename.

THE RULING STANDS AND IS UNCHANGED: spine is advisory, identity gates. What changes
is the membership. quick-folds is IDENTITY and it GATES. verdict_currency already
does this correctly (it reads the partition and prints "tier: partition via module
family quick/*"), so no code change follows — only this correction, so the next
reader does not inherit the error from here.

RESIDUAL TRAP, not fixed: the directory is still named "quick-folds" while its tier
is identity. The name is no longer load-bearing anywhere in code, but it will keep
misleading humans. Renaming it is churn against history; leaving it means the tree
reads wrong. Filed as a note rather than a task — decide it when the build is next
touched.

title: Distilling packs from verify.jsonl is NOT mechanical — the witness record does not exist in a transcript, and distillation would author the question
description:
The step-8 rationale assumes ledger transcripts carry 'most of what a semantic fixture needs' and could be distilled MECHANICALLY. Compared against real files, that assumption fails on the one part the pack format exists to protect.

verify.jsonl (identity-birth, 87 rows) top-level keys: id, request, body, status, result, reads, note, coverage. Raw JSON:API transcript.

fixtures.jsonl (identity-sensor) top-level keys: fixture_id, title, feature, glossary_terms, given, when, then, provenance, schema_version — and every then[] entry cites a WITNESS.

The witness is a SEPARATE observation record in observations.jsonl, and it is semantic, not HTTP:

  {"obs_id":"d1ec09cc57400f64","method":"OBSERVE","path":"probe/asset_active",
   "record":"witness","probe":{"assert":"asset_active","subject":"S1","op":"=="},
   "observed":true}

pack.py enforces (_witness_problem, ctkr/ctkr/oracle/pack.py:388-414) that every assertion cites a witness, the witness answers the SAME question, and the value agrees — because 'an unwitnessed expected value is hand-authored, whatever its provenance'.

Nothing in verify.jsonl is that record. A transcript row carries a status, a result blob, and a prose 'reads' note. To distil you must choose the glossary probe term, the subject binding, WHICH FIELD of result is the observed value and how to project it, the given/when/then role of each of 87 flat rows, and a title. Values can be lifted; the QUESTION and the PROJECTION must be authored — and this project forbids intuition-authored fixture values precisely there.

Worse: a distiller that mints both the assertion and its witness from one authored projection satisfies _witness_problem BY CONSTRUCTION. The witness agrees because the same hand wrote both. That defeats the pack's central defence rather than passing it — the 'how would I fake this?' answer to step 8.

DECIDE AND RECORD: either (a) re-observe the reachable builds through step 4's ledger behind the preflight, or (b) specify a distiller whose projection is itself derived from a bound glossary mapping and reviewed as instrument-tier, never per-build. Do not let (b) happen implicitly.
notes:
CLOSED AS ESTABLISHED, 2026-08-12 — this is a finding, not a task, and it has been acted on.

THE FINDING STANDS: distilling fixture packs from ledger transcripts is NOT mechanical. A fixture's `then` cites a WITNESS — a separate semantic record in observations.jsonl — and pack.py:388-414 enforces that because 'an unwitnessed expected value is hand-authored, whatever its provenance'. Values can be lifted from a transcript's `result`; the glossary probe term, the subject binding, and WHICH FIELD of the result is the observed value and how to project it cannot. And the fake-it answer is worse than the gap: a distiller minting both the assertion and its witness from one authored projection satisfies the witness check BY CONSTRUCTION, because the same hand wrote both. It does not pass the pack's defence, it hollows it.

WHAT IT CHANGED: it killed the cheap remedy proposed for hy6.44, which is now re-scoped rather than pursued. It is cited in farmos-port/results/port-verify/wave2-2026-08-11.md and in docs/design/not-done-register.md under 'no path to done'.

Closing because leaving an established, acted-on finding open makes the backlog read as unfinished work when the work it implies is tracked elsewhere (hy6.44, hy6.49).

title: port-verify does not fail a declared capability the pack never exercises — clean is vacuous over undriven surface
description:
verify_port() (ctkr/ctkr/oracle/port_verify.py:769-796) sweeps declarations three ways: a divergence naming a fixture not in the pack, a sanction citing an unknown decision, and a probe DECLARED-then-DECLINED. It does NOT check the reverse: a capability declared in port.manifest.json that the pack never asks about at all. That surface is untested and the verdict still reads clean.

Already realised, verbatim, in the wave-2 verdict step 8 cites as its evidence:

  identity-lab-test/build/port.manifest.json capabilities.operations =
    [record_log, set_log_status, set_effective_time, archive_asset]
  operations the pack actually drives = record_log (17 uses)
  NEVER DRIVEN = set_log_status, set_effective_time, archive_asset

That build scored 22/22, 0 NO VERDICT, clean=yes, and 3 of its 4 declared operations were never exercised. Under step 8 as written it is 'done'.

FIX: in verify_port, after the declines sweep, append a declaration_problem for every entry in manifest.capabilities.operations/probes that appears in no fixture when/then across the pack. A capability nobody asked about is a claim about itself that went untested, same class as declared-then-declined. verify_port already holds both inputs; this is a small addition to an existing loop.

(Probes happen to be fully covered in all four wave-2 packs; operations are not.)
notes:
verify_port now files a declaration_problem per declared operation/probe no fixture reaches. 8 mutations, no survivors. THE INVARIANT TEST IS THE POINT: no superset declaration can yield FEWER declaration problems, and none can turn a not-clean run clean — so declaring a capability can only cost the port (I2's sign preserved). Live: identity-lab-test declares 4 operations, its pack drives 1; it still reproduces 22/22 but is NO LONGER CLEAN. The other three are unchanged. Verdict-of-record amended at farmos-port bbdecf8.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY JUDGED. The evidence above is the builder's own mutation run, verified by me against the live tree and the suites. By this project's standing rule that is not load-bearing on its own — a fresh adversary has not read it.

title: Step 8 (Exercise) is unenforced prose — build the verdict-currency gate
description:
Step 8 was added to docs/design/fanout-wave-plan.md (dc55c7f) with NOTHING enforcing it. It is a paragraph in a plan. This is the same defect hy6.28 spent two days fixing at the observe step ('a gate nobody must remember to run is off by default'), reintroduced one layer up: step 4 got a PRECONDITION with a refusing tool (tools/oracle_preflight.py via tools/ledger.py); the wave boundary got one (ctkr/ctkr/elenchus.py --require-current, exit 2 including when it cannot tell); step 8 got a sentence.

BUILD: a verdict-currency sweep, modelled exactly on elenchus --require-current. Enumerate every port.manifest.json under farmos-port/port_runs/, and for each, require a report under results/port-verify/ whose pack_seal matches that build's current pack.seal.json. Exit 2 on: no verdict, stale seal, clean=false, or CANNOT TELL (no pack). Wire it as a PRECONDITION on wave-close sealing — the irreversible step elenchus already gates, so the call site exists. Absence of an answer is not a yes.

Evidence: dc55c7f adds 26 lines of prose and zero executable checks. grep for port-verify in any gate/hook/test in farmos-port returns nothing.
notes: PARTIAL, verified 2026-08-12 (leaving OPEN). The gate itself IS built: ctkr/ctkr/verdict_currency.py exists, enumerates port.manifest.json under farmos-port/port_runs/, requires a current verdict, exits 2 on missing/stale/unclean/undeterminable — uv run pytest tests/test_verdict_currency.py -v = 37 pass/0 fail fresh. But it is NOT wired as a precondition anywhere executable, which is half of this bead's own AC ('build the gate' AND wire it). Grep across MetaCoding and farmos-port for 'verdict_currency' outside the module/test/docs finds zero hits in any hook, CI job, Makefile, or CLI subcommand — only prose mentions in docs/design/wave-transition.md, enforceability.md, not-done-register.md, all of which themselves say 'nothing calls it' (citing hy6.54, itself still open and confirmed current by this same grep). Do not close hy6.46 until wiring exists; close only 'built', not 'built and wired'.

title: Give the destination a voice: refusals that cite, and a port that knows its own measured domain
description:
Duke, 2026-08-11: "The source has a voice, which we're calling the oracle. The
destination doesn't really have a voice. We should be able to ask it what it
needs to be able to hear when it starts to become distorted."

THE ASYMMETRY, precisely. The oracle can SURPRISE us — "the boundary said
otherwise" is the most valuable sentence in this project's history. The port
cannot, because the bridge is call-and-response over a script the recorder wrote:
we only ever ask it what somebody already thought to record. A voice is the
capacity to say something you did not ask for.

Three things a voice would let the port say, in increasing value:

  1. "Here is what I can be asked."  Half-exists — port.manifest.json declares
     capabilities. A static declaration is a written statement, not a voice.
  2. "I refuse this, and here is what I cite."  DOES NOT EXIST. Every refusal in
     the port is a mute `throw`. This is the wave-2 Elenchus's first pith
     question — every other assertion here answers "how do you know?"; a throw
     answers nothing.
  3. "You are asking me something nobody measured."  DOES NOT EXIST. Only
     port-verify knows coverage, and it computes it from OUTSIDE. The port has no
     idea when it is being driven past its evidence — which is exactly "hearing
     when it starts to become distorted."

TO CLOSE (2) and (3), which are one mechanism:
  - a refusal becomes a VALUE, not a throw: it carries either the fixture/probe
    id that witnessed the refused case, or an explicit `unmeasured` marker.
  - port-verify scores refusals in two buckets: witnessed vs asserted. It can
    already do three outcomes rather than two; this is the same discipline
    applied to the port's noes.
  - a build reports its own unmeasured-refusal rate. That number IS the
    distortion signal, and it is the port speaking rather than being read.

NOTE THE SYMMETRY WITH hy6.28: we built a preflight so a build cannot measure the
WRONG oracle. Nothing stops a build shipping a refusal nobody measured at all.
Same defect class, other end of the wire.

Related: hy6.8 states the generating rule as policy ("the residue is unmeasured
and is refused"), which makes an unmeasured no indistinguishable from a measured
one; and `MedicalRefusal: "may not be longer than 255 characters"` is quoted from
farmOS for a condition farmOS never applied.
notes:
SYNTHESIS REFRAME, 2026-08-12 (results/wave2/synthesis-wave2-2026-08-12.md).

THIS IS NOT A NEW MECHANISM. It is charter invariant I1 — every value declares its authority — with a hole in it. A refusal is a VALUE: it is the port's answer to a question. It currently declares no authority at all, which under I3 (absence of an answer is never an answer) is not a permissible state for any other value in this system.

So the question to work is not 'what could a refusal cite?' but: WHY IS THE PORT'S throw THE ONE VALUE EXEMPT FROM I1, AND WHAT BREAKS IF WE STOP EXEMPTING IT? That is cheaper, answerable, and inherits a decided vocabulary instead of minting one.

It also PREDICTS the failure the judges found. MedicalRefusal: 'may not be longer than 255 characters' quotes farmOS for a condition farmOS never applied. Under I1 that string is an assertion with authority DERIVED and no validated_against — the e6p shape, bound-but-unscorable, which this project has already ruled is silently worthless. The refusal surface is not a new problem; it is e6p on a surface nobody thought to score.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD WAS MISSING: what happens to refusals nobody measured. Two kinds, not the same:
  WITNESSED — cites a probe/fixture id where farmOS also refused.
  UNMEASURED — the port refuses because nobody asked the boundary. Per the Elenchus this is where EVERY high-severity wave-2 finding lives.

Blocking on UNMEASURED stops the port dead (hundreds of guards, one oracle). Ignoring it reproduces wave 2. THIRD PATH, and it is the shape we just built for readings: mark it, count it, RATCHET it so the set cannot grow silently. An unmeasured refusal ships, visibly, as recorded debt. port-verify already scores three outcomes rather than two, so it can carry the witnessed/asserted split without new machinery.

AWAITING DUKE'S RULING: may an UNMEASURED refusal ship, marked and ratcheted? Recommendation: yes — the alternative is a gate permanently red on day one, which enforceability.md says is deleted within the week.

title: The destination is not a running system — no server, no entry point, nothing anyone could use
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 across farmos-port @ ae37f89: no Bun.serve, no createServer,
no listen, anywhere. package.json declares one script (`test`) and no main,
module, bin or exports. The port is 34 library packages exercised by 980
in-process unit tests plus a bridge that answers questions when asked. There is
no artifact that can be started, served, curled, or handed to a farmer.

Duke, 2026-08-11: "this is the classic software folly of the ivory tower
architect. Our goal is to make a working system. So it must make contact with
reality."

The recipe (docs/design/fanout-wave-plan.md) has seven steps and ends at "Read".
There is no step whose completion means the thing RUNS. That omission is why
twenty-one builds could ship without anyone noticing there is nothing to run —
it was never a step that could be skipped, because it was never a step.

TO CLOSE, at minimum: one process that serves HTTP over the accumulated store
and lets a person record and read back a real farm event end to end, from a
client that is not a test. Then the recipe grows the step that says so.

Deliberately NOT scoped here: which subset of the domain it serves, what the
client is, auth, or persistence choices. The point is contact with reality, and
the smallest thing that achieves it beats the most complete thing that does not.
Note the exit test applies (Duke's standing protocol): whatever serves must let
a user leave with their data.

title: 17 of 21 wave-2 builds cannot be mechanically judged — their observations are ledger transcripts, not replayable packs
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 (farmos-port ae37f89). port-verify ran cold on the four
wave-2 builds that have a fixtures.jsonl: 60 assertions, 60 answered, 60
reproduced, 0 NO VERDICT, all clean. It had not been run on wave 2 at all — the
previous verdict in results/port-verify/ is logs-quantities, 2026-07-20, before
the wave began.

THE GAP: the other 17 builds shipped 34 port.manifest.json and 31 port_bridge.ts
— the entire apparatus for BEING judged — and no pack to judge them with. Their
observe/ lane wrote probes.jsonl and verify.jsonl: ledger transcripts, which the
mechanical judge cannot eat. Newest sealed pack in PACKS.jsonl is 2026-07-28;
wave 2 built through 08-07.

The observations EXIST. They are the wrong shape. A ledger row already carries
request, body, status, result and the ADR expectation — most of what a semantic
fixture needs.

TO CLOSE: every wave-2 build with a bridge has a replayable pack and a recorded
port-verify verdict, or a stated reason it cannot. Do NOT hand-author fixtures
from the transcripts — a fixture whose value was authored rather than observed
is the one thing this project has never allowed. Distil mechanically from the
recorded rows, or re-record.

WATCH FOR (the interesting part): these four scored 100%, and each pack was
recorded by the same lane that built the port. Expect the 17 to score worse, and
treat any that scores 100% first try with the same suspicion — a pack that only
asks what the builder thought to record is a pack the builder cannot fail.
notes:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-12. The remedy this bead assumed — mechanically distilling packs from verify.jsonl — was REFUTED by hy6.50 (now closed as established): a distiller minting both assertion and witness from one authored projection satisfies the witness check by construction and hollows the pack's central defence.

CORRECTED NUMBERS, measured: the seventeen shipped 30 manifests and 27 bridges (34/31 are workspace totals INCLUDING the four verified builds). Of the seventeen, TEN have an observation lane in the wrong shape; SEVEN have no observe/ directory at all (that half is hy6.49).

SO THE HONEST STATE: there is no cheap path. The ten with transcripts need re-recording against the oracle, not conversion. Nobody has costed that. This bead stays open as a TRUE statement of debt rather than a plan, and it should not be closed by anything that does not actually produce witnessed packs.

title: The advertised<->same_oracle contract is UNTESTED — one line in oracle_preflight silently disarms the new guard
description:
Fresh judge round two, farmos-port 587c193fbad818b084bcb4b6181d3ab6ffc3d87a.

The hy6.37 repair has two halves. Half A: oracle_preflight.preflight() returns 'advertised' (oracle_preflight.py:548-549). Half B: Ledger._require_same_oracle() reads report['advertised'] and refuses when the transport's own GET /api does not carry every gated type (ledger.py:379-424).

ALL THREE new tests inject their own gate — gate=lambda types, **kw: {'advertised': [...]} (test_ledger.py:621,637,648). Nothing anywhere tests half A. So the contract between the two halves is unheld.

MUTATION N4, one line, revert oracle_preflight.py:548 to
    return {'base_url': base_url, 'types': results, 'module_drift': drift}
RESULT: test_ledger.py rc=0 (29/29 green), test_oracle_preflight.py rc=0 (18/18 green). SURVIVED.

Then LIVE, with the stub farmOS from /tmp/otherfarm.py at 127.0.0.1:8099 and the gate on :8095 — the exact fixture the builder used to prove the fix:
  $ ORACLE=http://127.0.0.1:8099 python3 verify.py     # N4-mutated tools/
  total rows: 27
  row0: PREFLIGHT ok same_oracle= None
    S0 POST /api/taxonomy_term/animal_type 200 | drift: ADR states status 201, boundary answered 200
  PROBES SENT TO 127.0.0.1:8099 = 23
Unmutated, the same command refuses before any probe. So a one-line edit nobody's test would notice reopens hy6.37 completely, writes 'status: ok' on the PREFLIGHT row, and sends 23 probes to an oracle nobody cleared.

This is the epic's own recurring shape: a guard that turns itself off silently.

REMEDY: one test in test_oracle_preflight.py asserting preflight() returns a non-empty 'advertised' containing the requested types (the fake-oracle harness there already stubs the index). Better: assert the ledger's default gate satisfies the contract, so the two halves are pinned together rather than separately.
notes: FIXED in farmos-port 824dd3c. t_the_report_carries_ADVERTISED asserts preflight() returns the WHOLE index, not an echo of the request (an echo makes the caller's comparison vacuous). Belt and braces: ledger.py no longer fails open when the key is missing (hy6.43), so the N4 revert is caught twice — by the test AND by a runtime refusal. Verified live on the judge's own fixture: the mutant that sent 23 probes to the wrong oracle now sends 0.

title: The hy6.28 gate covers ONE of five wave2 builds — the other four are not on tools/ledger.py
description:
Fresh judge of hy6.28 (farmos-port 6a75c1d, MetaCoding 574ff0d).

The derived gate (no probing before it, none outside it) is a property of tools/ledger.py's Ledger class. Exactly ONE build uses it: port_runs/wave2/identity-farm-org/observe/verify.py.

  identity-transplanting/observe/verify.py  — NO oracle_preflight at all. It has a bespoke inline gate (verify.py:283-298): two GETs plus a POST/DELETE ping of transplant_days. The MODULE-DRIFT half never runs there, which is the half hy6.28 just made mandatory-by-default. It also POSTs a fixture to the oracle before any gate.
  identity-seeding/observe/verify.py:81     — hand-written 7-type require_types() at module level.
  identity-group/observe/verify.py:49       — hand-written 5-type require_types().
  identity-birth/observe/verify.py:38       — hand-written 4-type require_types().

Those three now inherit require_modules=True (a real gain), but they keep exactly the shape hy6.28 exists to kill: a list beside the run rather than derived from it. farm-org's was deleted because it was WRONG; the other three were not audited by derivation, only by eye. I spot-checked their lists against their probed paths and found no live under-declaration, but that check is grep-grade, not mechanical.

There is no additive adoption path. ledger.py deliberately exports evaluate_floors() as a plain function so hand-rolled ledgers can adopt the floors without a rewrite; it exports NO equivalent for the gate. A hand-rolled ledger cannot acquire property 2 short of moving onto the Ledger class.

REMEDY (either): export a gate the hand-rolled ledgers can call — e.g. derive_and_gate(collections, delete_order, log_collections) returning a require_gated(path) closure they call from their own probe() — or migrate the four. At minimum give identity-transplanting the real preflight.
notes:
MECHANICAL AUDIT DONE (fresh judge round two, farmos-port 587c193). I said in round one I had only grepped literal strings and that a live under-declaration might be hiding. Done properly now: AST over each verify.py, resolving module-level string constants, expanding f-strings and string concatenation, extracting resource types from BOTH constructible /api paths AND JSON:API 'type' literals in request bodies. Cross-validated: run against identity-farm-org it derives exactly the 7 types the shipped PREFLIGHT row gates on.

RESULT — the honest negative first:

  identity-seeding  declared 7, universe 7  -> UNDER-DECLARED: none
  identity-group    declared 5, universe 5  -> UNDER-DECLARED: none
  identity-birth    declared 4, universe 4  -> UNDER-DECLARED: none

No live under-declaration of the farm-org kind. The three hand-written lists are correct. The P1 I flagged as possible is NOT there.

  identity-transplanting  DECLARATION: NONE. Ungated universe of 8:
    asset--animal, asset--land, asset--plant, log--activity, log--observation,
    log--transplanting, taxonomy_term--animal_type, taxonomy_term--plant_type

Its bespoke inline gate (verify.py:283-298) covers exactly TWO of those eight — log--transplanting (a GET on LT) and taxonomy_term--plant_type (a POST/DELETE ping of transplant_days). The other SIX are probed with nothing established about them, and the module-drift half — mandatory by default since 6a75c1d — never runs there at all. Its gate also POSTs a real fixture to the shared oracle before any check.

So this bead's remedy narrows usefully: the type-list correctness of seeding/group/birth is fine and migrating them buys derivation-by-construction, not a bug fix. identity-transplanting is the one with an actual gap, and it is 6 types wide.

RECALL CAVEAT, stated rather than hidden: the analyser cannot see a path assembled from a runtime value (a links.next href, a collection name read from a response). All four builds' dynamic loops iterate lists built from module-level constants or literal tuples, which it does resolve, so the residual gap is small — but it is not zero, and this is static analysis, not an instrumented run.

title: A REFUSED index session still leaves its flush in the store — flush precedes health and there is no rollback
description: FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07. src/ingest/session.ts runs build.flush(store) before the measurements and the gate, so a session the gate REFUSES has already mutated the store, with no rollback. Observed on the same-sha-two-branch-labels path: three runs, three refusals, and the store carried the duplicates anyway. The verdict is honest and the damage still lands. Either flush into a staging slice and promote after the gate, or make the record's REFUSED status carry 'and the store was mutated anyway' explicitly rather than leaving a reader to assume otherwise.

title: quickBirth diverges from Birth.php, and the two-child fan-out has no committed probe
description:
FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07, read from the LIVE CONTAINER source rather than from my report. farmos-port port_runs/wave2/quick-folds/build/src/quick.ts vs Birth.php:
  :390-391  the source puts children in 'asset' and the mother in a SEPARATE 'mother' field; the fold injects the mother into assetIds
  :397      the name uses entityLabelsSummary(children) — cutoff plus '(+N more)'; the fold uses a plain join(', ')
  :336      each CHILD asset gets 'parent' => ; the fold sets no parent
  :371      a SECOND log is created, 'Weight of @asset is @weight @units'; the fold emits one log

The record's headline cites fixtures hy617m-*, and hy617m appears NOWHERE in the repo outside two lines of that markdown. There is no quick-folds/observe/ directory. Judge mutations: 3 detected of 13; M2/M4/M6 are each the SOURCE-CORRECT behaviour and the fixtures cannot tell them from the shipped code.

title: ledger _absence_check reads any non-200 as ABSENT — an expired token prints a clean run over live fixtures
description: FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07. farmos-port tools/ledger.py:387 is 'if s_ == 200: still_there.append(...)'. Anything that is not 200 counts as gone. An expired or revoked token mid-run makes every DELETE fail, the sweep return nothing and the by-ID check report clean — printing 'N fixtures created and none left behind' with the fixtures still on the SHARED oracle. Not an adversary; a live operational risk on a long run. The by-ID check is the AUTHORITY in this design, so a false clean here is the worst single failure the module can have.

title: ledger run() catches Exception, so SystemExit walks past the exit code — the instrument exits 0 while saying it failed
description: FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07, confirmed in the source. farmos-port tools/ledger.py:452 catches Exception; SystemExit is a BaseException. The finally runs, finish() computes code=1 and PRINTS the floor failure, and then SystemExit(0) propagates past 'return code' at :468. The process exits 0 while the instrument's own summary says it failed. Any ledger body that calls sys.exit() — or any library that does — turns a red run green.

title: src/testkit/floors.ts — a floor names the published field it is measured against
description:
From docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md, mechanism 4, and it is the smallest fix in that document.

ROOT CAUSE OF A FAILURE THAT RECURRED THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION: thresholds were not merely guessed — the instrument did not PUBLISH the quantity the builder was told to calibrate from. A section's ROW count is not its CHECK count, and only rows were visible. The fix that worked was three lines (farmos-port tools/ledger.py:425 publishes a coverage object on the SUMMARY row). The SHARED ledger initially lost that, which every hand-written version had, which is why the rule has to be structural rather than remembered.

THE RULE, stated so it can refuse things: a floor is not a number. It is a PAIR — a value and the name of the field the instrument publishes it against — and the instrument's own record must contain that field.

MEASURED TODAY: 22 smoke scripts, 4 to 11 assertions each, and ZERO publish how many checks they ran. A truncated run and a complete run are byte-identical.

Composes with discriminate(): registered pairs make the check count DERIVED rather than hand-maintained.
acceptance_criteria: evaluateFloors(floors, published) fails when published[f.measuredAs] is ABSENT — a floor over a field nobody emits is an INSTRUMENT failure, not a pass. Applied to scripts/smoke-*.ts. Three fixtures: (F4.1) a smoke script with three checks deleted fails BY NAME while the complete one passes — both print PASS today; (F4.2) a floor naming an unpublished field fails as INSTRUMENT, distinct from a check failure — this is what makes 'calibrate from a measurement that does not exist' a build failure instead of three rounds of guessing; (F4.3) an EMPTY run fails rather than passes.
notes: VERIFIED, tree 61a0b3a. src/testkit/floors.test.ts has F4.1 (truncation, line 62), F4.2 (unpublished-field is INSTRUMENT failure distinct from CHECK failure, line 157), F4.3 (empty run fails, line 256), all passing. evaluateFloors() refuses UNPUBLISHED_FIELD as its own FloorFailureKind, distinct tier from FLOOR_UNMET/CHECK_REFUSED. bun test src/testkit/ scripts/smoke-all.test.ts = 79 pass/0 fail.

title: src/testkit/discriminate.ts — contrast pairs and non-constancy as ONE primitive
description:
From docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md, mechanism 1. THE OBSERVATION THAT MAKES IT SMALL: a contrast pair and a mutation test are the same operation pointed in opposite directions — a contrast pair is a mutation applied to the SUBJECT; a mutation test is a contrast pair applied to the INSTRUMENT. Both are 'two inputs, one verdict function, the verdicts must differ, and the difference must be NAMED'. One function, not a framework.

It exists hand-rolled exactly once already: src/ingest/seam.test.ts:440-486, whose own comment states the principle — 'Each input class must produce a DIFFERENT refusal code, so a check that had collapsed into always-throw, or into never-throw, would be visible here.'

THREE RULES, each refusing something that passes today:
1. The verdict is a TAG from a closed vocabulary, never a boolean and never an exception. An uncaught throw classifies as OTHER:<msg> and FAILS the pair — a boolean makes non-constancy trivially satisfiable by an unrelated crash.
2. Every declared tag must be reached and no two cases may share one. A verdict collapsed to a constant fails on the first duplicate.
3. The pair is RECORDED into the run's published record, so a deleted pair stops appearing.

WHAT IT REFUSES TODAY: scripts/smoke-incremental.ts runs five passes and prints INCREMENTAL_SMOKE_PASS at :151; delete the assertions from passes 2 and 3 and it prints the same line, exit 0. Also refuses the shape that bit this session — a regression test whose broken half and fixed half give the SAME verdict is a duplicate-tag failure by construction.
acceptance_criteria: discriminate() ships with its own three fixtures: (F1.1) a pair differing only by an unrelated TypeError is REFUSED while a pair differing by refusal code PASSES — without this it is only a pair-counter; (F1.2) a verdict collapsed to a constant fails on duplicate tags and the restored one passes; (F1.3) seam.test.ts's six classes replayed through it yield byte-identical tags to the hand-rolled version. Ship the comment-invariance pair for the bring-up.sh consumer in the same change — three lines, and it is MetaCoding-02c's missing regression fixture.
notes: VERIFIED, tree 61a0b3a, fresh run. src/testkit/discriminate.test.ts has F1.1 (crash-vs-refusal-code contrast, describe at line 40), F1.2 (collapsed-verdict duplicate detection, line 103), and src/ingest/seam.test.ts:445 has F1.3 (six input classes replayed through discriminate(), EXPECTED_CODES asserted byte-identical). bun test src/testkit/discriminate.test.ts src/ingest/seam.test.ts = 46 pass/0 fail. Comment-invariance pair for bring-up.sh consumer shipped and closed separately as MetaCoding-02c (farmos-port tools/test_oracle_preflight.py: commented_drush_en_is_not_declared / an_uncommented_drush_en_is_still_declared / comments_only_is_a_parse_failure — verified present). All stated AC met.

title: MetaCoding's own CTKR artifacts were derived from a graph with 430 phantom worktree files and 267 missing edges
description:
Discovered while rebuilding the production stores for MetaCoding-9jt, 2026-08-06.

The pre-rebuild MetaCoding store held 786 file nodes for a 357-file tree. 430 of them pointed at paths that DO NOT EXIST — .claude/worktrees/agent-*/... copies of real source files. MetaCoding-wg7 stopped the walker from CREATING these (no dot-directory is descended any more) but nothing ever DELETED the ones already written, because the store was mutable and only ever grew. Separately, 267 tree-sitter edges present in a fresh oracle build at 05d8a93 were absent from that store, concentrated in ctkr/*.py and src/mcp/.

wg7's original finding was that role-equivalence twins were DOMINATED by cos-1.0 worktree duplicates. That is exactly the condition that persisted in the store every MetaCoding-derived CTKR artifact was computed from.

The store is now rebuilt and clean (358 file nodes, 0 non-existent paths, 0 stale). What has NOT been done is re-deriving anything downstream of it.

Pre-rebuild backup, for any comparison this needs: /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/store-backups-2026-08-06/MetaCoding.metacoding
acceptance_criteria: Enumerate the artifacts under .metacoding/ctkr/ derived from the MetaCoding graph, and for each: re-derive, or stamp 'derived_from: pre-2026-08-06 store, phantom worktree duplicates present' per graph-as-cache.md's migration rule (flag and keep for a LEDGER; the layer-3 default is not 'rebuild on doubt'). Whichever is chosen, the twin/role results that motivated wg7 must be re-checked against the clean graph, since duplicates were the finding.

title: coverage-claims' tree-sitter region derivation does not exist — no ERROR/MISSING check anywhere in src/
description:
From docs/design/within-file-coverage.md Part B. coverage-claims.md:77 defines the tree-sitter region as 'the set of files walkFs actually parsed without error'. THAT DERIVATION IS NOT IN THE CODE: grep -rn 'hasError|isMissing' src/ returns zero hits outside tests, and the only quantity available at the parse site is 'tree != null'.

Measured on a PHP file with one broken method: hasError true, class Good survives, class Broken's method is gone, and class After is ABSENT ENTIRELY (absorbed into the ERROR subtree). Nothing observes any of it. Implemented naively, the design's flagship DERIVED region would be a declaration.

BE HONEST ABOUT THE YIELD: 0 of 789 farmOS PHP files and 0 of 92 MetaCoding TS files have any ERROR or MISSING node. This is not a coverage measure. It is the only cheap signal that fires when a grammar is too old for the source it parses, which is the silent-and-catastrophic case.
acceptance_criteria: has_error plus the byte ranges of every ERROR and MISSING node recorded per file in MANIFEST.json; region derived as 'parsed with zero ERROR and zero MISSING'. TWO pieces of evidence, both required: (a) the broken-PHP fixture yields partial + recorded ranges + the missing class provably absent, CONTRAST the repaired file yields complete — today both are byte-identically HEALTHY; (b) an assertion that the count is ZERO across farmOS and MetaCoding, so the next reader cannot mistake this for a coverage measure.

title: Grammar wasm digest is not in the layer-2 key — every parse-derived fact is unrecomputable
description:
From docs/design/within-file-coverage.md Part A. package.json pins tree-sitter-wasms as a CARET range (^0.1.13) and src/extractor/parser.ts loads tree-sitter-{grammar}.wasm from whatever resolved. A grammar upgrade changes every parse tree, every symbol and every edge — and moves no key.

This is graph-as-cache.md:165 instantiated: an input left out of the key is a dimension the cache is blind to. It is a PREREQUISITE, not an enhancement: the cache model requires a reader to RECOMPUTE a key from the artifact's own recorded inputs, and without the grammar digest nothing derived from a parse tree can be recomputed — including everything both live stores hold today.
acceptance_criteria: tree-sitter-wasms pinned exactly; sha256 of each loaded .wasm folded into the layer-2 key beside extractor_version. Evidence: two builds of the same tree with two DIFFERENT wasm blobs produce DIFFERENT keys; CONTRAST identical wasm produces an identical key.
