title: NO_RELATIONAL_EDGES refuses a correct graph of a relationship-free codebase
description:
FOUND by a fresh architect 2026-08-04 while building a fixture for something else, and INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED by me at HEAD (d8bee31).

Fixture: 6 TypeScript files, each a class with two scalar fields, ZERO cross-references. scip-typescript runs clean, 6/6 documents, correspondence exact 6/6 ratio 1.0. Result:

  EXIT=1, status REFUSED, [NO_RELATIONAL_EDGES]

Contrast half (the architect's, measured): the SAME tree plus one file that calls another -> HEALTHY. The only difference between refused and healthy is a property OF THE SOURCE CODE, not of the index.

Consequence today: per health-gate.ts a REFUSED slice makes every empty MCP query refuse and graph_diff refuse unconditionally. So a valid graph of a data-model-only package, a types-only package, a constants module, or any leaf library is unusable.

THE SHAPE, and it is why this matters more than one bad threshold: NO_RELATIONAL_EDGES IS A COUNT USED AS A PROXY FOR CAPABILITY. A proxy is always refutable by finding a subject where the count is honestly zero. Only 'which lanes ran, and what edge kinds can they emit for this language' distinguishes THERE ARE NO CALLS from THIS LANE CANNOT SEE CALLS — no edge count ever will. fitness.ts rule (6) already states the consequence in its own comment: 'a rule that false-alarms on the most common invocation is a rule people disable.'

This is the FOURTH refutation in the same family (4kg/5fi round 1, 9ed round 2, qv0 + 5fi-suffix round 3), and the first one found without anyone attacking the gate — it fell out of building a fixture.

DO NOT FIX WITH A BETTER THRESHOLD. It is subsumed by MetaCoding-ev9: the achieved capability set goes in the cache key, a lane that emits no CALLS for this language means a CALLS query MISSES rather than the graph being REFUSED. Required test in the new model: this 6-file tree must build HEALTHY at full TS fidelity with zero CALLS edges, contrasted against the 7-file version with a real call — identical capability sets, different edge counts, both healthy.

INTERIM: if ev9 is not landing soon, this needs a stopgap, because it refuses real work today.

title: index fitness: the ingest capability guards the wrong layer — Store.upsertSymbol/addEdge write to the graph with no ticket and leave a stale HEALTHY
description:
FRESH-JUDGE-3 FINDING at tree HEAD 05d8a93 (src/ingest/ticket.ts sha256 6d1d29bb5ab9..., src/store/index.ts unchanged by the fix).

CLAIM UNDER TEST: ticket.ts:20 'YOU CANNOT WRITE TO THE GRAPH WITHOUT A SESSION THAT WILL JUDGE THE RESULT'; session.ts:225-226 'Nothing in src/ can write to the graph without one'; docs/design/index-fitness.md fake-it #3 'any direct Store.upsertSymbol leaves a stale HEALTHY ... Refuted and re-closed (MetaCoding-9ed)'.

MEASURED: false. Store.upsertSymbol and Store.addEdge are public async methods on the Store exported by the public barrel src/store, take no ticket, and call no gate.

EXECUTED END TO END (sandbox git-archive copy of HEAD, src/ingest/judge3-ticket.test.ts A1.5):
  runIndexSession -> HEALTHY, 12 symbols, commit aaaa...
  16 x store.upsertSymbol + 1 store.addEdge, no ticket, no session, no forgery
  store 12 -> 28 symbols; readIndexHealth still reads status HEALTHY,
  fitness.symbols 12, commit_sha aaaaaaa.
A stale HEALTHY over a store 2.3x larger than the record describes — bead 9ed's
original harm, reproduced with the fix in place, needing no evasion of any kind.

WHY THE TICKET DOES NOT CATCH IT: assertMayIngest is called from the five INGEST
PRIMITIVES (walker.ts:116/176/219 indexDirectory/indexFile/removeFile,
scip/loader.ts:89 loadScip, watcher). It is not called from the write methods those
primitives use. The seam is one layer above the writes it is about.

FIX DIRECTIONS (not prescribing): (a) move the check into Store.upsertSymbol /
addEdge / the FTS writer, taking the ticket (or a session-scoped Store handle) as a
parameter — the capability then guards the actual write; (b) hand sessions a
write-enabled Store and readers a read-only one, so the write methods are not on the
type most callers hold; (c) if neither is wanted, NARROW THE CLAIM in ticket.ts,
session.ts and index-fitness.md to 'the ingest primitives require a capability' and
move fake-it #3 back to OPEN, since it currently reads as closed.

DEFINITION OF DONE: whichever is chosen, the evidence must be the executed 12->28
attack, refused, plus a contrast half where a session's own writes still succeed.

title: The graph store is a CACHE, not state: key it on (repo, commit, fidelity) and rebuild on miss
description:
DUKE, 2026-08-04, and it reframes the whole index-fitness effort.

THE CLAIM: we should be able to delete all metacoding metadata in a project and recreate it with no loss. It takes time; that is what a cache is. Everything we have been treating as a correctness problem is downstream of treating a cache as state.

WHAT THIS DISSOLVES (all filed today, all patches around partial updating):
- MetaCoding-7f9 (fitness counts symbols from commits no longer checked out) — a keyed cache entry holds ONE commit. The question 'should we count old commits?' stops existing.
- MetaCoding-c03 (walker skips unchanged files so they keep an old indexed_at, and a correct graph gets REFUSED) — the entire defect is partial updating. measureGraphFreshness, added today to patch around it, becomes unnecessary complexity.
- MetaCoding-ae5 (a SIGKILL leaves symbols with no edges) — a partial cache entry is DISCARDED and rebuilt, not diagnosed. RUNNING becomes 'incomplete, rebuild me' rather than a health verdict.
- MetaCoding-19g (index-identity history) survives only if provenance is wanted for its own sake, not for correctness.

THE SECOND HALF, AND THE DEEPER ONE — fidelity must be DECLARED, not discovered. Today the same query yields different data depending on whether --scip ran and which language the repo is, and the analysis layer carries a corner case for each combination. The real defect is not that fidelity varies but that it is UNDECLARED: graph_callers returning [] means either 'no callers' or 'this lane cannot see calls', and hy6.16 is exactly that ambiguity cashing out over 41 rows. Put the fidelity profile IN THE CACHE KEY, let a query state what it requires (e.g. needs CALLS), and an entry built tree-sitter-only answers 'not built at that fidelity, rebuild with --scip' instead of returning an empty array that looks like an answer. Same typed-refusal machinery built today, keyed on CAPABILITY rather than on a health guess.

THE COST OBJECTION AND ITS ANSWER: rebuild-from-scratch is only free if rebuilding is cheap, and farmOS's PHP lane is a Docker site build — which is exactly why partial updating crept in. But the expense is not uniform. TWO LAYERS:
  indexer output (.scip)  EXPENSIVE (Docker, minutes)  key: repo + commit + toolchain version
  graph store             CHEAP (~90s / 30k symbols)   key: the above + fidelity profile
Evidence this works: on 2026-08-04 the farmOS full-signal graph was rebuilt by REUSING the 2026-07-17 .scip from farmos-site-i00 — the expensive layer was a cache hit and only the cheap layer was recomputed. Make the .scip content-addressed and the graph a disposable projection of it.

TO CLOSE: a design note deciding (a) the exact cache key at both layers, (b) what a miss does at each (rebuild vs refuse vs prompt), (c) how a query declares required fidelity and what the refusal looks like, and (d) which of 7f9 / c03 / ae5 / 19g are CLOSED AS DISSOLVED rather than fixed — each explicitly, since silently dropping them loses the evidence for why they existed. Then delete the complexity that only existed to support partial updating.
notes:
THREE LAYERS, NOT TWO — found 2026-08-04 while acting on this bead, and it changes where the fitness machinery belongs.

Inspecting the two production stores before evicting one:
  farmos-port/.metacoding/ctkr/  = export/{nodes,edges}.jsonl only — cheap, derived, disposable.
  MetaCoding/.metacoding/ctkr/   = intention.jsonl, intention_signals.parquet, intention_load.parquet, subsystem_cards.jsonl, port_briefs/*.md, presentations.parquet, hom_profiles.parquet ... AND llm_cost.jsonl.

That last one is the point. Those artifacts are LLM-DERIVED. Rebuilding them costs MONEY, not just time. The 'delete it and recreate it, it is only time' claim holds completely for the graph and NOT for these.

  layer            rebuild cost        disposable?
  .scip            minutes (Docker)    yes — content-addressable by repo+commit+toolchain
  graph store      ~90s / 30k symbols  YES — pure cache, the claim lands fully
  CTKR/LLM         DOLLARS             NO

CONSEQUENCE, and it inverts today's effort: the index-fitness machinery is in the WRONG LAYER. For the graph it is nearly pointless — if in doubt, evict and rebuild, which is this bead's whole argument. For layer 3 it is ESSENTIAL, because a paid artifact cannot be casually rebuilt, and an intention extraction computed over a CALLS=0 graph is hy6.16 WITH AN INVOICE ATTACHED. MetaCoding-0mu's artifact-staleness check (ctkrArtifactHealth refusing when manifest generated_at predates the newest finalized verdict) is therefore the most valuable thing built on 2026-08-04, and it did not exist at all until then.

SO THE RE-SCOPE OF THIS BEAD: do not just delete the partial-update complexity. MOVE the fitness concept down to layer 3, where the question 'was this derived from an established graph, and which one' is the question that actually has to be answered — and where a wrong answer costs money rather than 90 seconds. Layer 2 needs a cache key and an evict, not a verdict.

Corroborating live evidence, same session: the farmos-port store accumulated an ORPHAN slice 'farmos@?' (4446 symbols, 2026-08-01) because the repo name derives from the directory and the source was later indexed as 'farmos-src'. One dead entry under a name nobody will index again kept the ENTIRE store refusing. Under the current model the remedy is a prune-or-adopt rule (more state management); under the cache model it is an eviction. It was resolved by deleting the graph layer and rebuilding — ctkr/ preserved untouched, which is layer 3 being treated differently from layer 2 in practice for the first time.

title: index fitness: a successful HEALTHY reindex still leaves established=false — summarizeHealth counts tree-sitter EXTERNAL BOUNDARY NODES as an unestablished (repo,'') slice
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING at tree 7c03e77 (src/mcp/health-gate.ts sha256 a0a380dff6ea...). THIS IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES THE OUTCOME OF A REINDEX.

summarizeHealth enumerates slices with 'MATCH (s:Symbol) RETURN DISTINCT s.repo AS repo, s.branch AS branch' and sets established = (every slice is HEALTHY/OVERRIDDEN). The tree-sitter lane creates EXTERNAL BOUNDARY NODES for references it cannot resolve inside the repo — 'external::<name>', file '', source 'tree_sitter' — and these carry **branch = ''**. A session writes its health record for (repo, <git branch>) and never for (repo, ''). So the boundary-node slice is permanently UNKNOWN and established is permanently FALSE.

REPRODUCED FROM SCRATCH (sandbox judge2-ext3): a 6-file Python fixture using out-of-repo decorators (@dataclass, @property, @classmethod, @pytest.fixture), indexed by a normal session:
  session verdict: HEALTHY, failures []
  slices in the graph: fixture@main = 36 symbols, fixture@'' = 4 symbols
  the 4: external::dataclass, external::property, external::classmethod, external::fixture (source tree_sitter)
  summarizeHealth -> established: FALSE, slices [fixture@main=HEALTHY, fixture@''=UNKNOWN]
  empty graph query -> REFUSED INDEX_FITNESS_UNESTABLISHED
  graph_diff        -> REFUSED INDEX_FITNESS_UNESTABLISHED (unconditionally, since it refuses whenever !established)

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — BOTH PRODUCTION STORES ALREADY HAVE THE SLICE (read from COPIES, originals untouched):
  /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/MetaCoding/.metacoding  -> MetaCoding@main 18117 symbols + MetaCoding@'' 6 symbols
      (external::dataclass, external::classmethod, external::property, external::field_validator, external::fixture, external::skipif)
  /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/farmos-port/.metacoding -> farmos@3fe0ce7 4446 symbols + farmos@'' 354 symbols
      (external::ConfirmFormBase, external::AutowireTrait, external::farm, external::group, ...)
Both are the exact shape my fixture reproduces.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLANNED REINDEX: reindexing either store will produce a HEALTHY record for its real slice and will NOT clear this. established stays false, so every MCP graph query that returns zero rows still refuses, and graph_diff still refuses every time. The reindex is safe — it just will not deliver the outcome it is being run for. Non-empty queries are unaffected (they return ok:true with a caveat).

WHY IT SLIPPED: fitness.ts DID reason about boundary nodes for the fitness measure — 'External boundary nodes only ever appear as targets, so the filter on a does not exclude them' — so measureStoreFitness scopes correctly by (repo,branch). The reasoning was simply never carried across to summarizeHealth's slice ENUMERATION, which is a different question: not 'whose symbols count' but 'what counts as a slice that needs its own verdict'. A boundary node is not a slice of indexed code and cannot have a fitness verdict of its own.

FIX DIRECTION (small): exclude boundary nodes from slice enumeration — e.g. add a WHERE that drops rows whose branch is '' and whose symbols are all external (or simply 'WHERE s.file <> ""', since boundary nodes carry no file), or stamp boundary nodes with the session's repo/branch when they are created. Either way the regression evidence is a test asserting established=TRUE after a clean session over a fixture that produces boundary nodes — my Python fixture above is exactly that test, and it currently fails.
notes:
ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit 15760a5), NOT CLOSED — fresh reader closes.

summarizeHealth now enumerates slices with WHERE s.language <> 'external' OR s.file <> ''. PREDICATE JUSTIFIED, not taken because it was convenient: s.file = '' alone would also silence any future REAL symbol that happens to carry no file (a quiet slice disappearance, the exact failure class this gate exists to prevent); s.source = 'tree_sitter' is wrong outright, because src/scip/loader.ts creates the SAME external:: boundary nodes with source 'scip' and the tree-sitter lane's real symbols carry that source too. The explicit marker BOTH lanes set is language = 'external' (walker.ts ensureBoundaryNode, loader.ts ensureExternalBoundary), so the predicate is the CONJUNCTION of that marker and the absence of a file. A symbol naming a real file is enumerated as a slice no matter what else it says about itself.

EVIDENCE — PAIR scc in src/mcp/health-gate.test.ts. Half A: a REAL runIndexSession over the judge's Python fixture (out-of-repo decorators + bases); the test first asserts the fixture actually produced branch-'' rows and that every one of them is language 'external' with no file (otherwise it proves nothing), then asserts fixture@'' is not a slice and fixture is not unestablished. Half B: REAL symbols loaded on branch '' (a real file, not external) — still a slice, still UNKNOWN, established false. Both halves have a (repo,'') slice in the graph and a HEALTHY record for the real branch; only what the branch-'' rows ARE differs.
MUTATIONS: dropping the predicate reddens half A only; the convenient 'WHERE s.branch <> ""' reddens half B only.

FAKE-IT ASKED: 'how would I satisfy this and defeat its purpose?' — by widening the predicate until real slices vanish. That is why the conjunction is used and why half B exists as a standing test rather than a comment.

NOT DONE: no production store was touched; both remain UNKNOWN until reindexed. summarizeHealth is the only slice enumeration in src/ (grepped DISTINCT s.repo).
FRESH JUDGE 3 (tree HEAD 05d8a93, src/mcp/health-gate.ts sha256 e5c9a6d1ba9c...) — VERIFIED, with one bounded residue filed separately.

THE PREDICATE'S REASONING CHECKS OUT AGAINST THE SOURCE:
 - both lanes really do mint boundary nodes with language='external', file='',
   branch='' (walker.ts:368-385 ensureBoundaryNode; loader.ts:191-215
   ensureExternalBoundary) -- so 's.source = tree_sitter' would indeed have been wrong
   outright, since loader.ts:213 sets source:'scip' on the same shape.
 - 's.file = ""' alone would hide any future real fileless symbol; the CONJUNCTION
   (language='external' AND file='') is the narrower marker, and it is the one both
   lanes set.

ATTACKED, EXECUTED (sandbox copy of HEAD): can the predicate hide a REAL slice?
 - a fileless symbol with a real language ('typescript', file='') -> ENUMERATED.
 - a symbol with language='external' but a real file ('src/a.ts') -> ENUMERATED.
 - a symbol with language='' and file='' -> ENUMERATED ('' <> 'external' is true).
So the only hidden shape is the exact boundary-node shape. No real symbol a lane
writes can land in it: walker/loader always set a real language for real symbols.

BOUNDED RESIDUE (filed as its own bead): a repo whose ingest produced ONLY boundary
nodes now vanishes from summarizeHealth entirely rather than reading UNKNOWN.
Executed: a healthy j3r@main plus 4 boundary nodes for 'ghost-repo' and an honest
REFUSED record for ghost-repo@main ->
  slices = [j3r@main HEALTHY], established = TRUE, ghost-repo NOT enumerated,
  its REFUSED record never consulted, and gateQueryAnswer([], summary) returns
  ok:true rows:[] -- the hy6.16 indistinguishability.
This is narrow (summarizeHealth enumerates from the GRAPH, so a slice with zero
symbols was already invisible) but scc widened 'zero symbols' to 'only boundary
nodes'. CLOSING scc: the bug it names (a successful HEALTHY reindex leaving
established=false on both production stores) is fixed and the caller re-verified it
on a production MetaCoding reindex -- HEALTHY, one slice, no phantom @'' slice.
close_reason: Fresh judge 3 verified at HEAD 05d8a93: the predicate's reasoning holds against the live source (both lanes mint language='external'+file=''+branch=''), and no real symbol a lane writes can be hidden by it (fileless-with-real-language, external-with-a-file, and empty-language all still enumerate). Residue filed separately.

title: index fitness: 11 CTKR MCP tools have NO health gate, though health-gate.ts names motif mining and role-equivalence as refuse-by-default aggregates
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING at tree 7c03e77 (src/mcp/health-gate.ts sha256 a0a380dff6ea..., src/mcp/ctkr-tools.ts 2087 lines).

health-gate.ts's own header defines the AGGREGATING posture and enumerates who it is for: 'AGGREGATING consumers (graph_diff, CTKR motif mining, role-equivalence, cross-repo comparison, the eval harness, any rescoring pass) refuse BY DEFAULT, empty or not, and require an explicit acknowledgment. An aggregate silently absorbs a zero — and hy6.16 WAS an aggregate. This is the direct fix for the historical harm.'

MEASURED: src/mcp/ctkr-tools.ts contains NO reference to gateAggregate, gateQueryAnswer, summarizeHealth, or FITNESS — its entire import list is join/zod/McpServer/openCtkrArtifacts/EDGE_KIND_VALUES/types. registerCtkrTools IS wired into src/mcp/server.ts (line 26) and registers 11 live tools: ctkr.motif_search, ctkr.nearest_symbols, ctkr.pattern_search, ctkr.shape_distance, ctkr.role_equivalent, ctkr.centrality_query, ctkr.subsystems, ctkr.interface_of, ctkr.composition_rules, ctkr.subsystem_card, and one more.

So the two consumers named in the design BY NAME as the direct fix for the hy6.16 harm — motif mining (ctkr.motif_search) and role-equivalence (ctkr.role_equivalent) — are exactly the ones with no health channel at all. They return bare results with no ok/error discriminant, no caveat, and no acknowledge_unestablished_fitness parameter. hy6.16 itself was a role-rescore: this is the same tool class over the same unfit-graph condition.

Partial mitigation, stated fairly: CTKR tools read pre-built artifacts via openCtkrArtifacts rather than querying the live graph. That does not remove the exposure — those artifacts are DERIVED from the graph, so an unfit graph yields unfit artifacts and the aggregate absorbs the zero one level removed, with no record anywhere that the graph behind the artifact was never established. If anything the indirection makes it less visible, not more.

By contrast the six graph tools ARE correctly gated — I verified all six against a real production farmOS copy (graph_callers, graph_implementers, graph_neighbors, code_search, graph_cypher, graph_diff): all route through gateQueryAnswer/gateAggregate, empty+unestablished refuses, non-empty carries a caveat, graph_diff refuses unconditionally, and the refusal branch genuinely has no 'rows' property (answer.rows.map threw).

FIX DIRECTION: route the CTKR tools through gateAggregate with acknowledge_unestablished_fitness, and record in the CTKR artifacts themselves the health status of the graph they were derived from, so a consumer of an artifact can see it without re-deriving.
notes:
FIX SHIPPED 2026-08-04 (commit 70eb19f) — NOT self-closed; a fresh judge closes.

WHICH TOOLS ARE GATED: all eleven, at the registered-handler level, following
graph_diff's shape so the MCP surface stays consistent —
ctkr.motif_search, ctkr.nearest_symbols, ctkr.pattern_search,
ctkr.shape_distance, ctkr.role_equivalent, ctkr.centrality_query,
ctkr.subsystems, ctkr.interface_of, ctkr.composition_rules,
ctkr.subsystem_card, ctkr.functor_between.

Each now returns { ok:true, result, health, caveat? } or
{ ok:false, error:"INDEX_FITNESS_UNESTABLISHED", message, health } — the refusal
branch has NO `result` property, so a rescoring pass that reaches for rows
crashes rather than absorbing a zero. Refusal is BY DEFAULT on REFUSED /
RUNNING / UNKNOWN, empty or not; acknowledge_unestablished_fitness proceeds and
stamps the caveat. The parameter is advertised on every tool's
CTKR_TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS input_schema, so describe_api consumers can see it.
The raw functions (motifSearch, roleEquivalent, ...) stay ungated and exported,
exactly as graphDiffRows is — the gated surface is the tool surface.

DERIVED ARTIFACTS: an artifact inherits the unfitness of its input, and may be
staler than it. ctkrArtifactHealth(dataDir) answers two questions without a
Store handle:
  1. the health records beside the artifacts (<dataDir>/index-health.sqlite):
     none at all => UNKNOWN => refuse; any slice REFUSED/RUNNING/UNKNOWN =>
     refuse; OVERRIDDEN counts as established, as everywhere else.
  2. ctkr/manifest.json's generated_at vs the newest finished_at in the health
     records. If a verdict finalized AFTER the artifacts were built, the
     artifacts describe an EARLIER graph whose fitness at build time was never
     recorded — reported as an unestablished "(derived)" slice, refused by
     default, acknowledgeable. An absent manifest is UNKNOWN, never "fine".

WHAT IS STILL NEEDED (the bead's own fix direction, half-done): the manifest
does NOT record the health record it was built against. Timestamp ordering is
the strongest inheritance test available from the read side. The real fix is
for the ctkr batch runners (Python, schema.py ArtifactManifest) to stamp per
repo {run_id, status, commit_sha} into manifest.json at build time; then a
consumer sees the graph's fitness without re-deriving it, and a re-index
invalidates the artifact by run_id rather than by clock. Worth its own bead.

EVIDENCE (src/mcp/ctkr-gate.test.ts, 11 tests, all contrast pairs):
  A unestablished refuses / HEALTHY + fresh artifacts answers; RUNNING,
    REFUSED, UNKNOWN unestablished vs OVERRIDDEN established.
  B artifacts built BEFORE the verdict refuse though the graph is HEALTHY;
    the same fixture with the manifest stamp moved forward is established;
    no manifest => UNKNOWN.
  C ack=false does not compute AT ALL (proving a refusal never opens the
    artifacts, so a refusal cannot be confused with a missing-file error);
    ack=true computes and carries the caveat.
  D hy6.16's own shape: empty-over-unfit and empty-over-fit return DIFFERENT
    TYPES; reaching for .result on the refusal throws.
  WIRING: all eleven registered handlers driven against a data dir with no
    parquet at all — every one returns the typed refusal naming itself. Mirror:
    with fitness established, all eleven get PAST the gate and fail on the
    missing artifacts instead.
MUTATION-TESTED: always-proceed kills 4 tests; dropping the artifact-staleness
check kills 1; un-gating a SINGLE tool kills the wiring test with the DuckDB
"hom_profiles is not present" error it would otherwise have reached. Full suite
464 pass / 0 fail.
FRESH JUDGE 3 (tree HEAD 05d8a93, src/mcp/ctkr-tools.ts sha256 35d1dd8c31bd...) — the gating claim VERIFIED 11/11; the staleness rule has a real defect, filed separately.

VERIFIED (delegated to a fresh reader with line-number evidence, sandbox copy of HEAD):
 - ELEVEN, NOT TEN. registerCtkrTools (ctkr-tools.ts:2080) registers exactly eleven
   tools and every one wraps its handler in gateCtkrAggregate:
   motif_search 2082/2095, nearest_symbols 2108/2123, pattern_search 2136/2149,
   shape_distance 2162/2177, role_equivalent 2188/2208, centrality_query 2221/2235,
   subsystems 2247/2268, interface_of 2280/2308, composition_rules 2321/2355,
   subsystem_card 2370/2391, functor_between 2402/2433.
 - THE REFUSAL BRANCH HAS NO 'result': gateAggregate (health-gate.ts:181-195) returns
   {ok:false, error, message, health}; CtkrAnswer's ok:false variant omits the field.
 - A REFUSAL NEVER OPENS THE PARQUET: gateCtkrAggregate resolves the data dir, calls
   ctkrArtifactHealth (which reads ONLY index-health.sqlite and ctkr/manifest.json)
   and RETURNS EARLY at :206 before ever invoking compute(); openCtkrArtifacts is
   reached only from inside compute(). The suite's PAIR C proves it with a counter:
   compute() invoked 0 times on refusal, 1 on acknowledgment.
 - NO SECOND PATH: the eleven raw functions are exported but the only production
   importers are server.ts (registerCtkrTools, gated) and tools.ts (descriptions only).

DEFECT (filed as its own bead): the staleness comparison is a raw STRING compare, not
a date compare. ctkr-tools.ts:151-174 computes newestFinalize from finished_at and
tests 'newestFinalize > builtAt'. A malformed generated_at whose first character sorts
above a digit (e.g. 'not-a-real-timestamp') makes the comparison false and the manifest
passes. Reproduced by running it in the sandbox: generated_at:'not-a-real-timestamp'
against a HEALTHY record finalized 2026-02-01 -> established TRUE. A FUTURE
generated_at ('2099-01-01') likewise always passes -- no health record can finalize
later than the future.
 - absent/undefined generated_at -> manifestGeneratedAt returns null -> refuses (safe),
   though the slice is labelled 'no manifest.json' even when the file existed.
 - multi-repo: readAllIndexHealth takes the max finished_at across ALL slices with no
   repo filter, so a sibling repo's later verdict OVER-refuses this manifest. Wrong
   direction is the safe direction; noted, not a defect.
 - cosmetic: the docstring at ctkr-tools.ts:2076 still says 'all ten CTKR tools'.
close_reason: Fresh judge 3 at HEAD 05d8a93: all eleven registered CTKR handlers are wrapped in gateCtkrAggregate (line numbers in the note), the refusal branch carries no 'result', compute() is provably not invoked on refusal so no parquet is opened, and there is no second registration or live raw-function path. The staleness rule's string-comparison defect is filed as a separate bead.

title: index fitness: ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_NEW_COMMIT false-REFUSES a correct graph on a source-less commit — tree-sitter does not re-stamp unchanged files
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING at tree 7c03e77 (src/ingest/fitness.ts sha256 9a1dc30d0d02...).

THE DOCUMENTED CLAIM, which is FALSE: fitness.ts states 'Symbol.indexed_at is set from one constant per session, threaded through both lanes, and is not COALESCE-protected, so it is always overwritten', and rule (4) states it 'never false-alarms on a no-op re-index, because an idempotent MERGE still re-stamps indexed_at'.

The store-layer half is true (upsertSymbol writes indexed_at unconditionally; it is excluded from the preserveStructural COALESCE set). The LANE-layer half is false: src/extractor/walker.ts stamps the file Symbol's ast_hash with the content hash 'so the next pass can skip when content is unchanged', and a skipped file never calls upsertSymbol at all. The verification quoted in fitness.ts ('verified directly against a live ladybugdb store') probed the STORE, not a RE-RUN of the lane — an observation that could not have come out any other way, which is the non-discriminating-evidence failure iteration-methodology.md warns about.

MEASURED (sandbox judge2-stamp), reading DISTINCT s.indexed_at buckets after each run:
 run 1, commit A, 6 .ts files -> HEALTHY, contribution 24, one bucket: 24 symbols @ run-1 stamp.
 run 2, commit B, ONLY README.md changed (a docs-only commit) -> contribution 0, commitAdvanced TRUE -> **REFUSED [ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_NEW_COMMIT]**. Buckets unchanged: all 24 symbols still carry run 1's stamp — run 2 re-stamped NOTHING.
 run 3, control, one .ts file really edited -> contribution 4, and the buckets split 20 @ run-1 / 4 @ run-3. The measure DOES discriminate a real change; that is what proves run 2's zero is the skip, not a measurement artifact.

CONSEQUENCE: a completely correct, complete, up-to-date graph is persisted REFUSED whenever a commit touches no indexed source file (docs, CI config, lockfiles, .md, images, or any language no lane indexes). Per health-gate.ts a REFUSED slice makes every empty MCP graph query refuse, makes graph_diff refuse unconditionally, and makes status print 'its graph was unusable'. This is exactly the outcome fitness.ts rule (6) says it was designed to avoid: 'a rule that false-alarms on the most common invocation is a rule people disable.'

BLAST RADIUS / MITIGATION: with a SCIP lane in the run the loader re-ingests every document and re-stamps, so contribution stays large and the rule does not false-alarm (confirmed: judge2-red, same .scip re-ingested at a new commit, contribution 12 not 0). So this bites 'metacoding index <path>' WITHOUT --scip, and any lane combination where every lane skips unchanged files. It is also self-clearing in a rough way: once a run is REFUSED, previousEstablishedCommit returns null and the rule is disarmed until a HEALTHY run re-establishes.

FIX DIRECTION: contribution must count what this run VERIFIED, not only what it re-wrote. Either have the walker re-stamp indexed_at on skipped-unchanged files (cheap: it already knows the file is current), or measure contribution as 'symbols whose file the lane confirmed at this commit' rather than 'symbols this run re-wrote'. Whichever is chosen, fitness.ts's re-stamping paragraph must be corrected — and the evidence must be a RE-RUN of the lane, not a query against a store.
notes:
ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit 1278593), NOT CLOSED — fresh reader closes.

THE FALSE COMMENT IS CORRECTED IN PLACE (src/ingest/fitness.ts header + rule 4), and says what is actually true rather than a weaker version of the same claim: re-stamping is a property of the STORE's write path, not of a run; a lane that SKIPS a file never calls upsertSymbol, so nothing is merged and nothing is re-stamped. Rule (4) is safe for a NARROWER reason now stated exactly — the SCIP loader has no skip-unchanged path, so a run that requested SCIP and stamped no SCIP symbol really did fail to produce one.

THE FIX asks the right question instead of relaxing the rule. New measureGraphFreshness(store, repo, branch, rootPath) compares the STORE's own file rows (kind='file', ast_hash) against the bytes on disk — measured from the store, never from lane accumulators (walker's filesSkipped counts an unparseable file as skipped too, which is root 1 all over again). Rule (6) refuses zero contribution at a new commit only when the graph could NOT be shown to still BE the tree. Wired in session.ts and persisted on the record (freshness block).

DELIBERATE NON-CHOICES: staleness is NOT a standalone failure — a file whose grammar fails to parse never gets a matching hash and would refuse forever. Freshness can only ever DISARM the one rule; nothing passes because of it that a productive run would not already have passed. 'absent' (a stored path with no counterpart on disk: container prefixes, deletions) is REPORTED and not counted as drift, or farmOS's --load-scip paths would refuse every run.

commitSha === null: was PERMISSIVE (the rule could not fire), now degrades SAFE as commitUncertain -> ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_UNKNOWN_COMMIT, with the same freshness escape so a no-op re-index of an unchanged non-git tree still passes. commitSha = '' still counts as advancement.

EVIDENCE — PAIR c03 in src/ingest/fitness.test.ts, a RE-RUN OF THE LANE (not a query against a store, which is how the false claim survived). Half A: runIndexSession over 6 .ts files, then a docs-only commit — asserts contribution 0, ONE indexed_at bucket still holding run 1's count (the judge's own instrument), freshness stale 0, HEALTHY. Half B: the same zero contribution over a tree two files drifted from — REFUSED, and the message names src/f0.ts. Plus: checked === 0 never vouches; freshness does not make NO_SYMBOLS pass; the unnameable-commit pair.
MUTATIONS: restoring the old rule reddens half A; letting checked === 0 vouch reddens the escape-hatch test; dropping commitUncertain reddens the unnameable-commit pair. Baseline verified clean before and after, and the commit was re-run in an isolated worktree (134 pass / 0 fail) because another agent was editing the same files concurrently.

FAKE-IT ASKED: 'freshness becomes the new UNMEASURABLE' — answered by (a) it only disarms, never grants, (b) checked === 0 is not stale === 0, (c) EVERY stored file that exists on disk must match, so one fresh file cannot vouch for a tree.
FRESH JUDGE 3 (tree HEAD 05d8a93, src/ingest/fitness.ts sha256 5ffcff9650c3...) — the two load-bearing guarantees VERIFIED; one under-stated consequence recorded.

VERIFIED (executed, sandbox copy of HEAD):
 - checked===0 NEVER vouches: isGraphVerifiedCurrent({checked:0, absent:500}) = false,
   and isGraphVerifiedCurrent(undefined) = false. Absent input is treated as 'no',
   not 'fine'.
 - EVERY stored file present on disk must match: 499 fresh + 1 stale -> false.
 - freshness can only DISARM rule (6); it appears in no other branch of
   evaluateIndexOutcome. Confirmed by reading fitness.ts:714-750 -- verifiedCurrent
   is only ever read as '&& !verifiedCurrent' there and reported in GateResult.

UNDER-STATED CONSEQUENCE (real, bounded): 'absent' is reported and not counted as
staleness, which means a DELETE-ONLY commit is vouched as 'the graph still IS the
tree' while the graph still holds the deleted files' symbols. Executed: 6 .ts files
indexed at commit 1111...; commit 2222... deletes 3 of them and changes nothing else;
run 2 -> status HEALTHY, contribution.symbols 0,
freshness {checked:3, fresh:3, stale:0, absent:3}, verifiedCurrent TRUE, and the graph
still returns 2 symbols for the deleted src/f0.ts. So freshness DOES vouch for a graph
that is not the tree, in exactly one direction: deletions. The module comment names
'absent' as 'a number a reader can see, not a verdict' -- but it IS load-bearing for a
verdict here, because it is what lets verifiedCurrent stay true and disarm
ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_NEW_COMMIT. Worth one sentence in the header; not worth refusing
container-prefixed builds over.

RELATED, MITIGATED ELSEWHERE: a store holding 1 file of a 60-file tree measures
{checked:1, fresh:1, stale:0} -> verifiedCurrent TRUE. Freshness says nothing about
COVERAGE by design; LOW_CORRESPONDENCE is the rule that catches it (1/60 = 1.7% < the
0.1 floor). The two measures only jointly cover the case, which is the correct
division of labour but means neither can be read alone.

SEMANTIC MOVES that are NOT missed: a rename/move/add produces a new path the walker
does not skip, so contribution > 0 and rule (6) never reaches the freshness escape at
all. Only pure deletions and pure no-ops reach it.
close_reason: Fresh judge 3 at HEAD 05d8a93 re-ran the escape-hatch attacks: checked===0 never vouches, one stale file sinks the vouch, freshness appears only as a disarm of rule (6). The delete-only-commit consequence is recorded as a note and filed as a doc-accuracy follow-up.

title: index fitness: the ingest SEAM does not hold — 9 bypass shapes undetected, and indexFile is a public unguarded ingest primitive
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING against the index-fitness implementation at tree 7c03e77 (src/ingest/seam.test.ts sha256 a039721b3b73...).

THE CLAIM: session.ts and health.ts both assert that writing around the session is 'STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE rather than fixed-once' because indexDirectory/loadScip/watch are off the barrels and seam.test.ts 'FAILS THE SUITE when another module in src/ imports them'. MEASURED: it does not.

METHOD: git-archive copy of HEAD into a sandbox, node_modules symlinked; baseline seam.test.ts 3 pass/0 fail reproduced. Then 9 bypass modules written into src/bypass/ and the seam test re-run.

ALL NINE PASSED THE SUITE UNDETECTED:
 A multi-line import  'import {\n  indexDirectory,\n} from ...' (the shape prettier produces on any wrapped import)
 B renamed import     'import { indexDirectory as ingest } from ...'
 C namespace import   'import * as walker from ...; walker.indexDirectory(...)'
 D dynamic import     'const m = await import(...); m.indexDirectory(...)'
 E require            'const m = require(...)'
 F re-export chain    a shim doing 'export { indexDirectory as ingestTree } from ...' then a consumer importing ingestTree
 G indexFile          NO evasion needed — see below
 H watch              'watch' is NOT in the GUARDED list at all, despite being named in the claim
 (control) Z          the single-line 'import { indexDirectory } from ...' — the ONLY shape caught

CONTROL PROVES THE INSTRUMENT WORKS: with Z present the suite fails and names bypass/z-control.ts. So the scanner is not broken — it is exactly as wide as the synthetic bypass in its own mutation test, and no wider. findViolationsIn only inspects lines that START WITH 'import ', and its regex requires the identifier to be followed by ',' or '}', so 'as', multi-line, namespace, dynamic and require forms are all invisible.

THE DEEPEST HOLE NEEDS NO EVASION AT ALL: src/extractor/index.ts still exports indexFile (the seam test explicitly ASSERTS it is exported, as its regex contrast). indexFile(store, root, file, opts) writes symbols, edges AND tokens to the Store and is not in GUARDED.

BYPASS ACHIEVED END-TO-END (sandbox judge2-run): a real session established HEALTHY with fitness 24 symbols at commit aaaa...; then the multi-line bypass took the store 24 -> 40 symbols, and the public indexFile bypass took it 40 -> 52, both writing into the SAME (repo,branch) slice at a DIFFERENT commit. The persisted record still reads status HEALTHY, fitness.symbols 24, commit_sha aaaa... A stale HEALTHY over a store 2.2x larger than the record describes — precisely the 'write around the session' fake-it that health.ts claims is closed by construction.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the difference between 'closed by construction' and 'closed by a guard'. iteration-methodology.md requires that distinction be recorded, not hidden. Today it is recorded as construction and is in fact a guard with one covered shape.

FIX DIRECTION: an import-text scanner cannot enforce this. Either (a) enforce module boundaries with a real tool (dependency-cruiser / eslint no-restricted-imports / TS project references) which sees renames, namespaces and dynamic imports; or (b) make it a TYPE-level seam — have the ingest primitives require a token value that only runIndexSession can mint, so a caller literally cannot construct the argument; or (c) at minimum add 'watch' and 'indexFile' to GUARDED, match multi-line import blocks, and mutation-test the scanner against ALL of the shapes above rather than one.
notes:
FIX SHIPPED 2026-08-04 (commit 037926f, doc 4b0645d) — NOT self-closed; a fresh judge closes.

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY NOT A WIDER REGEX
The scanner was replaced, not widened. A text check over import syntax has
coverage equal to the shapes its author imagined; the bypass is whatever shape
they did not. New file src/ingest/ticket.ts makes the seam a CAPABILITY:

  * `IngestTicket` is NOMINAL (private field + private constructor), so calling
    indexDirectory / indexFile / removeFile / loadScip / watch without one is a
    TYPE ERROR in every import shape, and registered at runtime in a WeakSet so
    a `as unknown as IngestTicket` cast is a runtime refusal.
  * A ticket is bound to its (repo, branch) — a session on a scratch repo
    cannot license writes into another slice — and is revoked at finalize.
  * THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: a write into a slice whose record currently reads
    ESTABLISHED (HEALTHY/OVERRIDDEN) is REFUSED. To write into such a slice you
    must first take it off HEALTHY, and runIndexSession is the path that does
    that while finalizing a fresh verdict measured from what it wrote.
    Writing into an UNKNOWN / RUNNING / REFUSED slice remains permitted and
    CANNOT manufacture a stale HEALTHY — readers already refuse those.
  * The watch lane is admitted against an established record only when the
    record carries watching:true with the same run id (the design's named,
    not-re-judged incremental lane), so the licensing state is a readable fact.

IS IT A CONSTRUCTION OR A GUARD? Construction for the harm in this bead (stale
HEALTHY), because the check is syntax-blind and the record state gates it.
Guard-shaped residue, named: (a) FORGING THE RECORD is not closed — a module
can open IndexHealthStore and write HEALTHY with invented numbers; closing that
needs a signature the forger cannot compute; (b) a Store double with no dataDir
gets the UNKNOWN treatment (no record to go stale); (c) flip-to-RUNNING, write,
walk away is permitted by design and leaves the slice reading RUNNING forever.

EVERY SHAPE, RE-RUN AS AN EXECUTED TEST (src/ingest/seam.test.ts, 21 tests):
A multi-line import REFUSED; B renamed import REFUSED; C namespace REFUSED;
D dynamic import() REFUSED; E require() via createRequire REFUSED;
F re-export chain through a shim written at test time REFUSED;
G indexFile (the public barrel export) REFUSED; G' removeFile REFUSED;
H watch REFUSED; I loadScip REFUSED; Z single-line control REFUSED.
End-to-end: the 24 -> 40 -> 52 attack now leaves the store and the record in
agreement (symbol count unchanged, commit_sha unchanged, still HEALTHY).

CONTRAST HALVES (a suite where nothing can succeed is as blind as one where
nothing can fail): a session writes and the record describes what it wrote; a
second session grows the store and the record advances with it; a ticket DOES
write into an unestablished slice; the five input classes produce five distinct
refusal codes (NO_TICKET / FORGED_TICKET / REVOKED_TICKET / WRONG_SLICE /
ESTABLISHED_FITNESS_WOULD_GO_STALE) plus a permitted NO_THROW.

TYPE-LEVEL EVIDENCE: two tsc probes whose only difference is the ticket — the
call without one fails with "Property 'ticket' is missing", the call with one
compiles clean; plus an object literal is not assignable to IngestTicket while
the mint's return value is.

MUTATION-TESTED (the old instrument's synthetic resembled only the shape it
already caught): no-op assertMayIngest kills 14 of 21 tests; dropping only the
established-record check kills 14; making `ticket` optional kills exactly the
type test. Full suite green.

FAKE-IT ANSWER — what write path still reaches the graph while satisfying the
new check? Three, all named above: forge the health record; write into a slice
that is already unestablished (harmless by construction); or use the watch lane
by forging watching:true + run id, which reduces to forging the record.

FOLLOW-UP NOT DONE: the header comments in src/ingest/session.ts and
src/store/health.ts still describe the seam as "enforced by seam.test.ts, which
fails the suite when another module imports them". Both files were being edited
by a concurrent agent, so they were left alone to avoid a conflicting write.
FRESH JUDGE 3 (tree HEAD 05d8a93, src/ingest/ticket.ts sha256 6d1d29bb5ab9...) — NOT CLOSED. The ticket construction holds at the layer it guards and DOES NOT hold one layer down.

WHAT SURVIVED THE ATTACKS (all executed, sandbox git-archive copy of HEAD):
 - structuredClone(ticket) -> not in LIVE -> refused.
 - Object.create(IngestTicket.prototype) / Object.setPrototypeOf(literal, proto) /
   Reflect.construct(IngestTicket, ...) -> instanceof TRUE but LIVE false -> refused.
 - MODULE DUPLICATION: 'import("./ticket.ts?cachebust=1")' yields a SECOND class +
   SECOND WeakSet; a B-issued ticket through A.assertMayIngest and through the real
   indexDirectory both -> FORGED_TICKET. Duplication makes it stricter, not weaker.
 - Slice hijack: a ticket for scratch@x with repo/branch reassigned to an ESTABLISHED
   slice is stopped by the RECORD check (ESTABLISHED_FITNESS_WOULD_GO_STALE), not by
   the binding — see the defect below.

DEFECT A (real bypass, unnamed in the fix): Store.upsertSymbol / Store.addEdge ARE
THE INGEST LAYER AND ARE UNGATED. Executed end to end: session finalizes HEALTHY at
12 symbols; then 16 store.upsertSymbol calls + one addEdge from the PUBLIC barrel
'src/store' with NO ticket, NO session, NO record forgery -> store 12 -> 28 symbols,
record still status=HEALTHY fitness.symbols=12 commit_sha=aaaaaaa. That is bead 9ed's
original harm (stale HEALTHY over a store 2.3x the record) reproduced verbatim.
docs/design/index-fitness.md fake-it #3 names this exact mechanism -- 'any direct
Store.upsertSymbol leaves a stale HEALTHY' -- and marks it 'Refuted and re-closed
(MetaCoding-9ed)'. It is not closed. ticket.ts:20 'YOU CANNOT WRITE TO THE GRAPH
WITHOUT A SESSION THAT WILL JUDGE THE RESULT' and session.ts:225-226 'Nothing in src/
can write to the graph without one' are both false as written.

DEFECT B (nominality oversold, benign): 'IngestTicket.mint' is a PUBLIC static (only
'@internal' in a comment), and 'issueIngestTicket' is a public export, so the private
constructor buys nothing -- any module mints a LIVE ticket for any slice. That is by
design per seam.test.ts ('a ticket a bypasser can legitimately mint'), but the header's
'no caller outside this module can new one' reads as protection it does not provide.
The whole property rests on the RECORD check alone.

DEFECT C (fields are readonly only at the type level): Object.assign onto a REAL live
ticket rewrites .repo/.branch and it STAYS LIVE. The (repo,branch) binding is not
enforced at runtime; only the established-record check stops the resulting write.

DEFECT D (watch lane is authenticated by a published value): the watch lane admits a
ticket when rec.watching===true AND rec.run_id===ticket.runStamp. run_id is READ FROM
THE RECORD by anyone. Executed: with watching:true set, a self-minted mode:'watch'
ticket carrying the record's own run_id was PERMITTED and grew a HEALTHY slice
12 -> 14 with the record still reading fitness=12. During a live 'metacoding watch'
that state is legitimately true, so this needs no forgery at all.

CONFIRMED OPEN AS THE BUILDER NAMED IT: record forgery is reachable in one call --
IndexHealthStore.open(dataDir).write({status:'HEALTHY', fitness:{symbols:999999,...},
correspondence:{level:'exact',ratio:1}}) read back as HEALTHY 999999 symbols.

VERDICT: closed-by-GUARD for the import shapes, not closed-by-CONSTRUCTION for the
property. Keep open until either the Store write methods require the capability or
the claim in ticket.ts/session.ts/index-fitness.md is narrowed to what is true.

title: index gate: 'coverage' compares SCIP document count to local source files — it can read 100% with zero repo files indexed
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING against MetaCoding-0sd (commit 0c13fa2). The LOW_COVERAGE rule is the gate's answer to 'one trivial file of 273 passes > 0'. Its numerator and denominator measure DIFFERENT SETS, so it can be satisfied without indexing any of the repo.

 numerator   = max over lanes of lane.files; for a SCIP lane that is DOCUMENT COUNT, and a document's relative_path can be anything.
 denominator = censusSourceFiles(targetPath), which EXCLUDES node_modules/dist/dot-dirs.

MEASURED, sandbox (data-dir <scratch>/judge-0sd/data/vendor, FRESH — no stale store involved):
 index <10-file .go repo> --repo sf --load-scip vendor40.scip, where all 40 documents have relative_path 'node_modules/dep/vN.ts' and real occurrences
 -> scip.documents 40, symbolsUpserted 40, edgesAdded 78
 -> gate.ok TRUE, filesCovered 40, sourceFiles 10, coverage 1 (clamped), EXIT 0.
Zero of the 10 .go source files were indexed; the gate reports 100% coverage.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FIXTURE: for the --load-scip path the index is built OUT OF BAND (farmOS/Docker), so document paths come from the container filesystem and have no relation to the local tree at all — coverage is vacuous there by construction. For the in-process path, any lane that emits documents for vendored/generated/dependency files inflates the same numerator. This is the fosite family: a repo whose real language nothing indexes, where the selected lane emits documents for something else.

FIX DIRECTION: intersect — count only documents whose path resolves to a file inside the census set (and report the intersection size), instead of taking a raw max of lane.files.

Sandbox data-dirs only; production store untouched.
notes:
ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit 6c933a7), not closed — fresh reader closes. 'coverage' is replaced by CORRESPONDENCE (measureCorrespondence, src/ingest/fitness.ts): a set intersection over Symbol.file against censusSourceFiles' path SET, not a ratio of two different counts. Four-rung granularity ladder with the rung RECORDED: exact path / path suffix (survives an /app/web/ container prefix) / basename (survives an arbitrary prefix) / UNMEASURABLE(reason). So --load-scip is not structurally unmeasurable — farmOS-in-Docker measures at 'suffix', scip-php without the PSR-4 sidecar at 'basename', and a vendored index at neither. UNMEASURABLE emits UNMEASURABLE_CORRESPONDENCE and is NEVER a pass on its own. Evidence: PAIR 5 — the judge's vendor40 shape (40 node_modules/dep/vN.ts documents with real definitions and real edges) comes out UNMEASURABLE 0/40 while a 40-document index of the SAME tree with correct paths comes out exact 40/40, opposite verdicts from one gate. PAIR 6 brackets the ladder. Mutation M6 (count indexed files instead of intersecting) CAUGHT.
FRESH JUDGE (tree 7c03e77) — NOT CLOSING. The set-intersection fix is real at the exact/suffix rungs, but the BASENAME rung reproduces this bead's exact headline: 'can read 100% with zero repo files indexed'.

COUNTEREXAMPLE I RAN (sandbox, judge2-base2/3): local tree = 6 .go files under src/ (detectGrammar('.go') returns null, so the tree-sitter lane contributes nothing — the fosite shape this bead is about). Ingested a .scip whose 6 documents are all 'vendor/github.com/other/project/internal/svcN.go' — a DIFFERENT tree, sharing only BASENAMES.
RESULT: correspondence { level: 'basename', matched: 6, sourceFiles: 6, ratio: 1 }, fitness 6 symbols / 12 relational edges, VERDICT **HEALTHY**, failures []. Store query confirms every indexed file is under vendor/github.com/other/project/ — ZERO of the 6 local source files are in the graph.

WHY THE EXISTING DEFENCE DOESN'T HOLD: fitness.ts fake-it #2 relies on the vendor40 fixture, which 'intersects in ZERO places at every rung'. That is a property of that fixture's invented filenames, not of vendoring. Real vendored trees ARE copies of upstream repos, and basename collision is the norm (client.go, server.go, config.go, doc.go, errors.go; index.ts, types.ts, utils.ts). So the fixture cannot discriminate the case the bead is about. fake-it #4 named UNMEASURABLE as 'the weakest joint' — measured, the weakest joint is the BASENAME rung granting FULL ratio credit and thus a clean pass.

FIX DIRECTION: basename correspondence should not be able to produce a passing ratio on its own — either cap its ratio below the floor, require a corroborating signal (e.g. a suffix match for some minimum share), or emit a distinct failure code the way UNMEASURABLE does. It is currently the only rung whose 'match' carries no evidence that the two trees are the same tree.
RE-ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit eeb2bf8), NOT CLOSED — fresh reader closes. The judge's headline counterexample is now a standing test.

DECISION: a basename match is evidence that two trees use the same FILE NAMES. It is not evidence that they are the same tree, and NOTHING MEASURABLE FROM PATHS ALONE can promote it into one — scip-php-without-a-sidecar and a vendored upstream copy are structurally identical at that rung. So basename earns NO ratio (the quantity that means 'this share of the tree is in the graph' — null, like unmeasurable) and emits a new BASENAME_ONLY_CORRESPONDENCE failure: never a pass on its own, waivable with --allow-empty-index and then recorded OVERRIDDEN forever. A discount factor was rejected: any number that still clears the 10% floor leaves the headline intact.

THE RUNG IS KEPT, and keeping it is the point — it keeps the case legible in the record ('the names correspond and nothing else does') instead of collapsing into unmeasurable. WHY NOTHING LEGITIMATE BREAKS: a container-prefixed out-of-band build (farmOS in Docker, /app/web/...) lands on SUFFIX, untouched; and every session runs the tree-sitter lane over the LOCAL tree first (detectGrammar handles .php/.module/.install), so a farmOS --load-scip run has local relative paths in the store and lands on EXACT. Only a graph that shares nothing with this tree but file names is refused. Checked: neither production store has an index-health record yet, so no existing verdict changes.

ALSO FIXED while in here: exact and suffix are now counted TOGETHER (the suffix set contains every path in full, so a suffix match is a superset of an exact one) instead of first-rung-wins, which used to under-report a mixed build — 3 local files + 7 container-prefixed read as matched 3, not 10.

EVIDENCE — PAIR 5fi in src/ingest/fitness.test.ts: the judge's own fixture, 6 local .go files (detectGrammar('.go') null, the fosite shape) plus a .scip under vendor/github.com/other/project/ sharing only basenames -> level basename, matched 6, ratio null, REFUSED [BASENAME_ONLY_CORRESPONDENCE]; against the SAME 6 file names under a container prefix -> suffix, ratio 1, HEALTHY. Two foreign-path graphs of the same names, opposite verdicts, differing only in whether an indexed path CONTAINS a local path. Plus a mixed-build test pinning the exact+suffix union.
MUTATIONS: restoring basename's ratio reddens the vendored half only; restoring first-rung-wins reddens the mixed-build test only.

FAKE-IT ASKED: 'the waiver becomes the escape hatch' — it is --allow-empty-index, which finalizes OVERRIDDEN with the flag in the record forever, so the choice is visible at read time rather than being a silent pass. Named, not hidden.
FRESH JUDGE 3 (tree HEAD 05d8a93, src/ingest/fitness.ts sha256 5ffcff9650c3...) — NOT CLOSED. The basename fix is correct and is BYPASSED ONE RUNG UP, by the structure of real vendoring.

The previous judge's counterexample only landed on BASENAME because its invented
vendor paths did not preserve the upstream layout. Real vendored trees are COPIES:
vendor/github.com/ory/fosite/<the upstream repo-relative path>. Every local
repo-relative path is therefore a PATH SUFFIX of its vendored twin, and
measureCorrespondence's rung 2 (pathSuffixes over every indexed path) matches it.

EXECUTED (sandbox copy of HEAD, src/ingest/judge3-vendor.test.ts):
  local tree  = client.go, oauth2.go, handler/oauth2/flow_authorize_code_token.go,
                handler/openid/flow_explicit_token.go, token/jwt/jwt.go,
                internal/client_storage.go
  the .scip   = vendor/github.com/ory/fosite/<each of those>
  RESULT      -> {level:'suffix', matched:6, sourceFiles:6, ratio:1} and the gate
                 returns ok:true, failures:[] -- HEALTHY, ratio 1.0, with ZERO local
                 files in the graph. 5fi's literal headline, after the fix.

CONTRAST HALF (proves the instrument can still fail): same six files with the layout
FLATTENED (local a/*.go vs indexed z/*.go) -> {level:'basename', ratio:null} and
BASENAME_ONLY_CORRESPONDENCE, gate ok:false. So eeb2bf8 works exactly where the old
judge's fixture pointed and nowhere else.

MINIMAL FORM: a single-segment local path is a suffix of ANY path ending in that name.
local ['index.ts'] vs indexed ['/completely/unrelated/other-project/index.ts'] ->
suffix, ratio 1.0, HEALTHY.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN BASENAME DID: suffix earns a RATIO, so it does not merely
pass -- it reports 100% correspondence. The rung the design calls 'PATH evidence' is
path evidence only about the tail of the path, and a vendored copy shares the tail by
construction. Any fix must distinguish 'the indexed path IS the local path' from 'the
indexed path CONTAINS the local path under a prefix that is itself a repo boundary'
(vendor/, node_modules/, third_party/, .git-less nested checkouts) -- note that
DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_DIRS already knows several of those names, and rung 2 currently
ignores them.

NOT A REGRESSION FOR PRODUCTION: see the farmOS finding on MetaCoding-c03/this bead --
a real PHP tree lands on EXACT, so nothing about the production --load-scip build is
harmed by tightening rung 2.
PRODUCTION SAFETY CHECK for the farmOS full-signal --load-scip build (asked during the run): SAFE, verified rather than reasoned.

runIndexSession runs indexDirectory over targetPath UNCONDITIONALLY and FIRST
(session.ts:245), before the --load-scip lane, and detectGrammar (walker.ts:485-505)
returns 'php' for .php/.phtml/.inc/.module/.install/.theme/.profile/.engine -- the
Drupal extensionless set. So the local tree's own files are in the graph with
repo-relative paths.

EXECUTED end-to-end on a Drupal-shaped fixture (8 web/modules/farm/src/*.php plus a
farm.module), tree-sitter only, no scip:
  status HEALTHY, correspondence {level:'exact', matched:8, sourceFiles:8, ratio:1}
  indexed paths e.g. 'web/modules/farm/src/Thing5.php'
Layering a foreign-filesystem scip path ('/opt/drupal/web/modules/farm/src/Thing0.php')
ON TOP still reads {level:'exact', ratio:1}, because the first rung that intersects at
all wins and the tree-sitter rows already intersect exactly.

The builder's claim ('tree-sitter runs first over the local tree so it lands exact')
is CONFIRMED. 5fi's basename refusal cannot fire on that build.

title: index gate: a run that contributed NOTHING passes when the store already holds that repo
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING against MetaCoding-0sd's fix (commit 0c13fa2, src/cli/index-gate.ts sha256 174a7997f86c...). REFUTES the sub-rule 'NO_SCIP_DOCUMENTS means a stale store cannot mask an empty run'.

MEASURED, sandbox only (data-dir <scratch>/judge-0sd/data/stale):
 run A: index <10-file .go repo> --repo sf --load-scip productive.scip  -> EXIT 0, 2 symbols, 3 relational edges.
 run B: SAME data-dir/repo/branch, --load-scip barren40.scip (40 documents, each with ZERO occurrences)
        -> treeSitter.filesScanned 0, scip.documents 40, symbolsUpserted 0, edgesAdded 0
        -> gate.ok TRUE, coverage 1, symbols 2, relationalEdges 3, failures [] -> EXIT 0.
 Run B produced literally nothing and reported success on run A's graph.

DISCRIMINATING CONTRAST: the identical run B into a FRESH data-dir exits 1 (NO_SYMBOLS/NO_RELATIONAL_EDGES). Same probe, two store histories, opposite answers -> the difference IS the staleness, not the fixture.

WHY THE GUARD FAILS: NO_SCIP_DOCUMENTS counts DOCUMENTS, and an empty document is a document. symbols/relationalEdges come from storeCensus, which is repo-wide and cannot distinguish this run's contribution from any earlier run's. Re-indexing an already-indexed repo is the normal case, so the fosite shape survives on any store that has seen that repo once.

FIX DIRECTION: measure a DELTA (census before and after the run) or scope the census to this run's identity (indexed_at / repo_commit_sha already stamped on symbols), rather than counting documents.

Repro fixtures: <scratch>/judge-0sd/mkfixtures.ts, gorepo/. Sandbox data-dirs only; production $ORCHESTRATORS_ROOT/.metacoding untouched.
notes:
ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit 6c933a7), not closed — fresh reader closes. Dissolved into two facts per docs/design/index-fitness.md. (a) 'this run wrote nothing' is now measured per-run via Symbol.indexed_at (measureRunContribution, src/ingest/fitness.ts) instead of a repo-wide census; the document count that could never catch an empty document is gone. (b) zero contribution is DEFENSIBLE at the same commit into an already-fit store and REFUSED when the run claims a new commit (ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_NEW_COMMIT). Evidence: PAIR 4 in src/ingest/fitness.test.ts — the IDENTICAL barren run passes at commit W and is refused when it claims X, plus contribution vs fitness measured separately out of one real store (run A's stamp reads full, run B's reads zero against the same store). Also NO_SCIP_SYMBOLS_THIS_RUN: SCIP requested but no store-visible scip symbol stamped by this run. Mutation M9 (drop the commit rule) CAUGHT. NOTE the partial disagreement recorded in the design: the SAME-commit half of this finding is not treated as a defect, deliberately.
FRESH JUDGE (tree 7c03e77). RE-RAN the discriminating contrast MYSELF: identical barren run into a fit store, ONLY the claimed commit differing. same-commit -> no ZERO_CONTRIBUTION failure; new-commit -> REFUSED with ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_NEW_COMMIT. Also confirmed the architect's contested half directly: a re-index of an UNCHANGED tree contributes 0 symbols and is recorded HEALTHY at the same commit. contribution and fitness are two fields from two functions (verified in the persisted record: contribution 0 / fitness 24). Edge cases I ran: commitSha null (not a git repo) -> commitAdvanced FALSE, rule cannot fire = degrades PERMISSIVE, not safe; commitSha '' -> counts as advanced (safe direction); prev record REFUSED -> previousEstablishedCommit null -> rule disarmed until a HEALTHY run re-establishes. The ORIGINAL defect (repo-wide census substituted for this run's contribution) is FIXED. NOTE: the bead's literal repro (barren run B at the SAME commit into a stale store) still passes — now BY DELIBERATE DESIGN, not by accident. A consequential false-refusal defect found in this same rule is filed separately.
close_reason: Fresh-judge verified at tree 7c03e77: contribution measured per-run from the store and stored distinctly from fitness; ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_NEW_COMMIT discriminates on the commit alone (same-commit passes by design, new-commit refuses). Consequential false-refusal filed separately.

title: Add a real Go lane — scip-go computes interface satisfaction nothing else can recover
description:
MEASURED BY d1l.7 (MetaCoding 44cc29d). There is currently NO Go lane: ScipLanguage = 'typescript' | 'python' | 'php', INDEXERS has no Go entry, detectScipLanguages() can never return Go, normalizeScipLang() rejects 'go'. Every Go number in the d1l.7 spike was produced MANUALLY, out of band, with --scip-language ts passed for a Go index (a deliberate lie — no honest value exists). Production cannot reproduce it today. Side effect: 'language' reads 'ts' for all 2,879 Go symbols.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING, and this is the payoff: scip-go computes GO INTERFACE SATISFACTION (776 implementations in fosite) and it lands as real IMPLEMENTS edges at BOTH type and method level — e.g. fosite.Config.GetTokenEndpointHandlers -> fosite.TokenEndpointHandlersProvider.GetTokenEndpointHandlers. Go is STRUCTURALLY typed: nothing declares these, so they are NOT recoverable syntactically or by any tree-sitter pass. 586 edges from one repo for an 8.9s indexer run. That is precisely the substrate d1l.3 needs to map reference structures onto Rust trait targets.

fosite @a5f0b09b full counts: CALLS 3274, REFERENCES 7065, IMPLEMENTS 586, READS_FIELD 3936.

GOTCHA: scip-go MOVED to github.com/scip-code/scip-go — the old sourcegraph/ path fails to install.

ALSO: 42,126 external refs were dropped with no boundary node (PHP has Pass-2b, Go gets 0), so stdlib / net/http / crypto usage is invisible. Decide whether Go needs its own boundary pass.

TO CLOSE: Go is a first-class lane end to end, and the d1l.7 numbers reproduce from a plain 'metacoding index'.
notes:
RE-SCOPE 2026-08-04: PROMOTED TO P1 AND WIRED AS A BLOCKER ON d1l.2 (and hence, transitively, on d1l.3).

Two of the three reference implementations are Go. Without this bead the corpus is either empty (0sd: metacoding index --scip on fosite exits 0 with zero symbols) or manually produced and unreproducible by production, with 'ts' recorded as the language for 2,879 Go symbols. Everything downstream — d1l.10's file walk aside — reads that corpus.

It is also the cheapest large win in the epic: add 'go' to ScipLanguage / INDEXERS / detectScipLanguages / normalizeScipLang plus a "go" language code, and 586 IMPLEMENTS edges encoding Go interface satisfaction fall out of an 8.9s indexer run — relationships nothing declares in the source and no syntactic pass can recover. That is the substrate d1l.3 needs.

title: metacoding index --scip exits 0 with an empty graph when the wrong indexer is selected
description:
FOUND BY d1l.7 (docs/notes/2026-08-04-go-js-lane-spike.md, MetaCoding 44cc29d), reproducing MetaCoding-hy6.16 in a NEW repo.

'metacoding index <fosite> --scip' EXITS 0 AND REPORTS SUCCESS with a completely empty graph. Mechanism: ory/fosite is a Go repo that happens to ship package.json + tsconfig.json, so detectScipLanguages() selects scip-typescript; scip-typescript fails with 'no files got indexed'; the failure is CAUGHT AND LOGGED; the run reports success. The resulting store has 0 symbols and 0 edges of every type. Artifact: scratchpad data/go-native, complete and empty BY CONSTRUCTION.

This is the hy6.16 failure mode as a general defect rather than a one-off: a re-scoring pass ran on a graph with CALLS=0 / REFERENCES=0 and the empty result was mistaken for a real one. Anything that trusts exit 0 is exposed, including d1l.2 which is queued to index exactly this repo.

ROOT CAUSE: resolveScipWanted guards indexer AVAILABILITY, not indexer OUTCOME. Availability was never the risk.

TO CLOSE: a --scip run that produces zero indexed files fails loudly instead of succeeding quietly. The AC is a regression test asserting NON-ZERO edge counts BY TYPE, not process exit status — an assertion on exit 0 is precisely the check that already failed here.
notes:

PROPERTY (the red), not a block on the fosite instance: an index run may report
success only if the STORE it wrote holds, for the repo it just indexed, the
structural content that run claimed to produce — every requested lane completed,
a non-trivial share of the repo's source files was covered, and when SCIP was
requested the store holds symbols AND non-zero relational edges.

Implementation: src/cli/index-gate.ts (evaluateIndexOutcome / storeCensus /
censusSourceFiles), wired into indexOneRepo in src/cli/main.ts. Failure codes:
LANE_FAILED (a scip lane throwing is no longer swallowed by a catch),
NO_FILES_SCANNED, NO_SYMBOLS, NO_SCIP_DOCUMENTS, NO_RELATIONAL_EDGES,
LOW_COVERAGE (--min-coverage, default 0.10). index-all now exits non-zero if any
repo fails. Escape hatch --allow-empty-index (verified: EXIT=1 vs EXIT_ALLOW=0).

FAKE-IT QUESTION -> what it changed:
 - 1 trivial file of 273 passes a '> 0' threshold -> coverage floor instead of >0
 - one lane dies while a sibling succeeds -> lane failure is fatal for the run
 - '0 files scanned' vs 'scanned but 0 symbols' -> separate codes/messages
 - accumulators non-zero while the store is empty -> gate measures the store
 - store still holds a PREVIOUS good run's symbols -> NO_SCIP_DOCUMENTS checks
   THIS run's scip output independently of the store

green). Load-bearing assertions are NON-ZERO EDGE COUNTS BY TYPE read out of a

tested: disabling the coverage rule and the lane-failure rule each turned one

/.metacoding untouched, no serve contended):

VERDICT ON THE FIRST FIX: directionally right in WHAT it checks, structurally wrong in two ways. Not a redesign of the checks and not a two-line patch.

TWO ROOTS, FOUR DEFECTS:
  Root 1 — every measurement is taken from the nearest available number rather than from the set its claim is about. That is 4kg + 5fi + e6z (and the original 0sd, if 'availability instead of outcome' counts as the same substitution one level up). e6z is not a testing gap ALONGSIDE two bugs — it is the MECHANISM by which root 1 is invisible, and it will re-manufacture 4kg and 5fi under new names after any fix that does not change how the evidence is built.
  Root 2 — the verdict is an EVENT (a process exit code) rather than a STATE (a fact about the store). That is all of ae5. And note the asymmetry: root 1 has had all the attention, but ROOT 2 CAUSED THE ACTUAL 41-ROW LOSS in hy6.16. Root 1 governs whether the diagnosis is right; root 2 governs whether anyone ever hears it.

PROPERTY: a graph whose fitness for (repo, branch, commit) has not been established cannot produce an answer indistinguishable from one produced by a graph whose fitness has been.

KEY FINDING THAT CHANGES THE COST: Symbol.indexed_at ALREADY EXISTS, is set from one constant per run, threaded through both lanes, and is NOT COALESCE-protected — always overwritten. So per-run attribution needs ZERO schema change and ZERO migration. Edges attribute through their source symbol.

PARTIAL DISAGREEMENT WITH THE 4kg FINDING, recorded honestly: a no-op re-ingest at the SAME commit into an already-fit store is DEFENSIBLE — the store genuinely is fit. The real failure is the COMMIT-ADVANCING case (fitness established at W, run claims to advance to X, contributes nothing, downstream believes it sees X), which needs no threshold since repo_commit_sha is already stamped. The discriminating fixture 4kg needs is the commit-advancing one, not the same-commit one.

SEQUENCING: if only one thing ships, the persisted record + RUNNING marker (root 2) — smaller change, and it is the root that caused the measured loss. Measurement corrections second, EVIDENCE REWRITE ALONGSIDE not after, or e6z regenerates.

REJECTED: staging/atomic-promote (closes only ae5, ~2x a 169-222s ingest, and a validated-empty graph promoted atomically is still empty); per-run delta as a pass/fail RULE (false-alarms on the most common invocation); read-time-only (the diagnosis is only cheap at write time).

OPEN RED THE DESIGN DOES NOT CLOSE, stated rather than hidden: re-ingesting yesterday's .scip at a new commit re-stamps every symbol, so 'this run wrote symbols' passes while the graph holds yesterday's facts. Recording the index sha256 makes it visible to a reader — citation, not prevention.
