title: SPIKE: is tier-3 LM spec-binding cheap and precise at corpus scale?
description:
Raised BY d1l.6, which measured tier 1 and demoted it: section citations reach only 5.6% / 8.0% / 0.3% of exported symbols at N=10 lines (fosite / zitadel-oidc / node-oidc-provider). See docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md and MetaCoding @ 6291449.

With tier 1 demoted from backbone to seed, the epic's coverage now rests on tier 3 (LM-proposed IMPLEMENTS_SPEC bindings). That tier's cost and precision at corpus scale is UNMEASURED — which is the same failure mode d1l.6 just corrected one tier over: a load-bearing claim resting on reputation rather than a number. Measure it before d1l.12 is estimated.

Cheap upside to test in the same pass, also from d1l.6: citations reach 19-21% of Go FILES vs 6-8% of symbols. Propagating from a high-precision citation seed along callees / implementers / file neighbours may beat LM-proposing cold, and is far cheaper.

TO CLOSE: precision and recall of LM-proposed bindings against a held-out ground truth (the ~50 sections fosite's own comments name are the obvious oracle, per d1l.14), a per-KLOC cost figure, and a verdict on seed-propagation vs cold proposal.
notes:
RE-SCOPE 2026-08-04: PROMOTED TO P1 AND WIRED AS A GATE ON d1l.12.

This is the epic's LOAD-BEARING UNKNOWN. With tier 1 demoted to seed (d1l.6) and tier 2 living only in the target repo, coverage of the REFERENCE repos rests entirely on tier 3, and tier 3 has never been measured. That is the same failure mode d1l.6 just corrected one tier over — a load-bearing claim resting on reputation rather than a number — so it gets the same treatment: measure before anyone estimates d1l.12.

NOT BLOCKED ON THE CORPUS, DELIBERATELY. The LM-precision arm can run against raw fosite source plus the d1l.6 citation extractor, both of which exist today; only the seed-propagation arm (callees / implementers / same-file neighbours) needs an indexed graph. Gating this spike behind d1l.2 -> d1l.16 would leave the epic's biggest unknown unmeasured for the longest, which is backwards. If the propagation arm needs a graph before d1l.2 lands, re-index fosite locally out-of-band (scip-go + --load-scip, ~3 min) and SAY SO in the write-up per the sandbox-vs-production reporting rule.

HOLD OUT THE ORACLE. d1l.14 uses fosite's cited sections as ground truth. If this spike seeds propagation from the same citations and then scores itself against them, both numbers are circular. Split the set first and record the split.

FALSIFIABLE VERDICT REQUIRED, and pre-register the threshold this time — d1l.6 records not pre-registering its own as a weakness. Suggested: tier 3 is viable as a backbone only if it binds >=30% of function|method|class symbols at >=80% precision against held-out citations, for a cost under a stated dollars-per-KLOC figure. Below that, d1l.12 takes the seed-scoped v1 (~58 citation-bearing files) and the epic stops claiming corpus-wide spec coverage of the references.

title: Lift the wire-shape helper into the shared store — seven builds have met it
description:
The single most repeated defect of 2026-08-03: SIX instances across five builds of a guard refusing ANY array on a single-cardinality field, where farmOS refuses only at TWO. Measured uniformly across five fields on two entity types: 'x', ['x'], [{value:'x'}] and {value:'x'} are all accepted and unwrapped to one value; [] is accepted and reads back null; ['x','y'] is 422. Also three-state booleans (unmentioned reads false, a stated [] reads null) which a '?? false' materializer silently misreports.

WHY THIS IS A BEAD AND NOT SIX FIXES: every attempt to fix it by review failed, including mine — I fixed it in identity-medical and then REINTRODUCED it in identity-quantity-test with my own patch for the judge finding about it. In identity-birth the CORRECT version (normalizeMother) sat twelve lines below the wrong one (normalizeVet) in the same file. The rule was known and applied inconsistently by every author who knew it. The two builds that got it right (hy6.5 seeding, then hy6.10 group) did so by writing ONE helper and routing every field through it, and in both cases the sweep turned up an ADDITIONAL undeclared narrowing that site-by-site review had missed.

A remembered convention does not survive five parallel authors. Move the rule out of the sites.
acceptance_criteria: One exported wire-shape helper in the wave-1 shared store (unwrap arity-1 spellings, [] is unstated, refuse at >=2 with the boundary's own message; plus the three-state boolean read). Every existing build routes its single-cardinality fields through it — identity-medical, -quantity-test, -birth, -transplanting, -seeding, -group, -animal. Each conversion re-sweeps BOTH axes of every field and declares anything that stays narrow. The next port brief ships the helper rather than the rule.
notes:
hy6.3 birth ALREADY HAS a verify.py (committed 2026-08-03), so two of three are further along than this bead says. Verified independently: mutating an expectation yields DRIFT and exit 1 — a real checker, not a transcript.

BUT a CLEAN run also exits 1, because its cleanup cannot delete every fixture it creates. Cause is this build's own documented finding: a birth naming the child as its own mother makes that asset UNDELETABLE (403, referenced by another entity) until its parent is cleared, and the cleanup does not clear parents first. A script that exits non-zero when nothing is wrong is indistinguishable from one that exits non-zero when something IS wrong — the failure mode one step removed from a checker that cannot fail at all. Fix is a two-line PATCH-parents-then-delete loop.

Remaining: fix birth's cleanup; write checkers for identity-seeding and identity-transplanting. Models are hy6.9 probes.py and hy6.10 verify.py, both mutation-tested by their authors AND independently by me.
IGNORE THE PRECEDING NOTE ON THIS BEAD — it was misfiled. It describes birth's probe-ledger checker and belongs to hy6.27 (ledgers that cannot fail), where it is now recorded. Nothing in it bears on the wire-shape helper. Left in place rather than deleted so the record shows the correction rather than hiding it.
FIXED STRUCTURALLY 2026-08-03 (farmos-port 305c247/dda4e1e/ba10350; bound as wire-arity-is-one-helper in 07c19df). 856 -> 927 tests, 0 fail. Verified: exactly ONE unwrap implementation exists in the repo.
Canonical helper at wave1/shared-store/src/wire.ts. Converted birth, group, seeding, medical, quantity-test, transplanting, animal, land, and the wave-1 shared bridge. medical's assertSingleVet DELETED rather than deprecated - it was the weaker of two guards and the restate path had been reaching for it instead of the real one.

THE CONSOLIDATION EARNED ITS KEEP ON AN AXIS NOBODY WAS WATCHING. Three builds had written this helper independently and THE THREE DISAGREED, holding two LOOSER-than-source defects between them: [['x']] is 422 and {value:{value:'x'}} is 500 at the boundary, yet two builds RECURSED and recorded both; and [] is STATED UNSET rather than UNMENTIONED, which two of three collapsed - erasing the three-state boolean. NEITHER ANCESTOR HAD BOTH ROWS RIGHT. Every prior instance of this bug had been a narrowing, so nobody had looked for a widening. That is the argument for consolidating rather than patching, in one sentence.

SEVEN MORE NARROWINGS, and the two worst were SILENT CORRUPTIONS rather than refusals - worse, because nothing refuses and nothing reports:
1. medical restateVet was a SECOND DOOR: the bridge did String(req.vet), so ['Dr. A','Dr. B'] arrived as the string 'Dr. A,Dr. B', passed the guard, and recorded a vet nobody named - while the record path refused the identical value.
2. The WAVE-1 SHARED BRIDGE did String(test_method), collapsing two instruments into 'a,b' - on the very field whose ADR claimed its function was 'the only place that can put a value in it'. That door was SHARED. Six lab_test string fields had the identical shape.
3. quantity-test filtered empties BEFORE counting, where farmOS counts WIRE ELEMENTS (['Dr A',''] and ['',''] are both 422). ITS OWN TEST ASSERTED THE WIDENING AS IF IT WERE A PROPERTY.
4. The shared bridge dropped a scalar data_streams on the floor, plus six more !Array.isArray -> refuse narrowings (nicknames, id_tag x2, groups, children, parents): a bare scalar is a legal arity-1 spelling of a multi-value field.
5. A SEVENTH instance of the six-times defect - animal's is_sterile refused every array. Missed because that field's documented finding was about the three-state READ, so nobody re-checked its ARITY.
6. A second unwrap copy inside seeding's OWN file, eighty lines below the first.
7. land's [] punt settled, and animal's matching guard; messages now match the boundary.

A RULE I BRIEFED WAS WRONG AND THE AGENT CORRECTED IT: I said '[] accepted even on a REQUIRED field'. True only of birth's name, which DERIVES from a name_pattern; on a required field that derives nothing, land_type:[] is 422 'This value should not be null.' My fourth over-generalisation of the day. It changes nothing in the helper, and that is the design - the unwrap says 'stated unset' and the CALLER'S required check refuses the null.

MUTATION COUNTS, 15 mutations: refuse-any-array 89, ceiling-at-three 33, []-collapses 5, ?? false 3, recurse-nested 6, unwrapList-drops-scalar 3, {value:x}-stops-unwrapping 28, String(test_method) 3, drops-scalar-data_streams 1, String(lot_number) 1, empty-stops-winning 2, dedupe-in-field 1, asAct-nesting 2, splitLogFields-drift 3, no-act-id 10. Baseline and restore 0 throughout.
THE MUTATION PASS CAUGHT THE WORK OUT TWICE: reintroducing the shared bridge's String(test_method) - the sweep's best finding - BROKE NO TEST, because the bridge had no test seam at all (its dispatch was a closure inside runBridge). That fix had shipped with no evidence. And one mutation reported '0 fail' only because its replacement string had wrong indentation and SILENTLY DID NOT APPLY - the mirror of a checker that cannot fail. Both now assert the anchor matched. Written into iteration-methodology.md.

title: spine-asset folds archive MONOTONICALLY, and the boundary says reversible
description: port_runs/wave2/spine-asset/build/shared-store/src/store.ts:275 folds assetActive as 'any asset_archived event => inactive', one-way. MEASURED 2026-08-03 (hy6.2 probes P34/P36): PATCH archived:true then archived:false both return 200, the asset is active again, and last_archived is cleared. Bound as asset-archive-reversible (farmos-port 05ce635). The shipped fold cannot express a state the source reaches, and every test of the monotonic behaviour passes. spine-asset's own punt spine-asset-archive-monotonic pre-authorised this: 'continuity with the established spine, not a fresh decision. A fixture asserting un-archive would reverse it (add a latest-wins status kind).' That fixture now exists. FOURTH instance of the same shape in one day - an unmeasured assumption inherited as continuity, shipped, then contradicted on first boundary contact (the others: term delete permitted where farmOS refuses, term parent modeled single where farmOS accepts many, and the quick/category union assumption). The pattern is not carelessness: continuity is INVISIBLE IN CODE REVIEW, because a fold that matches the previous fold looks correct by construction.
acceptance_criteria: assetActive folds the LATEST archive statement, not the existence of an archive event; un-archive clears last_archived; a regression test asserts archive -> unarchive -> archive and would fail against the monotonic fold. The wave-1 asset spine that spine-asset inherited this from is checked for the same fold and fixed or explicitly scoped out.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-04 (farmos-port d0bb62e). 933/933 green. This was the last thing in the tree we KNEW was wrong.
THE DEFECT: assetActive folded MONOTONICALLY - any asset_archived event ever appended meant inactive forever - so the store could not express a state the source reaches. Measured on THREE bundles (animal/hy6.2, then land and group by a fresh judge): PATCH archived:true then archived:false both return 200, the asset is active again, last_archived is cleared. Reversal is asset-WIDE, not bundle-specific.
FIXED IN WAVE-1 TOO, which this bead's AC asked me to check and which turned out to carry the IDENTICAL fold - spine-asset inherited it from there. Fixing only the build that was filed would have left the ancestor to hand the same defect to the next spine that copies it, which is the mechanism that produced this in the first place.
THE SHAPE: archive is now a latest-wins register over an append-only log. asset_unarchived is a registered kind in both registries; the fold takes the LATEST statement; lastArchivedAt is DERIVED from the winning statement rather than stored, which is what makes the clear automatic instead of something a future author has to remember.
EVIDENCE, mutation-tested rather than assumed: reverting assetActive to the monotonic fold fails exactly two of the six new tests - the reversibility row and the view row (the others exercise lastArchivedAt, which the mutation did not touch). The anchor was ASSERTED before the mutation applied, per the lesson added the day before that a mutation which silently fails to apply reports 'the suite cannot catch this' - the mirror of a checker that cannot fail.
CONTROLS, because 'latest wins' must not degenerate into 'any statement toggles': un-archiving something never archived is a no-op; archiving twice stays archived; and the event history is asserted INTACT, since reversibility is a latest-wins READ over an append-only log and never a mutation. Also a test that assetView agrees with the fold - a build that fixed the fold and left the view reading its own copy would pass every other test.
THE PUNT IS MARKED RESOLVED, NOT DELETED. spine-asset-archive-monotonic named its own falsifier ('a fixture asserting un-archive would reverse it, add a latest-wins status kind') and was right that this was CONTINUITY rather than a decision. That is precisely why it survived a build and a review: a fold that matches the previous fold looks correct by construction, and only the boundary disagrees. Fourth instance of that pattern in two days.

title: The homeless cross-cutting base fields need one home store (quick, category)
description: farmOS injects base fields onto EVERY log and asset via hook_entity_base_field_info: farm_quick's 'quick' (asset+log) and farm_log_category's 'category' (log). Both are now DECIDED (quick-provenance, log-category-membership — both LWW wholesale) and NEITHER can be built, because there is no store that owns 'a log' or 'an asset' generally. spine-asset has a shared SpineAssetStore and spine-taxonomy-a has a shared TaxonomyTermStore, but logs are per-build (spine-log-maintenance, identity-sensor, identity-equipment-log, ...), so a base field on all logs has nowhere to live that is not one feature's private store. Putting it in a feature store is the wrong answer twice over: it is invisible to the other log builds, and it makes a cross-cutting fold owned by whichever feature happened to be built first.
acceptance_criteria: A home is chosen for cross-cutting injected base fields and both quick and category are built into it, on their bound decisions. The choice is recorded as a decision, not an accident of which build got there first. Closing this also closes the MEASURED gap in TaxonomyTermStore: a term referenced only by a log's category field deletes in the port and 403s in the source (observed 2026-08-03), because the term store cannot see log references.
notes:
TERMINOLOGY, because it caused real confusion 2026-08-03: a farmOS 'log' is a DOMAIN RECORD (log/observation, log/harvest, log/seeding, log/medical...), not a telemetry line. There is no Loki, no log shipping, no central sink and nothing to flush when connectivity returns — these are farmer-entered records that live in the local event-sourced store and sync like any other data. 'Log-owning store' means 'the store that owns the harvest-record entity'.

Scope grew 2026-08-03: this bead now also carries the ACT ID that quick-provenance (superseded to immutable act attribution) and composite-act-atomicity both need. Every event carries the id of the act that produced it; attribution is derived from the log rather than stored in a client-writable field, and it covers everything the act touched — including the quantities and terms farmOS structurally cannot stamp. So the home store must own: (1) the injected cross-cutting fields quick + category, (2) the act id on every event, (3) EventLog.appendAll as the only composite-write path (MetaCoding 4bc9d6c).
DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-03 by Duke (farmos-port 064b4b2). 856/856 green. Bound as cross-cutting-fields-have-one-home.

NOT A STORAGE QUESTION, and the bead's framing invited that reading twice. This port is event-sourced: there is exactly ONE event log and no table decision exists. The question was where fields farmOS staples onto entities FROM OUTSIDE (hook_entity_base_field_info) are allowed to live, when our builds are per-feature and the log builds never got a shared store the way spine-asset and spine-taxonomy-a did.

IT HAD ALREADY BECOME THE HOME BY ACCRETION. LogExtras had grown to FOURTEEN keys across lab_test, input, harvest, medical and seeding — and I APPROVED THE LAST TWO MYSELF that morning without noticing what the bag was turning into. Two of the fourteen (isMovement, locationIds) are base fields on EVERY log; the other twelve are one bundle's payload. Both kinds shared one optional interface, so nothing could tell a builder which kind they were adding. That is precisely the 'owned by whichever build got there first' failure this bead was filed to prevent, arriving through a side door I waved through.

THREE THINGS, NOW DISTINGUISHABLE:
  LogBaseFields - is_movement, location, category, quick. Every log has them.
  LogExtras     - vet, the lab* set, lotNumber. One bundle's payload. EXTENDS the above.
  the act id    - neither. It rides the EVENT, via asAct(), with eventsOfAct() answering 'what did this act touch?' from the log itself.

The split is a TYPE-LEVEL STATEMENT rather than a migration: LogExtras extends LogBaseFields so every existing reader keeps working and the suite stayed green. Moving call sites is mechanical and can follow. A big-bang migration would have been risk without an additional decision.

THE ACT ID is what quick-provenance (superseded to immutable act attribution) and composite-act-atomicity both needed. Carrying it on the EVENT is what makes it unrewritable — the source's quick is a client-writable register MEASURED to be clearable by any API client — and what lets attribution reach the quantities and taxonomy terms farmOS structurally cannot stamp, because it follows the event rather than a field injected onto two entity types. asAct keeps NESTED calls inside the outer act, so a helper that records on its own cannot silently split one act in two and make atomicity and attribution disagree about what 'one act' means.

SIX TESTS, including the ones that discriminate: two separate acts get DIFFERENT ids (a per-store id would pass the naive same-id test forever), a nested act does not start a second, and events emitted outside an act do not inherit one. Plus attribution reaching a quantity — the shape farmOS leaves unanswerable.

UNBLOCKS hy6.13's field-injection clause and the five quick/* builds (hy6.17-21), all decided-but-unbuildable until now. REMAINING under this bead: migrate the existing call sites onto the split, and actually build quick + category into LogBaseFields — the home now exists, the two fields are declared, and the semantics were bound earlier today.
FINISHED 2026-08-03 (farmos-port 305c247/dda4e1e/ba10350). 927/927 green.
category BUILT as decided, all four limbs measured INCLUDING THE TWO THAT DISCRIMINATE: PATCH [A] over [A,B] -> 1 entry (wholesale replace), and PATCH [] -> 0 entries (EMPTY WINS, so not a GSet). A GSet and an LwwRegister agree on every ADD, so additions alone could never have told them apart - that is the discriminating pair, and it is the same trap that made GSet look right for nicknames and quick. [A,A] -> 2 entries, duplicate-preserving as bound. New shared kind log_category_restated, isLog:false.
quick BUILT as the supersession says: carried verbatim, NO restatement verb, and THE ABSENCE IS EXECUTED AS A TEST (registry.has('log_quick_restated') === false, verified to discriminate). Measured that PATCH quick:[] clears it from any client - which is exactly why the port's real answer to 'what created this?' is the event's act id and not this field.
CALL SITES MIGRATED: LOG_BASE_FIELD_KEYS + splitLogFields + logFields(id) + a baseFields param on recordLog; seeding's isMovement/locationIds moved out of the payload bag. NO EVENT SHAPE CHANGED (asserted). asAct now wraps seeding's recording, birth's recordBirth/correctBirth/setBirthStatus, and the shared record_log op; nesting-stays-in-outer-act and act-closes-on-throw both asserted.
OPEN, deliberately not generalised: whether [] on a required field with a DEFAULT (rather than a derivation) behaves like name or like land_type - not sampled. And the three-state DEFAULT differs per field (is_sterile unmentioned -> NULL, is_location/is_movement -> false), each measured on its own field rather than inherited.
This unblocks hy6.13's field-injection clause and the five quick/* builds (hy6.17-21), which were decided-but-unbuildable for want of a home.
close_reason: Closed

title: bring-up.sh must enable the quick modules — the oracle cannot see the quick forms
description:
BLOCKS hy6.17-.21 (all five quick/* identity ports): their observe step cannot run.

MEASURED 2026-08-02 on the digest-pinned oracle: drush pm:list --filter=quick reports farm_quick, farm_quick_birth, farm_quick_group, farm_quick_inventory, farm_quick_movement and farm_quick_planting ALL DISABLED. bring-up.sh never enables them. A probe of the 'quick' base field at /api returned 422 'The attribute quick does not exist on the asset--equipment resource type' — that was the MODULE being absent, not the field being internal, so the probe measured the oracle and not farmOS.

ALSO BLOCKS the gating unknown on hy6.12: whether 'quick' is wholesale-replaceable at the JSON:API boundary. That question has now been answered wrongly twice by static source reading (see docs/design/composite-fold-question.md, claim A2) and must be settled by observation.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE EDIT: farm_quick's FieldHooks::entityBaseFieldInfo injects a base field onto EVERY asset and log. Enabling it changes the JSON:API surface every pack is recorded against.

DO IT PROPERLY: (1) add the six modules to bring-up.sh's drush en list — never by hand on the running container, or the oracle stops matching its own source of truth; (2) re-verify reproduction by re-recording port_runs/lexicon-bind/location/location-flows.json and confirming all TEN fixture ids still match sealed pack f3460165d338da4c6043262a05bd3a99 (verified matching on 2026-08-02 BEFORE this change, so a mismatch after is attributable); (3) only then run the quick observe passes. If reproduction breaks, this is a re-baseline and not an extension, and it needs Duke's call.
close_reason:
bring-up.sh now enables farm_quick + the five form modules as its own step, with the why and the risk recorded inline. Enabled on the live oracle 2026-08-02.

EXTENSION, NOT RE-BASELINE — measured, with the BEFORE recorded first so drift would be attributable: sealed pack f3460165d338 (10 fixture ids) vs re-record BEFORE enabling vs re-record AFTER enabling — all three IDENTICAL and in order. The 43 packs still reproduce with a base field newly injected onto every asset and log.

AND IT SETTLED THE GATING QUESTION ON hy6.12. With the module enabled, 'quick' is exposed at /api and: PATCH ['inventory'] -> 200; PATCH ['planting'] -> 200 and 'inventory' is GONE; PATCH [] -> 200, clearable; PATCH ['b','a','c'] -> 200, arbitrary order. It is a LAST-WRITER-WINS multi-value register, NOT grow-only, NOT a GSet — the judge was right and my GSet claim is dead. The primitive is element 3 (lww.ts). My earlier 422 probe is withdrawn: it measured the module being absent, not the field being internal.

METHODOLOGICAL FINDING worth carrying: 'is a multiple => TRUE farmOS field grow-only?' has now been answered WRONGLY TWICE by static source reading (nicknames -> ci2, which is why GSet is unbound; and quick here) and CORRECTLY TWICE by one cheap boundary PATCH. For this field shape, source reading is not evidence.

Commit fc81c0e. hy6.17-.21 are unblocked for observe.

title: FarmOS2 needs its own bun harness: 45 build test files import MetaCoding's kernel by relative path
description: BLOCKS deleting eval/ctkr/{port_runs,results} from MetaCoding. Found 2026-07-30 by watching the bun count, not by reading code: deleting the in-repo ledger dropped 'bun test' from 704 tests / 79 files to 414 / 34 — 290 tests across 45 files silently stopped running. They are the PORT BUILDS' own suites (wave2 spine + identity, wave1 shared-store), and they import MetaCoding's kernel by relative path: 'from "../../../../../../src/kernel/index.ts"', which only resolved while the ledger sat inside MetaCoding. In FarmOS2 those paths dangle and 'bun test' errors; in MetaCoding they are gone. So the naive move leaves 290 tests unrunnable in BOTH repos while every suite still reports green — exactly the 'green tick that measures nothing' this bead's own notes warned about. The deletion was reverted; MetaCoding holds a mirror copy again (its port.toml stays deleted, so FarmOS2 remains authoritative and MetaCoding's pytest reads the sibling via the search path). Duke's framing points at the fix: the build is the app and should not be married to the instrumentation — so the kernel needs to be a real dependency (published/linked package, or workspace protocol) rather than a relative climb out of the tree.
acceptance_criteria: FarmOS2 has its own bun harness (package.json + tsconfig) and 'bun test' there runs all 45 build suites green, with the kernel consumed as a declared dependency rather than a ../../.. path; MetaCoding's bun count after the ledger is deleted is explained term by term (which tests moved where), not merely observed to be smaller; only then is eval/ctkr/{port_runs,results} deleted.
close_reason: FarmOS2 has its own bun harness: package.json (@metacoding/kernel as a file: dep) + tsconfig.json; bun test there is 293 pass / 0 fail across 46 files, of which 290/45 are exactly the suites that had gone dark. MetaCoding side: src/kernel is a real package, resolved via a bun workspace symlink (tsconfig paths were shadowed by the builds' nested tsconfigs); bun 704/79 unchanged, pytest exit 0 / 1156 collected. Two mutation-verified gates in FarmOS2 test/kernel-pin.test.ts: no relative specifier may escape the repo root (byte-level scan, asserts >100 files scanned so an empty sweep cannot pass), and the resolved kernel must match kernel.pin.json (1.3.0 / 0335ef15) — closing the staleness hole bun's file: COPY semantics opened. Commits: MetaCoding bb66e82, FarmOS2 e8b16a1, both pushed. Step 5 (deleting eval/ctkr/{port_runs,results}) remains blocked on the synthetic-fixture question, not on this.

title: DESIGN: instrument / lens / source / ledger separation — kill the path-flag proliferation
description: Duke, 2026-07-29: per-command paths + METACODING_PORT_WORKSPACE are a code smell, not a fix. Design elicitation written to docs/design/instrument-lens-source.md. Diagnosis: a PORT has no identity in the system — only four separately-addressed piles (source / lens / ledger / build), so every artifact earns another flag (44 commands, 7 path-ish flags, now 1 env var). Fix has two halves: (a) make the port a first-class self-describing entity with a port.toml discovered by walking up from cwd, so paths become facts the port knows rather than arguments; (b) invert the dependency arrow so a lens depends on ctkr and ctkr NEVER imports a lens. Measured: the entire code-level coupling is ONE import (recorder.py:32) plus one hardcoded choices=['farmos'] (oracle_verify.py:34) — the instrument is already almost clean; what is dirty is physical location and test-fixture dependence.
acceptance_criteria: Boundary is MEASURED not declared: the instrument ships a synthetic toy target its own tests run against (today ctkr's tests use farmOS core-pack/hardening-pack, so farmOS cannot leave without gutting the suite), and a fitness test fails if farmos|drupal|farm_ appears in ctkr/ctkr/** or src/** outside changelogs. port.toml carries the source pin, and anything under [cache] is reconstructible from source+ledger by one command. The decisions-registry path stays fixed WITHIN the workspace — only the root is discovered — so a port cannot nominate the file that grades it (port_contract INVARIANT 2).

title: taxonomy/log_category identity completion: category field injection + LogCategorize union semantics
description: Unfiled BIG-PUNT from ff714c4, dropped for six days. taxonomy/log_category shipped SHELL-ONLY in spine-taxonomy-a because the real behaviour is identity-tier: (w2-taxa-lc-1) log_category injects a multi-valued 'category' entity_reference field onto EVERY log entity — cross-family, belongs to a log-owning store, not a taxonomy store; (w2-taxa-lc-2) the LogCategorize bulk action with append/replace union semantics, flagged as a candidate kernel primitive (union-or-replace collection register). Until this lands, the spine claim 'taxonomy/log_category is ported' is a shell.
acceptance_criteria: Field injection lives in the log-owning store, not the taxonomy store; union-vs-replace semantics observed against the live oracle before being chosen; the union-or-replace register either becomes a kernel decision or is explicitly declined with a reason.
notes:
OBSERVED + DECIDED 2026-08-03 (farmos-port de50b2a). Evidence: results/wave2/log-category-observation-2026-08-03.md, probe results/wave2/probe_hy613.py. Probe created and deleted its own terms+log; zero hy613-* left on the oracle.

AC clause 2 (union-vs-replace OBSERVED before being chosen) — MET, and the ordering earned its keep:
  PATCH [A]->[A]; [B]->[B] with A GONE; []->[] ; [C,A,B]->[C,A,B] order held; [A,A]->[A,A] NOT DEDUPED.
The [A,A] result is what source reading would have missed: array_unique lives in the ACTION (LogCategorizeActionForm:167-175), NOT in the field. A port that deduped the register would be STRICTER THAN ITS SOURCE — the same shape as the single-parent term store just fixed in hy6.14.

AC clause 3 (kernel decision or explicit decline) — MET, DECLINED. The union-or-replace collection register (w2-taxa-lc-2) is NOT added to the kernel. Three independently fatal reasons: (1) the register underneath is measured latest-wins, so append is a client-side read-modify-write and the kernel models convergence, not mutators; (2) a union register would CHANGE CONVERGENCE — two concurrent appends merge, where farmOS does two wholesale writes and the later wins, silently losing the earlier addition (divergence in the looks-like-an-improvement direction, on the exact axis the kernel exists to pin); (3) it would bake in dedup, contradicted by [A,A].

Bound as log-category-membership, three verbs over one register: category_restate (LwwRegister<readonly Handle[]>), log_categorize(append) = array_unique(array_merge(existing, submitted)) then wholesale write, log_categorize(replace) = same with existing empty. No sanctions — the port matches.

FOUR FOR FOUR: nicknames (ci2), quick (hy6.12), term parent (hy6.14), category (here). Four farmOS 'multiple => TRUE' fields, four latest-wins-wholesale answers, zero unions. GSet still unbound. The next such field should be ASSUMED LWW and measured to confirm, not argued from the writers.

BONUS, and it strengthens hy6.14: the term-delete-refusal known limit is no longer inferred. DELETE of a term referenced ONLY by a log's category field -> 403; control (unreferenced term) -> 204. The gap in the shipped TaxonomyTermStore is real, sized and located.

AC clause 1 (field injection lives in the log-owning store) — NOT MET, and it is not a coding task. There IS no log-owning store: spine-asset shares SpineAssetStore and spine-taxonomy-a shares TaxonomyTermStore, but logs are per-build, so a base field on ALL logs has nowhere to live that is not one feature's private store. Identical homelessness to 'quick'. Filed as MetaCoding-hy6.23 (P1) for both fields at once — putting either in a feature store would be wrong twice: invisible to the other log builds, and a cross-cutting fold owned by whichever build got there first. hy6.13 stays OPEN on that clause.
CLAUSE 1 MET + w2-taxa-lc-2 BUILT, 2026-08-07 (farmos-port 9662b7b).

Clause 1 was blocked on hy6.23, which landed 2026-08-03: 'category' is a base field in the shared LOG store (port_runs/wave1/shared-store), declared in LogBaseFields, NOT in the taxonomy store. category_restate was already built there. What was still missing is the second half of the identity — the LogCategorize bulk action.

BUILT NOW, and it turned up something source reading usually loses rather than gains: REPLACE DEDUPLICATES AND THE CLIENT PATCH DOES NOT. The action runs array_unique(array_merge(existing, submitted)) with existing empty in replace mode, and array_unique of a list is still array_unique. So:
    recategorize(log, [A,A])          -> [A,A]   (MEASURED at the boundary, 2026-08-03)
    categorize(log, [A,A], 'replace') -> [A]     (the action)
Same list, two verbs, two answers. Collapsing them would report a list the farm does not hold — the hy6.14 shape one level over. append also puts EXISTING FIRST: [A,B] onto [B] gives [B,A], not [A,B] or [B,A,B].

The mutator-not-convergence-rule claim is now FIXTURED rather than only argued: two concurrent appends computed from the same 'before' do not merge; the later wholesale write wins and the earlier addition is lost, as farmOS does. That is the direct evidence for declining the union-or-replace kernel primitive.

Seven fixtures, each half of a discriminating pair. Mutation-tested: removing the dedup and ignoring the mode flag each fail exactly the fixtures stating those rules. 940 tests pass.

WHY THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN: the ACTION's semantics are TRANSCRIBED FROM SOURCE, not observed. farmOS's LogCategorize is a Drupal Action plugin driven from the UI and the oracle's JSON:API index advertises no way to invoke it. The 2026-08-03 probe measured the REGISTER, which is how [A,A] became known — and this bead's own notes say the [A,A] result is what source reading would have missed. So the dedup claim rests on LogCategorizeActionForm:167-175 and is marked as such in the code. To close: either find a boundary route to the action (VBO endpoint, /api action, drush) and measure it, or record it as an explicitly source-derived divergence.
CLOSED 2026-08-07 (farmos-port 181302e). NO DIVERGENCE NEEDED — Duke authorised one and the port did not require it: it agrees with the source on every measurement.

THE REASON IT HAD NEVER BEEN MEASURED IS ITSELF THE FINDING. The Action plugin LogCategorize WRITES NOTHING — executeMultiple stashes the selected entities in a private tempstore and redirects to a confirm form. The append/replace switch, the array_unique and the wholesale rewrite all live in LogCategorizeActionForm::submitForm. So 'invoke the action' measures nothing, and JSON:API does not reach the form. That is why the 2026-08-03 probe could only reach the register.

MEASURED by populating the tempstore exactly as executeMultiple does and submitting the REAL form through Drupal's own FormBuilder against real entities, reading back with loadUnchanged. One layer below JSON:API, which is the layer the behaviour lives at — stated as such, not dressed up as a boundary probe. Seven results in results/wave2/log-categorize-action-measurement-2026-08-07.md, script kept as results/wave2/probe_hy613_action.php. Fixtures hy613m-*, deleted by ID in-run, zero left and re-verified on the oracle afterwards.

  M1 replace [A,A]            -> [A]     the ACTION dedups
  M5 direct field write [A,A] -> [A,A]   the REGISTER does not
  M3 existing [B], append [A,B] -> [B,A] existing first
  M6 append []  -> keeps      M7 replace [] -> clears
  M2 the select's [A=>A] shape -> [A]

M1 against M5 in ONE RUN is the dedup-lives-in-the-action claim measured rather than read — on the exact field where reading already failed this project once ([A,A]).

M1 against M2 settles something the reading raised: Drupal's #multiple select normalises to [value=>value], so a duplicate collapses in the value callback before submitForm runs. Both shapes still give [A], so array_unique is load-bearing on its own.

ALL THREE CLAUSES NOW MET. Clause 1 via hy6.23's shared LOG store (category in LogBaseFields, not the taxonomy store) plus SharedLogStore.categorize; clause 2 measured 2026-08-03 and now again for the action; clause 3 declined with reasons, and the mutator-not-convergence-rule half is FIXTURED — two concurrent appends do not merge, the later wholesale write wins.

The bound decision's 'NOT YET BUILT' clause was false and is AMENDED in place in both cm-decisions.jsonl and kernelConfig.ts, kept as history. The mirror test caught them out of sync when only one was edited.

Recorded as a SURFACE difference, not a semantic one: the port's log_categorize accepts any list where farmOS's is reachable only through a form whose selector cannot express a duplicate. M1 shows the computed result is identical either way.

NOT ESTABLISHED, in the doc: access control (ran as user 1, so the inaccessible-entity branch never fired), multi-entity submits, the HTTP form path. 941 tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: IDENTITY port: organization/farm — full recipe (mine -> observe -> decide -> build -> read)
description: TIERED UP by the 2026-07-22 amendment under structure blindness: cross-cutting farm-scoping constraints (vocab_new 0). Was originally spine-misc. Full identity recipe per the hy6 play. Source: /private/tmp/farmos-cell3-2026-07-19/farm-src/modules/organization/farm.
acceptance_criteria: Oracle surface declared and any new term taken through add-term --apply -> implement against the live boundary -> refine authority -> sealed pack -> bind-term; blind build against the sealed pack; fresh judge (never the builder) proves which tree it tested; adversary variants with ONE rule flipped each, every bug caught by exactly the fixture stating its rule.
notes:
PATH CORRECTION (2026-07-28): the source path in this description, /private/tmp/farmos-cell3-2026-07-19/farm-src, is DEAD — macOS's /tmp cleaner took every file and left the directory skeleton. Durable pristine clone: /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/farmos-src @ 3fe0ce7e23de807be9b8bc97a211ce934327db39 (farmOS 4.0.4) — the exact build all 43 sealed packs were recorded against. Read-only always.
BLOCKED 2026-08-07 on an oracle module, caught by the gate that exists for this (hy6.25 preflight) BEFORE any probing.

organization--farm is NOT advertised by the oracle's /api index (44 types, none of them organization--*). Probing anyway is exactly hy6.29's failure: 404s and 422s that read as findings about farmOS and are measurements of the ORACLE. The recipe forbids a source-read-only build.

Needs farm_organization + farm_farm. DECLARED, COMMENTED OUT, in ctkr/ctkr/oracle/bring-up.sh with the reason, because this is a RE-BASELINE decision and not a bring-up step: farm_farm is not an additive bundle, it installs four CROSS-CUTTING validation constraints (AssetParentFarm, LogAssetFarm, AssetMovementFarm, AssetGroupAssignmentFarm) that fire on entities other builds own and change how asset and log writes validate for EVERY bundle. That is the same cross-cutting property that tiered this bead up to a full identity port. The 43 sealed packs were recorded against a 126-module set without it.

DUKE'S CALL. If enabled: uncomment, re-run bring-up (do not hand-enable — the preflight's drift check compares against that file), then re-run the affected ledgers rather than assume the constraints changed nothing.

The other six remaining identity ports (hy6.13, .17-.21) all preflight OK — only this one is blocked.

Side effect worth knowing: writing the commented declaration is what surfaced MetaCoding-02c live. The preflight parsed the commented drush en as a declaration and failed 'declared-but-not-enabled', which blocked every port until fixed.
UNBLOCKED 2026-08-07. The module was never missing from the source — modules/organization/farm is right there, four validators and the organization type. It was not ENABLED on the oracle.

Enabled: drush en -y organization farm_farm, AFTER uncommenting the bring-up.sh declaration so the drift check compares against a file that already agreed. (First attempt used 'farm_organization', which is not a module — farm_farm.info.yml depends on 'farm:organization'.)

MEASURED rather than assumed: module set 126 -> 128, /api index 44 -> 46 types, and asset--animal now carries 'farm' in its relationships, so it is a real change to the asset shape. All four hardened ledgers re-run: birth, seeding, transplanting (94/44), group — every one exit 0, unchanged.

The validators are inert for now, and the source says why: LogAssetFarmValidator violates only when a log references assets from MORE THAN ONE farm, and with no farm organizations created that list is always empty. They will start biting once the port creates farms and assigns assets — which is what this bead is about.

Recorded honestly: the ledgers do not assert asset relationship key sets, so a REAL change to asset--* moved none of them. They would not have caught it. That is a gap in the ledgers, not evidence of safety.

organization--farm now preflights OK. Ready for the full recipe: mine -> observe -> decide -> build -> read.
OBSERVE + DECIDE DONE 2026-08-07 (farmos-port 2a63288). ADR: results/wave2/adr/hy6.11-farm-organization.md. Ledger: port_runs/wave2/identity-farm-org/observe/verify.py.

FIRST LEDGER BUILT ON tools/ledger.py — every guard the 2026-08-04 judge had to find one at a time arrives by construction. 26 rows, 15 value expectations over 14 fixtures, clean on two consecutive runs. Mutation-tested: section deleted / expect= dropped / unchecked row added, all three DETECTED.

THE FINDING, and my hypothesis was refuted by the boundary before I built on it: UNASSIGNED IS A VALUE, NOT A WILDCARD. I expected an unset farm to be permissive — the rules being about DIFFERING farms — and a child with no farm under a parent that has one is REFUSED (422, 'Assets must be in the same farm as their parents'). The source says why exactly: LogAssetFarmValidator pushes the literal id 0 for an asset with no farm, so it is a first-class member of the set array_unique counts. A port modelling null as matches-anything would ACCEPT writes farmOS refuses — the looser-than-source direction, same family as hy6.14's term store and hy6.13's [A,A].

CONSEQUENCE that was invisible until a fixture hit it: a log's LOCATION is a referenced asset, so moving a farm-scoped animal onto UNASSIGNED land is refused by LogAssetFarm before immobility is ever reached. A farm-scoped world must assign its land too.

The two immobility rules are SEPARATE: G3 refuses with 'group assignment logs', not 'movement logs'. Collapsing them into one has-history check would pass a suite that only exercised one.

STILL TO DO: the BUILD half (a farm-scoped store fold + its fixtures). The decision is recorded and the ledger re-runs clean, so the build has a checker waiting for it.

IT FOUND AN AMBIGUITY IN MY BOUND ROW AND DERIVED THE MISSING HALF rather than picking a side. An ambiguous decision is worse than a wrong one: either choice looks confirmed to whoever picks it.
IT RE-MEASURED THE JUDGE'S DEFECT RATHER THAN TAKING IT ON REPORT, and found two things the judge did not have: a one-element array holding 256 characters answers the LENGTH message not the cardinality one, so the ceiling applies to the UNWRAPPED value and a guard checking length first would be wrong in the opposite direction; and `mother` is a RELATIONSHIP, a different wire shape whose answer could not be inherited from the attribute case - measured separately, matches.
IT CLOSED ITS OWN UNFALSIFIABLE-GATE REPORT with a test seam and a mutation test rather than leaving the honest note. Deleting the passesGate calls now fails a test.
DECLARED COST OF PROJECTING, one cause three readings: a COPY is stale between saves AND outlives the record it came from; a projection is neither. Sharpest case - a child REMOVED from a birth log keeps a birth date and parent in farmOS from a record that no longer claims it, orphaned and unexplainable by any later read. The port stops answering while the act's chain stays readable. All three differences are READS, so nothing is refused.

THE BRIDGE WAS DOING THE SAME DAMAGE MORE QUIETLY: String(req.name) turned an array into 'a,b' before any guard could see it — not a narrowing but a SILENT CORRUPTION, worse, because nothing refuses and nothing reports.

W14 IS A ROW THE AGENT GOT WRONG AND ITS OWN LEDGER CAUGHT: it expected name:[] -> 422 because name is required. It is 201 — an empty array is UNSTATED even on a required field, and the name then derives. ADR corrected to the measurement rather than the probe being dropped.

title: RFC ingestion lane: rfc-editor XML -> SpecSection nodes with RFC 2119 levels
description: Start with RFCs - they are machine-readable (rfc-editor.org publishes XML, RFC 7991 v3) and well-structured. Extract section id/number/title/text/url, plus RFC 2119 keyword detection per section. Handle obsoletes/updates so status is accurate. OIDC Core is HTML-with-anchors and less regular - separate task, do NOT assume one parser serves both.
notes:
PROMOTED TO P1 2026-08-04 (re-scope after d1l.6 + d1l.7). Unaffected by both spikes and now on the critical path: d1l.10 and d1l.13 both need SpecSection nodes to bind to, and nothing about RFC ingestion depends on citation density or the Go lane. Do it early.

THE INGESTION LIST IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. d1l.6 counted which specs the reference implementations actually cite (docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md §2), and it does not match the epic's list:

 • ON THE EPIC'S LIST AND HEAVILY CITED: RFC 6749 (fosite 21 sections, zitadel 4, node 2), OIDC Core (zitadel 16, fosite 4), RFC 8628 device flow (zitadel 4), RFC 7662 introspection (fosite 3), RFC 9700 (node 2), RFC 8705 (node 3).
 • NOT ON THE EPIC'S LIST AND CITED ANYWAY — INGEST THESE: RFC 6819 (OAuth threat model; fosite cites SEVEN sections of it) and RFC 3986 (URI comparison; four sections, and redirect-URI comparison is a real correctness hazard in a port). RFC 8252 §7.3 also appears.
 • ON THE LIST BUT NEVER CITED WITH A SECTION: RFC 7519 and RFC 8414 appear at doc level only. Ingest them, but do not expect the citation seed to reach them.
 • node-oidc-provider's top-cited spec is OpenID4VCI (9 sections) — out of scope for this epic; do not ingest it just to make node's numbers look better.

 • VERSIONING GOTCHA: citations point at OIDC-Core-errata2 as well as plain OIDC-Core. Section ids must survive errata revisions, or two spellings of one section will look like two sections in every coverage query.

title: SpecSection node table + IMPLEMENTS_SPEC / TESTS_SPEC / CITES_SPEC / SPEC_REFERENCES edges
description:
Schema per docs/design/spec-anchored-porting.md section 4. SpecSection gets its own table rather than another Symbol.kind - it is a genuinely different kind of thing. IMPLEMENTS_SPEC carries confidence + source (citation|annotation|lm|manual) so the epistemology charter's provenance discipline applies unchanged.

requirement_level (RFC 2119 MUST/SHOULD/MAY) is the field that makes coverage meaningful: '78% of sections covered' is noise, '3 MUST-level sections unimplemented' is a release gate.
notes:
PROMOTED TO P1 2026-08-04 (re-scope after d1l.6 + d1l.7). Neither spike touched this bead's assumptions — schema is orthogonal to citation density and to the Go lane — and that is exactly why it moves to the front: it is now the widest-fan-out unblocked item in the epic (d1l.10, d1l.11 and d1l.13 all wait on it), and it is the one piece of the critical path no measurement can invalidate.

TWO SCHEMA CONSEQUENCES THE SPIKES DID CREATE:

1. IMPLEMENTS_SPEC.source NEEDS A 'propagated' VALUE. d1l.6's cheapest upside is structural propagation from a high-precision citation seed along callees / implementers / same-file neighbours (citations reach 19-21% of Go FILES vs 6-8% of symbols). Propagated edges are neither 'citation' (nobody wrote them) nor 'lm' (no model proposed them) and must not be confused with either — they carry the seed's authority attenuated by graph distance. Enum becomes citation | annotation | propagated | lm | manual, and a propagated edge should record the seed edge it descended from plus the hop count, or its confidence is unauditable.

2. TESTS_SPEC's SOURCE CHANGED. It will be populated from OIDF conformance-suite naming, NOT from mining the reference repos' tests (14 section citations across 65k lines of test code in all three repos combined — d1l.6 §2). source='conformance-suite' is a distinct provenance from anything Symbol-derived, and the FROM side may not be a Symbol in this repo's graph at all. Check that before building the table.

Implement the five elements as a real TS package the fan-out builders consume as FIXED input: (1) frozen event schema + closed event-kind taxonomy (resolving is-a-movement-a-log); (2) client ID + HLC scheme (kills the integer-counter attractor and the 7/7 unanimous punt); (3) ONE kernel-owned pickLatest/LWW comparator keyed on the HLC; (4) status-semantics contract (which projections are status-gated, declared); (5) binding CM-decision registry format consumed from ctkr decisions. Each of the five is ALSO rendered as an elicitation interview doc (ctkr decisions machinery) for Duke — implementation uses recommended picks, marked provisional until Duke resolves. Validation: re-express the 9h5.16 composed store ON the kernel and re-run all 27 fixtures + 5 cross-probes; the ID regression and punts must be structurally impossible (kernel provides the primitives).
close_reason: Shipped+merged: src/kernel/ (events/KindRegistry, ids, hlc, lww, status, decisions; 32 tests) + composed store re-expressed ON the kernel passing verbatim judges 17/17+10/10+5/5 + 5 prevention tests closing every observed failure mode. Five picks implemented and RESOLVED decided-for-me per Duke's blanket authorization (resolution record in docs/design/shared-kernel.md): movement-distinct-kind, replica-scoped ids, HLC total order, single pickLatest, status gates per live oracle; birth-uniqueness bound to earliest-HLC-wins/demote-to-observation. Two product-feel picks flagged for Duke's morning veto (taxonomy, birth-uniqueness).

title: Punt-promotion + decision extraction + agent interrupt protocol
description: Duke 2026-07-20, from the HLC unanimous-punt observation (7/7 builds independently deferred the cross-replica ordering — the kernel requirement EMERGED from deferral patterns). Three mechanisms on the ctkr decisions registry: (1) EXTRACT: 'ctkr decisions extract <build-dir>' collector that mines PORT_DECISIONS.md/ledgers from completed or in-flight builds into the registry (done manually in the 9h5.16 audit — automate it); (2) PUNT-PROMOTION: decisions with status deferred-with-dependency accumulate per topic; N punts on the same topic auto-promotes it to a kernel candidate in the elicitation menu (second-order system reading first-order declared inabilities — the cybernetic layer Duke asked for, observed working in the wild); (3) INTERRUPT: orchestrator watches the registry; when a pending shared decision blocks in-flight work per the feature x event-kind graph, message the affected agent to checkpoint+pause instead of rolling forward on a guess, then extract its decisions.

title: Feature x event-kind dependency graph: kernel-surface detector + wave scheduler
description: Duke 2026-07-20. Target-side bipartite graph (features <-> event kinds/projections they fold), built pre-build from adapter contracts + proposed event schemas — mostly LM-free. Every 9h5.16 conflict is an edge in this graph (group-assignment events folded by logs.groupMember AND location.assetsAtLocation). Uses: (1) shared kernel = high-degree event kinds, mechanically identified instead of judged; (2) wave scheduling — features sharing no kinds parallelize; features sharing kinds serialize through one expert builder or block on frozen kernel elements; (3) source-side complement is the mining read-trace (L3). Render with the existing graph tooling.

Report eval/ctkr/results/feature-kind-graph-2026-07-20.md.

title: Cross-builder differential fuzzing as discriminator miner
description: Second-opinion L1/L2/experiment 4. Build twice (from source, from fixtures), fuzz both adapters with generated flows, replay against live farmOS: every disagreement is a ce015be4-class discriminator found automatically. Compare discriminators-per-dollar vs ctkr mine-fixtures; the winner becomes the hardening engine for all 147 packs. Also converts the fixture pack from 'the spec' into 'the regression floor' via property-based replay (recorder.py already drives live farmOS).
notes:
RAISED TO P1 2026-08-11. This bead was specified 2026-07-19 and downgraded by the
wave plan to "informative, no longer gating". It is the mechanism Duke asked for
today without either of us remembering it existed: "fuzz both adapters with
generated flows, replay against live farmOS: every disagreement is a
discriminator found automatically... converts the fixture pack from 'the spec'
into 'the regression floor' via property-based replay."

THAT IS THE DESTINATION'S VOICE. A recorded pack can only ask the port what
somebody thought to record, so the port can never surprise us — and every
high-severity wave-2 finding lives in the complement of what was recorded
(normalizers, guards, refusals). Generated flows replayed against BOTH oracle and
port make the port speak on inputs no recorder chose. Disagreement is then found
rather than noticed.

Today's measurement is the argument: port-verify scored 60/60 on the four builds
that could be judged, and each of those packs was recorded by the same lane that
built the port. A pack that only asks what the builder thought to record is a
pack the builder cannot fail. Fuzzing is what makes 100% mean something.

title: Two-feature composition run: shared store, conflicting decisions
description: Second-opinion R1/experiment 3 — the smallest honest model of the fan-out. All experiments built ISOLATED stores; the real target is one event log / one asset model / one ID scheme with overlapping projections. Compose logs+quantities and location+movement into one shared store (packs exist for both); measure cross-feature fixture pass and COUNT conflicting design decisions. Known divergence evidence: identical inputs produced weaken-to-eventual vs preserve-via-convergence-rule. Output feeds the shared-kernel design (event schema, ID/HLC, binding CM-decision registry) that must ship before wave 1.
close_reason: Run+merged; report eval/ctkr/results/two-feature-composition-2026-07-20.md, build+judge committed under eval/ctkr/port_runs/compose-9h5.16/. R1 CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED: one blind builder composed both features into one store at 27/27 + 5/5 cross-probes (composition is feasible when one mind owns the overlap; the second feature even fixed latest-wins 'for free'), BUT the 7 prior isolated builds diverged on 4 of 5 shared axes from identical inputs (birth-uniqueness 3-way split incl. menu-choice conflict; additive-vs-latest-wins membership; UUID-vs-integer-counter IDs — the composed build itself regressed to a collision-prone counter; opposite pending/status gates). Shared-kernel prescription (5 elements, each divergence-justified): frozen event schema+kind taxonomy, ID+HLC scheme, one kernel latest-wins comparator, status-semantics contract, binding CM-decision registry. Fan-out must be kernel-first.

title: Signature-generation ablation: can the pipeline propose the adapter surface?

Have the pipeline (glossary + roles + mining lanes) propose the adapter contract for a FRESH feature; judge (a) against a hand-authored reference surface, (b) functionally — does a blind builder + observed fixtures over the GENERATED surface still pass the oracle? This is where the machinery could be decision-bearing: deciding WHAT to fixture. Highest-value next spend per the review.

title: Design-decision elicitation flows: surface, discuss, decide-for-me, or roll forward
description: Duke 2026-07-19, direct product direction from the first human CM review. When the target substrate differs from the source (which is every port), major design decisions should be SURFACED BEFORE build, not best-guessed and rolled forward — post-hoc changes cost a refactor cascade because these decisions ripple. Evidence this is real: the 9h5.4/9h5.8 ablations showed the CM-hard birth-log pick is pure builder judgment — same inputs, different builders chose preserve-via-convergence-rule vs weaken-to-eventual. The pipeline already produces the raw material (intent-CM decision menus, paradigm-divergence declarations from the meta-structural pass, port-decision records). Build the interaction layer: (1) a MENU of pending design decisions per feature, ranked by uncertainty x blast-radius (how far the decision ripples in the graph); (2) per decision, selectable flows: open an interview/elicitation discussion, 'decide for me' (agent picks + records rationale in the PD ledger), 'surface strong recommendations only', or 'roll forward' (explicit, logged, reversible-flagged); (3) decisions taken pre-build become pre-registered constraints the builder receives — connecting directly into the meta-structural pass's pre-registration discipline. This is the developer's primary role in the loop as agents handle implementation. Consider bd human as the persistence substrate for pending decisions.
close_reason: Shipped+merged: ctkr decisions collect/list/resolve (decisions.py 1078 lines, 27 hermetic tests, ctkr suite 430 pass). LM-free registry over intent-CM menus + paradigm-divergence declarations + card dissonance; blast radius from graph reach; four flows per Duke's spec (--interview terra-generated tradeoff doc, --decide, --decide-for-me with recorded rationale, --recommend, --roll-forward reversible-flagged); every committing resolution appends a PD record readable by verifyPort's waiver machinery = decisions become pre-registered constraints. Validated on 0p7 slice: UniqueBirthLog CM-hard surfaced with full 3-option menu + interview doc.

title: Semantic-mining pass: use graph+CM lanes to propose fixture candidates per feature
description: The golden path from the 9h5.8 matrix (Duke 2026-07-19). Invert the pipeline's role: instead of writing briefs the builder ignores, use the deterministic layers to FIND the non-obvious semantics that need fixtures. Inputs per feature: CM seeds (perfect ground-truth recall at $0.001 in 9h5.6), the code graph (constraints, hooks, workflow configs, field-flow edges), and a source-read lane (the 9h5.8 pure-LLM cell recovered latest-wins from source when fixtures missed it). Output: ranked fixture-candidate list (scenario + why non-obvious + where in source), each then OBSERVED against the live oracle before entering the pack — never intuition-authored. This is the fan-out's per-feature recipe: signatures + mined fixtures = the measured 17/17 combination.

Honesty check on logs+quantities: strict scope MISSES latest-wins (0/57 — the read logic lives in modules/asset/group, outside the feature boundary); with group in scope the source-read lane surfaces it at rank 2. title: scip-php emits no Read/Write access roles -> PHP READS_FIELD/WRITES_FIELD structurally impossible
description:
Occurrence-role histogram over the farmOS full-site scip-php index (farmos-fullsite.index.scip, bead i00): documents=726, totalOccurrences=18043, definitionOccurrences=5254, referenceOccurrences=12789, readAccessRoles=0, writeAccessRoles=0, drupalReferenceOccurrences=11309, localSymbolOccurrences=0.

FINDING: scip-php sets NEITHER SymbolRole.ReadAccess NOR SymbolRole.WriteAccess on ANY occurrence (0/18043). The loader's field-access branch (src/scip/loader.ts ~L348-354: targetKind=='field' && isWrite -> WRITES_FIELD; && isRead -> READS_FIELD) can therefore NEVER fire for PHP. Every PHP field access collapses to a plain REFERENCES edge. This is a scip-php output limitation, NOT a loader bug — scip-typescript/scip-python do set these roles.

IMPACT: PHP hom-profiles lose the read/write-field dimension. CALLS/REFERENCES/CONSTRUCTS are unaffected (CALLS is derived from callable target kind, not access role; verified 1933 CALLS + 906 CONSTRUCTS on this index).

SECONDARY: externalRefsSkipped=3903 are non-Drupal externals (symfony / PHP-stdlib) skipped by the Drupal\ gate by design (bead i00). drupalReferenceOccurrences=11309 vs kept boundary edges 4374 — the gap is refs to Drupal symbols that ARE defined in-index (resolved to real nodes, not boundary) plus refs whose enclosing caller could not be attributed.

OPTIONS: (a) accept the limitation, document PHP field-access as REFERENCES-only; (b) LSP overlay to recover read/write intent (heavy); (c) upstream scip-php PR to emit access roles; (d) tree-sitter PHP lane heuristic for $this->field = ... assignments to synthesize WRITES_FIELD.

Histogram reproducible: bun run scratchpad/repro/measure-i00.ts <index.scip> <psr4.json>.
notes:
Duke 2026-07-19: the data edges ARE the point — 'a lot of our actual benefit is through having those edges; proceeding without them feels like flying blind.' Pursue option (d) tree-sitter PHP heuristic lane for READS_FIELD/WRITES_FIELD now (immediate), and scope option (c) upstream scip-php PR (durable). Part of foundation-hardening epic 9h5.
Claude Fable 5 2026-07-19 (option d SHIPPED + option c SCOPED):

OPTION (d) DELIVERED — tree-sitter PHP field-access heuristic lane (src/extractor/edges.ts walkPhp). Synthesizes READS_FIELD/WRITES_FIELD from: $this->field / $obj->prop assignments (WRITES) + reads (READS), augmented assign ($this->count += 1) = both, Drupal ->set('f',…)/->get('f') accessors (string-keyed → external boundary node), and $entity->field_* idioms (field_ prefix → external boundary). All such edges carry a NEW provenance='tree_sitter_heuristic' attribute (Edge.provenance, new STRING column on READS_FIELD/WRITES_FIELD REL tables, additive ALTER — migrates existing DBs). SCIP-loader field edges now stamped provenance='scip' so downstream can tell them apart. farmOS validation (sandbox tree-sitter index of web/profiles/farm, 789 files): READS_FIELD 0→1089 (560 to declared props, 529 to external Drupal-field boundary nodes), WRITES_FIELD 0→252 (112 declared, 140 external). 1341 net-new data-flow edges, 100% provenance=tree_sitter_heuristic. Data-edge alphabet coverage for the farmOS PHP lane {READS_FIELD,WRITES_FIELD,TYPE_OF,RETURNS_TYPE,CONSTRUCTS} went 0/5 → 2/5; scip_fraction of PHP data edges stays 0.0 (all heuristic, correctly marked — that IS the point). Tests: 10 new PHP field-access cases in edges.test.ts (each idiom + negative local-var case) + 1 provenance round-trip in walker.test.ts; full suite 323 pass / 0 fail.

OPTION (c) UPSTREAM SCOPE — scip-php (davidrjenni/scip-php, PHP tool, cloned dev-main). ROOT CAUSE is narrow and fixable: src/DocIndexer.php. The ref() emitter (line 255) ALREADY takes an $role param (default SymbolRole::UnspecifiedSymbolRole) but the PropertyFetch branch (lines 175-187) calls $this->ref($pos,$symbol,$n->name) with NO role — so every property occurrence gets role 0. That is exactly why readAccessRoles=0/writeAccessRoles=0 over all 18043 occurrences. SymbolRole constants exist (Bindings/Scip/SymbolRole.php: WriteAccess=4, ReadAccess=8). The parser already runs nikic ParentConnectingVisitor (Parser/Parser.php:29) so every node has a 'parent' attribute — write-context detection is tractable with no new traversal. MINIMAL PR: in the PropertyFetch/NullsafePropertyFetch/StaticPropertyFetch branch, compute role from parent: $parent instanceof Assign/AssignOp/AssignRef && $parent->var === $n (also PreInc/PostInc/PreDec/PostDec, and by-ref Param/ArrayItem for completeness) → WriteAccess, else ReadAccess; pass it as ref()'s 5th arg. ~10-15 lines + imports of PhpParser\Node\Expr\{Assign,AssignOp,AssignRef,PreInc,PostInc,PreDec,PostDec}. Test fixtures live in scip-php's tests/ (occurrence snapshots). Caveat: compound LHS ($this->a->b = x) marks only the outermost fetch as write and inner as read — matches SCIP semantics from scip-typescript. Once merged, MetaCoding's loader Pass 2b field-access branch (src/scip/loader.ts:350-355) fires unchanged and yields provenance='scip' field edges that would supersede/co-exist with the heuristic lane. Source clone + farmOS source extraction + measurement scripts in scratchpad (sandbox, not committed).
close_reason: Option (d) shipped and merged: tree-sitter PHP field-access heuristic lane with provenance='tree_sitter_heuristic' marking (vs 'scip'). farmOS: READS_FIELD 0->1089, WRITES_FIELD 0->252, data-edge alphabet 0/5 -> 2/5. 341 TS tests green. Option (c) upstream fix scoped in notes (DocIndexer.php ~10-15 lines) — spun out as separate bead.

title: L3 spec-labeler mislabels large subsystems (graph-embedding attractor) + labels non-reproducible
description:
extract-spec deck defect caught by the T6 verifier on MetaCoding self-index. (1) COHERENCE: the 4 largest subsystems (~86% of members) get names+intent contradicting their members — ctkr core (2039) named 'Graph Embedding Pipeline', src/mcp (781, 91% pure) named 'Graph Embedding & Walk Generation' w/ intent about DeepWalk/Word2Vec while its interface exports EdgeKind/IndexState/CodeSearchInput. Strong 'graph embedding' attractor (MetaCoding's own graph/embedding/node vocab biases the labeler). Structural sections (interfaces/roles/composition) are CORRECT; only the LLM name+intent are wrong. Small homogeneous subsystems label correctly. (2) REPRODUCIBILITY: 9/14 card NAMES changed on identical re-run (card_ids stable; haiku temp=0 still varies + 27/291 cache misses), contradicting the 'labels stable at temp=0' claim.

## Context
Parent MetaCoding-z4w. Structural extraction is sound; the NL layer fails on exactly the biggest subsystems that matter most for a re-implementation reference. Likely fixes: (a) evidence selection via role centroids not diluted sampling; (b) hierarchical labeling — label roles/sub-clusters first then summarize the subsystem FROM its role labels (grounds summary in structure); (c) stronger model than haiku for the summary pass; (d) de-bias the attractor; (e) deeper: 2039-member subsystem is too coarse — recursive partition split. Empirical 2026-07-14, verifier on the full extract-spec run ($0.42, 14 cards).
notes:
FIXED (2026-07-14). Root cause: the subsystem name+intent — the single highest-stakes label — was built from a diluted member sample + raw code slices + FTS, ignoring the interface exports and role labels the structural lane had already extracted, so haiku pattern-matched MetaCoding's graph/embedding/node vocab.

Fixes (ctkr/ctkr/spec_cards.py, extract_spec.py, graph_loader.py):
1. HIERARCHICAL labeling — the subsystem summary is now built FROM the already-labeled roles + interface provides/consumes + top composition ops + data shapes, exports-first, not a raw member dump.
2. EVIDENCE SELECTION — feed the top interface exports (what the subsystem PROVIDES) with their L3 contracts + role labels/descriptions; raw domain-vocab slices dropped from the subsystem prompt.
3. STRONGER MODEL — subsystem pass routed to claude-sonnet-4-6 (configurable via --subsystem-model / DEFAULT_SUBSYSTEM_MODEL); cheap per-element labels stay on haiku. 14 sonnet + 277 haiku calls.
4. DE-BIAS — system prompt instructs: name from what the interface exports + roles DO, and do NOT use graph/embedding/node/walk/pipeline buzzwords unless the exports support them.
5. REPRODUCIBILITY — fixed two PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent set orderings feeding the subsystem prompt (structural_ids slice; name_tokens set iteration into the fts_terms Counter) + made search_tokens deterministic (ORDER BY rank, symbol_id). Prompts now byte-identical across 4 hash seeds; warm-cache re-run = 291/291 cache hits, 0/14 name changes (was 9/14). card_ids already stable. prompt_version bumped v1->v2; docstring 'stable at temp=0' claim replaced with honest 'regenerable view over structural ground truth'.

BEFORE -> AFTER (scip self-index, mc-v3):
2039 (ctkr core)  'Graph Embedding Pipeline'          -> 'Analysis Artifact Schema & Data Models' (intent: canonical Pydantic data models; exports LineRange/PatternRow/CentralityRow/ArtifactManifest)
781  (src/mcp)     'Graph Embedding & Walk Generation' -> 'Code Analysis Tool API' (intent: 'primary MCP tool layer for code analysis'; exports EdgeKind/IndexState/CodeSearchInput/GraphNeighborsInput)
651               'Code Graph Embedding & Walk'       -> 'Code Index Store' (exports Store/LoadScipOpts)
455               'Graph Embedding & Node Vectorization' -> 'Analysis Artifact Store and Schema' (exports CtkrHandle/openCtkrArtifacts)
Small cards stayed correct: 378 'SCIP Index Loader & Parser', 70 'LSP Client & Service Wrapper', 55 'Role Equivalence Evaluation Runner'. The graph-embedding attractor is gone from all 14 cards.

Cost: $0.42 (before, all-haiku) -> ~$0.58 (after: haiku cheap labels + sonnet 14 subsystem passes), +~$0.16. Tests: pytest 198 passed/3 skipped (excl centrality); bun test 292 pass/0 fail; new prompt-determinism verified across 4 PYTHONHASHSEEDs.

Partition-split (recursive re-partition of the 2039 subsystem) intentionally NOT done — noted follow-up; the labeling fixes alone made all 4 big cards coherent.

title: Functor search commits zero-margin ties as mappings — add margin-aware acceptance
description:
On real code the seeded-constraint-propagation commits near-random assignments within saturated structural equivalence classes. autogen<->ag2 (verbatim fork): 96% of mappings sim>=0.95, MEDIAN MARGIN 0.0000, 91% margin<0.01; byte-identical anchor classes (ConversableAgent, GroupChat, AssistantAgent) mapped to WRONG targets. Depth-2 WL did not break enough symmetry on real code (worsened by CALLS=0).

## Context
The functor is honest at the aggregate level (fidelity/cycle-consistency rank fork ~2x above unrelated pair) but the per-symbol mapping is untrustworthy. Fix: do NOT commit a mapping whose margin < threshold — emit it as 'ambiguous/unresolved' (the margin column already exists). Report ambiguity mass instead of arbitrary ties. Depends partly on MetaCoding CALLS-edges bead. Empirical finding 2026-07-14, real Orchestrators corpus.
notes:
Implemented margin-aware honesty (does NOT change the mapping — reports the truth about it):

functorSearch.ts: new config commitMinMargin (default 0 = byte-identical to prior behavior). FunctorSearchResult gains ambiguityMass (fraction of committed mappings with margin<deltaAmb; ==ambiguityRate). FunctorMapping gains isAmbiguous (margin<deltaAmb, or <commitMinMargin when the gate is armed). When commitMinMargin>0, ambiguous mappings are FLAGGED (not dropped — kept in mapping/functor_edges) and excluded from the confident coverage/fidelity accounting.

Artifacts: FunctorRow.ambiguity_mass (float, default 0.0) + FunctorEdgeRow.is_ambiguous (bool, default False) added to schema.py canonical, *_COLUMNS tuples, functorRunner COLSPEC, hand-written types.ts, codegen'd types.gen.ts. functor_id now folds commit_min_margin into the config blob (config-for-id), so gated runs are addressable distinctly. Additive columns → old artifacts round-trip.

MCP functor_between: new min_margin query param (DB-side margin>=floor filter via artifacts.functorEdges.minMargin). Result now surfaces functor.ambiguity_mass, n_ambiguous, per-row is_ambiguous, and an honest-framing _note when ambiguity_mass>=0.5 ('N% coin-flip ties — per-symbol mapping UNRELIABLE; aggregate metrics still meaningful'). Tool descriptions + describe_api input_schema updated.

Tests: functorSearch fixture test — saturated graph (8 identical twins) yields ambiguityMass>0.9 + all isAmbiguous; clean orthogonal isomorphism yields ambiguityMass==0, none flagged; commitMinMargin gate keeps rows but zeroes confident coverage. functor_between test — saturated f:sat_ez fixture surfaces ambiguity_mass=0.75/n_ambiguous=3/note, min_margin drops ties. Python roundtrip tests assert both new fields. bun test src/ctkr src/mcp = 181 pass/0 fail; pytest test_schema = 26 pass. Determinism preserved (default path byte-identical).

NOTE: this reports honesty; it does not improve the mapping. The margin collapse is intrinsic to name-blind typed-edge profiles on real code (median margin 0.0000).
close_reason: Closed

title: scip lane emits REFERENCES but ~zero typed CALLS — the most discriminating edge is missing from hom-profiles
description:
On the real Orchestrators corpus, scip-python emitted ~60k REFERENCES and ZERO typed CALLS. Confirmed earlier on MetaCoding too (marginal-entropy showed CALLS=0 in hom-profiles). scip's occurrence model routes call-sites to REFERENCES, so the most discriminating edge dimension (who-calls-whom) is absent; profiles collapse to REFERENCES/READS_FIELD/CONTAINS count-vectors that look alike across most methods.

## Context
Root cause of the functor precision problem on real code (autogen<->ag2 fork: fidelity 0.18, median margin 0.0000, anchor classes mis-mapped). Fix options: derive CALLS from scip REFERENCES whose target is an invoked function/method, or ensure the tree-sitter CALLS survive the scip merge. High leverage: affects role_equivalent, functor discovery, and every hom-profile consumer. Empirical finding 2026-07-14 on archbox Orchestrators corpus.
notes:
CALLS recovery measured on archbox (2026-07-14). Commit 9664166 derives CALLS edges from callable REFERENCES in the SCIP loader. LOCAL: CALLS 0->4299 edges on MetaCoding self-index; marginal-entropy CALLS importance NONE->HIGH (+0.3132 bits, 4th of 15 kinds). ARCHBOX autogen v0.2.40 vs ag2: CALLS 0->29278 edges (2nd largest kind). Functor autogen->ag2: fidelity 0.180->0.199 (+10.6%), coverage 0.686->0.678, cycle 0.543->0.539. Median margin STILL 0.0000 (margin collapse NOT broken; pct>0 = 24.2%). Anchor classes STILL mis-mapped: ConversableAgent->BaseEvent, GroupChat->CaseResult, AssistantAgent->Depends. VERDICT: CALLS recovery is a real signal (HIGH importance, measurable fidelity lift) but is NOT sufficient alone to break the margin collapse or fix anchor-class mapping. The bottleneck is elsewhere -- likely profile saturation from the high-dimensional hom-vector space where structurally similar but semantically different classes remain indistinguishable.
IMPLEMENTED + MEASURED (2026-07-14, commit 9664166). Fix: SCIP has no call occurrence role, so the loader now ADDS a CALLS edge when a resolved REFERENCE target is a callable (keeping REFERENCES). LOCAL (MetaCoding --scip): CALLS 0 -> 4299 edges; marginal-entropy CALLS +0.0000/NONE -> +0.2208/HIGH (4th strongest); overall entropy 4.850 -> 4.872. ARCHBOX autogen0.2.40<->ag2 fork: fidelity 0.180 -> 0.199, coverage 0.686 -> 0.678, cycle 0.543 -> 0.539 — NEGLIGIBLE. Margin collapse PERSISTS: median 0.0000, 89% <0.01 (baseline 91%). Anchor classes still mostly mis-map at zero margin. VERDICT: CALLS recovery is correct hygiene (real +0.22 role-discrimination dimension, likely helps partition/labels) but does NOT fix isomorphism precision — because derived-CALLS overlaps REFERENCES (adds little NEW info). The margin collapse is FUNDAMENTAL to name-blind typed-edge profiles on real code, not a missing-edge artifact. Real fixes: MetaCoding-265 (margin-aware acceptance = report ambiguity honestly), role-level not symbol-level gates (extraction port-verifier already does this), and for same-name FORK detection specifically a lexical tiebreaker (names ARE legit signal there; not for cross-stack ports where names don't survive).
