title: Marginal-entropy measurement harness for edge kinds
description: Measure each edge kind's marginal contribution to hom-profile entropy on a --scip corpus, so edge-taxonomy work is driven by data (which edges actually move entropy toward clean GO) rather than by entropy-check's static list.
design: Leave-one-edge-kind-out (and add-one-in) over hom_profiles: recompute shannon_entropy/top5 with each EdgeKind ablated. Rank kinds by entropy delta. Reuse ctkr entropy-check plumbing. Corpus at 4.845 BORDERLINE is the baseline.
acceptance_criteria: A ranked report of per-edge-kind marginal entropy delta on the scip corpus; verdict on whether RAISES/DECORATES are worth the extractor cost before building them.

title: Add DECORATES edge kind (decorator application) to extractor
description: New typed edge: decorator symbol -> decorated symbol (Python '@dec', TS '@Decorator'). First confirm ANNOTATES doesn't already capture decorator application.
design: PREREQUISITE CHECK: inspect what ANNOTATES currently emits (types.ts lists it uncommented; may be type-annotation edges, not decorators). If ANNOTATES already covers @decorators, close this as redundant and instead document the semantics. Otherwise add DECORATES via tree-sitter (decorator syntax nodes in py/ts).
acceptance_criteria: Either: DECORATES edges emitted for decorated fixtures AND ANNOTATES-vs-DECORATES semantics documented; OR bead closed with a note that ANNOTATES already covers it.

title: Add RAISES edge kind (exception flow) to extractor
description: New typed edge: function/method -> exception/error type it raises or throws. Extends EdgeKind enum + EDGE_KIND_VALUES + schema PLAIN_EDGES.
design: Tree-sitter lane: Python 'raise X(...)' and TS/JS 'throw new X()' / 'throw X'. Map the thrown/raised type reference to the enclosing function symbol. SCIP lane: emit if the type is resolvable, else tree-sitter-only. No RAISES today (grep of edges.ts/scip loader confirms absent).
acceptance_criteria: RAISES edges emitted for a fixture containing raise/throw; entropy-check on a --scip corpus shows a populated RAISES column; hom-profile entropy delta measured vs baseline.

title: Extend edge taxonomy: RAISES + DECORATES to sharpen hom-profiles (BORDERLINE→GO)
description:
Push hom-profile entropy from BORDERLINE to a clean GO by adding the genuinely-missing typed edges, so Phase 2a role-equivalence and Phase 2b functor discovery get sharp role classes.

## Context
Empirical finding 2026-07-13: on a --scip self-index of MetaCoding, hom-profile shannon_entropy=4.845 bits (BORDERLINE, top5=67.7%, 16.4% pairs >0.9 sim), up from 3.818 (BLOCKED) with tree-sitter only. The scip CALLS/REFERENCES lift (+1.03 bits, edges 3002->8367) crossed the 4.0 gate. entropy-check still recommends richer edges for sharper roles. IMPORTANT: its hardcoded message lists READS_FIELD/WRITES_FIELD/RETURNS_TYPE/CONSTRUCTS which ALREADY EXIST in the 14-kind EdgeKind enum (added by MetaCoding-e54/3s5/9le). The TRUE gaps are RAISES (exception flow) and DECORATES (decorator application; ANNOTATES may already partially cover it). Drive further edge work by measured marginal entropy, not the static list.
notes: MEASURED OUTCOME (2026-07-13, MetaCoding --scip self-index): entropy 4.845 -> 4.850 (+0.005, NOISE). Still BORDERLINE. New edges negligible on this corpus: RAISES=6 edges (+0.004, LOW), ANNOTATES/decorators=0 edges (NONE - verify on a decorator-heavy repo). Signal is carried by REFERENCES (+1.62), CONTAINS (+1.18), READS_FIELD (+0.61). CALLS=0 in hom-profiles (scip routes call-sites through REFERENCES). Conclusion: the deliverable that paid off is the ijo.3 marginal-entropy harness, which proves exotic edge kinds have diminishing returns here and localizes the real signal. BORDERLINE->GO lever is NOT more edge kinds; likely CONTAINS-scaffolding down-weighting and/or verifying ANNOTATES fires on decorator-heavy code.

title: serve reopen-on-refresh: pick up a reindex without restart
description: Read-only serve is snapshot-pinned at startup (scripts/spike-refresh.ts: a live RO handle does NOT see another process's commits; only a full Database reopen does). So after a reindex, serve keeps serving the startup snapshot until restarted. Add a cheap reopen trigger.
design: graph.lbug is a single file. Stat its mtime; when it advances past the open-time mtime, swap in a fresh read-only Store (open new, route new calls to it, close the old once in-flight queries drain). Trigger by: (a) mtime check before each tool call (debounced), or (b) the indexer touching a generation/manifest file that serve watches. Surface the swap via the existing index-state staleness fields. Requires routing tool handlers through a getStore() accessor instead of a captured const.
acceptance_criteria: With serve running, a  completes and a subsequent describe_api/graph_callers call reflects the new graph without restarting serve.
close_reason: serve reopen-on-refresh: Store.generation() mtime marker + currentStore() accessor reopens the read-only handle when graph.lbug advances; all graph/text/describe handlers route through it; dedup + grace-delay close. smoke-reopen.ts (REOPEN_SMOKE_PASS) + full gauntlet green.

title: ladybugdb concurrency: reads during indexing
description: Spikes (scripts/spike-lock.ts, spike-refresh.ts) established ladybugdb's real lock semantics: the exclusive lock excludes only OTHER WRITERS — read-only opens coexist with a live writer on the same dir (both directions), but a read-only handle is snapshot-pinned at open time and needs a full reopen to advance. The 'easy 80%' (read-only Store.open for serve/query/status) is DONE and merged. This epic tracks the remaining freshness/coordination work.
design: Done: readOnly Store.open; serve/query/status read-only so they coexist with index. Remaining: serve reopen-on-refresh, checkpoint cadence, optional blue-green, optional single-writer daemon.
close_reason: 3/4 children done and merged; sole remainder gh0.4 (single-writer daemon) is deferred-optional and remains tracked as its own deferred bead. Duke approved closing during 2026-07-19 foundation-hardening review.

title: metacoding status CLI + serve startup empty-store warning
description: Give humans the same signal: a 'metacoding status' command, and a one-line stderr warning at serve startup when the store is empty (Claude Code surfaces MCP stderr). Also echo the resolved data dir on serve — index already prints it as JSON, serve prints nothing.
design: Add 'status' subcommand in src/cli/main.ts that resolves the data dir (cli/data-dir.ts) and prints store.summary() human-readable. In serveMcp() (mcp/server.ts:34) after Store.open, if summary.symbols===0 write to stderr: '⚠ 0 symbols at <dataDir> — run: metacoding index . --scip'. Always log the resolved dataDir to stderr on serve start.
acceptance_criteria: 'metacoding status' prints indexed/empty + counts + dataDir for the cwd repo. Starting serve on an empty store emits the warning to stderr; on an indexed store it logs the dataDir and no warning.
close_reason: metacoding status CLI (human + --json) and serve startup stderr echo + empty-store warning. Tested on indexed/empty/json.

title: store.summary(): single source of truth for index state
description: Add Store.summary() returning a cheap snapshot of what's actually in the store. The current code has no count/status method at all; every consumer reinvents emptiness checks or skips them.
design: New method on Store (src/store/index.ts). One Cypher: MATCH (n:Symbol) RETURN count(n). Plus distinct (repo, repo_commit_sha) and max(indexed_at) from the temporal columns. Return { dataDir, symbols, repos: [{repo, commit, indexedAt}], indexed: symbols>0 }. Keep it a read-only single round-trip so it's safe to call on serve startup and from describe_api.
acceptance_criteria: Store.summary() returns symbols=0 / indexed=false on a freshly-opened empty dir, and accurate counts + repo/commit list on an indexed dir. Covered by a smoke test (scripts/smoke-*.ts) exercising both the empty and indexed paths.
close_reason: Store.summary() added (pure store read: symbols, indexed, per-repo snapshots). Verified by SUMMARY_SMOKE_PASS (empty=0/false, filled>0/true).

title: Surface index state in describe_api
description: Agents are already instructed to call describe_api first. Make it report store.summary() so the agent self-detects an empty/unindexed workspace instead of trusting [] from graph_callers et al.
design: In mcp/tools.ts describeApi() (and its wiring in mcp/server.ts:184), add a 'store' block: { indexed, symbols, repos, dataDir }. No new tool, no protocol risk — just enrich the payload the agent already fetches.

title: punts.jsonl still carries the falsified is_location WRITE claim — the ADR was corrected, the machine-read ledger was not
description:
From results/wave2/synthesis-wave2-2026-08-12.md, dispositioning residual 2 the wave-2 Elenchus deliberately left for a human. VERIFIED AT farmos-port@6a3c0c5, and the Elenchus's claim is PARTLY STALE — corrected here rather than repeated.

WHAT THE ELENCHUS SAID: 'hy6.8-is-location-is-advisory.md and the punt land-is-location-not-enforced still carry the sentence commit 2d3df92 falsified... still there at 824dd3c.'

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. The ADR BODY was corrected: results/wave2/adr/hy6.8-is-location-is-advisory.md opens with a 21-line banner dated 2026-08-03, 'FALSIFIED IN PART — READ THIS FIRST', stating WRITE enforced / READ advisory and citing 2d3df92. Anyone who OPENS the file gets the right answer. That half of the finding is closed.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE WORSE HALF. port_runs/wave2/identity-land/build/punts.jsonl:4 is UNCORRECTED:

  {"punt":"land-is-location-not-enforced","what":"is_location is advisory: a movement into a land with is_location=false succeeds and the asset reads as located there (M4).",...,"status":"measured, divergence declined, escalated"}

The 'movement... succeeds' clause is a WRITE claim and WRITE is enforced — measured 422 location.0.target_id on log--activity and log--observation alike. The punt asserts the opposite of the measurement, carries status 'measured', and cites probe M4 which the ADR's own banner says is NOT REPRODUCIBLE AS WRITTEN (no request payload in its ledger row, no probe script shipped).

WHY THIS IS THE WORSE HALF: prose gets a banner a human reads; punts.jsonl is a MACHINE-READ ledger with no banner mechanism. A composition step or a future decision sweep reading punts.jsonl gets the falsified claim with no warning attached, and it is labelled 'measured'.

ALSO: the ADR FILENAME and H1 title both still assert 'is NOT enforced' unqualified. The banner sits above them so an opener is safe; a filename grep or a title listing is not. This is the 'ADR filename asserting the opposite of its body' shape the Elenchus lists elsewhere as its own defect class.

FIX: correct the punt row's 'what' to the measured WRITE/READ split, or supersede it with a new row — matching whatever PACKS.jsonl-style append-only convention punts.jsonl follows. Decide separately whether punts.jsonl needs a falsification mechanism at all, since prose has one and it does not.
acceptance_criteria: punts.jsonl no longer asserts that a movement into a land with is_location=false succeeds, and the correction cites 2d3df92 and hy6.6; if punts.jsonl is append-only, the correction is a new row rather than an edit.

title: identity-group's crash-safe cleanup is decorative: the finally sets a dead variable and cleanup is straight-line after it
description:
Found while harvesting the 2026-08-07 ledger sweep (MetaCoding-60u). Verified
directly at port_runs/wave2/identity-group/observe/verify.py:498-512.

  try:
      run_checks()
  except Exception as exc:
      ... FAILURES.append(...)
  finally:
      _ran = True          # <- read NOWHERE. grep confirms: line 505, one hit.
  # CLEANUP follows as straight-line code, OUTSIDE the block.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT BROKEN, stated precisely so nobody over- or under-reacts:

- For an ordinary Exception, cleanup DOES run — because `except Exception`
  swallows it and control simply falls through. It works by accident of control
  flow, not by the `finally`.
- For a BaseException it does NOT. SystemExit or KeyboardInterrupt propagates
  past `except Exception` and skips the cleanup entirely, stranding fixtures in
  the SHARED oracle. That is exactly MetaCoding-k1t's class, one file over — and
  k1t is being fixed in tools/ledger.py by catching BaseException. This build
  does not use that path.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE BUG: commit f58582c is titled "fix(hy6.31/
.32/.33/.34): the group ledger had NONE of the guards — J1, J3, J7 detected".
J7 IS the crash-safe cleanup. The commit credits itself with a guard the code
does not implement, and the `finally` is what makes it LOOK implemented — a
reader checking for "is cleanup in a finally?" sees a finally and stops.

This project reconstructs its own history from commit messages (a process agent
rebuilt four days of analysis from git log alone), so a commit that credits
itself with an unimplemented guard is worse than the guard being absent.

TO CLOSE: move the cleanup inside a finally that actually wraps it, catch
BaseException as tools/ledger.py now does, ship the red (a body raising
SystemExit must still clean up AND still exit non-zero), and correct the record
about f58582c.

title: 0bm step3: toolchainDigest's MALFORMED_DIGEST refusal is never exercised — the same unreached-refusal shape M6 fixed for NO_ARTIFACTS, in the same function
description:
MEASURED at 68b528d, isolated archive of HEAD.

MUTATION W10: delete the per-lane recheck inside toolchainDigest (src/toolchain/identity.ts:296-301) —
    if (!isDigest(a.digest)) { throw new ToolchainIdentityRefused('MALFORMED_DIGEST', ...); }
SURVIVED all 43 fixtures. 43p/0f mutant, 43p/0f restored.

NOT AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT. registerLoadedArtifact validates digests ENTERING the registry, so the default-argument path is indeed covered by that earlier check — but toolchainDigest takes an EXPLICIT readonly ArtifactIdentity[] as its parameter, and nothing on that path went through the registry. toolchainDigest([{lane:'x',kind:'file',source:'s',digest:'not-a-digest'}]) throws at HEAD and returns a well-formed sha256 under W10. Every fixture that exercises MALFORMED_DIGEST goes through registerLoadedArtifact (identity.test.ts:202's eight prefixed cases, added by 5f62f91 for N1), so the copy of the check inside toolchainDigest is asserted by nothing.

SEVERITY IS P2 BECAUSE REACHABILITY IS THIN TODAY. The two explicit-array callers are scripts/toolchain-preflight.ts:79, whose artifactsFrom(result) builds identities from digestFile/digestPackage/dockerImageId (all well-formed by construction), and layer2Key's second parameter, which has no production caller at all. So this is a latent hole, not a live one.

WHY FILE IT ANYWAY. It is the EXACT shape the builder found and fixed one refusal over: mutation M6 showed NO_ARTIFACTS in this same function was computed and never exercised, and leg 4 of F3.5 was written for it. The identical question was not then asked of MALFORMED_DIGEST three lines below, and the answer is the same. A refusal no fixture reaches is the same object as no refusal — this module's own thesis (identity.ts:277, quoting oracle_preflight.py:351).

FIX: one case — expect(() => toolchainDigest([{lane:'x',kind:'file',source:'s',digest:'sha256:TODO'}])).toThrow(/MALFORMED_DIGEST/) — plus the contrast that a well-formed explicit array returns. Confirm by re-running W10.

title: 0bm step3: the lock's COVERAGE is unchecked — 3 caret deps the design names are undeclared, and the only lane-count floor is on a script nothing runs
description:
Judged at a84b649. Step 3 shipped a drift check that is genuinely load-bearing for
the lanes it declares (five independent lock mutations all go red under `bun test`).
What nothing checks is WHICH LANES IT DECLARES, and the lock's coverage is the one
thing a lock cannot report about itself.

1. THE LOCK DOES NOT COVER WHAT THE DESIGN NAMES. lessons-as-mechanism.md:149-152
   enumerates the caret-ranged toolchain: tree-sitter-wasms, scip-typescript,
   scip-python, SCIP_PHP_IMAGE, AND `intelephense ^1.18.5`,
   `typescript-language-server ^5.1.3`, `@ladybugdb/core ^0.15.4`. The lock ships
   8 lanes and the last three are absent. They still resolve by caret
   (package.json:69,80,86). A reader of the design document would expect them
   covered; they are not, and nothing says so.

2. THE ONLY GUARD ON LANE COUNT IS ON A SURFACE THAT DOES NOT RUN. The floors in
   scripts/toolchain-preflight.ts (lanesDeclared >= 8, grammarLanes >= 4) are the
   only mechanism that would notice a lane being deleted or a fifth grammar being
   added to walker.ts:116-120 without a lane. That script is in no package.json
   script, is not in scripts/smoke-all.ts's SCRIPTS list, and is not named
   `smoke-*.ts` so smoke-all's own new-script census cannot see it either. There
   is no CI and no hook. Its floors have never gated anything.
   (`bun test`'s live check hardcodes the four grammar names, so deleting a lane
   IS caught for those four -- verified, N14/N24 both go red. A FIFTH grammar is
   not.)

   Note also that the min: 8 floor's `why` says it was "counted from
   toolchain.lock.json when it was first written" -- i.e. derived from what the
   run produced, which is lessons-as-mechanism.md:264's fake #4 verbatim.

3. THE DOCKER LANE'S SOURCE IS NOT THE IMAGE THAT RUNS. src/scip/run.ts:60 reads
   `process.env.METACODING_SCIP_PHP_IMAGE ?? "davidrjenni/scip-php:latest"`. The
   lock hardcodes the default tag. Set the env var and the preflight measures an
   image nothing indexes with, while reporting on the lane by name. Nothing binds
   the declared source to the value the code actually uses.

4. NOTHING CROSS-CHECKS THE REGISTRY AGAINST THE LOCK. preflight.ts re-reads
   `<root>/node_modules/tree-sitter-wasms/out/*.wasm` BY PATH; parser.ts resolves
   its wasmDir through `require.resolve("tree-sitter-wasms/package.json")`. Today
   those are the same directory. Under a nested/hoisted/pnpm/workspace install
   they are not, and the preflight would report OK about a blob no parse ever
   touched. `loadedArtifacts()` holds the bytes that were actually loaded and is
   never compared to the lock.

5. isDigest's LENGTH/CHARSET HALF IS UNASSERTED. Mutation N1 -- loosening
   /^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/ to /^sha256:/ -- SURVIVED all 31 fixtures. Both
   fixtures aimed at this guard use strings that fail on the PREFIX alone
   ("TODO" in preflight.test.ts:125, "0.1.13" in identity.test.ts:186), so
   nothing proves a `sha256:`-prefixed non-digest is refused. Consequence:
   `registerLoadedArtifact` would accept `sha256:TODO` as measured identity.
   One case -- digest: "sha256:TODO" must be MALFORMED_DIGEST -- closes it.

6. THE LOCK'S `version` IS READ AND NEVER COMPARED. `LOCK_VERSION = 1` is
   exported and has no consumer; readLockfile does `Number(lock.version ?? 0)`
   and discards it. Mutation N22 (forge the version to 999) SURVIVED. A v2 lock
   format read by a v1 checker is silently accepted. Small, but it is a declared
   constant that checks nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Either declare intelephense / typescript-language-server / @ladybugdb/core as lanes or record in toolchain.lock.json's why WHY they are out of scope. A bun test fixture asserts the lock's grammar lanes are a superset of the grammars walker.ts loads (derived, not a hardcoded list of four). The docker lane's source is derived from src/scip/run.ts's SCIP_PHP_IMAGE rather than duplicated. digest: 'sha256:TODO' is refused as MALFORMED_DIGEST (kills mutation N1). Verified by re-running N1 and N22 as KILLED.

title: Verdict currency: 39 of 41 manifests declare no module, quick-folds' tier rests on a family guess, and the printed remediation is unexecutable for 14 of the 15 builds it names
description:
MetaCoding@523a128 / farmos-port@b57b77d. Three findings that share one cause: the DATA the gate needs is not in the manifests, so the gate infers it from names and then labels the inference 'partition via ...'.

1. THE DECLARED-MODULE PATH IS ALMOST ENTIRELY UNUSED. Counted, not sampled: 2 of 41 manifests declare a 'feature' (identity-quantity-test and spine-misc). The other 39 are resolved by name-derived lookups. The builder disclosed this; it is confirmed and it is larger than it sounds — 'manifest declares module X' is the ONLY lookup in _candidate_lookups() (line 192) that is not mediated by a directory name.

Census of tier sources on the live tree (41 rows):
   6  directory name (FALLBACK)                — labelled honestly
  16  module tail <name>                       — name-derived, labelled 'partition via'
  13  cluster <dirname> / package <pkg>        — name-derived, labelled 'partition via'
   1  module <slug>                            — name-derived
   1  module family <family>/*                 — name-derived, LOOSEST
   2  manifest declares module <feature>       — the only record-anchored path
So 31 of 41 rows say 'partition via' about a lookup whose key came from a directory name. They all happen to land on the right module today, which I verified row by row against the 41 partition rows. The label still overstates what decided them, and 'a build tiered by the fallback is visible as such' (docstring, line 73) is true only for the 6 that reach the literal NAME_RULE.

2. quick-folds. Duke's ruling of 2026-08-12 — quick-folds is IDENTITY per the recorded partition, and the earlier hy6.51 note calling it spine was wrong — IS CORRECT ON THE DATA, and I could not refute it. Both partition files carry five quick/* rows (birth, group, inventory, movement, planting), all tier=identity, all with evidence 'composite multi-entity fold (QuickForm creates asset+log+relations); vocab 0 but structure lane UNAVAILABLE (u00) — tiered UP per cost-asymmetry'. port_runs/wave2/quick-folds/build/port.manifest.json declares it ports exactly those five (farm_quick_birth/group/inventory/movement/planting at farmOS 4.0.4). Five modules, all identity: the build is identity.

The GATE agrees with the record, but not because it read a row about this build. There is NO 'quick/folds' module row, and the manifest declares no 'feature', so resolution falls to the LAST and loosest lookup:
   tier: partition via module family quick/* (quick/birth, quick/group, quick/inventory, quick/movement...)
family is dirname.split('-')[0] (line 217). The answer is robust in direction — if one quick/* row were spine, unanimous() returns UNKNOWN, which also gates — but the gate is agreeing with Duke by coincidence of a name prefix, not by reading a record about quick-folds.

The fix is DATA, and it is blocked by the schema: 'feature' is read as a single string (line 333), so a build that ports five modules cannot declare them. Let the manifest declare a LIST of modules, have quick-folds declare its five, and this row becomes record-anchored and the family heuristic can be deleted.

3. THE REMEDIATION INSTRUCTION DOES NOT WORK FOR 14 OF 15. The refusal prints
   Run: ctkr port-verify <build>/observe/fixtures.jsonl --port <build dir> --json > results/port-verify/<build>.json
Checked each of the 15 named builds for <build>/observe/fixtures.jsonl. Present for exactly ONE (wave1/input). Absent for the other 14 — 11 have no observe/ directory at all (that IS their finding: 'no observe/pack.seal.json'), and wave1-c1/portA and portB share a pack one level up at wave1-c1/observe/, which the seal ascent knows about and the printed command does not. A gate whose printed next step fails for 93% of the builds it refuses is one someone switches off.

Filed by a fresh judge.
notes:
Parts (a) and (b) done. The report now distinguishes 'the partition NAMED this build' from 'a partition row found by GUESSING the module from a directory name' — live: 33 guessed, 2 declared, 5 fallback. feature now accepts a LIST. THE ASYMMETRY IS IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED: TIER_RANK={spine:0,identity:1,unknown:2}; the name-derived reading is computed first and a manifest's declaration decides ONLY when it is >= as strict. An overruled declaration is printed with its reason and the row is NOT marked tier_anchored; declared modules that disagree resolve UNKNOWN. So a self-declaration can RAISE scrutiny and never LOWER it — 'the thesis does not write its own reading' (I2) holds. PART (c) NOT DONE and still open: the printed remediation command assumes <build>/observe/fixtures.jsonl and is unexecutable for 14 of the 15 builds it names.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY JUDGED. The evidence above is the builder's own mutation run, verified by me against the live tree and the suites. By this project's standing rule that is not load-bearing on its own — a fresh adversary has not read it.

title: Per-package manifests are conflated under one build name, and _matches lets one verdict satisfy every build it is a suffix of (mutation SURVIVED)
description:
MetaCoding@53f28ca / farmos-port@b57b77d. Two ways the gate can be satisfied without the work being done.

(1) PER-PACKAGE MANIFESTS ARE CONFLATED. discover() takes the build name from rel[1] - the second path component - so every manifest under one build directory produces a Build with the SAME name, the SAME seal and the SAME verdict lookup. Real counts in wave2:

  spine-asset/build/{compost,equipment,material,plant,product,seed,water}/port.manifest.json  -> 7 rows, all named 'spine-asset'
  spine-taxonomy-a  -> 5 rows,  spine-taxonomy-b -> 4 rows

The headline '34 build(s) declare a manifest' therefore counts manifests while calling them builds; there are only 21 build directories. Consequence: ONE verdict named spine-asset would mark all seven packages verified, and no per-package verdict is even representable - the port field is matched against the build directory name, which cannot distinguish compost from water. Advisory today because these are spine, so it is not currently load-bearing; it becomes load-bearing the first time an identity build ships more than one package.

(2) _matches IS UNTESTED AND OVER-BROAD.

    def _matches(port_field, build_name):
        return port_field == build_name or port_field.endswith(build_name)

Suffix matching is unanchored: a verdict whose port is 'w2-identity-land' satisfies any build named 'identity-land', 'land', or 'entity-land'. Nothing constrains the verdict to the wave either, so a wave-1 verdict for a same-named build would satisfy a wave-2 build. No wave-2 collision exists today - I checked all 21 directory names - so this is latent, not live.

MUTATION EVIDENCE. Against a corrected baseline where all 13 tests pass, I replaced the body of _matches with 'return True' - i.e. ANY verdict satisfies ANY build. The full suite still passed:

  *** SURVIVED *** M10 verdict port matching made universal (any verdict satisfies any build)

It is the only mutation of 12 that survived; the other 11 were each caught. There is no test for _matches at all.

FIX: key builds by their path relative to the wave (so spine-asset/compost is its own row), anchor the match on a wave-prefix-stripped exact comparison rather than endswith, and add the missing red: a verdict naming build A must NOT satisfy build B.
notes: VERIFIED, tree 61a0b3a. Per-package manifests are now separate build rows (keyed by path relative to wave), and _matches is anchored/exact rather than unanchored endswith. Covered by test_PER_PACKAGE_manifests_are_separate_builds, test_a_verdict_for_ONE_package_does_not_verify_ITS_SIBLING, test_a_SINGLE_package_build_is_still_exactly_one_row, test_one_verdict_cannot_satisfy_a_build_its_name_merely_ENDS_WITH, test_a_verdict_from_ANOTHER_WAVE_does_not_satisfy_this_one, test_matching_is_EXACT_on_the_declared_id_or_the_build_key, test_two_builds_declaring_the_SAME_port_id_are_not_scored, test_DISTINCT_port_ids_are_scored_normally — all pass fresh, matching the bead's own M10 mutation regression.

title: Wave scoping silently exempts wave1 and wave1-c1 - 6 live builds with sealed packs and no verdict; only wave0-pilot is actually retired
description:
MetaCoding@53f28ca / farmos-port@b57b77d.

current_wave() gates only the newest wave* directory. The stated justification (verdict_currency.py:99-102):

    'sweeping every historical wave puts retired pilot builds (wave0-pilot, whose
     packs PACKS.jsonl records as RETIRED) permanently in the failing column'

The premise is true and NARROW. port_runs/PACKS.jsonl has exactly 2 RETIRED rows, both wave0 pilot packs, and their reason says: 'The pilot's deliverables are complete and superseded by the wave1/wave2 lanes.' So the retirement record covers wave0-pilot only, and explicitly calls wave1 a live lane.

The implementation excludes wave1 and wave1-c1 too. Those are not retired pilots:

  port_runs/wave1/{activity,harvest,input,observation}/build/port.manifest.json  (4 manifests)
  port_runs/wave1-c1/{portA,portB}/port.manifest.json                            (2 manifests)

and they have sealed packs:

  port_runs/wave1/{activity,harvest,input,observation}/observe/pack.seal.json
  port_runs/wave1-c1/observe/pack.seal.json

results/port-verify/ contains only the four wave-2 identity verdicts. So six builds hold a manifest and a sealed pack, have no verdict of record, and are invisible to the gate - and 'has a sealed pack' is precisely the condition the gate treats as 'this build could have been driven'. At least log/input is recorded IDENTITY tier in the partition.

An exclusion justified by wave0-pilot's retirement should exclude wave0-pilot, not everything that is not newest. Note also that the newest-directory rule is lexicographic over os.listdir - 'wave10' would sort before 'wave2' and silently move the gate to the wrong wave.

FIX: scope by the retirement record (skip builds whose pack is RETIRED in PACKS.jsonl) rather than by recency, or make --wave accept multiple waves and default to all non-retired. Either way wave1/wave1-c1 should be answered for, not omitted.
notes: VERIFIED, tree 61a0b3a. Wave scoping now keyed off the PACKS.jsonl retirement record rather than directory recency; wave1/wave1-c1 are answered for. Covered by test_an_OLDER_wave_that_was_never_retired_is_still_answered_for, test_a_build_whose_pack_the_RECORD_retires_is_exempt, test_retirement_keeps_the_gate_from_being_permanently_red, test_a_pack_seal_that_is_NOT_in_the_retirement_record_is_not_exempt, test_wave_narrows_the_sweep_by_hand — all pass fresh. Note: hy6.58 (closed separately, commit 61a0b3a) subsequently found and fixed a P0 in this same retirement-scoping mechanism (unscoped retired-seal exemption); that fix is verified live in the current 37/37 run, so this bead's scoping-by-retirement approach is confirmed sound as of HEAD.

title: The advertised verb discriminate() does not enforce — dropping its result is the cheapest green for every adopter
description:
discriminate() returns a DiscriminationResult and never throws (src/testkit/discriminate.ts:130-134). assertDiscriminates() is the enforcing verb. But discriminate() is the name in the design document (docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md:78), in the module header, in the file name, and in the pointer added to CLAUDE.md:198-201.

MEASURED, tree 751e7442, 2026-08-12:

    await discriminate({ name: "...", verdict: () => "SAME", cases: { A: "a", B: "b" } });

returns ok:false — DUPLICATE_TAG + UNREACHED_TAG — and the test containing it is GREEN, because nothing consumed the result. A pair that REFUSED, inside a passing suite. That is failure shape #1 from the design document ('an instrument that cannot fail') reproduced at the adoption seam of the mechanism written to close it.

The stated reason for the non-throwing default (discriminate.ts:131-134: the module's own fixtures must observe a REFUSAL without the suite dying) is real but argues only for the EXISTENCE of a non-throwing form, not for it owning the short name.

FIX: make discriminate() throw on !ok and export the raw form under a name that reads like what it is (e.g. discriminateRaw / runPair), used only by discriminate.test.ts. Migrate seam.test.ts's 'if (!result.ok) throw new Error(explain(result))' onto it.
NOTE the interaction with MetaCoding-04i and mechanism 4: today a dropped result is at least still in recordedPairs() with ok:false, so publishing the record (floors.ts) is the other half of this fix, not a substitute for it.
acceptance_criteria: The verb named in CLAUDE.md and the design document fails a suite when its pair refuses; a fixture proves a dropped/ignored refusal does not produce a green test; the module's own fixtures still observe refusals via the explicitly-named raw form.
notes: VERIFIED BY FRESH MUTATION, tree 61a0b3a. discriminate() now throws on !ok; observeDiscrimination is the non-enforcing raw form used only by the module's own fixtures. Independently re-mutated: commented out 'if (!r.ok) throw new Error(explain(r))' — discriminate.test.ts's RECORD_SINK_UNWRITABLE throw-assertion test failed as expected. Tree restored, diff-verified clean. Regression test: discriminate.test.ts:234 'discriminate() THROWS with the named difference; ignoring the result is not green'.

title: EMPTY_TAG is a declared PairFailureKind with no fixture — deleting the check survives the suite
description:
src/testkit/discriminate.ts:72 declares EMPTY_TAG in the closed PairFailureKind vocabulary and discriminate.ts:150-156 raises it. Nothing exercises it.

MEASURED, tree 751e7442, 2026-08-12: neutering the EMPTY_TAG push -> 33 pass / 0 fail across src/testkit/discriminate.test.ts + src/ingest/seam.test.ts. SURVIVED. It is the only failure kind in the vocabulary with no fixture (NOT_A_PAIR, RESERVED_TAG_DECLARED, NON_TAG_VERDICT, UNCAUGHT_THROW, UNDECLARED_TAG, WRONG_TAG, DUPLICATE_TAG and UNREACHED_TAG were each independently mutated and each KILLED at least one fixture).

This is the file whose own header says the instrument tier applies to the testkit before anything else, and whose own test file opens with 'a check only ever seen to pass is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail'. An unexercised member of a closed vocabulary is the unnamed escape member that vocabulary exists to prevent.

FIX: a fixture for cases: { "": x, ALLOWED: y } (and the blank-string variant) asserting EMPTY_TAG, plus the passing contrast with a named tag. Three lines.
acceptance_criteria: Neutering the EMPTY_TAG push fails at least one fixture, and the same pair with a non-empty tag passes.
notes:
EMPTY_TAG now has a fixture at src/testkit/discriminate.test.ts:268-278 — it asserts the kind is produced AND that the declared tag is the empty string, so the closed vocabulary has no unreachable member.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE, NOT AGAINST A REPORT: 64 pass / 0 fail across src/testkit on 2026-08-12.

TWO CAVEATS, both honest:
1. NOT INDEPENDENTLY JUDGED. No fresh adversary has read this work.
2. ITS EVIDENCE COMMIT WAS LOST. The agent that did this work was killed by an API error, and before dying it reported that its changes had already been swept into MetaCoding e477693 — a commit labelled fix(hy6.60) that actually carries 13 files from three different agents, because one of them staged everything. So the code is present and passing, but the mutation table that would normally accompany it does not exist. See MetaCoding 96877c9, which records the misattribution and adds a hook refusing the stage-everything flag.

title: explain()'s 'the difference must be NAMED' half is untested — the assertion is satisfied by the vocabulary line
description:
src/testkit/discriminate.test.ts:117-119 carries the comment 'the report NAMES which tags were never reached' and asserts:
    expect(explain(r)).toContain("WRONG_SLICE");
    expect(explain(r)).toContain("ALLOWED");

Those two strings are ALREADY in explain()'s second line — '  vocabulary: [${r.declared.join(", ")}]' (discriminate.ts:270). So the assertion passes for ANY explain() that echoes the declared vocabulary, whether or not it says anything about what was unreached.

MEASURED, tree 751e7442, 2026-08-12:
  - mutate discriminate.ts:271 so the per-tag lines become '  <redacted>' (drop tag -> observed entirely)  -> 33 pass / 0 fail. SURVIVED.
  - mutate discriminate.ts:272 to drop f.detail, printing only f.kind               -> 33 pass / 0 fail. SURVIVED.

Only explain()'s FIRST line is load-bearing anywhere, and only via 'rejects.toThrow(/DUPLICATE_TAG/)' (discriminate.test.ts:189) — mutating explain() to a header-only string containing the literal 'DUPLICATE_TAG' kills exactly one test, and that one only because of the regex.

WHY IT MATTERS: 'the difference must be NAMED' is the fourth of the four things the module says a pair is (discriminate.ts:6-8) and the one the commit message leans on ('reported by name, not as expected X got Y at the first assertion'). It is the only one of the four with no fixture that can fail.

FIX: assert on structure, not substrings — e.g. that explain() contains a line matching /! UNREACHED_TAG: .*"WRONG_SLICE"/ and a line matching /NO_TOKEN -> NO_TOKEN/, and a contrast asserting a tag that WAS reached is not reported as unreached.
acceptance_criteria: Mutating explain() to drop the per-tag observed lines fails a fixture; mutating it to drop f.detail fails a fixture; the intact explain() passes.
notes:
explain()'s NAMED half is exercised at src/testkit/discriminate.test.ts:124-156 — the report must contain the named difference, which is the third of the three rules discriminate() exists to enforce.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE, NOT AGAINST A REPORT: 64 pass / 0 fail across src/testkit on 2026-08-12.

TWO CAVEATS, both honest:
1. NOT INDEPENDENTLY JUDGED. No fresh adversary has read this work.
2. ITS EVIDENCE COMMIT WAS LOST. The agent that did this work was killed by an API error, and before dying it reported that its changes had already been swept into MetaCoding e477693 — a commit labelled fix(hy6.60) that actually carries 13 files from three different agents, because one of them staged everything. So the code is present and passing, but the mutation table that would normally accompany it does not exist. See MetaCoding 96877c9, which records the misattribution and adds a hook refusing the stage-everything flag.

title: The four clean verdicts rest on packs recorded before step 4's own preflight precondition — the seal carries no preflight attestation
description:
All four wave-2 packs step 8 cites were recorded 2026-07-23:

  identity-sensor      provenance.recorded_at 2026-07-23
  identity-plant-type  2026-07-23
  identity-lab-test    2026-07-23
  identity-structure   2026-07-23

Step 4's oracle preflight became a non-optional PRECONDITION on 2026-08-07 (hy6.25/hy6.28), because two ports on 2026-08-03 probed bundles that were never enabled and recorded as findings about farmOS what were measurements of the oracle. The only four packs step 8 can currently reach predate that gate by two weeks and were never subjected to it.

pack.seal.json carries: derivations, fixture_ids, fixtures_blake3, observations_blake3, pack_id, recorded_at, seal, source_system. There is no field attesting that the recording ran behind a passing preflight, so step 8 cannot tell an ungated pack from a gated one, and a 100%-clean verdict over an ungated pack is exactly the composition hole hy6.28 closed one step upstream.

FIX: mint a preflight attestation into the seal at record time (module set + oracle pin + preflight verdict), and have port-verify refuse — or at minimum mark NOT-GATED — a pack whose seal carries none. Then decide whether the four 2026-07-23 packs need re-observation.

title: Wire --require-current into the irreversible steps (freeze, seal, re-baseline, elicitation menu)
description: The charter and the wave plan now say a kernel freeze / wave seal / oracle re-baseline / elicitation menu may not proceed on a stale reading of the whole, and ctkr/ctkr/elenchus.py --require-current implements the refusal. NOTHING CALLS IT. That is the hy6.28 shape exactly — a gate that exists, is cheap, is correct, and is invoked by nobody — and it is fair to say the mechanism is currently prose plus a command. TO CLOSE: each irreversible step invokes it, or a documented reason why that step is exempt. Note the deliberate asymmetry this must preserve: the FLAGS must keep exiting 0 (mutation-tested), only the ACT is gated.
notes:
DISPOSITION CHANGED 2026-08-12, and the change is worth recording because it reverses my own recommendation.

docs/design/enforceability.md recommended DELETING --require-current under disposition 3 (admit it is philosophy, delete the executable pretence), on the grounds that the irreversible step it guards — wave-close sealing — is a human act with no code path, so the flag was a gate hung on nothing.

THAT REASONING IS NOW STALE. Duke ruled on 2026-08-12 that the wave transition IS a command and that `wave open` REFUSES while the predecessor is open, with a --force override that records its reason (docs/design/wave-transition.md). The call site is no longer absent — it is DECIDED AND UNBUILT, which is a different status entirely. Deleting the flag now would mean re-adding it when wave-close lands.

SO: KEEP, blocked on the wave-close command rather than orphaned. What must NOT happen is this sitting here for another month while its bead still says 'wire it into the irreversible steps' — if wave-close does not get built, the deletion recommendation comes back, because a gate awaiting a call site that never arrives is indistinguishable from a gate hung on nothing.

Note the asymmetry with hy6.54: verdict_currency has a second home (a ratchet in bun test) and should get it regardless. --require-current has only the one.

title: One gate injection now disables two guards, and 19 of 29 ledger tests run with the new one off — this one was closeable, not just nameable
description:
Fresh judge round two, farmos-port 587c193.

ledger.py:404-406 fails open when the gate's report carries no 'advertised':
    advertised = (report or {}).get('advertised') if isinstance(report, dict) else None
    if not advertised:
        return None
Measured, both branches:
  C. gate=lambda ...: {'stub': True, 'types': [...]}  against a transport whose index advertises NOTHING we declared -> preflight PASSED, transport calls during preflight: [], PREFLIGHT row same_oracle: None.
  D. gate=lambda ...: {'advertised': []}              -> preflight PASSED, same_oracle: None.

The builder named this in the docstring ('one injection turns off two guards') and closed hy6.38 on that basis. For the resource_type() fail-open that was the right call and I said so — failing closed would refuse /oauth/token. THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT: there is no legitimate call that needs it. It exists so the test suite's StubGate (test_ledger.py:170-186, returns {'stub': True, 'types': ...}) keeps working.

Scale of it, measured by MUTATION N8 (make an absent 'advertised' a refusal): test_ledger.py fails 19 of 29. Nineteen tests run today with the same-oracle guard silently switched off, including test_hy628_run_gates_before_the_body_and_a_REFUSAL_probes_NOTHING, whose 'calls == 0' assertion would no longer hold against a real gate (the same-oracle check legitimately sends one GET /api).

That is the 'flagged, not closed' move this session already corrected once. Closing it is cheap: give Ledger an explicit field (e.g. same_oracle=True) and refuse when the gate reports no index unless the ledger opted out — then StubGate-based tests DECLARE that they are running without the check instead of getting it silently.

Also missing: there is no test at all pinning the fail-open. If someone changes it in either direction, nothing says so.

MUTATION N6 (drop 'same_oracle' from the PREFLIGHT row) also SURVIVED — the row field the builder claims as evidence (claim 3) is untested.
MUTATION N7 (compute missing from the gate's 'advertised' instead of declared_types()) also SURVIVED — the three new tests use fixtures where those two sets are equal, so they do not pin which set is compared.
notes: CLOSED, not documented — the judge asked directly whether naming it was enough, and here the answer was no. No legitimate caller needs the fail-open; it existed so StubGate kept working. A gate that will not say which oracle it cleared is now a refusal (absent AND present-but-empty), and require_same_oracle=False is an explicit field a harness sets and a build does not. Blast radius the judge measured first: 19 of 29 tests ran with the guard silently off, including the one asserting a refusal probes nothing.

title: The same-oracle check catches SUBSET differences only — superset, same-index-different-pin, and the docker container identity all pass
description:
Fresh judge round two, farmos-port 587c193.

ledger.py:414 computes missing = declared_types() - seen and refuses only when that is non-empty. So the check is 'the transport's index is a SUPERSET of what I declared'. Measured against the shipped code:

  A. SUPERSET: gate saw 46 types; transport reaches a DIFFERENT host advertising 49 (all 46 plus asset--plant, log--medical, organization--farm).
     -> preflight PASSED. gated = ['asset--animal','log--activity']
  B. IDENTICAL INDEX, different farmOS build/pin: preflight PASSED. Nothing in the check reads a version, an image pin, a Drupal build id or a site uuid.

The docstring at ledger.py:389-393 claims more than that: 'a same-host-different-module-set — the quiet case, and the one hy6.25 exists for — is caught by the type comparison rather than by the hostname.' Only half true. hy6.25's actual case is a module HAND-ENABLED and therefore present — a SUPERSET — and the type comparison cannot see it. It catches the module that is MISSING, which is the loud half.

THIRD UNBOUND IDENTITY. There are now three names for 'the oracle':
  $ORACLE           the ledger's transport            (each build)
  $ORACLE_URL       the gate's HTTP base_url          (oracle_preflight.py:93)
  $ORACLE_CONTAINER the module-drift docker container (oracle_preflight.py:94, installed_modules())
587c193 binds the first two, partially. NOTHING binds either to the third. Point ORACLE_CONTAINER at a different container and the module-drift verdict — the half hy6.28 just made mandatory — is about a farmOS nobody probed, and same_oracle still records OK.

ALSO (cosmetic, but this project treats it as a defect class): a same-oracle refusal writes 'NOTHING BELOW THIS LINE RAN — no probe, no fixture, no cleanup needed' (ledger.py:367-370) after one GET /api HAS gone out through the transport. Measured: transport calls actually made: [('GET', '/api')]. The row understates its own traffic.

REMEDY: compare a site identity, not a type set — GET /api/asset/animal?page[limit]=0 is not it, but Drupal exposes a site uuid via drush and farmOS's /api meta carries links; at minimum have the gate return base_url and the ledger assert that a same-host probe reaches it, and bind ORACLE_CONTAINER by asserting the container's own base URL. Failing that, narrow the docstring claim to what the check actually does.
notes: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED in farmos-port 824dd3c: the docstring overclaim is fixed (the check is stated as the SUBSET check it is, with the hand-enabled/superset case named as what it CANNOT see), and the third unbound identity $ORACLE_CONTAINER is named in the same place. The refusal row no longer claims nothing ran when one GET /api has gone out. STILL OPEN, and this is the substance: nothing binds $ORACLE_CONTAINER to either HTTP identity, so the module-drift verdict can be about a farmOS nobody probed. A pin/build-id comparison would also close the identical-index-different-build case. Both need a farmOS identity beyond the type list.

title: The ledger's gate is not bound to the ledger's transport — it can clear a different oracle than the run probes
description:
Fresh judge of hy6.28 (farmos-port 6a75c1d).

tools/ledger.py:300 defaults gate=require_types and tools/ledger.py:348 calls self.gate(types) with NO base_url. require_types therefore uses oracle_preflight.DEFAULT_BASE_URL, which reads the env var ORACLE_URL (oracle_preflight.py:93). Every observe build reads a DIFFERENT env var for its transport: ORACLE (identity-farm-org/observe/verify.py:38, and the same in the other four).

Demonstrated, verbatim:

  $ ORACLE=http://127.0.0.1:9/nowhere python3 -c "..."
  verify.py transport target (ORACLE): http://127.0.0.1:9/nowhere
  gate target (oracle_preflight DEFAULT_BASE_URL / ORACLE_URL): http://localhost:8095
  gate returned OK for base_url = http://localhost:8095
  => the gate cleared http://localhost:8095 while the ledger would probe http://127.0.0.1:9/nowhere

The Ledger has no field naming the oracle it is probing, so it cannot pass one, and nothing cross-checks the two. The property says a build may not begin probing before the preflight; today it may begin probing oracle B after preflighting oracle A. The PREFLIGHT row it writes even records base_url — of the wrong host — as evidence.

Realist check: with both vars unset the two agree, and a genuinely wrong target fails loudly on every request rather than silently. But the whole point of hy6.25/.28 is that oracle-shaped failures read as farmOS findings, and a HALF-wrong oracle (right host, older pin, different module set) is exactly the quiet case.

REMEDY: give Ledger a base_url field, default os.environ.get('ORACLE', ...), and pass it into the gate — or standardise on one env var name and assert it.
notes:
JUDGE ROUND TWO (farmos-port 587c193): close CONFIRMED for the demonstrated hole, with one correction to these notes.

REPRODUCED LIVE, not taken on the transcript. Started /tmp/otherfarm.py on 127.0.0.1:8099, ran the real identity-farm-org verify.py with ORACLE pointed at it and the gate on :8095:
  RUN: aborted by UngatedProbe: THE GATE CLEARED A DIFFERENT ORACLE. It found 46 resource types; this run's own transport reaches an index of 2 that is missing: asset--group, asset--land, log--observation, organization--farm, taxonomy_term--animal_type.
Verbatim match. Zero probes sent. The 'a dead host is not sufficient' claim is also true: ORACLE=http://127.0.0.1:9 dies at verify.py's own module-level TOK = token() with URLError before the ledger exists, so the reachable-but-different host really is the discriminating fixture.

CORRECTION TO THESE NOTES. 'a type comparison, not a hostname one, because the quiet case is the same host with a different module set' overclaims. The check is declared_types() SUBSET-OF transport-index. It catches a module that is MISSING. It does NOT catch a SUPERSET — measured: a different host advertising 49 types where the gate saw 46 passes — and hy6.25's own case (a module HAND-ENABLED, therefore present, gone on the next rebuild) is a superset case. Nor does it see a pin change with an identical index. Filed as hy6.42, with the third unbound identity ($ORACLE_CONTAINER) alongside.

And the repair is only as live as its untested contract: see hy6.41 — one line in oracle_preflight.preflight() disarms it with all 47 checks still green.

title: Migrate the three pre-ledger checkers onto tools/ledger.py — they still hand-declare their preflight types
description:
hy6.28 gave Ledger-based builds a preflight whose type list is DERIVED from the
run's own collections, and refuses any probe outside it. identity-birth,
identity-seeding and identity-group are pre-ledger: 500-940 line hand-written
checkers that call require_types() with a HAND-WRITTEN LIST. They inherit the
require_modules default flip (the drift check is now required) but NOT the
derivation — so each is exactly the shape farm-org was found in: a declaration
that can name fewer types than the run probes, passing by being asked the wrong
question.

TO CLOSE: either they run on Ledger, or their type lists are cross-checked
against their actual probe traffic. Do NOT hand-audit and declare them correct —
that is self-verification, and the farm-org gap survived two readings.

Check for the same gap while migrating: ledger.py's guards (per-section floors,
finally-cleanup, by-ID absence, links.next pagination) were adopted additively by
these three, not by construction.
notes: DUPLICATE of MetaCoding-hy6.36, which the hy6.28 judge filed with a wider and more accurate scope: FOUR builds, not three. I missed identity-transplanting entirely — it has NO oracle_preflight at all, only a bespoke inline gate (two GETs plus a POST/DELETE ping), so the module-drift half never runs there and it POSTs a fixture to the shared oracle before any gate. Work the real one.

title: The FormBuilder caveat is missing from the BOUND kernel decision, and the atomicity claim was measured on the wrong side of a catch
description:
FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07. The caveat that driving a Drupal form through FormBuilder is not the HTTP boundary is stated twice and relied on across ~22 claim sites in 6 files — including the BOUND decision log-category-membership (kernel-9h5.24/build/cm-decisions.jsonl:41, kernelConfig.ts:366), which carries no caveat at all.
And it is not a formality. The probes instantiate the PLUGIN as the form object, so QuickForm::submitForm()'s catch (EntityMalformedException) at QuickForm.php:133-142 is never traversed — meaning the quick-folds manifest's headline 'NO ATOMICITY: a form that dies halfway leaves what it created' was measured on the wrong side of the catch. Over HTTP that path is a 200 with a messenger error; in the probe it is a raised Throwable. Same for FormBuilder.php:1307's programmatic-input NULL-fill, which flips Birth.php:338's archived => empty($child['survived']) between the two paths.

title: The 43 sealed packs were never re-recorded against the 128-module oracle, and pack provenance cannot represent the change
description:
FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07. port_runs/PACKS.jsonl: 43 rows, latest recorded_at 2026-07-28, zero on or after 08-07. All 41 live packs carry source_version '4.x' and NO module set, so no artifact anywhere could show a pack was recorded against a different oracle than the one now running. Ask the methodology's own question — would this look identical whether or not the claim were true? Byte-identical.
Commit 8458c9e named this risk itself ('some assert 201s and 422s on writes those validators would now see') and said it should be followed by re-running the affected ledgers; the follow-through re-ran FOUR hardened ledgers, not the 43 packs. And the four-ledger evidence is admitted non-discriminating for the one change that was measured: farm_farm adds 'farm' to asset relationships, and the ledgers do not assert asset relationship key sets. The evidence class that passed is the class blind to the change that happened.
Also: the module count is not re-derivable — drush pm:list --status=enabled --type=module gives 127, not the claimed 128, and the counting method is not stated. Either re-record, retire, or add module-set provenance to a pack.

title: Four guards lost when the four ledgers were consolidated — the 'union by construction' claim is not true
description:
FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07. Missing from tools/ledger.py but present in a hand-written build: (1) preflight refusal — it lives only in oracle_preflight.py and every adopter must remember to call it by hand, which is the exact 'guard nobody must remember' shape hy6.28 exists for; (2) a RAISING PREDICATE becomes a crash rather than recorded drift (group had this); (3) recover_untracked — seeding's own measured D7 case produces an entity with NO returned id, invisible to both the by-ID check and the prefix sweep; (4) derived check(). Either carry them or delete the 'by construction' language from the module docstring and the commit record.
ALSO: identity-group/observe/verify.py:504-505 is 'finally: _ran = True' and _ran is never read — the cleanup that commit f58582c credits with closing J7 is straight-line code after the try.

title: ledger floors do not bind: Floors() and sections=[] defaults make the empty run a success
description: FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07. tools/ledger.py:145 Floors(fixtures=0, checks=0), :201 sections=[], :128 Section.min_fixtures=0 are all defaults, and nothing cross-checks declared floors against anything. A ledger with no sections and default floors exits 0 with an empty failure list — while evaluate_floors' own docstring says 'the cheapest green is an EMPTY run... Both are failures rather than successes'. The J8 padding admission is also understated: section_of derives the section id from the leading letters of a probe id the padder writes, so per-section attribution costs an f-string; padding also satisfies the structural guard via expect=lambda r: True; and ghost uuids 404, so the authoritative by-ID check stays silent. Needs a meta-floor: a ledger that declares no sections, or floors of zero, is itself a defect.

title: src/testkit/mutate.ts — mutant must parse, anchor must match, baseline clean before AND after
description:
From docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md, mechanism 5. Deliberately LAST: it is the expensive general form of what discriminate() and floors buy cheaply, and if those catch the cases that mattered this earns much less than the session's experience suggests — which should change the decision rather than be argued away.

THREE GUARDS, each paid for by a real failure:
1. THE MUTANT MUST PARSE. A mutant that died of SyntaxError exited 1 and looked exactly like a detection. Parse — not typecheck — is the right bar, since bun test does not typecheck and requiring it would reject legitimate mutants.
2. THE ANCHOR MUST HAVE MATCHED. A replacement with wrong indentation silently did not match, the suite ran unmodified, and '0 fail' read exactly like 'the suite cannot catch this'.
3. BASELINE CLEAN BEFORE AND AFTER, restoring from a byte copy and mutating in a TEMPORARY WORKTREE rather than in place.

SCOPE: instrument tier only, and the instruments are enumerable rather than a policy — src/ingest/fitness.ts, src/ingest/ticket.ts, src/store/build.ts, the toolchain identity module, the census, and src/testkit/ itself.

THE ARCHITECT'S OWN ATTACK ON IT: worktree isolation is the same thing that can leave the suite pointed at a stale tree — iteration-methodology.md:22's 'a validation workflow graded a tree that did not contain the change'. The harness must PRINT the tree digest it tested.
acceptance_criteria: Four fixtures: (F5.1) an unparseable mutant reports UNPARSEABLE, never KILLED, contrasted with a parseable failing mutant reporting KILLED — indistinguishable today; (F5.2) a non-matching anchor reports NOT_APPLIED, never SURVIVED, contrasted with a matching anchor whose mutant survives, which is a finding — both read '0 fail' today; (F5.3) a dirty baseline is refused before any mutation runs, and the printed tree digest matches the mutated tree; (F5.4) delete one case from recognizeDeclaration and the census names the type.

title: ctkr/ctkr/oracle/custody.py — the guard that does not depend on being imported
description:
From docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md, mechanism 2 — the architect's own strongest claim, and the failure that cost this session hours TWICE.

THE NAIVE FIX IS DEAD ON ARRIVAL, and the document kills it explicitly: 'put the guards in ledger.py and require every probe to import them' fails because the OAuth password grant is six lines of urllib. Enforcement-by-import over a shared external resource is the text-scanner failure of seam.test.ts in another medium — its coverage is the set of entry points its author imagined, and the stranding probe was the one they did not. src/ingest/ticket.ts works for the graph store ONLY because MetaCoding owns that write path. Nobody owns farmOS's.

SO THE GUARD SITS OUTSIDE THE PROBE, IN THE THING THAT BRACKETS IT. --begin takes a paginated by-ID census of every collection the build's declared resource types resolve to (the list oracle_preflight already requires it to name). --end re-censuses and diffs; any id present at end, absent at begin, and tracked by no ledger in the run is reported by id, collection and name.

LOUD AND ADVISORY, NEVER A DELETION. Deleting a row the bracket did not create is what ledger.py:357 already refuses by name; on a shared oracle 'clean up what you find' is the most dangerous possible behaviour.

HANDLES WORSE, stated by the architect rather than discovered later: the census cannot attribute, so concurrent runs see each other's rows as unexplained. Mitigation is to RANK by whether a name matches any known run prefix, and the honest fallback is to accept the noise — a false positive costs a minute of reading; the false negative cost hours and recurred.
acceptance_criteria: Called from ctkr/ctkr/oracle/runner.py around every oracle-touching build, plus a CLI for hand runs. The probe changes NOTHING — the guard must not be in its import graph. Three fixtures: (F2.1) a probe that creates one fixture and does not delete it is reported by id, and the same probe with cleanup is clean — BOTH exit 0 today; (F2.2) a DERIVED-NAME log matching no fixture prefix is reported, proving the census is by id and not by prefix; (F2.3) a run creating and correctly deleting 70 rows across the 50-row page boundary is clean with no pagination false positive, contrasted with MAX_PAGES=1 where the leak is invisible.

title: lab_test has no cleanup script and no absence check — its fixtures came through the sealed-pack recorder
description:
Split out of MetaCoding-hy6.31 on 2026-08-07, because it is a different job from the other four.

birth, seeding, transplanting, group and medical all had a cleanup script with a .created ledger, so hardening them meant adding a by-ID absence check to something that existed. lab_test has NEITHER: port_runs/wave2/identity-lab-test/observe/ holds only fixtures.jsonl, observations.jsonl and pack.seal.json. The fixtures (w2z- prefix) were created through the ctkr oracle recorder, not through a probe script, so there is no per-run ledger of created ids and nothing anywhere asserts they were removed.

The oracle is SHARED. A recorder run that dies, or one whose fixtures outlive it, strands entities that no build owns — and for a log bundle with name_pattern the strays carry farmOS-derived names that no prefix sweep can see (the hy6.31 hole).

Checked 2026-08-07: zero w2z- rows and zero derived Lab-test logs on the oracle, so nothing is stranded right now.
acceptance_criteria: The recorder harness records the ids it creates, and a check reaches them BY ID after the run, following logs through the assets they reference. Proven by the same neutered-cleanup contrast the other five carry: with the delete pass disabled the by-ID check FAILS while a name-prefix sweep reads clean; with it enabled, both are clean. tools/ledger.py supplies the by-ID absence check, the 403 reach-through and pagination.

title: TS extractor blind spots: arrow-function declarations, and anonymous class/object-literal MISATTRIBUTION
description:
Two different severities in one bead because they share a call site.

OMISSION — 'export const useThing = (a) => {...}' parses as lexical_declaration > variable_declarator > arrow_function and typescript.ts:117-141 has a case for none of the three. Zero symbols, zero candidates. 1,285 arrow_function occurrences in MetaCoding's OWN src/.

MISATTRIBUTION, and this one is worse — 'export default class { hidden() {} }' has node type 'class', not 'class_declaration', so recognizeDeclaration returns null (typescript.ts:138-140) and walk recurses at :112-114 WITH PARENT STILL THE FILE SYMBOL. The graph gains 'method a.ts::hidden' CONTAINED BY THE FILE: a containment relation that does not exist in the source. Same shape for object-literal methods — const o = { render() {} }.

The misattribution half is the case the census in within-file-coverage.md explicitly CANNOT catch: the type is claimed, output was emitted, and it is wrong. It needs the cross-lane differential instrument instead.
acceptance_criteria: Arrow-function declarations emit symbols. Anonymous class and object-literal methods are either attributed correctly or not emitted at all — never attributed to the file. Evidence for the second half must be the cross-lane check: SCIP places 'hidden' inside the anonymous class, tree-sitter places it inside the file, and the disagreement is detected.

title: PHP extractor blind spots: promoted properties, attributes, new, class constants
description:
The four the census (within-file-coverage.md) would rank first for farmOS. Each is a fix the census exists to have found.

1. CONSTRUCTOR PROPERTY PROMOTION — 376 occurrences in farmos-src. 'public function __construct(private LoggerInterface $logger)' yields NO field symbol: php.ts:132-179 recognizeDeclaration has no property_promotion_parameter case. And the loss compounds — a method body reading $this->logger produces a READS_FIELD candidate (edges.ts:1138-1175) whose target does not exist, isDrupalEntityField is false (name lacks the field_ prefix), so walker.ts:326-329 drops it SILENTLY. Every promoted service dependency in modern Drupal/Symfony is invisible, and so is every read of one.
2. ATTRIBUTES — 587 occurrences. No attribute_group case in walkPhp; zero ANNOTATES for PHP. Drupal declares every plugin this way.
3. new Foo() — 472 object_creation_expression occurrences; the PHP lane emits no CONSTRUCTS at all.
4. class constants — 393 class_constant_access_expression, 35 const_declaration.
acceptance_criteria: Each form emits the symbol or edge it should. Evidence per within-file-coverage.md #2: the promoted-constructor class yields the field symbols AND the READS_FIELD for $this->logger; CONTRAST the classically-declared equivalent, which yields both today. Identical semantics, different syntax, and the graph must stop depending on which was used.
notes:
PORT RELEVANCE, flagged 2026-08-07 — read before parking this as 'PHP polish'.

Duke deprioritized PHP work because farmOS is the only PHP project. But farmOS IS the port SOURCE, and these two gaps are relationships that exist in the code being ported and are absent from the graph the port reads:

  * 376 promoted constructor parameters -> every service DEPENDENCY of a modern Drupal/Symfony class is invisible, and so is every $this->dep read of one (the READS_FIELD candidate is dropped for want of a target).
  * 587 attribute_group -> Drupal declares every PLUGIN with an attribute. Zero ANNOTATES for PHP means plugin identity is not in the graph.

So this is not generic PHP extractor quality. Whether it matters depends on whether the port recipe's mining step leans on service dependencies or plugin declarations — if it does, this is a hole in the instrument, not in a language lane. Left at P2 pending that call.

title: The static capability table is WRONG for PHP — five of eleven edge kinds it claims cannot be emitted
description:
BLOCKS implementation of docs/design/coverage-claims.md. Found by a fresh architect 2026-08-06 (docs/design/within-file-coverage.md, fixture 2), by running the SHIPPED extractors rather than reading the doc.

graph-as-cache.md:81 states, without language qualification, that the tree-sitter lane emits CONTAINS/EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS/USES_TRAIT/READS_FIELD/WRITES_FIELD/CONSTRUCTS/RAISES/RETURNS_TYPE/ANNOTATES/TYPE_OF.

For PHP, FIVE of those eleven are FALSE. src/extractor/edges.ts:1040-1068 (walkPhp) dispatches on exactly six node types: class_declaration, interface_declaration, assignment_expression, augmented_assignment_expression, member_access_expression, member_call_expression. No attribute_group, no object_creation_expression, no throw_expression, no return_type. So the PHP lane emits CONTAINS/EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS/USES_TRAIT/READS_FIELD/WRITES_FIELD and NOTHING ELSE.

WHY THIS IS P0 AND NOT A DOC NIT: coverage-claims.md makes that table LOAD-BEARING. A 'complete' ANNOTATES claim would be minted over all 789 farmOS PHP files while 587 attribute_group nodes sit unseen — an authoritative empty answer to 'what annotates this Drupal plugin'. That is MetaCoding-hy6.16 reproduced WITH the new design's blessing, which is strictly worse than today's silence. coverage-claims.md:147 names this exact failure: 'a wrong row in the static capability table does maximum damage per byte'. It is already wrong, before a line has been implemented.

MEASURED on /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/farmos-src (789 PHP files): attribute_group 587, object_creation_expression 472, class_constant_access_expression 393, throw_expression 47, const_declaration 35.
acceptance_criteria: The table is corrected per-language, AND ships with the fixture that catches its regression: a PHP file containing new Foo(), throw new Bar(), #[Attr] and a typed return asserts ZERO CONSTRUCTS/RAISES/ANNOTATES/RETURNS_TYPE from the tree-sitter lane; CONTRAST: the same four shapes in TypeScript emit all four. Same edge kinds, two languages, opposite verdicts. A doc edit alone does not close this.
notes:
DEPRIORITIZED 2026-08-07 (Duke): farmOS is probably the only PHP project this is used on, and the focus is the port. Downgraded P0 -> P2.

The P0 framing was 'blocks coverage-claims implementation'. That is still true and still the trigger: nothing in CODE consults this table today, so it cannot poison a query yet — it becomes load-bearing the moment coverage-claims ships. Fix it THEN, or delete the table's PHP row rather than carry a false one.

title: docs/design/index-fitness.md: two claims the code does not support (Store.upsertSymbol re-closed; basename distinguishes vendoring)
description:
FRESH-JUDGE-3 FINDING at HEAD 05d8a93 (doc last touched 4b0645d).

1. Fake-it #3 says 'any direct Store.upsertSymbol leaves a stale HEALTHY ... **Refuted and re-closed (MetaCoding-9ed)**'. Executed at HEAD: a bare store.upsertSymbol loop took a HEALTHY slice from 12 to 28 symbols with the record still reading fitness 12. The doc names the exact mechanism and marks it closed. See MetaCoding-qv0.

2. Line ~186: 'Basename correspondence distinguishes farmOS-in-Docker (every farm_animal.module appears in both sets) from a vendored-dependency index (no basename corresponds).' Two problems: (a) eeb2bf8 made basename a REFUSAL, so the sentence describes the superseded design; (b) the premise is false — a vendored copy shares basenames by construction, and worse, it shares path SUFFIXES, so it lands on rung 2 with ratio 1.0. See MetaCoding-5fi.

Item 6 of 'Evidence that must ship with it' ('an unrelated-basename index UNMEASURABLE') should also be restated now that basename is a named failure code rather than a rung that passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: ctkr artifact staleness compares generated_at as a STRING, so a malformed or future stamp defeats it
description:
FRESH-JUDGE-3 FINDING at HEAD 05d8a93 (src/mcp/ctkr-tools.ts sha256 35d1dd8c31bd...), from the MetaCoding-0mu verification.

ctkr-tools.ts:151-174 computes newestFinalize as the max finished_at over readAllIndexHealth and refuses when 'newestFinalize > builtAt'. Both operands are raw strings; there is no Date parse and no format validation on manifest generated_at (manifestGeneratedAt, :117-126, accepts ANY string).

REPRODUCED by running it in the sandbox copy of HEAD:
 - generated_at: 'not-a-real-timestamp' vs a HEALTHY record finalized 2026-02-01
   -> 'n' (0x6e) sorts above the digits of an ISO stamp -> comparison false ->
   ctkrArtifactHealth returns established TRUE. The staleness refusal that exists to
   catch an unrecorded build stamp is silently skipped by a garbage build stamp.
 - generated_at: '2099-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' -> always passes; no verdict can finalize
   later than the future.

SAFE BY CONTRAST (so the check is not inert): absent/non-string generated_at ->
manifestGeneratedAt returns null -> refuses. And in a multi-repo store the max is
taken across ALL slices with no repo filter, which OVER-refuses (safe direction).

FIX: parse both sides as dates, refuse when either fails to parse, and refuse a
generated_at in the future by more than a small skew. DONE = a test whose two halves
are 'malformed stamp -> refused' and 'valid fresh stamp -> permitted'.

COSMETIC, same file: the docstring at :2076 still says 'Register all ten CTKR tools'; there are eleven.

title: src/ingest/session.ts and src/store/health.ts still claim a seam scanner that no longer exists
description:
FRESH-JUDGE-3 FINDING at HEAD 05d8a93. Three comments assert a semantic the code does not implement — the exact failure class this repo has a receipt for (group_member's comment claiming farmOS semantics it did not implement; a gate test calling a hook that does not exist).

src/ingest/session.ts:16-17  '... nothing else in src/ may (enforced by src/ingest/seam.test.ts, which FAILS THE SUITE when another module in src/ imports them)'
src/ingest/session.ts:128-130 'It is not an ingest entry point: src/ingest/seam.test.ts fails the suite if any non-test module in src/ other than this one calls it.'
src/store/health.ts:40-41   '... and why src/ingest/seam.test.ts fails the suite if another module in src/ imports the raw primitives.'

Importing indexDirectory / loadScip / ingestPrebuiltScip from another module fails NOTHING today. A reader who trusts these three comments will believe a module boundary is enforced when only the runtime record check is.

The builder named this as FOLLOW-UP NOT DONE on MetaCoding-9ed (both files were being edited by a concurrent agent). It is confirmed still present at HEAD.

FIX: replace all three with what is true — the primitives require an IngestTicket (src/ingest/ticket.ts) and refuse a write into a slice whose record currently reads established — and say plainly that module-boundary enforcement is NOT part of it.
