title: Fitness counts symbols from OLD commits still in the store — 10k stale symbols vouched for a fresh verdict
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-04 verifying the first gated production reindex of MetaCoding (commit 05d8a93).

'status' reports 30709 symbols across 4 repo rows:
  MetaCoding @ 1ddb475  6171 symbols  indexed 2026-07-17
  MetaCoding @ 5565f6f  4058 symbols  indexed 2026-07-17
  MetaCoding @ (none)     13 symbols  indexed unknown
  MetaCoding @ 05d8a93  20467 symbols indexed 2026-08-04  <- this run
The HEALTHY verdict cites 30696 symbols — i.e. THE FITNESS MEASURE SUMMED THE CURRENT RUN'S 20467 WITH ~10242 SYMBOLS FROM JULY AT COMMITS THAT ARE NO LONGER CHECKED OUT.

measureStoreFitness is scoped (repo, branch) and NOT by commit, so symbols indexed from earlier commits on the same branch persist and count toward the verdict. The run's own CONTRIBUTION is measured correctly and separately (root 1 is not regressed) — the problem is the FITNESS half.

WHY THIS MATTERS, and it is the same family the whole design is about: a store that had 30k symbols from an old commit and produced only a handful this run could still report a large, healthy-looking fitness number. It is 4kg's coasting shape one level down — not the pass/fail rule (ZERO_CONTRIBUTION_AT_NEW_COMMIT still fires on zero), but the NUMBER a reader is shown and would reasonably trust. Corroborating signal in the same record: freshness reported absent 430 — 430 stored files that no longer exist on disk.

OPEN QUESTION the fix must answer rather than assume: is the honest fitness (a) symbols at the CURRENT commit only, (b) all symbols with stale ones reported separately, or (c) all symbols plus a prune of superseded commits at session finalize? (a) is cleanest but may undercount legitimately-unchanged files that the walker skipped and never re-stamped — note this interacts directly with c03's freshness measure, which exists precisely because skipped files keep an old stamp. Decide with a measurement, not an argument.

TO CLOSE: a contrast pair — a store carrying a large old-commit population where this run contributed little must NOT report that population as the current verdict's fitness, while a store whose files were legitimately skipped as unchanged MUST still count them.

title: index fitness: index_identities citation is not comparable — the health store keeps one row per (repo,branch), so a reader has no previous run to compare against
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING at tree 7c03e77.

The STANDING OPEN RED (fake-it #5 in fitness.ts, open red #2 in the design) is correctly NAMED and I confirmed it is still reachable exactly as described. MEASURED (sandbox judge2-red): the same yesterday.scip ingested twice, day 1 at commit aaaa and day 2 at commit bbbb -> day 2 is HEALTHY, contribution 12 (scipSymbols 6), commitAdvanced TRUE. The graph holds day-1 facts while the record claims commit bbbb. Reachable, as named. Good.

The DEFENCE offered is citation: hashIndexFile records path+sha256+size 'so a reader can SEE it'. The recording half works — I confirmed index_identities carries path, sha256 eef719a3c77e03b6..., size 912, and that the sha256 is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two runs. So the repetition is genuinely detectable in principle.

THE GAP: the claim in both fitness.ts and health.ts is that this makes the repetition 'VISIBLE TO A READER COMPARING TWO RUNS'. There is no second run to compare against. The health schema is 'PRIMARY KEY (repo, branch)' with 'ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE', so writing day 2's record DESTROYS day 1's. At any moment a reader can see exactly one index_identities value and has nothing to compare it to — the identical sha256 that proves the repetition is only visible to someone who recorded the previous value out of band.

So the open red's mitigation is weaker than documented: the citation is recorded but not comparable. This is a small, honest correction to a deliberately-open item, not a claim that the red should have been closed.

FIX DIRECTION: append run records to a history table (or keep a bounded ring of previous records) so the current record can carry 'previous index identity' alongside prev_commit_sha — which the record already does for commits, and which is exactly the shape needed here. Then formatHealthLine can say 'ingested the SAME .scip as the previous run (sha 
eef719a3) at a NEW commit', which is the sentence the open red actually wants a reader to see.
notes:
ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit 05d8a93), NOT CLOSED — fresh reader closes.

CHOSE retrievability over correcting the doc down, because the doc's claim was the RIGHT claim and only the mechanism was missing — and the record already does exactly this shape for commits (prev_commit_sha). Both were done: the mechanism ships AND docs/design/index-fitness.md's open-red-#2 paragraph now states what is and is not true.

MECHANISM: new append-only index_health_history table (id, repo, branch, status, written_at, record) alongside the one-row-per-slice index_health; only FINALIZED records are appended, because a RUNNING row is rewritten every 5s heartbeat and a log of heartbeats would bury the thing it exists to show. Each record now carries prev_index_identities (the previous run's identities, read before the RUNNING row overwrites it). describeIndexRepetition(rec) renders the sentence the open red actually wants — 'ingested the SAME index file as the previous run (path sha eef719a3) at a NEW commit (aaaaaaa -> bbbbbbb): the graph may hold the PREVIOUS commit's facts while the record claims this one' — and formatHealthLine prints it on the HEALTHY and OVERRIDDEN lines, so status/serve/describe_api show it. readIndexHealthHistory(dataDir, repo, branch, limit) is the reader; a health DB written before this returns [] rather than implying agreement.

THE OPEN RED IS STILL OPEN and the test asserts it: half A's second run of the same .scip at a new commit still reports contribution > 0 and commitAdvanced true. Comparable citation, still not prevention.

EVIDENCE — PAIR 19g in src/ingest/fitness.test.ts: two REAL sessions at two commits per half (--load-scip both times), same .scip vs different .scip; asked of the STORE ALONE after the fact the two halves give opposite answers (describeIndexRepetition non-null containing 'SAME index file' + 'NEW commit' vs null; formatHealthLine likewise), and day 1's record SURVIVES day 2 in history with the byte-identical sha256 sitting next to it.
MUTATIONS: dropping the history append reddens it; dropping prev_index_identities reddens it.

FAKE-IT ASKED: 'the history grows without bound / becomes noise' — only finalized verdicts are appended (one row per completed index run, not per heartbeat), and the reader defaults to the newest 20.
FRESH JUDGE 3 (tree HEAD 05d8a93, src/store/health.ts sha256 d0b24e649d30...) — VERIFIED by execution, closing.

 - DAY 1 SURVIVES DAY 2: two real runIndexSession runs at commits 1111.../2222...
   -> readIndexHealthHistory returns 2 rows, NEWEST FIRST, commit_sha[0]=2222...,
   commit_sha[1]=1111... The DO-UPDATE row is unchanged; the append-only table is
   what preserves day 1. Only finalized records append (health.ts:290: 'if
   rec.status !== "RUNNING"'), so the 5s heartbeat rewrite does not bury the log.
 - PRE-HISTORY DBs RETURN [] rather than implying agreement: built a health sqlite
   containing ONLY the index_health table (no index_health_history) with a HEALTHY
   row; readIndexHealthHistory -> []. The mechanism is real, not accidental:
   openExisting does NOT run SCHEMA (only open() does), so the SELECT throws and
   readIndexHealthHistory's catch returns []. Note that this makes 'no history table'
   and 'no rows' the same answer -- honest for the migration story, but a reader
   cannot tell the two apart.
 - THE REPETITION IS VISIBLE FROM THE RECORD ALONE: describeIndexRepetition on a
   record carrying prev_index_identities with a matching sha256 and an advanced
   commit emits: 'ingested the SAME index file as the previous run (/out/farmos.scip
   sha deadbeef) at a NEW commit (1111111 -> 2222222): the graph may hold the PREVIOUS
   commit's facts while the record claims this one'. formatHealthLine prints it as a
   warn line under HEALTHY. Empty prev_index_identities -> null (no false positive).
 - THE OPEN RED REMAINS OPEN AND IS ASSERTED AS SUCH: the record status stays HEALTHY;
   nothing in evaluateIndexOutcome reads index_identities, so this is citation, not
   prevention -- exactly what fitness.ts:568-584 and health.ts:46-55 now say.
close_reason: Fresh judge 3 at HEAD 05d8a93 executed all three claims: two real sessions leave 2 history rows newest-first with day 1 intact; a pre-history health DB returns [] not agreement; describeIndexRepetition emits the same-.scip-at-a-new-commit sentence from the record alone, and the open red is still open (status stays HEALTHY, no gate rule reads identities).

title: index fitness: readIndexHealth/readAllIndexHealth THROW on a half-created health DB, and index-state.ts claims they never throw
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING at tree 7c03e77 (src/store/health.ts sha256 7a0d0f4d6e8e...).

IndexHealthStore.openExisting only checks existsSync on index-health.sqlite; it does not verify the schema. If a session is killed between 'new SqliteDb(...)' creating the file and 'db.exec(SCHEMA)' committing the table, the file exists with no index_health table and every reader throws 'no such table: index_health' out of prepare().

MEASURED (sandbox judge2-halfdb): created the file with bun:sqlite and closed it immediately without the schema, then:
  readIndexHealth(dataDir,'fixture','main')  -> THREW: no such table: index_health
  readAllIndexHealth(dataDir)                -> THREW: no such table: index_health
  summarizeHealth(store)                     -> survived ONLY because that store had zero symbols, so it never reached readIndexHealth. With any symbol present it iterates slices and calls readIndexHealth per slice, so it throws too.

CONSEQUENCE: summarizeHealth is on the path of EVERY gated MCP tool, so the server raises instead of returning the INDEX_FITNESS_UNESTABLISHED refusal. gatherIndexState calls readAllIndexHealth, so 'metacoding status' and describe_api throw as well — and src/index-state.ts's header states 'Pure read: it asks the Store for a summary and shells out to git read-only; it never mutates and never throws.' That comment is false on this path.

SEVERITY: this fails CLOSED (an exception, never a spurious HEALTHY), so it is an availability/robustness defect rather than a safety hole. It is narrow but it is squarely in the crash window this whole feature exists to handle — 'the process died partway' is ae5's founding scenario, and this is the one way dying partway breaks the reader instead of informing it.

HOW I FOUND IT: session.test.ts 'PAIR 7 — a SIGKILLed run leaves fitness UNESTABLISHED' failed in my sandbox with this exact stack (health.ts:248 prepare -> readIndexHealth -> session.test.ts:207). On a cold/slower machine the SIGKILL lands inside the create-schema window. The test is therefore also TIMING-FLAKY (it passed on a later run in the same sandbox); see the separate note below.

FIX DIRECTION: openExisting should treat a missing/!unreadable table as UNKNOWN rather than propagating — wrap the read in try/catch returning null, or run CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in a transaction so the file is never observable without its schema (or both). Whichever, add a test that constructs a schema-less health DB and asserts the reader reads UNKNOWN, since that is the regression evidence.

RELATED: session.test.ts PAIR 7 is timing-sensitive — it kills the CLI at a fixed delay and asserts a RUNNING record exists. On a cold module cache the kill can precede the record. Worth making the kill wait on the record's appearance rather than on a clock.

title: index gate verdict is not persisted: an interrupted or gate-failed run leaves a store that status/serve report as healthy
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING (the 'what if the process dies partway' attack) against MetaCoding-0sd, commit 0c13fa2.

MEASURED, sandbox (data-dir <scratch>/judge-0sd/data/killed):
 'index <node-oidc-provider> --load-scip index.typescript.scip' SIGKILLed at 40s -> exit 137.
 storeCensus of the resulting store: 1,724 symbols, and 0 edges of EVERY kind — i.e. exactly the MetaCoding-hy6.16 shape (symbols present, CALLS 0 / REFERENCES 0), because the SCIP loader upserts symbols before edges.
 'metacoding status --data-dir <that dir>' then prints: 'Indexed: 1724 symbol(s) across 1 repo(s)' with no indication the run never finished.

The gate is a verdict on a PROCESS EXIT, not a fact about the STORE. gatherIndexState (src/index-state.ts) derives 'indexed' from a symbol count, so describe_api / serve / status cannot see that the last run was killed or refused. Anything that reads the store rather than watching the exit code — which is every MCP consumer — is still exposed to the failure family MetaCoding-0sd exists to close.

Partial mitigation observed: a SUBSEQUENT gated run into that store DID fail (exit 1, NO_RELATIONAL_EDGES) — but only because the kill landed before any edges were written. Once any edges exist, MetaCoding-4kg (stale coasting) applies and the next run passes.

FIX DIRECTION: persist the gate result (and an in-progress marker) into the store per (repo, branch), and have gatherIndexState/describe_api surface 'last index run: FAILED/INTERRUPTED' alongside the symbol count.
notes:
ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit 6c933a7), not closed — fresh reader closes. The verdict is now a STATE: src/store/health.ts persists index-health.sqlite beside graph.lbug, written RUNNING on session entry and finalized HEALTHY/REFUSED/OVERRIDDEN on exit. A SIGKILLed process never reaches finalize, so the record says RUNNING forever — closed BY CONSTRUCTION, nothing has to detect the death. pid + heartbeat_at let a reader distinguish 'running now' from 'abandoned' (isAbandonedRun), which is the cry-wolf failure the design named. gatherIndexState reads it; 'metacoding status' prints an index-fitness block beside the symbol count, INCLUDING when the store has zero symbols (a run that died before writing anything is not the same as 'never indexed'). Evidence: PAIR 7 in src/ingest/session.test.ts — a real CLI index is SIGKILLed as soon as the RUNNING row appears (deterministic, not a sleep), and the assertions are on the RECORD and on a graph tool RESPONSE, never on an exit code; the mirror half lets the same command finish and gets HEALTHY plus an { ok:true, rows: [] } from the identical query. Mutation M5 (skip the RUNNING marker) CAUGHT.
FRESH JUDGE (tree 7c03e77, health.ts sha256 7a0d0f4d6e8e...). INDEPENDENTLY RE-RAN: (a) RUNNING written on entry, finalized on exit — observed across ~20 sandbox sessions; (b) COPIES of BOTH production stores (never written to): /Users/dukejones/work/WorldTree/farmos-port/.metacoding and .../MetaCoding/.metacoding have NO index-health.sqlite; a real populated farmOS copy (354+ real Drupal PHP symbols, 2 slices) reads readAllIndexHealth=[] -> both slices UNKNOWN -> established=false, and graph_callers on a REAL symbol REFUSES with INDEX_FITNESS_UNESTABLISHED. Absent file reads UNKNOWN, never HEALTHY — confirmed on real data; (c) status/formatHealthLine surfaces the verdict; (d) RUNNING record -> established=false and empty queries refuse. Two residual holes filed separately: PID reuse in isAbandonedRun, and readIndexHealth THROWING on a half-created health DB.
close_reason: Fresh-judge verified at tree 7c03e77 against COPIES of both real production stores: absent health file reads UNKNOWN (never HEALTHY), queries refuse, RUNNING written on entry and finalized on exit. Two residual holes filed separately.

title: index-gate tests do not protect the gate: three mutations leave all 12/19 tests green
description:
FRESH-JUDGE mutation run against MetaCoding-0sd's evidence (src/cli/index-gate.test.ts sha256 85194e08bd39..., 12 tests; src/cli suite 19 tests). Baseline verified green BEFORE and AFTER every mutation; each mutation asserted its anchor matched (perl ... or die) so a silent no-match could not be read as 'the suite cannot catch this'.

SURVIVING MUTATIONS (12 pass / 0 fail, or 19/0 for M3):
 M1  DEFAULT_MIN_COVERAGE 0.1 -> 0.004. The floor's VALUE is untested: the only LOW_COVERAGE case is 1/273 = 0.37%, and the only passing case is 100%. The default could be silently dropped from 10% to 0.4% — gutting the rule the builder chose OVER a '> 0' check — with every test green.
 M2  storeCensus edge query de-scoped from (repo, branch) (WHERE ... OR true). Every test store holds exactly ONE repo, so cross-repo contamination is invisible. This matters directly for MetaCoding-d1l.2, which indexes a CORPUS into one store: a de-scoped census lets another repo's CALLS vouch for this repo's empty graph.
 M3  In src/cli/main.ts, replace 'const census = await storeCensus(store, opts.repo, opts.branch)' with a census fabricated from the indexer's own accumulators (symbolsUpserted/edgesAdded). All 19 src/cli tests stay green. The gate's CENTRAL claim — 'measured out of the STORE, never the accumulators' — is true in the code and protected by NO test: the store-reading tests call storeCensus directly, and the one wired CLI test uses an empty .scip whose accumulators are also zero, so it cannot tell the two apart.

WHAT WOULD FIX M3: one wired test where the accumulators are NON-ZERO and the store is EMPTY (or vice versa) — the two must give opposite verdicts.
WHAT WOULD FIX M1: a case just above and just below the floor (e.g. 9% fails / 11% passes).
WHAT WOULD FIX M2: a store holding a populated repo B and an empty repo A; the gate must refuse A.
notes:
ADDRESSED 2026-08-04 (commit 6c933a7), not closed — fresh reader closes. The evidence rule changed, which is what this bead was actually about: every load-bearing test is now a CONTRAST PAIR whose halves give OPPOSITE verdicts, and each describe block names the mutation it kills. The old index-gate.test.ts is deleted, not patched. All three survivors are now caught, measured with both methodology guards (anchor asserted to match exactly once or abort; baseline verified 35 pass / 0 fail BEFORE and AFTER; restore from sha256-verified byte copies, never git checkout): M1 DEFAULT_MIN_COVERAGE 0.1->0.004 CAUGHT by PAIR 3, which BRACKETS the floor (9% refused / 11% established) instead of testing 0.37% vs 100%. M2 edge census de-scoped from (repo,branch) CAUGHT by PAIR 2, a store holding a populated repo B and an empty repo A (plus the branch variant) — load-bearing for d1l.2's shared corpus. M3 fitness fabricated from the indexer's accumulators CAUGHT by wired PAIR 1b, a warm re-run whose accumulators are all zero while the store is full; its half 1a is the mirror, 40 healthy-looking documents with an empty store. 11 mutations run, 11 caught. Full log: scratchpad/mutation.log + mutation-results.json. The scan-based seam test is itself mutation-tested inside the file (it must flag a synthetic bypass) so it cannot be an instrument capable of reporting nothing but success.

title: page[limit]=200 is a lie — farmOS caps JSON:API collections at 50 and nothing follows links.next
description:
FOUND BY THE FRESH JUDGE 2026-08-04 (results/wave2/judge-hy6.27-checkers-2026-08-04.md), present in ALL THREE ledgers and in the judge's own survey tool.

MEASURED: GET /api/asset/animal?page[limit]=200 returns 50 ROWS and a links.next. farmOS caps JSON:API collections at 50 regardless of the requested limit. All three verify scripts request 200 in their prefix sweeps and in the collection half of the absence check, and NONE follows links.next.

NO LEDGER SILENTLY PASSED BECAUSE OF THIS: the by-ID half of the absence check is unaffected, since it does a direct GET per id. So the primary net holds. But the secondary net is materially weaker than its own comments claim, and any future code that reaches for the collection sweep as the primary check inherits a 50-row ceiling it does not know about.

TO CLOSE: a shared paginating helper that follows links.next to exhaustion, used by every sweep in every ledger, with a fixture proving it reaches past row 50 (seeding's ~70-row run is a ready-made case). title: Birth and seeding ledgers pass vacuously: no floors, and each lacks the other's guard
description:
FOUND BY THE FRESH JUDGE 2026-08-04 (results/wave2/judge-hy6.27-checkers-2026-08-04.md, farmos-port). Three mutations made birth report 'clean: every probe matched its ADR status AND value; no fixtures left behind' while doing substantially less than it was written to do.

  birth       ran 35 of 62 fixtures with the standing-act, uniqueness, lineage, status and un-claiming sections deleted -> EXIT 0, reported clean
  seeding     ran 24 of ~60 with sections E/F/G/H deleted — INCLUDING SECTION G, the derived-name section that is the entire reason its by-ID cleanup exists -> EXIT 0, reported clean
  transplanting caught it: exit 1, 'only 27 fixtures tracked (expected >= 40)', 'only 55 probes carried a VALUE expectation (expected >= 94)'

J2 SILENTLY DROP ONE expect= (keep expect_status): invisible to birth AND to seeding's structural guard, which only fires when a row has NEITHER expectation. Transplanting caught it at 93 < 94.

J3 ADD A ROW CARRYING NO EXPECTATION: seeding's M6 guard caught it; birth and transplanting accepted it silently.

THE SHAPE: seeding's structural guard and transplanting's floors were invented INDEPENDENTLY and NEITHER BUILD HAS THE OTHER'S. Birth has neither. Each guard catches what the other misses, and the union is what a checker needs.

Calibration note the judge recorded honestly: transplanting's floors are COUNTERS and a counter can be padded (J8: pad CHECKED with filler check() calls and CREATED with fake uuids -> exit 0). The floors detect ACCIDENTAL truncation, which is what they were built for. That is scope for calibration, not a defect.

title: Seed propagation: extend the citation seed along callees / implementers / file neighbours
description:
Raised BY d1l.6 ("cheap upside worth one bead"), which measured tier 1 and demoted it from backbone to seed: docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md §3.4, MetaCoding @ 6291449.

THE OBSERVATION. Citations reach 19-21% of Go FILES but only 6-8% of exported SYMBOLS. File-level coarse binding is ~3x better than symbol-level, and the graph already knows the rest of the structure. A cited symbol's callees, its implementers, and its same-file neighbours are strong candidates for the SAME spec section — and propagating from a high-precision seed is exactly what the existing graph is for. d1l.6's judgement: this is a better spend than LM-proposing cold.

WHAT IT DELIVERS. IMPLEMENTS_SPEC edges with source='propagated', carrying the seed edge they descended from and the hop count, so confidence is auditable and a propagated edge is never mistaken for a citation or for an LM proposal (see d1l.8 note — the enum needs the value).

GATED ON d1l.15, which measures propagation-vs-cold-proposal as one of its two arms. Do not build this before that verdict; do not let the verdict evaporate if it comes back positive — that is what this bead exists to prevent.

DEPENDS ALSO ON d1l.10 (the seed) and d1l.2 (the graph to propagate through).

HELD-OUT ORACLE APPLIES: if propagation is seeded from the same citations d1l.14 scores against, both numbers are circular. Split before propagating.

title: oracle_preflight: a COMMENTED-OUT drush en line is parsed as declared, so the drift check silently passes
description:
Found by a fresh judge re-running MetaCoding-hy6.25 independently (farmos-port tools/oracle_preflight.py sha256 aac5b798b43a4344132090f415df388145b43256dde7d6a75ed0bcbe6b05089a, last commit 0c12ec2).

declared_modules() joins line continuations and then regex-matches `drush\s+(?:en|pm:enable)\s+-y\s+(...)` over the WHOLE file text. It never strips shell comments. So a bring-up.sh step that has been commented out --- the single most likely way a module stops being enabled --- is still counted as DECLARED.

REPRODUCED (on a scratchpad COPY of ctkr/ctkr/oracle/bring-up.sh, the real file untouched): comment out the 'enable remaining log types' step, then run

  python3 tools/oracle_preflight.py log--medical --bring-up <copy>

Correct answer is exit 2 (farm_medical is installed on the oracle but the rebuild script as written would NOT re-enable it, so every value recorded now stops reproducing). Actual answer:

  ok   enabled module set matches bring-up.sh (no hand-enabled drift)
  === ORACLE PREFLIGHT OK --- safe to probe ===
  EXIT=0

This is exactly the failure hy6.25 exists to prevent --- the preflight passing while the oracle is in a state a build would be wrong to probe --- reached through the parser rather than through the API.

WHY THE EXISTING TEST DID NOT CATCH IT: tools/test_oracle_preflight.py t_parse asserts 'comment text leaked into the declared set' using the fixture line '# a comment mentioning farm_ghost should not count'. That comment contains no drush invocation, so the assertion could not have come out any other way --- it is a non-discriminating observation of exactly the kind docs/design/iteration-methodology.md warns about. The test claims comment-safety and only measures prose-safety.

FIX DIRECTION (validated by the judge, not applied): drop lines whose lstrip() starts with '#' after the continuation join, before the regex. Measured on both files: real bring-up.sh 30 modules -> 30 (no false alarm, no regression), commented-out copy 30 -> 28 with farm_medical correctly absent.

DEFINITION OF DONE: the fix ships with a t_parse case whose fixture is a REAL commented-out 'drush en -y <module>' line and which fails before the fix.

NOT a defect: the flag-after form 'drush en <mod> -y' is also unparsed, but that direction is fail-safe --- it under-declares, producing a loud exit 2 false alarm rather than a false pass (verified live against asset--sensor).
close_reason: Fixed and mutation-tested in farmos-port: declared_modules strips whole-line comments before parsing. Hit LIVE while declaring hy6.11's modules commented-out — the preflight read the explanation as a declaration and failed 'declared-but-not-enabled', blocking every port. Three regression checks: a commented block is not declared while a real one in the same file still is; an uncommented multi-line drush en IS still declared (the contrast); and a comments-only file remains a PARSE FAILURE rather than becoming a vacuous pass.

title: No tree-sitter fallback for .go/.js — lanes 3 and 4 are dark, and so is FTS
description:
MEASURED BY d1l.7 (MetaCoding 44cc29d). The tree-sitter fallback for Go and JS DOES NOT EXIST: detectGrammar() returns null for .go, .js, .mjs and .cjs, so a --scip false run yields filesScanned 0, symbols 0, edges 0 AND TOKENS 0. Artifacts: scratchpad data/go-ts-only and data/js-ts-only, both complete and empty. The grammars ARE bundled — dispatch and a per-language extractor are what is missing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE GRAPH: no tokens means no FTS either, so the full-text lane over the AST blind spots (string/DI/reflection usage) is dark for both languages too.

AND IT FALSIFIES A LOAD-BEARING PREMISE: d1l.7's own bead argued 'tree-sitter fallback covers citation mining even if scip-go disappoints, which caps the blast radius'. That cap does not exist. d1l.10 (citation-mining extractor) must own its own file walk — the d1l.6 spike script already does this, so the pattern is available to copy.

UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS worth trying first, from the spike: point .js at extractTypeScript. May be nearly free; may be wrong. Measure, do not assume.

TO CLOSE: either the fallback works for .go/.js with non-zero symbols AND tokens, or it is documented as deliberately unsupported and every plan resting on it (starting with d1l.10) is corrected.

description:

title: Wire oracle_preflight into the recipe — a gate nobody must remember to run
description:
hy6.25 shipped tools/oracle_preflight.py (farmos-port 0c12ec2), mutation-proven and cheap. Nothing wires it in: a build can still skip it entirely, or run it while under-declaring the resource types it actually touches. Both failure modes reproduce the exact silent degradation hy6.25 exists to prevent — the preflight passes because it was asked the wrong question.

TO CLOSE: the preflight runs as a precondition of the observe step (recipe doc + the probes.py/verify.py template), and the declared type list is derived from or cross-checked against what the build's probes actually request, so under-declaration is detectable rather than free.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, filed as children rather than reopening:
  hy6.36 (P1) the gate covers ONE of five wave2 builds; identity-transplanting has no oracle_preflight at all, and seeding/group/birth keep hand-written lists. No additive adoption path exists for the gate the way evaluate_floors() gives one for the floors.
  hy6.37 (P2) the gate is not bound to the transport — Ledger calls require_types() with the ORACLE_URL default while every build probes ORACLE; the gate can clear a different oracle than the run probes (demonstrated).
  hy6.38 (P3) resource_type() fail-open is a third, INVISIBLE escape hatch that the docstring's 'how would I fake this?' list does not name.
  hy6.39 (P3) nothing reads the PREFLIGHT row back out of an artifact.

title: Three batch-2 probe ledgers cannot fail — convert them to checkers
description:
identity-birth, identity-seeding and identity-transplanting ship append-only observe/ ledgers: no expected values, no non-zero exit, and re-running APPENDS a second copy rather than checking the first. A transcript that cannot fail is not evidence.

The cost is already concrete and not hypothetical: hy6.8's probe M4 records no request payload and that build shipped no script, so when hy6.6 measured the OPPOSITE result for is_location nobody could recover which door M4 used. The bound row was corrected by re-measuring from scratch. That is the price of a ledger that transcribes.

Two builds have the working pattern — hy6.9's probes.py and hy6.10's verify.py, ~120 portable lines: each row carries the value its ADR cites, a mismatch writes a drift key, the run exits non-zero, and the file is TRUNCATED each run so re-running is a check. Both caught real errors on their first run, and both were mutation-tested by their authors AND independently by me.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three ships a verify script on the hy6.9/hy6.10 model, mutation-tested so it is proven capable of failing. Any drift found on first run is reported as a finding, not silently reconciled — that is where the value is. probes.jsonl may stay as the append-only record of discovery, but must be LABELLED history rather than a check, as hy6.10's manifest now does.
notes:
CORRECTION to scope: hy6.3 birth ALREADY HAS a verify.py (committed 2026-08-03), so two of the three are further along than this bead's title says. Verified independently: mutating an expectation yields DRIFT and exit 1 — a real checker, not a transcript.

title: Oracle preflight: assert the bundles a build needs actually resolve
description: Twice on 2026-08-03 a MISSING oracle module silently degraded a port to source-read-only, which the recipe forbids: farm_quick (hy6.22, blocking the whole quick/* family and the gating unknown on hy6.12) and farm_medical + farm_transplanting (hy6.7, /api/log/medical 404). In both cases the agent discovered it only after starting the recipe, and in the farm_quick case an earlier probe returned 422 'the attribute quick does not exist' which LOOKED like a finding about farmOS and was actually measuring the oracle. That is the expensive failure mode: not a crash, but a measurement of the wrong thing that reads as evidence. The oracle's enabled-module set is an unchecked assumption every identity port depends on.
acceptance_criteria: A preflight a build runs before probing: given the resource types it intends to touch, assert each returns something other than 404 and fail loudly with the bring-up.sh remedy if not. Cheap enough to run unconditionally. Bonus: assert the oracle's enabled-module set matches what bring-up.sh declares, so a hand-enabled module (which vanishes on rebuild) is detected rather than silently relied on.
notes:
--- 2026-08-04 (agent, NOT closed — left for a fresh judge) ---
SHIPPED in farmos-port @ 0c12ec2 (pushed to WorldTreeNetwork/FarmOS2 main):
  tools/oracle_preflight.py       the gate, GET-only, ~0.9s, exit 2 = stop
  tools/test_oracle_preflight.py  21 checks, runs without an oracle
  README.md                       "Before you probe" section
Invocation (in the file header and the README):
  python3 tools/oracle_preflight.py log--medical asset--plant taxonomy_term--log_category

RED as a property: a build may not begin probing while any resource type it
names is unresolvable, OR is provided by a module the rebuild script would not
re-enable. Second half = the bonus criterion, and it is DONE: the drift check
parses `drush en` out of MetaCoding/ctkr/ctkr/oracle/bring-up.sh, adds the farm
profile's own roots (dblog + farm_login/farm_setup/farm_ui/farm_update from
farm.install), walks the dependency closure over a read-only `drush php:eval`
extension listing, and reports installed non-core modules that are NOT
reachable. Hand-enabled + depended on by THIS build = fatal; hand-enabled and
unused = warning.

AC1 (resolve or fail loudly with the bring-up.sh remedy): done. Types are
checked against the /api index AND GET-ed at their collection, with the BODY
required to be JSON:API — status codes do not discriminate (farmOS 404s with
HTML). Remedy names the providing module from a PROVIDED_BY table DERIVED from
the 4.0.4 source (config/install bundle config -> owning module; regeneration
command is in the docstring), and tells the agent to edit bring-up.sh and
escalate rather than run drush against the SHARED oracle.
AC2 (cheap enough to run unconditionally): 0.9s with drift, 0.75s without.

MUTATION EVIDENCE (full transcript in the commit message): 9 distinct loud
failures proven, incl. log--maintenance (real bundle, module absent) -> exit 2;
a bring-up.sh copy with farm_medical removed -> "HAND-ENABLED module(s) this
build depends on" exit 2 WHILE log--medical still returns 200 (the contrast a
status-only probe cannot produce); parse-zero bring-up.sh -> fatal, not a skip;
oracle unreachable -> named remedy, not a traceback (that one was a real defect
the mutation run found). Every mutation anchor was asserted to match first.

FINDINGS ON THE LIVE ORACLE (2026-08-04): 126 modules installed; enabled set
matches bring-up.sh EXACTLY — zero hand-enabled drift, zero declared-but-absent.
44 advertised resource types. log--maintenance is NOT among them: farm_maintenance
ships in the farm profile and is not enabled, which is why
port_runs/wave2/spine-log-maintenance has no observe/ dir and its manifest says
"no oracle-observed maintenance fixtures at spine tier". That build was
source-read-only for a reason nobody had named — worth a follow-up bead.

NOT DONE: nothing wires the preflight into the recipe/probes.py templates, so a
build can still skip it or under-declare the types it touches. That residue is
structural and should be a separate bead.
No mutation of any kind was made to the shared oracle (GETs, one /oauth/token
POST, one read-only drush php:eval).

title: IDENTITY port: quick/planting — full recipe on the answered fold question
description:
Split from MetaCoding-hy6.12 after the composite-fold question was answered (docs/design/composite-fold-question.md): the frozen kernel v1.3 IS sufficient for composite fan-out — N appends to EventLog, each stamped into the 'quick' GSet, ordered by HLC — because farmOS has NO cross-entity atomicity (0 startTransaction in all of modules/) and its own composite-act attribution is already a grow-only field. A port that made these acts atomic would DIVERGE while looking like an improvement.

Shape for this form: 1 plant asset + up to 3 logs (seeding/transplanting/harvest) from one act; the widest fan-out of the five

Full identity recipe (mine -> observe -> decide -> build -> read). Needs the live oracle for observe. Denormalize-on-write stays feature-local exactly as -5ln did; MetaCoding-dvv is now a v1.4 promote decision (rule of three fired) and does not block this build.
notes:
DECISIONS BOUND 2026-08-03 (hy6.12, farmos-port). Every one of the five cites quick-provenance:
  - quick_stamp = append-on-create, EXACTLY ONE id; 4.0.4 has no verb stamping a pre-existing entity, so append and set are indistinguishable — do NOT build a grow-only accumulate.
  - quick_restate = LwwRegister<readonly string[]> keyed by HLC (lww.ts). GSet is UNBOUND and is the REFUTED answer.
  - Attribution is PARTIAL: quick exists on asset+log only (FieldHooks.php:31-36). Do NOT stamp quantities or terms.
NO CROSS-ENTITY ATOMICITY, and the failure surface is INTERLEAVED, not a clean prefix: QuickLogTrait saves the quantity (QuickQuantityTrait:79) BEFORE the parent log is validated (:82) and saved (:88), and QuickTermTrait::createOrLoadTerm writes a term during buildForm. A port that makes these atomic diverges while looking like an improvement.

QUICK/PLANTING SPECIFICS:
- CITE planting-season-memory (bound 2026-08-03): Planting.php:434 writes farm.quick.planting.seasons into Drupal State and :63 reads it back as the season autocomplete default. Port it as REPLICA-LOCAL UI PREFERENCE, OUTSIDE THE LEDGER, never merged. Faithful replication would be worse than diverging — Drupal State is site-global, so one user's planting changes everyone's default. The row carries NO sanctions list and that is correct: nothing at the boundary asks a question this diverges on.
- NOT covered by that row: the season TERMS are real domain data (the season field on the plant asset, via createOrLoadTerm) and port normally.
- CONDITIONAL, MIXED-STATUS EMISSION (:452-491): three log types, each SKIPPED when unsubmitted (:456-458); is_movement derived for seeding/transplanting ONLY (:470-473); status set PER-LOG from a per-log checkbox (:476-479). One act emits a mix of done and pending logs, which different projections admit differently under status.ts — see the bound pending-status-gates row (STATUS_CONTRACT is per-projection, not one blanket rule).
- createOrLoadTerm is upsert-by-natural-key with a race window. The nearest kernel primitive is GuardedFirstWrite, but NO decision names it for terms — if the build needs it, that is a new binding, not a reach.
OBSERVE ATTEMPTED AND FAILED 2026-08-07 — recorded so nobody reads the sibling beads' progress as covering this one.

Quick forms have no API route (see hy6.17's note); they are driven through Drupal's FormBuilder. birth, group and movement measured cleanly. THIS ONE DID NOT:

  hy6.19 inventory — the form refused my values: 'Adjustment type field is required' and 'Log type field is required'. Nothing was created. The reset/increment/decrement fold is UNOBSERVED, so whether it is FoldReduce is still an open question.
  hy6.21 planting — TypeError: mb_strlen() got an array, a value-shape error on my side, before any create. The widest fan-out (asset + up to 3 logs) is UNOBSERVED.

Both need a value set read out of each plugin's buildForm rather than guessed. DO NOT BUILD EITHER FROM SOURCE READING ALONE — that is the mistake hy6.13 spent this session not making, on a field where reading had already been wrong once.

Harness to reuse: results/wave2/probe_hy6qf_fanout.php (drive + measure) and probe_hy6qf_cleanup.php (teardown, children before parents — the first version stranded two entities on the shared oracle because entity_reference_integrity_enforce refuses to delete a referenced entity).
BUILT 2026-08-07 (farmos-port 1402a1f), port_runs/wave2/quick-folds/. Observation: results/wave2/quick-forms-fanout-2026-08-07.md — every shape MEASURED by driving the real Drupal form through FormBuilder against the pinned oracle (the forms have no JSON:API route) and reading the entities back. Fixtures torn down by ID, boundary verified at 0 leftovers and 0 quick-stamped entities.

Provenance is the ACT, not the field: each fold runs inside asAct so eventsOfAct answers 'what did this act touch?'. Deliberately NOT atomic — farmOS has zero startTransaction in all of modules/, so N appends under one act id is fidelity; making it atomic would diverge while looking like an improvement, which is the composite-fold answer.

14 fixtures, each paired with a contrast. Mutation-tested, six mutants all detected (wrong bundle per form, per-mode bundles, reset-as-increment, always-three-logs, one-act-for-everything). 955 tests pass.

quickPlanting: the widest fan-out, and it was measured at both ends. All three log types -> FOUR entities from one act (asset--plant + log--seeding + log--transplanting + log--harvest), one identical quick ['planting'] on every one. No logs -> 1 asset and nothing else.

The asset name is COMPOSED from season + location + crop ('2026 Field Lettuce'), so the same act without a location yields a different name ('2026 Lettuce') — which is the contrast fixture and why a fold ignoring name composition fails.

title: Taxonomy decision-gaps: parent cardinality, term-delete with dangling children, term revisioning
description: Unfiled BIG-PUNT from ff714c4. Both shipped taxonomy stores (TaxonomyTermStore hierarchical, TaxonomyVocabStore flat) left three questions undecided: single- vs multi-parent hierarchy, what happens to children when a term is deleted, and term revisioning. They currently hold whichever answer the builder happened to pick — an unrecorded decision is a divergence nobody can score.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three is observed against the live farmOS oracle and recorded as a bound decision or an explicitly sanctioned divergence; the shipped stores are reconciled to the answer.
notes:
OBSERVED 2026-08-02 against the restarted pinned oracle. Evidence: FarmOS2 results/wave2/taxonomy-decision-gaps-2026-08-02.md. Reproduction verified BEFORE probing (lexicon-bind/location re-recorded: 10/10 fixture ids identical, in order, vs sealed pack f3460165d338da4c6043262a05bd3a99). Probes created and deleted their own terms; zero hy614-* left on the oracle.

(1) PARENT CARDINALITY — MULTI-parent, and NO acyclicity at the boundary. PATCH to two parents -> 200, reports 2. PATCH a parent to be the child of its own child (2-cycle) -> 200 ACCEPTED. PATCH a term to be its own parent -> 200 ACCEPTED. farmOS's TaxonomyTermForm excludes self+descendants from the parent options, but that is UI-ONLY. A port that enforces acyclicity is STRICTER THAN ITS SOURCE — a divergence, and the dangerous kind, because every test of the stricter behaviour passes.

(2) TERM DELETE — THERE ARE NO DANGLING CHILDREN. DELETE a parent that has a child -> 403 'Can not delete ... as it is being referenced by another entity.' Controls that make it a finding rather than a permissions accident: a childless unreferenced term deletes fine (204), and the SAME term deletes fine (204) once its child is detached. The blocker is the inbound reference. This is a REFUSAL semantic — first-class evidence under o8b.

(3) REVISIONING — none. All 11 vocabularies carry new_revision: false, and GET ?resourceVersion=rel:latest -> 400 'An invalid resource version identifier'. Latest write wins.

RECONCILE against the shipped TaxonomyTermStore: (3) AGREES and is correctly grounded in the config. (1) the store models SINGLE parent — stricter than the source, but it DECLARED the gap, so this is a decision to bind, not a defect. (2) IS A DEFECT: term_store.ts:176 deleteTerm emits unconditionally with no guard, and :110 describes 'children are left dangling (parent points to a gone id)'. The store permits an act farmOS REFUSES and then models a state the source can never enter. The fix is to REFUSE, not to cascade or orphan.

NOT BOUND, deliberately. The instrument resolves exactly ONE registry (DECISION_REGISTRY_RELPATHS is fixed to port_runs/kernel-9h5.24/build/cm-decisions.jsonl) whose own header scopes it to 'the logs+location composed store', and it mirrors kernelConfig.ts BOUND_CM_DECISIONS verbatim with prevention.test.ts asserting equality. Writing a sanction any port may then cite is a load-bearing edit in two trees and a scope decision — not a side effect of an observation run. NEXT UNIT: bind the three, fix deleteTerm, ship the regression test that would catch it.
ALL THREE BOUND + THE DEFECT FIXED, 2026-08-03 (farmos-port 3bc2aa9 + e139460). 305/305 green.

(2) TERM DELETE — the defect is closed. deleteTerm now REFUSES while any live term references the target (TermReferencedError, mirroring the 403); no cascade, no orphan. The defect had shipped WITH a test that locked it in ('ancestor walk stops at a deleted (dangling) parent' deleted a referenced parent and asserted the dangling result). That test is gone; seven replace it and FIVE GO RED against the unguarded store — verified by reverting the guard, not assumed. The two that stay green are the controls asserting deletes SUCCEED (childless 204; same term 204 after detaching), because a store refusing every delete would satisfy the refusal alone. The guard scans all live terms, not childrenOf() — childrenOf resolves the parent's vocabulary first and cannot see a cross-vocabulary reference, which is its own test. Unpublished children still block. TermReferencedError is deliberately NOT 'unsupported': the op IS ported.
KNOWN LIMIT, documented at the guard: the only inbound reference modeled is term->parent. farmOS refuses on ANY referencing entity including log_category's 'category' field on logs — punted to hy6.13. A term referenced only by a LOG deletes here and would 403 in the source.

(1) PARENT CARDINALITY — Duke's call: STORE THE SET, WALK A TREE. parent is an ordered LIST folded latest-wins WHOLESALE (same shape as nicknames/quick; a union would have been the third repeat of a settled mistake). Writes accept multiple parents AND cycles, like the source. ancestorsOf/depthOf walk parent[0] — the declared narrowing, and what log_category's loadTree already assumes. The cycle guard is now LOAD-BEARING rather than defensive, since the source can genuinely hold a cycle. NOT DONE: multi-path DAG depth — unobserved rule, and the source's readers never exercise it; that is a future observation, not a build decision.

(3) REVISIONING — bound as preserve. new_revision:false on all 11 vocabs, ?resourceVersion 400s. The store already agreed and was correctly grounded in the config; the row makes the assumption explicit so a future flip to new_revision:true is a re-decision instead of a silent behaviour change.

REGISTRY: term-parent-cardinality sanctions term_depth ONLY (term_parent and term_children are faithful). Unlike w0a-2's scoping this sanction is NOT provable-narrow — multi-parent depth in the source is genuinely unobserved, which is what makes it a declared narrowing rather than a claim of agreement. term-delete-refusal and term-revisioning carry NO sanctions: the port matches the source. Verified via load_decisions/decision_covers, 11 rows resolving.

title: Calibration study: does intention extraction recover what the RFC actually says?
description:
The payoff for the wider program. Run T5a/b/c intention harvest over fosite; compare the harvest against the RFC sections fosite's own comments cite. Precision and recall become computable numbers - the external oracle that intention doc 7.2/10 says the program lacks.

Second question worth answering with the same setup: does convergence across three independent orgs/languages look different from farmOS's N=2 same-community convergence? If yes, that quantifies how much of farmOS's signal is habit rather than intent.
notes:
PROMOTED IN IMPORTANCE 2026-08-04 (re-scope after d1l.6): THIS IS NOW THE EPIC'S PRINCIPAL PAYOFF, and the one thing the demotion of tier 1 did NOT damage.

WHY. d1l.6 found tier-1 citations too sparse to be a coverage backbone (5.6% / 8.0% / 0.3% of exported symbols) but that measurement is about DENSITY, and this bead needs AUTHORITY. The ~50 distinct sections fosite's own comments name (61 context-resolved) are the authors' own statement of which section each piece of code answers to. Precision and recall of an intention harvest against a few dozen ground-truth pairs is a real computation and does not require breadth. The calibration-instrument argument in the design §2 survives the spike intact, and is now the STRONGEST remaining reason to build tier 1 at all.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOW ASSUME:
 • The oracle is fosite's ~50 sections, plus zitadel's 38 as a second, independent oracle from a different org. node-oidc-provider supplies 27, of which the plurality are OpenID4VCI — it is a poor oracle for this epic's target RFCs and should not be weighted equally.
 • The seed set is NOT a random 5%: the cited sections are the load-bearing ones (RFC 6749 §3.1/§4.1, device flow, introspection, redirect-URI comparison). That helps validity (the oracle covers the code that matters) and hurts generality (recall measured only where authors bothered to cite). State that limit in the write-up rather than letting a reader assume corpus-wide recall.
 • The oracle is HELD OUT. If a propagation or LM pass (d1l.15) is seeded from the same citations, precision measured against them is circular. Split the citation set before any binding pass runs, or this study measures nothing.
 • The second question (three independent orgs vs farmOS's N=2 same-community convergence) now carries a caveat from d1l.7: cross-language edge-density comparisons measure the LANGUAGE until proven otherwise (IMPLEMENTS 586 Go vs 24 JS; 88% type_alias inflation on JS symbol counts). Normalise to function|method|class, or "convergence" will be a Go-vs-JS artefact.

Nothing d1l.6 measured (citation density in fosite/zitadel/node) and nothing d1l.7 measured (the Go lane, the tree-sitter hole) touches it. It needs only d1l.8 (schema) and d1l.9 (sections).

title: Citation-mining extractor: comments -> CITES_SPEC edges
description:
Tier 1. Mine RFC/spec citations out of comments across all indexed repos. This is the reference implementations' own authoritative statement about which section each piece of code answers to - no inference, no LM, no adjudication. Cheapest ground truth in the program.

Blocked by the citation-density spike; if that comes back sparse, re-scope this task before building it.
notes:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-04 after d1l.6 + d1l.7. WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOW ASSUME:

1. TIER 1 IS A SEED AND AN ORACLE, NOT THE BACKBONE. Measured (docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md, 6291449): 6.61 / 4.11 / 1.62 section citations per KLOC and 5.6% / 8.0% / 0.3% of exported symbols within 10 lines (fosite / zitadel-oidc / node-oidc-provider). Whole-corpus yield is ~195 raw citations -> ~115 distinct (spec, section) pairs. "Cheapest ground truth in the program" survives; the implied breadth does not. Do not size anything downstream off this bead's output.

2. IT STILL MUST BE BUILT, AND IT IS CHEAP. scripts/spike-citation-density.ts (~350 lines) is the working prototype; productionising is (a) a real comment lexer and (b) emitting CITES_SPEC edges. Hours, not days.

3. IT MUST OWN ITS FILE WALK. d1l.7 (docs/notes/2026-08-04-go-js-lane-spike.md, 44cc29d) found there is NO tree-sitter lane for .go/.js/.mjs/.cjs at all — detectGrammar() returns null, so symbols 0, edges 0, FTS tokens 0. The extractor cannot ride the tree-sitter walker for the two Go repos or the JS repo, i.e. for the entire reference corpus. The d1l.6 script already walks files itself; follow that pattern.

4. DEPENDENCY ON MetaCoding-279 REMOVED (2026-08-04, this re-scope). 279 (no tree-sitter fallback for go/js) does NOT block this bead, precisely because of (3): the spike's own conclusion is that d1l.10 reaches Go and JS comments without tree-sitter. 279 remains real and worth fixing for FTS on Go/JS, but it must not serialise citation mining behind a new-language-extractor project.

5. PATTERN LIST IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. Four families the obvious regex list misses, all of which must ship: connector words ("RFC 8693 in section 2.1"); openid.net/specs/<anything>.html#anchor (FAPI and openid-financial-api-* do not match openid-*-1_0); textual "OpenID Connect Core 1.0, section 3.1.3.6" (zitadel's dominant form — this alone took zitadel from 4 to 16 OIDC-Core sections); draft-ietf-*-NN#. None of the three repos use @see/@spec — keep that pattern for tier 2 only.

6. INDENTED DECLARATIONS ARE NOT OPTIONAL. fosite's densest file (oauth2.go, 28 citations) is one interface block; attributing only to ^func roughly halves the yield. Bind to exported interface methods and struct fields too.

7. MARKDOWN CITATIONS OUT OF SCOPE HERE (44 in fosite, 18 in node, 5 in zitadel). Not symbol-adjacent; a doc-ingestion lane is a separate bead if anyone wants them.

8. THE SEED'S PRIMARY CONSUMER IS NOW d1l.14 (calibration oracle), not coverage. Ship in a shape where "the sections fosite's own comments name" is directly queryable, per-repo.

title: SPIKE: measure RFC-citation density in fosite / zitadel-oidc / node-oidc-provider
description:
Half-hour check that decides the epic's shape. Tier 1 (citation mining from comments) is claimed to be the highest value-per-effort step, but that claim rests on reputation, NOT on measurement. Count comments matching rfc\d+#section-[\d.]+, 'RFC N, Section X.Y', section-symbol refs, openid-connect-core anchors, @see/@spec tags. Report: citations per KLOC, distinct sections cited, and what fraction of each repo's exported symbols sit within N lines of a citation.

If density is high -> tier 1 is the backbone and most of the mapping is free.
If sparse -> tier 1 collapses and the epic leans on tier 2 (annotations in identikey-oidc) + tier 3 (LM proposal). Re-scope before building anything.
notes:
SPIKE COMPLETE (2026-08-04, commit 6291449) — NOT CLOSED, awaiting epic re-scope decision.

MEASURED (pinned: fosite a5f0b09, zitadel/oidc 3c8b704, node-oidc-provider 4550cc3):
  section citations/KLOC:  fosite 6.61 | zitadel 4.11 | node 1.62
  distinct sections:       50 | 38 | 27  (~115 union across corpus)
  files with >=1 citation: 18.8% | 21.1% | 1.7% (4 of 235)
  exported symbols within 10 lines of a citation: 5.6% | 8.0% | 0.3%
  (N=3: 2.7/2.7/0.0; N=20: 8.6/12.5/0.3 — curve is flat, not clipped)
  test-code section citations: 7 | 7 | 0 across 65k test LOC

VERDICT: RE-SCOPE. Tier 1 does not collapse but is NOT the backbone.
'A large spec<->code mapping for free' is false by ~an order of magnitude.
node-oidc-provider — named in the design as citing constantly — is the sparsest by 4x
and what it cites is mostly OpenID4VCI, not the core RFCs.

CONSEQUENCES:
- d1l.10 (extractor): keep but demote to seed+oracle; must not gate anything. Cheap (hours).
- Tier 1's real value is the CALIBRATION ORACLE (design §2) -> benefits d1l.14.
- Coverage backbone must be tier 2 (annotations in identikey-oidc); d1l.11 (spec_coverage) can proceed independently.
- d1l.12 (spec_implementations/consensus/divergence) GOT HARDER: needs dense bindings in the reference repos, citations give 5-8%. Now depends on tier 3 at corpus scale — re-estimate, or scope v1 to the ~58 citation-bearing files.
- d1l.13 (TESTS_SPEC): the reference repos' tests are NOT a source (14 citations / 65k LOC). Must come from OIDF conformance suite naming.
- New cheap upside: propagate section bindings along the graph from the high-precision seed (citations reach 19-21% of Go FILES vs 6-8% of symbols).
- New unmeasured risk: tier 3 LM binding precision/cost at corpus scale is the epic's new load-bearing unknown — deserves its own spike before d1l.12 is estimated.

Findings: docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md
Script:   scripts/spike-citation-density.ts (reproducible: bun scripts/spike-citation-density.ts <repo> ...)

title: Write up what the OIDC exercise taught the porting workflow
description: Feed findings back into MetaCoding's porting design docs.
notes:
SCOPE NOTE 2026-08-04 (re-scope after d1l.6 + d1l.7). The write-up must carry the two spikes' methodological lessons, not just the OIDC feature findings — they are the more transferable output:

1. A DENSITY CLAIM ABOUT A CORPUS IS NOT EVIDENCE UNTIL IT IS COUNTED. The epic's tier-1 backbone rested on "fosite and node-oidc-provider cite RFC sections constantly", from reputation. Measured: 6.6 / 4.1 / 1.6 per KLOC, and the named exemplar (node-oidc-provider) was the sparsest of the three by 4x. Half an hour of counting re-shaped an epic.
2. EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE OF AN INDEX. hy6.16 reproduced in a new repo: a --scip run produced a complete, empty graph and reported success. The only honest assertion is non-zero edge counts BY TYPE, queried out of the store.
3. A DOCUMENTED FALLBACK IS NOT A FALLBACK UNTIL IT IS RUN. "Tree-sitter fallback caps the blast radius" was in the design and in a bead description; there is no tree-sitter lane for .go or .js at all.
4. CROSS-LANGUAGE COUNTS MEASURE THE LANGUAGE UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE (IMPLEMENTS 586 Go vs 24 JS; 88% type_alias inflation in JS symbol counts).

Also record the shape change itself: the epic moved from citation-mining-as-backbone to seed-plus-propagation, and the calibration-oracle argument (d1l.14) survived the demotion of the thing it was attached to. That distinction — density vs authority — is the reusable idea.

title: Spec-to-code linkage: bind RFC sections to graph nodes
description: Porting from a spec means tracking coverage against the spec, not against the source repo. Explore attaching spec-section identifiers (RFC 6749 s4.1.3, OIDC Core s3.1.2.1) to graph nodes so 'what have I not ported yet' becomes a graph query. This is the piece that distinguishes spec-driven porting from code translation.
close_reason: Superseded by d1l.8 (schema), d1l.9 (RFC ingestion) and d1l.10 (citation mining), which decompose it properly

title: CTKR role-equivalence: map reference structures onto Rust trait targets
description: fosite's handler/storage split is claimed to map ~1:1 onto Rust traits. Test whether ctkr same-role equivalence surfaces that automatically rather than by hand. Success criterion: the tool proposes the trait boundary a human would have chosen.
notes:
STRENGTHENED 2026-08-04 by d1l.7 — this bead just acquired the substrate it was missing, and a hard prerequisite.

THE NEW ASSET. scip-go computes GO INTERFACE SATISFACTION: 776 implementations in fosite, landing as 586 real IMPLEMENTS edges at BOTH type and method level (e.g. fosite.Config.GetTokenEndpointHandlers -> fosite.TokenEndpointHandlersProvider.GetTokenEndpointHandlers), for an 8.9s indexer run. Go is structurally typed — NOTHING in the source declares these relationships, so they are not recoverable by grep, by tree-sitter, or by any syntactic pass. This is exactly the handler/storage-split-to-Rust-trait mapping this bead is about, computed for free. It is a genuinely new asset the epic did not know it had.

PREREQUISITE WIRED: depends on d1l.2 (the corpus), which in turn depends on d1l.16 (there is no Go lane yet). Previously this bead had no dependencies at all, which was wrong — CTKR role-equivalence over an unindexed corpus is not a task.

CONSTRAINT FROM d1l.7 THAT CHANGES HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED: qualified-name SHAPE differs by lane. Go is package-FQN (github.com/ory/fosite.Fosite.WriteAccessError) and filePathOf() returns null for 100% of Go definitions; JS/TS/PHP are file-shaped (lib/helpers/errors.js::InvalidToken). No cross-language role matcher may key on string form — it must key on structure. Likewise IMPLEMENTS density is 586 (Go) vs 24 (JS): a role-equivalence score that leans on implements-degree will rank Go above JS for reasons that are about the type system, not the role.

title: Index the three reference OIDC implementations into a shared corpus
description: Cross-repo corpus so CTKR motif mining has something to compare. Three independent implementations of one spec is close to an ideal CTKR input: same semantics, different naming, different languages.
notes:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-04 after d1l.7 (docs/notes/2026-08-04-go-js-lane-spike.md, 44cc29d). THIS BEAD CANNOT PROCEED ON GO AS THINGS STAND.

BLOCKERS (all wired): MetaCoding-0sd (P1, index --scip exits 0 with an empty graph — fosite ships package.json+tsconfig.json so scip-typescript is selected, fails, and the failure is swallowed), MetaCoding-d1l.16 (there is NO Go lane at all: ScipLanguage = typescript|python|php, INDEXERS has no go entry, --scip-language rejects 'go'). Every Go number in the spike was produced MANUALLY with --load-scip --scip-language ts, which is a deliberate lie about the language column.

ESCAPE HATCH IF d1l.16 IS SLOW: drive scip-go out-of-band per repo and ingest with --load-scip, exactly as the spike did. Acceptable ONLY if (a) the run is scripted and committed so the corpus is reproducible, and (b) every ingest ASSERTS non-zero CALLS and IMPLEMENTS counts by type. An assertion on exit status is precisely the check that already failed (0sd).

WHAT A CORRECT RUN LOOKS LIKE (fosite @a5f0b09b, scip-go v0.2.7, 273 docs, 2,879 symbols):
CALLS 3274 | REFERENCES 7065 | IMPLEMENTS 586 | READS_FIELD 3936 | everything else 0.
node-oidc-provider @4550cc33 (scip-typescript, 413/413 files, 12,617 symbols):
CALLS 2557 | REFERENCES 3875 | IMPLEMENTS 24 | CONSTRUCTS 237.
Use these as the regression baseline; a corpus that does not reproduce them is empty or wrong.

OPERATIONAL FACTS:
 • Budget ~3-4 min store-load PER REPO. Indexers are fast (3-9s); loadScip is the cost (169s Go, 222s JS). Three-repo corpus ~10 min of ingest — fine, not interactive.
 • scip-go MOVED: github.com/scip-code/scip-go, NOT sourcegraph/. The old path fails to install.
 • npm install node-oidc-provider's deps BEFORE indexing: the spike measured 33,337 externalRefsSkipped with no node_modules, understating what a real JS index resolves.
 • zitadel/oidc was NOT indexed by the spike (same Go lane, no new lane information). Index it here and check its numbers against fosite's.
 • Go drops 42,126 external refs with NO boundary node (PHP has Pass-2b, Go gets 0). Every net/http and crypto/* call is invisible in the resulting corpus — record this as a known hole rather than discovering it in d1l.12.
 • The spike's artifacts were SANDBOX (session scratchpad). This bead is the one that writes to the production data dir; say which path explicitly when it closes.
GATE CAVEAT (from the MetaCoding-0sd fix, 0c13fa2): the index gate now FAILS a run whose coverage falls below --min-coverage (default 10%), so any repo genuinely indexed only in part — or a docs-only repo — will now exit non-zero unless run with --allow-empty-index or a lowered --min-coverage. Expect this when adding corpus repos; it is the gate working, not a new defect. Every run reports gate.coverage in its JSON, so check that number before reaching for the flag: reaching for --allow-empty-index to silence a real partial index is precisely the hy6.16 failure the gate was built to stop.

UPSIDE, same commit: this bead and d1l.16 can now TRUST THE EXIT CODE when indexing fosite, rather than hand-asserting edge counts after each ingest the way the d1l.7 spike had to.
CORRECTION 2026-08-04 — MY EARLIER NOTE ON THIS BEAD WAS WRONG. It said this bead and d1l.16 'can now TRUST THE EXIT CODE when indexing fosite' after the 0sd fix (0c13fa2). They cannot. A fresh judge refuted the gate (MetaCoding-4kg, P1) and a fresh architect confirmed the reading: the gate's checks read a REPO-WIDE census, so a run that contributes nothing into a store that ALREADY HOLDS that repo exits 0 with gate.ok true. A shared corpus is BY DEFINITION a store that already holds repos, so the second and every subsequent ingest here is exactly the coasting case.

WHAT REMAINS LOAD-BEARING until 4kg and 5fi are fixed: this bead's own instruction to assert NON-ZERO CALLS and IMPLEMENTS BY TYPE after every ingest. Do not substitute the exit code for it. The architect's note on why: an exit-status assertion is precisely the check that already failed in hy6.16.

ALSO RELEVANT HERE: e6z M2 — the gate's (repo, branch) scoping of the edge census is correct in code but undiscriminated by any fixture, because every test store holds exactly one repo. A SHARED CORPUS STORE IS WHERE THAT WOULD BITE, and this bead builds the first one.

title: Spec-anchored porting: spec sections as first-class graph nodes
description:
Design: docs/design/spec-anchored-porting.md

A second port shape alongside the farmOS loop. farmOS ports FROM a codebase, so intent must be inferred. Here there is NO source codebase - there is a written spec (RFC 6749/6750/7636/8414/9068/9700, OIDC Core) and N independent implementations of it: ory/fosite (Go, Apache-2.0), zitadel/oidc (Go, Apache-2.0), panva/node-oidc-provider (JS, MIT). Target: identikey-oidc (Rust).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE FEATURE: it is a calibration instrument for the whole intention-extraction program. The program's core problem (intention doc 7.2/10) is that it has no external ground truth - farmOS's N=2 rewrite separates intent from idiom empirically but nothing says what the intent WAS. Here the intent is written down normatively, so harvest precision/recall against cited RFC sections become computable numbers rather than adjudicated impressions. And the three implementations are different orgs, two languages, concurrent and independent - so convergence is evidence about the SPEC, not about a shared community's habits.

Core idea: bind spec sections into the graph as first-class nodes, so 'what have I not implemented', 'how does everyone else do 4.1.3', and 'where do implementations disagree' all become graph queries, tracked against the SPEC rather than against a source repo.

Tracked from the IdentiKey side as identikey-core-ror.

=====================================================================
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-04 AFTER TWO SPIKES. READ THIS BEFORE PLANNING WORK.
=====================================================================

d1l.6 (docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md, 6291449) and d1l.7 (docs/notes/2026-08-04-go-js-lane-spike.md, 44cc29d) both came back partly against the plan. The epic survives and is SHARPER, but three of its stated foundations were false.

WHAT WAS FALSIFIED

1. "Citation mining yields most of the mapping for free" — FALSE by an order of magnitude. Section citations run 6.61 / 4.11 / 1.62 per KLOC and touch 5.6% / 8.0% / 0.3% of exported symbols at N=10 lines (fosite / zitadel-oidc / node-oidc-provider). The whole-corpus yield is ~195 raw citations, ~115 distinct (spec, section) pairs. Tier 1 is a SEED, not the backbone.

2. "node-oidc-provider cites constantly" — FALSE, and it is the COUNTER-example, not the exemplar: 4 of 235 files carry a section citation, and what it does cite is dominated by OpenID4VCI, not the core RFCs this epic targets. Anywhere the epic treats it as the reference case, that is now wrong.

3. "Tree-sitter fallback caps the blast radius if the Go lane disappoints" — FALSE. There is no tree-sitter lane for .go/.js/.mjs/.cjs at all: symbols 0, edges 0, FTS tokens 0. And there is no Go SCIP lane either — every Go number in the spike was produced manually with --scip-language ts, a deliberate lie. On top of that, metacoding index --scip on fosite EXITS 0 WITH AN EMPTY GRAPH (hy6.16 reproduced; MetaCoding-0sd).

WHAT SURVIVED, AND WHAT IS NEW

• Tier 1 survives as a precise, cheap SEED (~115 sections, a ~350-line script that already exists) and — more importantly — as the CALIBRATION ORACLE of design §2. That argument needs AUTHORITY, not density, and the citations have it. d1l.14 is the beneficiary and is now the epic's principal payoff.
• The cited sections are not a random 5%: they are the load-bearing ones (RFC 6749 §3.1/§4.1, device flow, introspection, redirect-URI comparison), clustered in ~58 protocol-flow files where the real logic lives.
• GENUINELY NEW ASSET: scip-go computes GO INTERFACE SATISFACTION — 586 IMPLEMENTS edges from fosite alone, at type AND method level, for an 8.9s indexer run. Go is structurally typed, so nothing declares these and no syntactic pass can recover them. That is precisely the substrate d1l.3 needs to map reference structures onto Rust traits. The epic did not know it had this.
• Two specs the epic never listed are heavily cited and must be ingested: RFC 6819 (threat model, 7 sections in fosite) and RFC 3986 (URI comparison, 4).

THE CORRECTED SHAPE: SEED + PROPAGATION, NOT CITATION-MINING-AS-BACKBONE

Tier 1 seeds a small, high-precision set. Coverage of the TARGET comes from tier 2 annotations (unaffected by any of this — d1l.11 can proceed today). Coverage of the REFERENCE repos comes from propagating the seed through the graph (d1l.17) and/or tier-3 LM proposal (unmeasured), and that is now the epic's load-bearing unknown — measured by d1l.15 BEFORE d1l.12 is estimated.

ORDER (P1 first): d1l.16 Go lane + MetaCoding-0sd empty-graph guard -> d1l.2 corpus; in parallel d1l.9 RFC ingestion + d1l.8 schema (unaffected by both spikes, widest fan-out, nothing can invalidate them) and d1l.15 the tier-3 spike (deliberately NOT gated on the corpus). Then d1l.11 spec_coverage (tier 2, earliest daily value), d1l.10 seed extractor, d1l.14 calibration study. d1l.12 and d1l.13 are DEMOTED TO P3: d1l.12 rests on the unmeasured tier and must not be estimated before d1l.15 reports; d1l.13 lost its assumed source entirely (14 section citations across 65k lines of test code in all three repos COMBINED) and must be re-sourced from OIDF conformance-suite naming — real, but external work, and worth doing only once identikey-oidc actually runs the suite.

HONEST VALUATION. The epic claimed a large free spec-to-code mapping and it does not have one. What it does have: a real external oracle for the intention program (the thing the program most lacks), a divergence capability nothing else offers, and free Go interface-satisfaction edges. That is still worth building — but the coverage story now depends on an unmeasured tier, and if d1l.15 comes back badly, d1l.12 should ship scoped to the ~58 citation-bearing files and the epic should stop claiming corpus-wide spec coverage of the references.

title: shared-store asset_active is trivially true for never-created handles
description: Fresh-reader finding from the sensor round (MetaCoding-ej0): wave1/shared-store/src/store.ts assetActive() returns 'no asset_archived event for this handle', so ANY garbage or never-created handle reads active=true. A sensor emits no asset_created either (it births through sensor_asset_created), so asset_active(sensor) currently passes only by this looseness — the probe cannot distinguish 'active asset' from 'no asset at all'. The trivially-satisfiable-check family the iteration methodology targets. Fix direction: assetActive should require SOME birth event for the handle (asset_created OR a feature-local *_asset_created kind) before answering true; a handle with no birth is UNANSWERABLE, never true. Related latent wrinkle: folds keyed off asset_created (e.g. store.assetName) do not see sensor assets. Builder+reader agreed pre-existing, not introduced by 3b3dad4.
notes: FIXED c84afed, fresh-read VERIFIED (reader-5xa): all six identity ports reproduce exactly (sensor 14/14, structure 6/6, plant_type 18/18, lab_test 22/22, equipment 7/7, material 5/5), bun 201/201, pytest 875. (2) birth==family-asset is convention-bound, not enforced: a future non-birth asset-family kind carrying assetId would fake a birth (asset_archived is deliberately family lifecycle). (3) WAVE-BOUNDARY DIVERGENCE for the Elenchus: spine-asset's own store answers FALSE (a value) for unknown handles with no unanswerable channel, and its createdEvent birth-detection recognizes only asset_created (would miss sensor_asset_created) — two readings of the same question, deliberately not harmonized.

title: Fixture schema admits non-reproducible and non-agnostic fixtures
description: Two schema-level gaps found by observation. (1) A relative 'at' plus any timestamp-returning probe produces a fixture that cannot self-verify — w0b first self-verified at 63.6%, every failure a uniform +24s wall-clock gap; caught only because self-verify ran twice, fixed by hand. Forbid relative at in such flows or teach the format a flow-relative expected value. (2) There is no way to mark a fixture corroboration-only / order-sensitive: w0a-2's observed 3.0 encodes farmOS insertion-id order (6 permutations yield 4 distinct values), so it scores as a false green today and a false failure under any other replica ordering.
close_reason: Shipped + proven. (1) Relative-at + timestamp-probe now REJECTED at load (ProbeSpec.returns_timestamp); verified by rebuilding the original w0b defect — rejected with reason and fix, before the oracle is touched. (2) Order-sensitivity is DETECTED, not declared: detect_order_sensitivity() finds same-effective-time writes against one subject; re-recording w0a's flow against live farmOS classified it corroboration-only unprompted, with the reason, in provenance. Evidence class travels WITH the pack (Provenance.evidence_class), precedence pack < manifest < --marks, but a pack-carried mark cannot be UNDONE: a port attempting to re-admit an unscoreable fixture gets a declaration problem. No fixture ids churned (provenance is outside the content hash). 585 py / 475 TS.

title: Recorder must record a REFUSAL instead of dying on it
description: record_session aborts on the first AdapterError, so a write the source REFUSES — the sharpest semantic signal available — kills the run instead of becoming a fixture. w0b lost 1 of 12 flows this way, and the UniqueBirthLog 422 (farmOS refuses a second birth claim rather than resolving it) became a footnote instead of an asset. Add an expect_refusal / observed-error step so refusal semantics are recordable.
close_reason: Shipped + proven live. 'refused' is a glossary assertion term answered by the ATTEMPT; FlowSpec.expect_refusal declares an expected refusal while RefusalNotObserved prevents fabricating one when the source accepts; RecordingClient now logs the refused request so the source's own words reach provenance (previously discarded — the exception propagated before any observation was appended); record_session_result survives per-flow failures and the CLI reports UNRECORDED FLOWS and exits non-zero; the runner verifies a refusal by attempting it, so an implementation that ACCEPTS a refused write fails (a divergence no read-side probe can see). PROOF: the flow the pilot lost (w0b-two-birth-records-one-animal) now records 1/1 and self-verifies 100% against live farmOS, with the 422 captured verbatim. 578 py / 475 TS.

title: Single-repo / endofunctor mode for functor discovery (diagonal exclusion + depth-as-dial)
description:
functor_between currently assumes distinct repos (C_A -> C_B). Add a single-repo mode: functor_between(R, R) with the diagonal (s->s) EXCLUDED, to surface non-trivial INTERNAL functors — isomorphic subsystems within one project (a pattern instantiated twice, parallel modules). Without diagonal exclusion the search returns the trivial identity (coverage 1.0). Also codify depth-as-a-dial in the tool docs.

## Context
From the 2026-07-13 design discussion. Cross-repo isomorphism is the native case; single-repo needs diagonal exclusion. Depth is a use-case knob: --depth 1 profiles for role/symmetry SURFACING (role_equivalent — you WANT the orbits), --depth 2 (WL refinement, commit 611ae33) for precise 1:1 correspondence (it deliberately shrinks orbits). Zero-profile ~22.7% is a shared structural-isolation floor at any depth. Directly useful for the subsystem-spec-extraction use case: verifying two subsystems within one project are isomorphic, and as the port-verifier (functor_between(S_original, S_reimplemented)). See docs/design/ct-functor-discovery.md and docs/notes/functor-spike/2hop-findings.md.

title: Friendly single-writer lock error

title: Staleness detection: graph vs current HEAD + dirty files
description: Emptiness is only half the trap; the worse half is a graph frozen at index time that LOOKS right after the tree moved. graph_callers silently goes stale once files change. We already ship live lsp_references as the fallback — this tells the agent WHEN to prefer it.
design: Extend store.summary() / describe_api with staleness: compare the stored repo_commit_sha against live 'git rev-parse HEAD' and count dirty files via 'git status --porcelain'. Surface { headBehind: bool, indexedCommit, currentCommit, dirtyFiles }. describe_api note: 'graph indexed at X, HEAD is Y, N dirty files — prefer lsp_references for changed files.'
