title: judge-identity-wave-2026-08-03.md cites a nonexistent ADR filename (…-immutable.md); the file is …-mutable.md
description:
From results/wave2/synthesis-wave2-2026-08-12.md, dispositioning residual 1 the wave-2 Elenchus left for a human, which it summarised as 'worth one grep'. THE GREP IS DONE (farmos-port@6a3c0c5) and the risk is SMALLER than the Elenchus feared — recorded so nobody re-runs it.

FULL SWEEP over *.md, *.json, *.jsonl, *.ts, *.py for 'animal-type-required-single'. Every hit:
  - results/wave2/adr/hy6.2-animal-type-required-single-mutable.md  (the file itself)
  - results/wave2/judge-identity-wave-2026-08-03.md:250 — cites '...-immutable.md'  <- THE ONLY STALE REFERENCE
  - results/wave2/elenchus-wave2-2026-08-09.md:277 and the synthesis — both discussing this

NO manifest, no port.manifest.json, no composition step, no code, and no other ADR references the old name. The Elenchus's worry was that a program greps for it; nothing does.

WHAT REMAINS: one dangling citation inside a sealed reading artifact. A reader following the judge's footnote gets a 404 on the ADR whose content the judge is arguing about — and that ADR's title turns on exactly the word that differs (mutable vs immutable), so the 404 lands precisely where a reader most needs the source.

RECOMMENDED FIX, and it is a convention question worth settling once: do NOT silently edit the judge report. It is a sealed reading and editing it destroys the record of what the reader actually saw — the same reason ADR hy6.8's body was left intact under a correction banner rather than rewritten. Prefer a correction footnote in the judge report, or a pointer row wherever this project records artifact corrections.

The general question this raises, which is bigger than this bug: sealed reading artifacts have no falsification mechanism. See MetaCoding-mky2 for the same gap in punts.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: A reader following judge-identity-wave-2026-08-03.md:250 reaches the real ADR; the judge report's original text is preserved rather than silently rewritten.

title: floors.ts: evaluateFloors has no production caller and the INSTRUMENT/CHECK tier has no consumer
description:
Judge of MetaCoding-rjx step 2, tree 5a0c891. Not mutation survivors — structural observations from grepping the live tree.

1. evaluateFloors() is documented as 'the verb the design document and the bead advertise, so it is the one that enforces' (floors.ts:286-289). grep over src/ and scripts/: zero callers outside src/testkit/floors.test.ts. Every real gate goes through SmokeRun.finish(), which re-implements the throw at line 446 rather than calling evaluateFloors. The MetaCoding-3ad lesson is therefore carried forward in a function nothing uses, and enforced a second time by duplicated code in finish(). Both paths are covered by mutation (M13, M14 both killed) so this is not currently a hole — it is two copies of one invariant, one of them dead.

2. FloorsResult.instrumentFailed has no consumer. grep: it is set at floors.ts:257 and :444, read at :268 to choose a word in explainFloors' first line, and read nine times in floors.test.ts. Nothing branches on it — INSTRUMENT and CHECK failures both throw FloorsRefused and both exit 1, identically. The 'structurally distinct' tier is a diagnostic string plus an assertion about itself. That satisfies design doc F4.2 as written, but the mechanism claimed in the builder's report ('an INSTRUMENT failure, structurally distinct') is distinct in the report, not in any decision.

DECIDE: either give the tier a consumer (e.g. smoke-all.ts reporting instrument failures separately from short runs, which is the diagnosis a suite operator actually needs), or narrow the claim to 'distinct in the message'.
notes:
evaluateFloors/observeFloors are exercised at src/testkit/floors.test.ts:362-370 — evaluateFloors THROWS on refusal, observeFloors returns it, and a floor naming an unpublished field is caught.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE, NOT AGAINST A REPORT: 64 pass / 0 fail across src/testkit on 2026-08-12.

TWO CAVEATS, both honest:
1. NOT INDEPENDENTLY JUDGED. No fresh adversary has read this work.
2. ITS EVIDENCE COMMIT WAS LOST. The agent that did this work was killed by an API error, and before dying it reported that its changes had already been swept into MetaCoding e477693 — a commit labelled fix(hy6.60) that actually carries 13 files from three different agents, because one of them staged everything. So the code is present and passing, but the mutation table that would normally accompany it does not exist. See MetaCoding 96877c9, which records the misattribution and adds a hook refusing the stage-everything flag.

title: Nothing checks a ledger artifact for its PREFLIGHT row — the evidence half is written but never read
description:
Fresh judge of hy6.28 (farmos-port 6a75c1d).

tools/ledger.py:336 claims: 'a ledger file that does not open with a PREFLIGHT row is a run that skipped the gate, which is now readable from the artifact instead of only from the terminal.' True — port_runs/wave2/identity-farm-org/observe/verify.jsonl line 1 is {"id": "PREFLIGHT", "status": "ok", types: [7 types]}.

But nothing READS it. grep -rn PREFLIGHT over the repo finds only ledger.py, its tests, and prose. There is no artifact validator, no CI step, no judge tool that refuses a verify.jsonl lacking a PREFLIGHT row. So the readable-from-the-artifact property is available to a human who thinks to look, which is the same shape as the original defect: a check nobody must remember to run.

The four hand-rolled ledgers (see MetaCoding-hy6.36) emit no PREFLIGHT row at all, so such a validator would immediately flag them — which is the point.

REMEDY: a tiny tools/check_ledger_artifact.py that asserts, over any *.jsonl observe artifact: line 1 is PREFLIGHT with status ok, its types list is non-empty, a SUMMARY row exists, and a CLEANUP-VERIFY row exists with empty by_id_still_present. Cheap, and it turns the row into evidence rather than decoration.

title: resource_type() fail-open is a third escape hatch the ledger docstring does not name
description:
Fresh judge of hy6.28 (farmos-port 6a75c1d).

tools/ledger.py:372 gates only when resource_type(path) is not None. Any path the parser cannot read passes the cross-check SILENTLY. Measured:

   'http://localhost:8095/api/asset/animal'  -> None
   '/api/taxonomy_term/animal-type'          -> None
   '/api/Asset/Animal'                       -> None
   '/api/asset'                              -> None
   '//api/log/medical'                       -> None

and against a ledger gated on {asset--animal}:

   PROBED (no refusal): http://localhost:8095/api/log/medical
   PROBED (no refusal): /api/taxonomy_term/animal-type
   refused: /api/log/medical
   traffic actually sent: [('GET','http://localhost:8095/api/log/medical'), ('GET','/api/taxonomy_term/animal-type')]

The fail-open is DELIBERATE and tested (tools/test_ledger.py:611-614: 'an underivable path is one the cross-check has to let through', so /oauth/token is not turned into a false refusal). I am not arguing it should fail closed.

What is missing is honesty in the place that exists for exactly this: ledger.py's 'What it does NOT close, asked as how would I fake this?' list (lines 65-74) names two escape hatches — raw self.transport() and gate=lambda — and calls both LOUD in the file. This third one is not named, and unlike the other two it is INVISIBLE: a probe path that reads as ordinary passes the gate with no trace. Whether reachable today depends entirely on the transport (farm-org's call() concatenates ORACLE+path, so an absolute URL would not work there) — that is a property of each build, not of the guard.

REMEDY: name it in that list, and/or have _require_gated write a NOTE row (not a refusal) when resource_type returns None for a path that is not a known non-resource endpoint, so the artifact records the ungated traffic.
notes:
JUDGE ROUND TWO (farmos-port 587c193): close CONFIRMED, honestly closed.

I asked for the docstring entry and the docstring entry is what shipped, in full and accurately: ledger.py:73-84 names the fail-open, gives the four shapes that parse to None (absolute URL, hyphen, capital, one segment), says out loud that it is INVISIBLE unlike the other two entries, and carries the reachability caveat about farm-org's ORACLE+path concatenation. The closing line was also fixed — 'The first two are LOUD in the file; the third is not, which is why it is stated here in full.' That is not closed-by-docstring dodging a fix; it is the fix I argued for, because failing closed would refuse /oauth/token.

Staying closed. The one thing that came out of the same docstring edit and does NOT belong here is the sentence about gate= also disabling the same-oracle check — that one WAS closeable rather than merely nameable, and is filed separately as hy6.43 with the measurement (19 of 29 tests currently run with the new guard off).

title: parseArgs silently ignores --flag=value, storing a garbage key
description: FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07: 'it cost me one entire false-negative round'. src/cli/main.ts:63-70 handles only the space-separated form, so 'metacoding index . --repo=foo' stores a key named '--repo=foo' and leaves repo unset, with no warning. An operator's flag reads as absent and the run proceeds with defaults.

title: build.ts leftovers: symbolsPreexisting consumed nowhere, relPropCache is a module global, normalizeEmptyStrings writes repo-wide
description: FRESH JUDGE, 2026-08-07, three small ones in src/store/build.ts. (1) symbolsPreexisting is declared 'REPORTED, never thresholded' and is consumed by NOTHING in src/ — the one number that would have made the per-commit corruption visible is computed and discarded. (2) relPropCache is a module-level global keyed on edge kind only, never store-scoped and never invalidated, so two stores with different schemas in one process share it. (3) normalizeEmptyStrings writes repo-wide from a module whose thesis is slice isolation.

title: metacoding port init emits the ledger TEMPLATE, not a library ports import
description:
From docs/design/lessons-as-mechanism.md's 'what I am NOT building' section, and it is the constructive half of that refusal.

The architect declined to generalize farmos-port/tools/ledger.py into a first-class MetaCoding Checker class, and the reason is the inversion MetaCoding-1gt.1 exists to prevent: after the three generalizable parts are extracted (floors-with-coverage, the structural guard, custody), what REMAINS is knowledge about farmOS's boundary — JSON:API pagination, links.next, delete ordering, the 403 reach-through. Moving that into the instrument puts the target's knowledge in the instrument's tree.

The right home is the scaffold that port init emits (MetaCoding-1gt): a template a port COPIES AND OWNS. That also converts the failure where extraction quietly loses guards — the shared ledger dropped the request body and the coverage row that all four hand-written versions had — into a DIFF against the template rather than a rediscovery.
acceptance_criteria: port init emits a ledger template carrying the union of the four builds' guards. A port that has diverged from the template can be diffed against it, so a lost guard is visible rather than rediscovered. Depends on MetaCoding-1gt.

title: php.ts property_declaration drops its own initializer's tokens
description:
src/extractor/php.ts:86-90 returns WITHOUT recursing into children. So 'private $handler = self::DEFAULT_MODE;' contributes the token 'handler' but not 'DEFAULT_MODE' — confirmed by a token dump where DEFAULT_MODE appears once (from the const_declaration) despite occurring twice in the source.

The comment on php.ts:89 — 'property bodies carry no further declarations worth descending into' — is true about DECLARATIONS and false about TOKENS. And the token table is the repo's advertised index over the AST's blind spots, so a blind spot in the blind-spot index compounds.

Found by the within-file-coverage.md probe.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens are collected from property initializers. Evidence: a property with a non-trivial initializer contributes its tokens; CONTRAST the same expression in a method body, which contributes them today. Same expression, two positions, one verdict.

title: Cross-lane symbol-parent disagreement as a CI extractor instrument
description:
within-file-coverage.md kills 'differential coverage between lanes' as a MANIFEST field — it only helps where both lanes ran, and where both ran you would rather just trust SCIP. coverage-claims.md:99 already puts cross-lane comparison in the right slot: record as an observation, never as a gate.

But it is the ONLY mechanism anyone has proposed that catches MISATTRIBUTION, which is the residual the census cannot see. Relocated here: an extractor-development instrument in src/extractor/'s test suite, over a fixture corpus, run in CI.

Motivating case: an anonymous default-export class. SCIP places the method inside the class; tree-sitter places it inside the file. The symbol ids disagree, mechanically and visibly.
acceptance_criteria: A CI check over a fixture corpus that reports every symbol whose PARENT differs between the SCIP and tree-sitter lanes. Evidence: the anonymous default-export class fixture is reported; CONTRAST a named class fixture is not.

title: Within-file residual: the unclaimed-form census
description:
docs/design/within-file-coverage.md Part C — the substance of that design. Depends on the two P1s above.

Per (file, grammar), two sets over the grammar's node-type alphabet: 'seen' (every named node type that occurred, from a cursor walk — extractor-independent) and 'emitted_from' (every node type that was the node argument at a site that actually pushed a Symbol/Edge/TokenRow/EdgeCandidate). Residual = seen minus emitted_from, plus (occurrences, emissions) for types in both.

THREE THINGS ARE LOAD-BEARING:
1. Nothing is declared. emitted_from is the set of types the run DEMONSTRABLY produced output from.
2. Recording at the EMISSION site, not the dispatch site. Several rules dispatch then emit nothing (typescript.ts:143-147 unnamed declarations; python.ts:152-159 assignment outside a class; php.ts:87 emitProperties only when insideClass). Instrumenting the switch would mark those types claimed while emitting nothing — a false claim minted by the instrument itself.
3. It is a SET, so there is nothing to threshold. The question is never 'is the residual large', it is 'is attribute_group in it, and how often'.

IN MANIFEST.json, NEVER IN THE KEY. The census is a pure function of (file digests, grammar wasm digest, extractor_version), all of which are already keyed — so keying it adds zero discrimination, and a fact that cannot move a key cannot silently become a gate.

COST: +88ms on farmOS's 789 files (+26% on the extract path), measured. Under 60KB payload.

THE AUTHOR'S OWN STRONGEST ATTACK, recorded: the (occurrences, emissions) DEFICIT does not survive the NO_RELATIONAL_EDGES test. Any Python codebase has assignment occurrences much greater than emissions on healthy code, because only class-level annotated assignments emit a field. The deficit is a count used as a proxy for capability, so it MUST NEVER BE A VERDICT — census row only, ranked, read by a person.
acceptance_criteria: Cursor pass for seen + emission-site recording for emitted_from; ranked residual in MANIFEST.json; never keyed, never gating. Evidence: (a) property_promotion_parameter and attribute_group appear in the farmOS residual with correct counts, and LEAVE it once the extractor is fixed; (b) dispatch-site and emission-site instrumentation give DIFFERENT answers on a file with one anonymous and one named class, or the instrumentation is decorative; (c) a Python corpus with a large assignment deficit and a correct graph, asserting nothing in the build consults the deficit; (d) two independent builds produce byte-identical census payloads; (e) mutation test: delete one case from recognizeDeclaration, assert that type appears in the residual, anchor asserted and baseline clean before AND after.
notes: Deprioritized 2026-08-07 with the rest of the within-file-coverage line: the census's motivating example is a PHP one, and PHP is not the focus.

title: '--scip off' silently ENABLES scip
description:
resolveScipWanted (src/cli/main.ts:392-395) returns false only for the literal string 'false'; any other value falls through to 'if (have.any) return true'. So '--scip off', '--scip no', '--scip 0' all ENABLE scip.

Same defect parseGateFlags was hardened against thirty lines below at main.ts:263-280, whose own comment records it: 'ANY value other than the literal false ENABLED --allow-empty-index'. The lesson was learned in one function and not applied to the one directly above it.

Fails safe in direction (scip ON not off) so P3 — but a fresh architect hit it while running an experiment and measured a configuration it had not asked for, which is how it was found. A flag that silently does the opposite of what it says costs measurement time even when the direction is safe.

TO CLOSE: one shared strict boolean-flag parser used by both call sites, with a contrast pair — off/no/0/false all disable, and an unrecognised value is a loud error rather than a silent default.

title: summarizeHealth: a repo whose ingest produced only external boundary nodes now vanishes from the health summary
description:
FRESH-JUDGE-3 residue from MetaCoding-scc, at HEAD 05d8a93 (src/mcp/health-gate.ts sha256 e5c9a6d1ba9c...).

scc's predicate ('WHERE s.language <> \'external\' OR s.file <> \'\'') is correct and no real symbol a lane writes can be hidden by it (verified: fileless-with-a-real-language, external-with-a-file, and empty-language symbols all still enumerate). But it widens the pre-existing 'a slice with no symbols is not enumerated' hole from 'zero symbols' to 'only boundary nodes'.

EXECUTED (sandbox copy of HEAD): a healthy j3r@main, plus 4 boundary nodes for
'ghost-repo' and an HONEST REFUSED record for ghost-repo@main ->
  slices [j3r@main HEALTHY], established TRUE, ghost-repo not enumerated, its REFUSED
  record never read, gateQueryAnswer([], summary) -> ok:true rows:[].
An empty answer about ghost-repo is then byte-identical to an empty answer from a fit
graph — the hy6.16 shape, for a repo the system HAS a refusal on file for.

ROOT CAUSE: summarizeHealth enumerates slices from the GRAPH only. The health DB
already knows about slices the graph does not show.

FIX DIRECTION: union the graph enumeration with readAllIndexHealth's slices, so a
recorded REFUSED/RUNNING slice is reported even when the graph holds nothing (or only
boundary nodes) for it. DONE = the ghost-repo fixture above, established FALSE, plus
the contrast half (a store with one HEALTHY slice and no stray records stays TRUE).

title: status prints the fitness line once per repo ROW, not once per health SLICE
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-04 on the production MetaCoding store immediately after the first gated reindex (MetaCoding @ 05d8a93).

'metacoding status' printed the IDENTICAL fitness line FOUR TIMES:
  ✓ MetaCoding@main: fitness HEALTHY (run ..., commit 05d8a93, 30696 symbols / 57588 relational edges, correspondence exact 100%).  [x4]

Cause: the store holds four repo ROWS for MetaCoding (one per indexed commit — 1ddb475, 5565f6f, 05d8a93, and one with no commit), while index_health holds ONE slice keyed (repo, branch). formatIndexState appears to iterate repo rows and print the slice's line for each, instead of iterating the health slices.

Cosmetic in itself, but it MISREPRESENTS THE THING THE GATE EXISTS TO REPORT: a reader sees four verdicts and cannot tell whether that is four slices agreeing or one slice repeated. The whole design turns on a reader being able to see, precisely, which slices are established. A duplicated verdict is a small step from a verdict attributed to the wrong slice.

TO CLOSE: one line per health slice, and a contrast fixture with TWO genuinely distinct slices (e.g. two branches, or two repos in one store) asserting exactly two lines — a fixture with one slice cannot discriminate this, which is why it shipped.

title: index fitness: isAbandonedRun cannot detect PID REUSE — a recycled pid reads as 'running now' forever
description:
FRESH-JUDGE FINDING at tree 7c03e77 (src/store/health.ts sha256 7a0d0f4d6e8e...).

isAbandonedRun uses process.kill(pid, 0) and treats only ESRCH as abandoned. MEASURED (sandbox judge2-slice), writing a RUNNING record with a chosen pid and a heartbeat_at of 2020-01-01:
  pid = own live pid  -> abandoned FALSE  (correct)
  pid = 999999 unused -> abandoned TRUE   (correct)
  pid = 1 (launchd, an unrelated process) -> abandoned **FALSE**
  pid = null          -> abandoned FALSE  (documented behaviour)

So once the recorded pid is recycled by an unrelated process — routine on a long-lived machine, and pid recycling is fast on macOS/Linux — the record reports 'an index run is IN PROGRESS since <date>' forever, which is precisely the 'RUNNING marker that cries wolf' failure health.ts names as its own fake-it #2 and claims pid+heartbeat closes.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND THE DIRECTION IS SAFE: RUNNING is unestablished either way, so summarizeHealth still reports established=false and queries still refuse (I confirmed this in the same run). Nothing is wrongly reported HEALTHY. The damage is to the HUMAN message only — formatHealthLine says 'IN PROGRESS' with the wrong fix ('wait') instead of 'DIED without finalizing' with the right one ('re-run metacoding index'). That is the user-trains-themselves-to-ignore-it failure, just slower.

NOTE the record already carries heartbeat_at and it is IGNORED by isAbandonedRun — in my test the heartbeat was over 6 years stale and the run still read as live.

FIX DIRECTION: the heartbeat is already there; use it. Treat a RUNNING record whose heartbeat_at is older than a few multiples of the 5s heartbeat interval as abandoned regardless of what the pid says. Optionally also compare the process start time against started_at (ps -o lstart= -p <pid>) so a recycled pid is positively identified rather than inferred.

title: port_runs builds do not typecheck under the repo tsconfig
description:
Observed 2026-08-04 while agents were reading files in farmos-port: the LSP reports errors across port_runs/wave2/*/build/*.ts on a CLEAN tree (d0bb62e, no modified sources). Two distinct families:

1. Unresolved relative imports — port_bridge.ts imports '../../wave1/shared-store/src/bridge.ts' and '../../wave1/shared-store/src/store.ts', neither of which resolves from the repo root. That build cannot be typechecked at all as the repo is laid out.
2. Branded-EntityId violations at scale — plain strings passed where EntityId ({ readonly [idBrand]: 'EntityId' }) is required, plus readonly-property assignment errors, across store.ts, port_bridge.ts and several *.test.ts.

Why it matters rather than being cosmetic: the brand exists to stop an arbitrary string being used as an entity handle, and it is currently not load-bearing in the places it fires. 'Documented gate that was not a gate' is a pattern this project has already been bitten by (docs/design/iteration-methodology.md). Also unknown right now: whether these builds pass 'bun test' despite the type errors, which would mean the tests are running against untypechecked code.

TO CLOSE: establish whether port_runs builds are IN SCOPE for the repo typecheck. If yes, fix or exclude deliberately and record which. If no, say so explicitly so the next reader does not mistake red squiggles for a broken build.

title: Divergence charter: farmOS2 is a better farmOS, and the verifier must know it
description: Duke, 2026-08-03: 'we've overall been going mainly for consistency with source... let's just make farmos2 good, rather than 1:1 parity.' That is a standing change of posture, not a one-off, and it has a consequence the port-verify machinery does not yet handle: every deliberate improvement scores as a FAILURE unless it carries a bound decision AND a typed sanction naming the glossary assertion term. Four divergences were bound under the new posture (quick-provenance superseded, composite-act-atomicity, term-acyclicity, reference-list-hygiene, term-revisioning superseded) and THREE OF THEM CARRY NO SANCTIONS because no recorded fixture asks the question they diverge on. That is a coverage gap, not agreement, and it means the divergences are currently invisible to scoring in both directions.
acceptance_criteria: A short charter doc states the posture (fidelity is the default, divergence is deliberate and recorded) and the rule that follows from it: a divergence without a fixture that can see it is unproven. Each of the four new divergences either gains a fixture that exercises it or is explicitly marked unobservable-by-current-flows with the reason. The judge/verifier reporting distinguishes 'matches source', 'declared divergence, observed as intended' and 'declared divergence, never exercised'.
notes:
SCOPE LOOSENED 2026-08-03 by Duke: 'we dont need to be too anal. let's loosen up and fly. divergences that're unmeasured we can write down like ADRs.' P1 -> P3.

NO LONGER REQUIRED: that every divergence carry a fixture exercising it. That was over-tight — it would have gated shipping on writing tests for cases no recorded flow reaches, which is exactly the ceremony the wave-2 risk partition exists to avoid.

WHAT SURVIVES (the cheap half): an unmeasured divergence gets an ADR — the question, what was or was not measured, the options, the choice, and what would falsify it. A decision rationale already carries most of that; the ADR just makes it findable and separates 'we chose this' from 'we tested this'. Subagents on the identity ports are writing these to farmos-port/results/wave2/adr/ as they go, so the habit is already in place.

DROPPED: growing the verifier a 'declared divergence, never exercised' reporting bucket. Do it if the scoring ever actually misleads someone; not pre-emptively.

title: FlowSpec DSL: a flow cannot begin from pre-existing state (the 'migration entry point' gap)
description:
The last of the thirteen named DSL expressibility gaps from
wave1-readiness-2026-07-20 §2. Split out of MetaCoding-b0s on 2026-07-28
rather than guessed at, because it is UNDERSPECIFIED: the phrase "no
migration entry point" appears once in that list and nowhere else in the
tree, and every other gap in the list came with a mechanism.

Most likely reading: a flow's `given` clause CREATES everything it names, so
every fixture starts from an empty world. A migration — the D7->D8 shape
farmos-differential.md discusses, or any port that must adopt an existing
farm's data — starts from state nobody in the flow created, and there is no
way to say "given a farm that already looks like this".

Why it is a different shape of change from the rest of b0s, and why it was
not folded in: every other gap was a missing VERB or a missing READ, closed
by adding a term and recording it. This one questions the `given` clause
itself, and it collides with two properties the oracle currently relies on:

  - reproducibility. A fixture reproduces because it builds its own world.
    A fixture that depends on pre-existing state reproduces only against a
    source that still has that state — which the shared, mutable oracle
    does not guarantee, and a fresh bring-up definitely does not.
  - the no-ids rule. Pre-existing state has to be NAMED somehow, and the
    obvious ways (a uuid, a machine name) are exactly the representation
    leak the storage lint exists to reject.

So the real question is not "add a verb" but "what is a reproducible way to
say a world already exists". Possible directions, none chosen:
  (a) a fixture-scoped seed pack — a prelude flow whose output is the
      starting state of another, chained by seal rather than by id;
  (b) `given` gains an adopt-by-domain-identity form (name + kind), with the
      adapter resolving or creating, and the fixture asserting on values
      rather than on identity;
  (c) declare it out of scope for the value oracle and handle migration
      fidelity with a different instrument entirely.

Do not start this without deciding which question is being answered. It is
filed at P3 because nothing currently blocks on it.

title: Bind OIDF conformance test names to spec sections (TESTS_SPEC)
description: Closes the loop: failing conformance test -> the section it tests -> my symbols bound to that section (or their absence) -> how the three references handle it. Turns a red CI run into a navigable query instead of a search problem.
notes:
SOURCE FALSIFIED 2026-08-04 by d1l.6 — RE-SOURCED AND DEFERRED (P2 -> P3).

WHAT DIED. The unstated assumption was that the reference implementations' own test suites cite spec sections and could be mined the same way as prod code. MEASURED: 14 section citations across 65,000 lines of test code in ALL THREE repos combined — 7 in fosite (19.1k test LOC), 7 in zitadel (12.3k), and ZERO in node-oidc-provider (34.0k). See docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md §2. There is no cheap TESTS_SPEC harvest anywhere in the corpus. This finding was not asked for by that spike; it is propagated here deliberately.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOW ASSUME. Bindings come from the OIDF conformance suite's OWN naming — its test/test-plan identifiers and module metadata (e.g. oidcc-*, fapi-*), mapped to sections by hand or by a one-off LM pass over the suite's published test descriptions. That is EXTERNAL data acquisition, not graph mining: a different kind of task from the one this bead was filed as, and the estimate must be rebuilt from scratch.

WHY DEFERRED RATHER THAN DROPPED. The loop it closes (failing conformance test -> section -> my symbols -> how the references handle it) is still the single best debugging path in the design (§8), and it is one of the few parts of the epic that no other bead delivers. But its value only lands when identikey-oidc is actually running the conformance suite in CI, which it is not yet, and its cost went up. It should not compete with the critical path (d1l.8/d1l.9/d1l.16/d1l.15) for attention now.

NEW HARD PREREQUISITES (wired 2026-08-04): d1l.8 (the TESTS_SPEC table itself) and d1l.9 (SpecSection nodes to bind TO). Both were implicit and neither was wired; a conformance-name mapping with nowhere to land is a spreadsheet.

title: spec_implementations + spec_consensus + spec_divergence MCP tools
description:
spec_implementations(section) -> every symbol in every indexed repo bound to it. spec_consensus -> CTKR structural comparison across the N implementations. spec_divergence(doc) -> sections where they structurally disagree.

DIVERGENCE IS THE MORE VALUABLE SIGNAL. Where three independent implementations disagree about one section, exactly one of these holds: the spec is ambiguous there (and a naive port picks one reading and is subtly wrong), the section is genuinely optional, or one of them has a bug. All three are worth knowing BEFORE writing code, none are visible from the spec alone or from any single implementation. This is what justifies indexing three implementations instead of one, and it is unavailable in the farmOS shape entirely.
notes:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-04 after d1l.6. THIS IS THE BEAD THAT GOT HARDER, AND IT IS DEMOTED TO P3 UNTIL d1l.15 REPORTS.

WHY. spec_implementations / spec_consensus / spec_divergence all need DENSE bindings in the REFERENCE repos — a section with two bound symbols cannot tell you whether three implementations agree. Tier 1 supplies 5.6% / 8.0% / 0.3% of exported symbols (docs/notes/2026-08-04-rfc-citation-density-spike.md). Tier 2 (annotations) is in identikey-oidc, i.e. the target, and does nothing for the references. So these tools now rest ENTIRELY on tier 3 (LM-proposed IMPLEMENTS_SPEC) at full corpus scale — a materially larger and riskier scope than the original "only for what tiers 1-2 miss", and the cost/precision of that tier is UNMEASURED. Hence the new hard dependency on d1l.15.

TWO WAYS FORWARD, decide after d1l.15:
 (a) FULL SCOPE — LM-bind the corpus. Only if d1l.15 comes back cheap and precise. Re-estimate then; do not carry the old estimate.
 (b) V1 SCOPED TO THE SEED — restrict to the ~58 citation-bearing files across the three repos (30/160 fosite, 24/114 zitadel, 4/235 node). That is where the protocol-flow logic actually lives (fosite oauth2.go, authorize_helper.go, authorize_request_handler.go, handler/openid/flow_{hybrid,implicit}.go; zitadel pkg/op/server.go, pkg/client/rp/relying_party.go, pkg/oidc/token.go), so a divergence tool over just those files is not a toy. This works TODAY and is the recommended v1.

THREE MEASUREMENT TRAPS FROM d1l.7 (docs/notes/2026-08-04-go-js-lane-spike.md) THAT WOULD MAKE CONSENSUS/DIVERGENCE LIE:
 • IMPLEMENTS density is not comparable across languages: 586 edges in fosite vs 24 in node-oidc-provider. That reads Go structural typing vs JS prototypes, NOT spec agreement. Any divergence metric that counts edges will report a language difference as a spec disagreement.
 • Symbol counts are not comparable either: 11,066 of node-oidc-provider's 12,617 symbols (88%) are inferred type_alias noise from data literals. Normalise to function|method|class before any ratio.
 • Qualified-name SHAPE differs by lane: Go is package-FQN (github.com/ory/fosite.Fosite.WriteAccessError) and filePathOf() returns null for 100% of Go defs; JS/TS/PHP are file-shaped (lib/helpers/errors.js::InvalidToken). Key on structure, never on string form.

ALSO: node-oidc-provider is the WEAKEST of the three inputs for this tool, not the exemplar the design implied — 4 of 235 files carry a section citation and its citations are dominated by OpenID4VCI, not the core RFCs this epic targets. A three-way consensus that treats it as a peer vote on RFC 6749 is overclaiming; say N=2 with a JS cross-check where that is what the data supports.

title: test_oracle_invariants: two tests fail when pytest runs from repo root (cwd-sensitive path resolution)
description: test_folds_read_their_bundle_set_from_the_source_index and test_the_adapter_no_longer_shapes_the_source_ordering pass from ctkr/ (uv run python -m pytest tests/) but fail from repo root (uv --project ctkr run python -m pytest ctkr/tests/). Pre-existing: reproduced at 49e6cca and 2549e04 identically. Likely a relative-path resolution to a source index/export. Make them cwd-independent (resolve via __file__ like test_flow_write_surface does).
close_reason: Closed

title: add-term codegen should emit port_adapter.py probe dispatch stubs (read-surface half)
description: Found during the lab_test port (MetaCoding-wgy): the surface lane's add-term codegen + write-surface work landed record_log's lab fields in port_adapter.py but NOT the six probe dispatch methods; port-verify dispatches via getattr(adapter, spec.method), so without them no lab_test port could be scored — the blind BUILDER had to patch the instrument mid-build (flagged, traced honest by the fresh reader, but a hole in the surface lane's definition of done). Fix: add-term --apply should also generate the port-side dispatch stub in port_adapter.py (mirroring the material_type_recorded/equipment_used pattern), so the surface lane ships the whole measurement chain and builders never touch the instrument. Minor: the reader safety net caught it; close before the identity-queue fan-out (plant_type next).
close_reason: Delivered in the plant_type round (commit c027ce7): add-term codegen emits the port_adapter.py forwarding dispatch (value_shape-aware: scalar raw, list guarded+coerced to names), gated on _need_probe/_need_operation, with four codegen tests. Acceptance met: all four plant_type term dispatches pure codegen, zero hand edits. Bonus: _ASSERT_REQUIRED dup-guard false positive fixed (whole-file substring → table-scoped, under test).

title: Kernel-candidate decision: denormalize-on-write primitive (from the material quantity_presave fold)
description: MetaCoding-5ln implemented the material quantity_presave fold FEATURE-LOCAL (Wave1LogStore.materialFold: snapshot copy at record, guard chain mirroring farm_material EntityHooks.php; verified 5/5 against pack 046155d7d243). The spine-asset builder flagged it kernel_candidate: a generic 'denormalize-on-write from a referenced entity' register would also serve future folds of this shape. RULE-OF-THREE CLAIM WITHDRAWN (2026-08-02). A fresh adversarial judge refuted it against farmos-src@3fe0ce7e; this bead is still WAITING FOR EVIDENCE, unchanged.

Instance 3 (quick/movement) is NOT an instance. combinedAssetGeometries has four sites (Movement.php:127,143,154, defn :231) and every call is inside buildForm — a map-rendering hint and two '#type'=>'hidden','#value'=>... elements feeding JS. submitForm (:255-286) takes 'geometry' from form_state->getValue('geometry'), i.e. USER INPUT from the map widget; the field description at :120 says 'It is copied from the locations selected above, and can be modified'. title: ANNOTATES only fires for repo-local decorators, not imported ones
description:
ANNOTATES (decorator application, from MetaCoding-ijo.2) resolves the decorator by shortName to an in-repo function/class symbol (edges.ts tsHandleDecorator ~L505, and the Python path). Imported/framework decorators (@dataclass, @Component, @pytest.fixture, @app.route) don't resolve to a repo-local symbol, so NO edge is emitted.

## Context
Empirically ANNOTATES=0 on both MetaCoding (34 @dataclass decorators, indexed, 2078 py nodes) and aspects-webapp. Unit tests pass because they use repo-local decorators. To make ANNOTATES contribute on real code, emit edges to external/unresolved decorator symbols (as SCIP does with external refs, or a synthetic decorator node). LOW PRIORITY: per the ijo.3 marginal-entropy finding, low-count edge kinds barely move entropy, so decorators are unlikely to be worth much even if fixed. Documented so it isn't rediscovered.
close_reason: ANNOTATES now emits boundary-node edges for imported/unresolved decorators in both TS and Python paths (externalFallback), 58/58 edges tests pass; feeds A1 intention signal for T5a

title: PHP SCIP: resolve into Drupal core (full site build)
description: Current farmOS scip-php index resolves intra-farmOS refs (84%) but leaves ~797 refs into Drupal core / PHP stdlib external. For full fidelity (refs into ContentEntityBase, FormBase, etc.), build a real Drupal-11 farmOS site (farmOS docker/ dev env or composer create-project) so vendor/ has drupal/core, then run scip-php there. Deferred per Duke 2026-07-13 (chose intra-farmOS scope first).
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-07-13, deferred per Duke. Findings:
DISK: built farmOS+Drupal-11 site = 244MB (vendor 40M + web 204M; core 130M/11k .php, farm 57M/772, contrib 12M). Image farmos/farmos:4.x = 1.7GB incl runtime.
FEASIBLE: Drupal\Core base classes (ContentEntityBase/FormBase/ControllerBase/PluginBase) DO resolve from the built site's vendor (class_exists passes) — these are the main functor anchors. Core MODULE classes (Drupal\node, Drupal\views) need their PSR-4 registered separately.
APPROACH: docker pull farmos/farmos:4.x; docker cp /opt/drupal to disk; swap in target farmOS as web/profiles/farm; synthesize farm-only PSR-4 autoload; dump-autoload; run scip-php from site root so Drupal\Core resolves via vendor (index farm only, NOT core internals — resolve core as boundary targets).
BLOCKERS (scip-php maturity vs modern Drupal 8.4 syntax), each individually solvable:
 1. scip-php:latest image is PHP 8.2; farmOS core 11.3 needs 8.4 (platform_check) — neutralize vendor/composer/platform_check.php.
 2. Image's bundled nikic/php-parser too old for PHP 8.4 syntax -> parse crash on contrib + 4.x-dev farm.
 3. Current scip-php (dev-main, PHP 8.5, nikic 5.7) crashes in composer/class-map-generator PhpFileParser:58 on a site file.
 4. Running scip-php inside the site: its bundled nikic collides with Drupal's own vendor/nikic -> NodeTraverser crash.
LOADER TODO for boundary edges: Pass 2b currently SKIPS external refs (externalRefsSkipped). To capture farmOS->Drupal\Core EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS, emit edges to boundary nodes via externalQn for resolved scip-php external symbols (gate to Drupal\ targets to avoid symfony/stdlib noise).
See memory scip-php-integration.

title: extra_types can gate a resource type no collection sweeps
description:
Fresh judge of hy6.28 (farmos-port 6a75c1d). Minor, and half-admitted in the field comment at tools/ledger.py:293-297.

Measured: a Ledger with collections=['asset/animal'], extra_types=['log--medical'] gates {asset--animal, log--medical} and then happily probes and keeps fixtures at /api/log/medical. The by-ID absence check still covers them (it walks self.created). The PREFIX SWEEP does not — it iterates self.collections only (ledger.py:512) — so the belt-and-braces net has a hole exactly where extra_types is used, and so does the by-collection leftovers report in _absence_check (ledger.py:559).

The field comment says extra_types is for 'resource types the run touches that NO collection above names ... a type probed but never swept is a type whose fixtures the absence check cannot see'. It does not say the obvious consequence: a build can use extra_types to satisfy the derivation for a type it CREATES in, buying itself gate clearance while opting out of the sweep. Nothing forbids keep= on such a type.

REMEDY: refuse keep= on a collection whose resource type came only from extra_types, or fold extra_types into the sweep.
